observation: Proceeds from liquidated damages and bank interest income were recorded as liabilities in the General Fund (GF) and Trust Fund (TF) books of accounts, respectively, while unidentified balances remained unreconciled and still lumped as liabilities in the TF, aggregating to ₱2.656 Million, a non-conformance to PD 1445 and NGAS Manual for LGUs, thereby affecting the reliability, accuracy and faithful presentation of certain balances presented in the financial statements for the period ending December 31, 2022.

Sixty-two (62) reconciling items (comprising of unbooked stale checks, debit/credit memo, interest income, and book errors) remained unrecorded/unadjusted in the books of accounts while three (3) already closed PPSB bank accounts were still prepared with Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS) despite their questionable existence, totaling ₱917,848.09 and ₱130,495.60, respectively, contrary to Sections 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, resulting in a net understatement of ₱697,633.53 which affected the accuracy and reliability of the Cash in Bank and the corresponding accounts reflected in the financial statements for CY 2022, aside from the doubtful existence of those bank accounts already closed with a net negative balance in the books of accounts amounting ₱64,920.50.

Various claims were paid in January to October CY 2022 without bearing the approval of the proper officials on the disbursement vouchers, obligation requests and payrolls while some of these documents were signed by unknown representatives, aggregating to ₱42.638 Million, due to failure to implement a sound internal control system on obligations and disbursements, contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445, Section 344 of RA 7160, NGAS Manual and the Local Treasury Operations Manual, resulting in unauthorized transactions, weak internal control system and that the full accountability over the disbursed funds could not be established.
Disbursements related to infrastructure projects implemented thru straight contracts have various deficiencies, as follows:

Various procurement-related disbursements totaling ₱22.227 Million were not adequately supported with the required documentary requirements and with other noted deficiencies, in contravention to Section 4(6) of PD 1445, COA Circular 2012-001 and RA 9184 and its revised IRR, thus, the regularity and propriety of such disbursements could not be ascertained.

Honoraria were paid to some officials of other local and national agencies, and to the hired legal consultant, with either incomplete documents or bereft of legal basis, totaling ₱502,220.00, inconsistent with the specific provisions of Section 4 of PD 1445, COA Circular 2012-001, DBM’s Compensation Policy Guidelines No. 98-1, and RA 7160, thereby affecting the propriety, validity and legality of these transactions.

Similar procurement items included in the Annual Procurement Plan (APP) of LGU-Baungon were not consolidated on a quarterly basis and improperly presented per department/office instead as one procuring entity, in violation to the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, thereby defeating the main purpose of consolidation procedure and the numerous unnecessary purchases and splitting of contract had been undertaken by the BAC, including the unwarranted resort from competitive bidding to alternative methods of procurement.

Seven (7) issued replacement checks totaling ₱64,834.33 were drawn without Disbursement Vouchers (DVs) and with incomplete documentary requirements, thereby, failed to provide evidential proof that the procedural requirements for the issuance of check were complied with pursuant to pertinent provisions of Republic Act No. 7160, Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for LGUs and Local Treasury Operations Manual and created doubt on the regularity and validity of the disbursed transactions.

Various reimbursements for fuel were included in the travel claims of various municipal officials and employees totaling ₱481,494.86 without adhering to the proper procurement procedures prior withdrawal/delivery and to the required documentation to support the transactions, inconsistent with the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184 and PD 1445, thus defeating the intentions of the said law to promote economy, competitiveness, transparency and accountability in the procurement process and cast doubt on the validity and legality of the disbursed transactions.

Registration fees paid in advance totaling ₱489,000.00 for trainings/seminars/conferences to be attended by some municipal officials and employees were improperly treated as an outright expense rather than as an individual cash advance, in violation to Section 2.0 of COA Circular No. 96-004, hence, the accountabilities over these supposed-to-be cash advances were not established at the time of payment and that various documents to substantiate the disbursed transactions were not attached. Moreover, with this current fiscal practice, the government funds are not properly safeguarded against possible wastage.

Disbursement Vouchers and payrolls, including their related supporting documents, were not stamped “PAID” in violation of COA Circular No. 92-389 dated November 03, 1992, thereby, opens the possibility of reusing the supporting documents for another claim of the same nature of expenditures and shows a weak internal control in the disbursement of government funds.

Various salaries and wages, RATA and loyalty cash awards/incentives paid to some municipal officials and employees from January to November CY 2022, totaling ₱529,001.43, were not completely substantiated with relevant documentary requirements as prescribed by COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thereby casting reservations on the validity and propriety of the disbursed transactions and may result to issuance of audit suspension or disallowance.

Payments for monetization of leave credits and terminal leave benefits lacked the necessary documentation as required by COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thus, the validity and propriety of the disbursed transactions could not be ascertained amounting to ₱1,139,184.52.

Completed project remained as “Construction in Progress (CIP)” not reclassified to its appropriate Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) account, inconsistent with Section 27 of IPSAS 1 and Section 50 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs), Volume I, thereby resulting to an erroneous balances of CIP, Accounts Payable and the PPE accounts thus affecting its fair presentation in the financial statement at year-end.

The accuracy and reliability of the year-end balance of the Cash in Bank- Local Currency, Current Accounts in the total amount of P1,508,894,592.67 is doubtful due to: a) non reversion of unclaimed checks in the cashbook balance totaling P57,343,501.89, b) erroneous treatment of cash on hand as deposit in transit, c) reconciling items remain unadjusted, and d) cashbook balance does not reconcile with SL contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, Section 43 of Chapter 1 of MNGAS, Section 3.3 and 3.4 of COA Circular No. 96-011, Section 74 of PD 1445, and Section 181 of GAAM Volume 1.

The existence of the reported PPEs and the reliability of its balances at year-end in the total amount of P12,536,009,089.41 could not be ascertained due to the inability of the Inventory Committee to conduct the physical count on the subject accounts, failure of the PGSO to update the property card, no conduct of regular reconciliation of PGSO and Accounting Office property records, existence of unrecognizable items in the schedule, and failure to record the donated zoo animals in the books contrary to existing rules and regulations.

Prescribed policies and procedures for an effective control and accounting of inventories such as: perpetual inventory system, maintenance of stock cards and conduct of physical count of inventories are not strictly adhered to contrary to Sections 112 and 122 of PD 1445, Section 4.s, 114, 120, 126 and 124 of the Volume 1 of the Manual of the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs, thus casting doubts on the existence and accuracy of the reported balance of the Inventories in the Financial Statement as of December 31, 2022

Premiums paid for insurance of various PGB properties were expense outright and no adjusting entries were recognized for the unexpired portion, contrary to IPSAS I and Section 62 of the MNGAS Volume 1, thus affecting the fairness of the balance reported in the FS at year end.

Prescribed policies and procedures for an efficient control over the granting, utilization and liquidation of cash advances are not strictly adhered to contrary to COA Circular No. 97-002 February 10, 1997 as amended by COA Circular No. 2006-05, COA Circular No. 2015-009 and Section 101.2 of PD No. 1445, and COA Circular 2012-001, thus affecting the accuracy of the presented balances as of year-end and casting doubt on the propriety of the cash advance granted to the affected personnel and put the government funds in the possession or custody of the special disbursing officers at risk from being indemnified in case of possible loss, respectively.

Cost not attributable to the infrastructure projects were recorded as Construction in Progress (CIP) in the books of the Special Education Fund of the Province, contrary to IPSAS 1 and 17 and Section 4 of the MNGAS Volume 1 thus affecting the fairness of the reported balances in the year-end financial statement.

The Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) for the year 2022 was not submitted to COA contrary to Paragraph 21 and Paragraph 14 of the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1 and 24, thus precluding the audit team to verify where and how its resources were obtained and used in accordance with the approved budget.

The accrual basis of accounting was not strictly applied in the recording of revenue and liability arising from hospital and professional fees generated by all eight (8) provincial hospitals, delay on receipt of return to hospital and denied claims, Journal Entry Vouchers drawn to recognized receivable, income and trust liabilities for prior and current year had no supporting documents, and presence of huge amounts of slashed, returned and denied claims contrary to the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) No. 1 and 9 and Sections 2, 111 and 123 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thereby affecting the fairness of presentation of the financial statement at the end of CY 2022 as well as denying the Provincial Government on the use of the forgone income, as a result of the slashed, returned and denied claims, to other beneficial projects that would redound to the benefit the general public.

The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) failed (1) to furnish the auditor on time the copies of purchase orders and perfected contract procured within five (5) working days after execution and (2) to submit back the one-hundred twelve (112) endorsed contracts for deficient documentation to support the procurement activities aggregating an amount of P 899,071,226.63, contrary to the provisions of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations and Section 3.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-001, thus preventing the auditor from undertaking timely review and ascertain the compliance of the procurement process and the regularity of the awarded contracts to RIRR of RA 9184.

The Bids and Awards Committee failed to strictly adhere to the submission of pertinent documents supporting the contracts on the procurement for the supply and delivery of three units of double cab vehicles and one unit of brand new 10 wheeler self-loading truck with boom crane in the amount of P5,967,000.00 and P9,998,000.00, respectively and observed that inconsistencies on procurement activities runs counter to the specific provisions of Republic Act No. 9184, and the relevant provisions of COA Circular No. 2009-001, casting doubts on the regularity of the procurement process, the validity of the awarded contract and its subsequent payment.

The Province paid terminal leave benefits to (14) fourteen employees who are not yet separated from the service contrary to Rule XVI of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order (EO) 292 as amended by Civil Service Commission (CSC) Memorandum Circular No. 41 s. of 1998. Moreover, payments of Terminal Leave Benefits totaling P 29,021,828.05 to the officials and employees of the Provincial Government of Bukidnon as of December 31, 2022 were not supported with complete documents required under COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012 to ensure that said payments are free from encumbrances, thus, affecting the validity thereof.

The take home pay of some employees of the LGU is below the minimum required by Section 55 of the General Provisions of Republic Act 11639 or the General Appropriations Act of 2022 due to the leniency of the LGU in restricting deductions of obligations in their salaries, thus failing to ensure in receiving decent portion of their earnings.

Payments of the Collective Negotiations Agreement (CNA), Service Recognition Incentive (SRI), and Economic Assistance were either not supported with the required documents, proof of compliance with the PS limitation or lack legal basis, contrary to existing rules and regulations.
The Provincial Government paid Premium on Wages to personnel hired thru job order contracts without specific legal basis, thus casting doubt on the propriety and regularity of the transaction.

The procurement duration of the sub-projects under Investments in Rural Enterprise and Agriculture and Fisheries Productivity (I-REAP) exceeded the suggested procurement timeline per PRDP Module 2- I-REAP Procurement Guidelines and scheduled procurement plan provided in the Implementation Management Agreement (IMA), respectively, thereby, causing the delay in the awarding of the contract and the implementation of the specific projects thus depriving the intended beneficiaries of immediate use and enjoyment of the project.

Appropriate documents for the procurement of goods for PRDP projects totaling P1,971,706.00 were not attached to the submitted contracts to support compliance to the activities identified in the procurement timeline prescribed by PRDP Module 2- I-REAP Procurement Guidelines, thus casting doubt on the validity of the contracts and propriety procurement process, respectively.

Funds received from government agencies for the Financial Assistance to LGUs Hit by Typhoon Odette and Local government support fund – Support to barangay development program (LGSF-SBDP) totaling P26.306M and P72.027M, respectively remained outstanding as at December 31, 2022 and the undisbursed balances were not yet returned to the Source Agencies or to the National Treasury in violation of Section 99 of Presidential Decree No. 1455, COA Circular No. 94-013 and Local Budget Circulars 135 and 141.

Lack of internal control on ensuring that infrastructure projects funded by PGB are constructed at government owned sites and the availability of documents required for application of building permit, contrary to Section 305 of RA 7160, PD 1445 and PD 1096, thus risking implemented projects to claim from other parties and delay in completion of the projects and depriving the Province of its benefits from the expected income for the commercial buildings, respectively.

Failure of the Bids and Awards Committee to submit the necessary documents to the contracts on the procurement of eleven (11) 20% Development Fund projects totaling P 215,566,035.48 as required by the provisions of RA 9184 and its Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations and COA Circular 2009-001 precludes the auditor from ascertaining its compliance to the procurement process, validity of the award.

Projects that are not implementation-ready totaling P407.2 million and P200.7 million for the current year and the Continuing Appropriations, respectively, were integrated into the 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) Programs, Projects, and Activities (PPAs) for CY 2022, inconsistent with the directive of DBM-DOF-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1 dated November 4, 2020, resulting to a low utilization rate for the current year and for the Continuing Appropriations- 20% LDF, thus, the fund was not optimally utilized which consequently deprived the public of the benefits that could have been derived from the immediate and maximum use of the funds.

Discrepancy amounting to P3.3Million between the Report on Sources and Utilization of DRRMF and the accounting records due to non- reconciliation, contrary to Sections 111 and 123 of Presidential Decree No.1445, thereby creating doubt on the accuracy of both report and records and affecting the correctness and accuracy of the disclosure made in the Notes to Financial Statements.

The existence, validity and accuracy of the reported Inventories’ balances amounting ₱35,340,153.07 could not be ascertained due to the non-preparation of RIS and SSMI particularly for Construction Materials Inventory and the non-reconciliation between the records of the Municipal Accounting Office and the RPCI, in violation of section 111 (2) of PD 1445, par. 44 of IPSAS No .12 and, sections 121, 122 and 124 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Vol. 1 thus, casting doubts on the accuracy and reliability of the Inventories presented in the CY 2022 Statement of Financial Position.

The disbursements for advances for travelling expenses totaling ₱563,936.00 were directly recorded as Traveling and Training Expenses instead of recording them as Advances to Officers and Employees, in violation to Section 2.0 of COA Circular No. 96-004 hence, the Advances to Officers and Employees asset account have been understated while the Traveling and Training Expenses were overstated and, the accountability of the concerned official/employee to strictly liquidate his cash advance within (30) days after his return to his official station was not established.

The LGU’s financial, medical and burial assistance totaling ₱4,050,828.00 were not supported with complete documentation thus, non-compliant to Section 4(6) of PD 1445 and Sections VI and VII of DSWD MC No. 11, series of 2019 hence, the propriety, legality, and validity claims could not be ascertained.

The LGU made honoraria payments to its municipal workers and volunteers totaling ₱2,003,900.00 which were not supported with Approved Daily Time Records (DTRs) or duly verified/ accepted accomplishment reports thus, not in accordance to the documentary requirements set by COA Circular No. 2012-001 hence, cast doubts on the basis of the claims, which may result to the issuance of Notice of Suspension, if not immediately complied.

The LGU granted financial assistance for prizes for sports activities o its various puroks, sitios and chapels to their respective purok leaders, sitio leaders and chapel officers totaling ₱126,500.00, who were not authorized representatives of their barangays, and without any documents to support that such financial assistance were used for their intended public purposes, in violation of section 384 of R.A. 7160, section 4(2) and (6) of P.D. 1445 and items 3 and 5 of the General Requirements for all types of Disbursements as provided by COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby casting doubt on the propriety and legality of the transactions.

729 out of 776 (94%) procurement transactions had attached documents which indicated different modes of procurement undertaken per transaction thus, non-compliant to Section V of Annex H of the Revised IRR of RA 9184 and instructions on the preparation of a Purchase Order per Volume II of the NGAS for LGUs hence, created doubts as to the propriety of the transactions and the actual procurement process undertaken.

The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) had a discretionary method in breaking ties among suppliers with the same price quotations for 226 (100%) procurement transactions for meals and snacks totaling P3,057,262.50, in violation to Appendix 11 of the Revised IRR of RA 9184 and GPPB Circular No. 06-2005 thus, cast doubts on the propriety and legality of the transactions and the procurement process undertaken.

Disbursements for the labor component of construction projects totaling P939,750.00 for the period January to November 2022, lack complete documentation in violation of Section 4(6) of the PD No. 1445, thus the validity and propriety of the disbursements cannot be established.

Purchases of supplies and materials were not recorded using the Perpetual Inventory Method or debited to an Inventory Account but instead were treated immediately as expenses, which is not in accordance with Sections 114, 52, 116, 121 and 123 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual for LGUs, thus, exposing the assets to loss and the accountability thereof cannot be established.

Disbursements of vehicle parts for repairs and maintenance, aggregating P672,028.05 for the period January to October 2022, were not supported with complete documentation required in Item 9.1.3.4 of COA Circular 2012-001, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the disbursements.

Fuel disbursement vouchers and its supporting documents are observed to contain different discrepancies, contrary to COA Circular 2012-001, Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, Sections 305(a) and 350 of RA No. 7160, and Section 7.2 of the 2016 Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA No. 9184, thus, the legality, validity, accuracy and propriety of the said transactions cannot be established. Moreover, it resulted to an overstatement of expenses in the FY 2022.

Various financial reports/documents related to the Philippine Rural Development Project (PRDP) were still not submitted to the audit team contrary to Sections 3.4.1 to 3.4.5 of the PRDP Financial Management Operations Guidelines, thereby, precluding timely validation and audit of financial transactions involving the PRDP Project of the municipal government.

Requisitions of supplies, equipment, and materials needed for each quarter by various offices were not consolidated. Moreover, the Project Procurement Management Plans (PPMPs) of each office were also not consolidated into one Annual Procurement Plan (APP), which is not in accordance with Sections 7 and 48.2 of RA No. 9184 IRR and Section 116(c) of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual for LGUs, resulting in evasion of the public bidding requirement and thereby providing no assurance on the reasonableness of the procurement cost.

The LGU’s procurement process through alternative methods is deemed improper, ineffective, and inefficient as evidenced by the following instances: a) incomplete details provided on purchase orders, b) advance deliveries, c) partial/multiple deliveries, and d) non-imposition of liquidated damages for delayed deliveries, which is not in accordance with Item 3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-003, thereby resulting to irregular transactions and exposes the government to unnecessary risk.

Extensions of contract time were granted to contractors without sufficient documentation to justify the claim, in violation of Annex E of the Revised IRR of Republic Act (RA) No. 9184, thereby casting doubt on the validity of the time extension and precluding the LGU from collecting liquidated damages from the contractors.

Disbursements totaling P17.145M for the Rehabilitation of 14 Barangay roads funded out of the financial assistance from the Provincial Government of Bukidnon were recorded as Construction in Progress, a Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) account, instead of as Repairs and Maintenance (R&M), an expense account, contrary to paragraph 13 of IPSAS 17, thereby, overstating PPE account and understating the R&M account of the LGU by the same amounts.

Two completed buildings in the sum of P24.494M and three fully liquidated fund transfers totaling P47.116M from the Provincial Government of Bukidnon (PGB) were still recorded in the Buildings Account and Due to LGUs account, respectively, in the Trust Fund books of accounts of LGU despite liquidation of fund to the source agency, a non-compliance to Section 104 of the NGAS and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thus, resulted to:

Fund Transfers totaling P1.4M to 12 Barangays of Dangcagan for KALAHI CIDDS project as LGU’s counterpart funded out of the 20% Development Fund were not supported with complete documentation and were erroneously recorded as an outright expense, a non-compliance to COA Circular No. 2012-001 and COA Circular No. 94-013, which may result to weak or non- monitoring of funds transferred to the barangays and affected the financial statements of the LGU for CY 2022 as follows:

The LGU failed to comply with the recording requirements of Real Property and Special Education Taxes provided under Section 20, 22 and 23 of the Manual on New Government Accounting System, thus, affecting the Financial Statements of the LGU as follows:

Reconciling items comprising of stale checks, unrecorded disbursement and quarterly interest amounting to P542,032.82 and accounts payable in the amount of P1,445,116.37 remained unrecorded/unadjusted in the books of accounts, contrary to COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the balances of Cash in Bank and the corresponding expense and income accounts in the financial statements in the calendar year 2022.

The Municipality appointed 377 Job Orders from the period January 1 to March 23, 2022 and paid the amount of P2.352M for their wages for January to February 2022 despite the absence of approved Annual Budget for calendar year 2022, a non-compliance to Section 305 (a) and Section 323 of Republic Act 7160, thus, the legality of the appointments and disbursements cannot be established.

The Municipality of Dangcagan granted medical and burial assistance in the amount of P1.486M as Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) but failed to establish clear guidelines thereof which resulted to various deficiencies noted in audit contrary to Section 123 and Section 4 (6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, thus, validity, and propriety of the transaction could not be established and payment thereof may expose government funds to possible misuse.

The LGU failed to formulate and prepare a Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Fund Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP) or Annual Investment Plan (AIP) for the prior years’ unexpended Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Fund (LDRRMF) in the total amount of P13,343,802.01 contrary to COA Circular 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012, and NDRRMC-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-1 dated March 25, 2013. Thus, the prior years’ unexpended LDRRMF remained unutilized and the LGU failed to meet the purpose of the fund which to provide support to disaster risk reduction and management activities of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (LDRRMC).

Disbursement vouchers for payments of seven (7) vehicles totaling P7.274M were not completely supported with required documents and observed to have deficiencies a non-compliance to Section 4 (6) of PD No. 1445, otherwise known as the “Government Auditing Code of the Philippines”, COA Circular No. 2012-001, and Procurement Manual for Local Government Units, thus, doubt exist as to the validity and propriety of the disbursements and procurement thereof were not done efficiently.

Three (3) projects in calendar year 2015-2021 in the sum of P2.897M remained uncompleted and balance of two (2) projects that are considered completed totaling P424,615.686 was not reverted to the surplus as of December 31, 2022 in the 20% Development Fund, a non-compliance to Sections 322 and 336 of Republic Act 7160, thus, the fund was not fully utilized and the amount of P560,664.66 was spent other than its intended purpose.

Fuel consumption of the LGU did not undergo proper procurement process, were not properly monitored and reported by the General Services Office (GSO), and were not properly supported with complete documentary requirements contrary to Section 88 of P.D. 1445, and the provisions of RA No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRRs) as well as the provisions of the Manual on Audit of Fuel Consumption of Government Motor Vehicles as prescribed by COA Circular No. 77-61 dated September 26, 1977, thus, transparency, accountability, equity, efficiency, and economy in the procurement of fuel could not be guaranteed exposing the Government to possible wasteful, excessive, unnecessary, and irregular expenditures for fuel consumption in the total amount of P3,351,406.21 and resulting to expenditures in excess of the budget totaling to P203,082.24.

The LGU paid Gasoline Allowance totaling to P163,500.00 for the fuel consumption of private motor vehicles of agriculturists and midwives traveling to the various barangays of the Municipality contrary to Section 5(a) of E.O. No. 77 casting doubt as to the regularity of the disbursements.

Disbursements for Traveling Expenses totaling to P3,480,169.58 did not comply with the allowable daily travel expenses and documentary requirements prescribed by the provisions of E.O. No. 77 dated March 15, 2019 and COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, casting doubt as to the propriety of the claims, resulting to over-payment of traveling expenses totaling to P117,321.00 and could result in the suspension of the claims totaling to P1,523,655.21.

The Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivable balances of LGU Don Carlos as of December 31, 2022 reflected material discrepancies amounting to P 36,358,965.35 and P36,508,769.76, respectively, as compared to the balances stated in the Summary of Delinquent Taxes as of year-end due to non-compliance with Section 20, Vol. 1 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs), thereby casting doubt on the reliability and accuracy of the said accounts in the financial statements.

The accuracy and reliability of some Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) and Liability accounts presented in the CY 2022 Statement of Financial Position are doubtful due to items in the subsidiary ledgers under “Unidentified Subsidiary Accounts” totaling P61.113 Million and P4.341 Million, respectively, contrary to Section 111 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 10, Chapter 1, Volume II of the NGAS Manual for LGUs, thus, casting doubt as to the existence, accuracy and reliability of the amounts presented in the financial statements.

The agency’s reciprocal/intra-agency receivables and payables accounts amounting to P8.412 million were not fully eliminated upon consolidation of the financial statements, a departure from the requirements of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) No. 6 and Section 111 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thus, affected the fair presentation of the specific accounts in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2022, particularly, current Receivables and Intra-Agency Payables accounts both overstated by P8.412 million.

The agency’s unexpended balance of the Local Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) totaling P7,435,835.65 as of year-end was not transferred to the Special Trust Fund in the Trust Fund books nor discussed in the Notes to Financial Statements contrary to Sections 5.1.10 and 5.1.16 of COA Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012 and Sections 6.4 and 6.5 of NDRRMC-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-1 dated March 25, 2013, resulting to the understatement of the Cash account under the Trust Fund and moreover, non-transfer of the unexpended balance exposes the funds to risks of being used for purposes other than for which the LDRRMF was established.

The agency’s reported balances for its Inventory accounts aggregating to P5.165 million as of December 31, 2022 could not be relied upon due to inconsistent observance of the Perpetual Inventory Method and failure to conduct periodic physical count of inventory items, contrary to Sections 114 and 124 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual for LGUs, Vol. 1, thereby casting doubts as to the existence, completeness and accuracy of the balances presented in the CY 2022 Financial Statements.

The agency was not able to implement the guidelines on the increase of capitalization threshold for tangible items from P15,000.00 to P50,000.00 for various semi-expendable properties procured, a departure from the requirements set forth in COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022. The noted departures are as follows: (a) Improperly accounted Property, Plant and Equipment items - P166,280.00; (b) Semi-expendable items classified as Inventories – P274,870.00; (c) Items below the threshold but capitalized - P186,440.00; and (d) Items not Supported with Inventory Custodians Slip - P649,018.00, thus, the accuracy and reliability of the balances presented in the agency’s Financial Statements as of December 31, 2022 could not be assured.

Disbursement Vouchers pertaining to Collective Negotiation Agreement (CNA) Incentives and Service Recognition Incentive (SRI) for FY 2022 amounting to P4.6 Million were not duly supported with the required documents inconsistent with the provisions of PD No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’, DBM Budget Circular No. 2022-3 – ‘Guidelines on the Grant of the Collective Negotiation Agreement (CNA) Incentive for FY 2022’, COA Circular No. 2012-001 – ‘Prescribing the Revised Guidelines and Documentary Requirements for Common Government Transactions’ and DBM Budget Circular 2022-4 – ‘Guidelines on the Grant of Service Recognition Incentive to Government Employees for FY 2022’, thus, casting doubt as to the validity and legality of the aforementioned disbursements and likewise precluding the audit team from effectively and timely evaluating the said transactions.

The agency’s various disbursements of the Local Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) aggregating to P1,612,901.32 (gross) were not among the pre-disaster preparedness activities allowed to be charged from the fund, contrary to Section 5 of Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-1 issued by the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC), the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) and the Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG), thus, depleted the fund and preventing the full attainment of the objectives of the fund for which it was established.

Economic Assistance amounting to P3,350,000.00 was granted to officials and employees of the LGU despite not being supported by any legal basis which allows the said payment, inconsistent with the provisions of PD No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’, DBM Budget Circular No. 2006-1 – ‘Grant of Collective Negotiation Agreement (CNA) Incentive’, COA Circular No. 2012-003 – ‘Updated Guidelines for the Prevention and Disallowance of Irregular, Unnecessary, Excessive, Extravagant and Unconscionable Expenditures’ and COA Circular No. 2013-003 – ‘Reiteration of Audit Disallowance of Payments without Legal Basis of Allowances, Incentives, and Other Benefits of Government Officials and Employees in the NGAs, LGUs, and GOCCs and their Subsidiaries’ thus, casting doubt as to the validity and legality of the aforementioned disbursements.

Payments for labor pertaining to projects implemented by Administration contained incomplete supporting documents and integrated inconsistent policies in the accounting of the said projects, contrary to the principles mandated in PD No. 1445 –‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’, the 2016 Revised IRR of RA No. 9184 – ‘Government Procurement Reform Act’ and the executed Pakyaw Agreement, thus casting doubt as to the propriety and regularity of the transactions and precluding the auditor from the effective examination and verification thereof.

Inconsistencies in the timelines of the Contracts, Purchase Orders and Notices to Proceed have been observed contrary to the principles mandated in the Revised IRR of RA 9184 thus, hampering the continuous conduct of the procurement process leading to interruptions in the commencement and delivery of projects and goods, respectively.

Paid disbursement vouchers totaling P695,111.26 incurred in CY 2022 was not recorded in the books of accounts of the LGU, contrary to Paragraph 3.10 of the IPSAS Conceptual Framework, due to the non-submission thereof by the Municipal Treasurers Office (MTO) to the Municipal Accounting Office (MACCO), thereby, overstating the Cash Account of the LGU by the herein stated amount.

Additional cash advances were granted to Accountable Officers despite failure to settle the previous cash advances due them, contrary to Section 4 and 5 of COA Circular No. 97-003 dated February 10, 1997, thereby resulting to an unliquidated cash advance as of December 31, 2022 totaling ₱27,589,455.01, exposing the funds to possible misuse and making the Asset and Expenses account unreliable.

The procurement of various inventories for distribution and consumption of the LGU totaling at least P21,819,370.50 in CY 2022 did not undergo proper procurement procedure such as competitive bidding, shopping, or small value procurement, as maybe applicable, contrary to Section 2 of RA 9184 and was procured thru ‘cash advance’, contrary to Section 3.2 of COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997,thereby constituting irregular expenditures.

The improper procurement method employed, the non-submission of reports relative to distributed/consumed inventories, and the non-maintenance of Stock Cards (SC) and Supplies Ledger Cards (SLC) resulted to the failure of the LGU to report actual inventories procured and used within the period and difficulty in determining the actual balances of the inventories of the LGU at year end, contrary to Paragraph 44 and 46 of IPSAS 12, thus, the Inventory reported at ₱95,337,787.07 in CY 2022 could not be ascertained.

The LGU failed to adjust the balances of the Financial Statements in the appropriate period, and to disclose the prior period errors amounting to P43,363,514.96 (net) contrary to IPSAS 3, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Disbursements from trust fund totaling P29,759,115.40 in CY 2022 were treated as an automatic reduction of liability (Due to NGA, Due to LGU) and addition to the LGUs Government Equity despite LGUs failure deliver/perform completely its obligation in accordance to the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and existing budget circulars, as applicable, contrary to Paragraphs 44-47 and BC11 of IPSAS 23, thereby, understating the Liability Account of the LGU by P25,332,866.97 with specific impact on Government Equity, indeterminate.

Procurement/construction of assets funded from the trust fund totaling P11,215,860.11 and P7,018,226.54 in CYs 2021 and 2022, respectively, were not recorded as assets but deducted immediately to the Trust Fund Liability Accounts of the LGU, contrary to Paragraph 14 and 26 of IPSAS 17 and IPSAS 23, thereby, understating the Property, Plant and Equipment Account of the LGU by P19,333,761.65.

The CY 2021 balances of Government Equity, Transfers from General Fund of Unspent DRRMF and Trust Liability – DRRM reported in the Financial Statements did not tally with the correct balance in the books of the LGU and no restatement and disclosures were made relative thereto, contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, thus, the ending and beginning balances of Government Equity Account in CYs 2021 and 2022, respectively did not tally, having a difference of P20,585,420.48, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The non-submission of the MTO of the Certified List of Taxpayers and Taxes Due caused the MAO to record the tax receivable and deferred credits at the beginning of the year based on estimates prepared by the Municipal Assessor’s Office, contrary to Section 20, Volume I of NGAS for LGUs which resulted to unreliable RPT receivable balance as of year-end amounting to P7,420,821.65 and P6,647,053.61, respectively and hindering the proper monitoring of tax collections and delinquencies.

The LGU records RPT-Basic and SET accounts net of discounts for taxpayers who paid real property tax in advance contrary to Chapter 2 of PD 1445 thereby understating both the RPT-Basic and SET and Discount on Advance Payments account by P1,075,839.34.

The balance of the LGU’s total Outstanding Loans Payable amounting to P46,488,293.72 in the subsidiary ledgers is higher by P1,858,829.43 with the creditor’s records contrary to Section 111 and 112 of PD 1445 because of the inadequate controls in the conduct of timely reconciliation of the LGU’s records with that of the creditor, thus, the Loans Payable and Cash in Bank balance as of December 31, 2022 under the GF Proper is overstated and understated by the same amount, respectively.

Penalties resulting from delayed payments of RPT/SET by taxpayers were not recorded in full and were lumped together with the RPT- Basic and SET contrary to Chapter 2 of PD 1445, thereby understating the Fines and Penalties account by P783,394.79 and overstating the RPT- Basic and SET accounts by the P774,543.89.

Utilization/liquidation of fund transfers from other LGU and General Fund recorded in the Trust Fund books were not recognized as revenue despite that conditions thereof have already been met, contrary to Paragraphs 45 & 46 and BC11 of IPSAS 23, thereby understating the revenue account of the LGU and caused the Trust Fund to report a deficit totaling P1,720,885.71 equivalent to the amount of recorded expense on the said fund during the period.

The unexpended Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Fund (LDRRMF) in CY 2010 amounting P456,381.00 was not reverted to the General Fund contrary to Section 21 of RA 10121, thus, depriving the Municipality’s constituents of the social services.

The Municipal Accounting office missed to recognize and record receivables/collectibles in the General Fund books of accounts of the LGU of delinquent and disconnected consumers of Kadingilan Water District (KWD) in an accumulated amount of ₱ 859,574.22 which was not in accordance to IPSAS 1 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby, understating the total receivable and income accounts in the respective years the transactions were incurred and eventually affecting the Government Equity account in the LGU’s Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2022.

Properties donated by LGU Kadingilan, originally funded by the Provincial Government of Bukidnon, were derecognized in the General Fund books of account of the LGU upon transfer to various barangays without proper authority and Deeds of Donation contrary to the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between the Municipal Mayor and the Provincial Governor, thereby, understated the total assets and total government equity by ₱ 3.985 million as of December 31, 2022 and affected the propriety, legality and validity of the donations.

Completed projects under Trust Fund aggregated to ₱ 14.6M were still recorded under the ‘Construction in Progress (CIP) – Infrastructure Assets’ account in the books of the agency as of December 31, 2022 contrary to the provisions of COA Circular 2015-009 and Section 104, Volume I of NGAS Manual for LGUs tainting the propriety, accuracy and reliability of the affected accounts.

Numerous agricultural equipment turned-over by Department of Agriculture (DA) Regional Field Office 10 to LGU Kadingilan, thru the Municipal Mayor, last March 3, 2022 were not recognized in the General Fund books of account of the LGU upon receipt in contravention to a specific provision in the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between the Municipal Mayor and the DA 10 Regional Executive Director, henceforth, understated the total assets and total government equity by ₱ 1.589 million as of December 31, 2022 and possible loss of assets.

(a) Complete delivery/installation of office cubicle was already recognized and recorded as an asset under “Furniture and Fixtures” and a liability under “Accounts Payable” in the books of accounts, respectively; (b) LGU Kadingilan allowed advance payment and progress payment for the said project classified as “GOODS”, contrary to Section 17.14 of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), COA Circular No. 2015-009 and Section 3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-003, thereby, overstated the total assets and total liabilities by ₱ 2.480 million as of December 31, 2022; said transactions if not favorable to the government and might fall under an irregular transaction.

Erroneous journal entry made to match the expense accounts in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts resulted in the overstatement of accounts payable and total expenses both by ₱ 723,854.00 in the Statement of Financial Position and Statement of Financial Performance, respectively, in CY 2022, contrary to Section 111(2) and 112 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Annex B of COA Circular 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thus, affecting the accuracy and reliability of the Statement of Financial Position and Statement of Financial Performance, respectively, in CY 2022.

LGU Kadingilan collected several advance cash payments from numerous barangays which aggregated to ₱ 5,550,898.20 as of December 31, 2022 intended for the rehabilitation and maintenance of barangay roads even before the projects were implemented and were wrongly treated as trust funds contrary to Section 88.1 and Section 3(4) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, therefore, the propriety and validity of the collections could not be ascertained.

The collections/income from the LGU’s Municipal Food Terminal from May 9, 2017 to October 1, 2022 in the total amount of ₱ 1,420,305.76 were erroneously recorded in the Trust Fund under the account “Due to LGUs” and were eventually transferred and recorded in the General Fund under the account “Subsidy from Other Funds”, contrary to IPSAS 1, COA Circular No. 2015-009, Section 65.1 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 17, Volume I, Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for LGUs, thus, casted doubts as to the correctness, accuracy and reliability of the affected accounts.

LGU Kadingilan missed to return the unspent amount of ₱ 123,397.17 pertaining to the various Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) booked in the General Fund to the Bureau of the Treasury as of December 31, 2022 which was not in conformity to the Philippine Supreme Court Decision G.R. No. 208566 dated November 19, 2013, thus, continuous possession might result to legal charges which is truly detrimental to the interest of the LGU.

The 1,164 Kadingilan Water District (KWD) Service Contracts were not signed by the Municipal Mayor and the consumers in contravention to the definition of a contract in the Civil Code of the Philippines, thus, tainted the legality and validity of the water connections and inferred high vulnerability of the LGU to possible infringements that would arise in the future.

The Municipal Treasurer’s Office did not strictly impose the 20% penalty of the unpaid water bills of delinquent consumers of Kadingilan Water District (KWD) contrary to Section 5 of the Water Service Contract, thus, the LGU lost the opportunity to earn more and augment its local revenues and some consumers tend to be abusive of not paying their bills on time.

Payments of honoraria to the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) in the total amount of ₱ 744,150.00 for CY 2022 was not in accordance to Section 5.7.1 of COA Circular 2012-001, Section 5.3 of DBM Budget Circular 2004-5A and Section 3.0 of DBM Budget Circular 2007-03, therefore, the propriety, legality and validity of the payments could not be ascertained.

The inclusion of unreconciled “beginning balances” in the subsidiary ledgers totaling to ₱ 125.614 million affected the accuracy and reliability of some real accounts presented in CY 2022 Statement of Financial Position, inconsistent to Section 111 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 10, Chapter 1, Volume II of the NGAS Manual for LGUs.

Various disbursements related to the Municipal Food Terminal from April 6, 2018 to December 31, 2022 that include procurement of two hundred fifty-two (252) sacks of commercial rice aggregated to ₱ 558,807.24 were charged against its accumulated income lodged in the Trust Fund contrary to Section 4.1 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-003, therefore, the propriety, validity and legality of the payments could not be ascertained and might be considered as irregular transactions.

Payment of surveying fees for the Socialized Housing Project of the LGU located at Panas, Salvacion, Kadingilan amounted to ₱ 250,000.00 was debited against the “Accounts Payable” account particularly continuing appropriation of LGU Equity for Farm to Market Road (FMR) Malacapit and Bagor instead of “Surveying Expenses” contrary to Section 3.1 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-003 and Section 1 of DILG-DBM Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1, hence, this might fall as an irregular transaction.

Failure of the Inventory Committee to conduct a physical count of all the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts owned by the Municipality, aggregating to P351,922,353.22 net of accumulated depreciation, or 49.44% of the total assets as of December 31, 2022, and non-maintenance of property cards per category of PPE by the General Services Office, all were not in compliance with the provisions of Section 111 (1) of P.D. 1445 a and Sections 119 and 124 of the MNGAS for LGUs, Volume 1, thus the existence, correctness, and valuation of the accounts cannot be ascertained.

Payables and the corresponding assets and expenses recorded at year-end of CY 2022 were not supported with adequate documentation, a non-adherence to Section 40 of Book VI of Executive Order (EO) No. 292, Section 4.s. of the NGAS Manual for LGUs, and Annex B of COA Circular 2015-009, thereby the accuracy, validity, and propriety of the recorded accounts cannot be ascertained.
Submit additional documents for items enumerated in Annex G that would substantiate the validity and accuracy of the amounts recorded as payables.

Continuing Appropriations of the 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) were significantly underutilized by the LGU, contrary to Items 3.2.3 and 4.0 of the DBM-DOF-DILG JMC No. 1 dated November 4, 2020, thus deprived the municipality and its constituents of the optimal benefits of development projects for efficient and effective local governance and for the promotion of the general welfare of the people.

The subsidiary ledgers of some accounts under the General Fund as of December 31, 2022 had an unreconciled balance of P3,533,700.36 against the major accounts in the general ledger/trial balance, which is contrary to Section 111 of PD 1445 and Chapter 2 Sec. 10 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Vol II; thus, the accuracy of the account balances could not be ascertained.

Procurements of construction materials are debited to the "Construction in Progress" (CIP) account instead of the "Construction Materials Inventory" (CMI) account. Moreover, the disbursements were not supported with any documentation indicating that the construction materials were already issued for construction, which is not in accordance with the Revised Chart of Accounts for LGUs as prescribed in COA Circular 2015-009 and Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, resulting the CIP and CMI accounts to be misstated and the validity and accountability of the issuance of the materials cannot be determined.

Some procurement of meals and snacks amounting to ₱ 1,490,223.50 were not subjected to competitive bidding due to the splitting of contracts contrary to Section 26 of COA Circular 92-386 dated October 20, 1992 and Section 7.3.4 and 54.1 of the revised IRR of RA No. 9184, thus, affecting the validity, propriety and legality of the procurements and the Municipality missed to avail volume/wholesale discounts or lower prices associated with bulk purchases through competitive bidding.

The Project Procurement Management Plan (PPMP) and the Annual Procurement Plan (APP) prepared by the LGU were not in conformity with the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) prescribed format, contrary to Sections 6 and 7 of the Revised IRR of RA No. 9184; thus, essential information was missing in the APP and PPMP, and the propriety of the procurement conducted in the calendar year 2022 cannot be established.

Copies of contracts and purchase orders and all the required supporting documents were not submitted to the Office of the Auditor within five (5) working days from execution/issuance thereof, contrary to COA Circular Nos. 2009-001 and 2012-001, thereby precluded the Audit Team from conducting a timely review, evaluation, and prompt detection/correction of deficiencies of the procurement.

Disbursements for repairs and maintenance, aggregating P949,349.00 for the period January to December 2022, were not supported with complete documentation required in Item 9.1.3.4 of COA Circular 2012-001, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the disbursements.

The LGU recorded two completed projects in the total amount of ₱ 56.441M funded out of the financial assistance from the Provincial Government of Bukidnon, as part of its Property, Plant and Equipment, even if the ownership thereof was not of the LGU due to the absence of Deeds of Donation, inconsistent to the provisions set under IPSAS 17 and 23, thus, overstating the PPE and Government Equity accounts in the General Fund.

LGU counterpart for the Construction of New Public Market remained in the “Trust Liabilities” account in the General Fund after being reverted to unappropriated surplus to finance other priority projects under Supplemental Budget No. 03, CY 2021 in contrast to IPSAS 1 and Section 99 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, henceforth, it understated the government equity and overstated the total liability by ₱ 8.51 million as of December 31, 2022.

A discrepancy of ₱ 5.31 million existed between the Due to LGUs Account in the books of LGU Kibawe and the reciprocal Due from LGUs Account in the books of the Provincial Government of Bukidnon (PGB) as of December 31, 2022, contrary to Sections 111 and 123 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thus, affecting the correct and proper presentation of the “Due to LGU” account in the financial statements for the Calendar year 2022.

Fuel consumption was not strictly monitored and controlled due to the non-preparation of Monthly Report of Official Travel/s, Report of Fuel Consumption and the like as required under COA Circular No. 77-61, thus, casted doubts on the correctness, accuracy validity and reasonableness of the consumption of Fuel, Oil and Lubricants expense amounting to in the amount of ₱ 6.428M.

Local Government Support Fund-Support to the Barangay Development Program of the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (LGSF-SBDP) from Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) amounted to ₱ 30 million was invested to high yield savings account instead of depositing it to the LGU Trust Fund-Proper account, and/or directly using such funds for the specific purpose for which the said funds were given which was not in accordance to Section 21 of COA Circular 92-382, DBM Local Budget Circular No. 144 and Section 305 (e) of R.A. 7160, therefore, casted doubts as to the propriety, validity and legality of the money transfer and might deprive the constituents of the Municipality of the benefits that could be derived from immediate completion therefrom.

Some procurement of supplies amounting to ₱ 744,800.00 were not subjected to competitive bidding due to the splitting of contracts contrary to Section 26 of COA Circular 92-386 dated October 20, 1992 and Section 54.1 of the revised IRR of RA No.9184, thus, affected the validity, propriety and legality of the procurements and the Municipality missed to avail volume/wholesale discounts or lower prices associated with bulk purchases through competitive bidding.

Interest income earned by the LGU amounted to ₱ 350,862.95 remained in the Trust Fund under “Other Payables” account as of December 31, 2022 in contravention to Section 66 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thereby, depriving the LGU to augment its revenues to finance priority local programs, activities and projects.

The Municipal Mayor was granted with special cash advances, aside from travel, intelligence and confidential expenses, which accumulated to ₱ 300,000.00 in CY 2022 in contrast to Section 4.1.4 of COA Circular No. 97-002, thus, the propriety, legality and validity of the cash advances could not be ascertained.

Payments of honoraria to the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) in the total amount of ₱ 205,606.00 were not duly supported with Notices of Award (NOA) as specified under Commission on Audit Circular 2012-001, thus, raising doubts on the validity and propriety of the claim.

Honoraria paid to various employees of LGU Kibawe having additional workload besides their original job descriptions amounted to ₱ 193,500.00 were not substantiated with a clear and definite legal basis contrary to Section 95 of RA No. 7160 and Section. 61 of General Provisions, General Appropriations Act 2022, thus, the validity, propriety, and legality of the disbursements could not be ascertained.

LGU Kibawe missed to return the unspent amount of ₱ 170,470.35 pertaining to the various Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) booked in the General Fund to the Bureau of the Treasury as of December 31, 2022 which was not in conformity to the Philippine Supreme Court Decision G.R. No. 208566 dated November 19, 2013, thus, continuous possession might result to legal charges which is truly detrimental to the interest of the LGU.

Payments for numerous funeral expenses which aggregated to ₱ 137,000.00 for the period January to August, 2022 lacked Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between the Municipal Mayor and the proprietor of Villanueva Funeral Homes in contravention to Section 4.6 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, therefore, the propriety, validity and legality of the disbursements could not be ascertained.

Payment for Special Risk Allowance (SRA) to qualified health workers of the LGU for the period January to December, 2021 amounted to ₱ 54,000.00 were charged against the 30% Quick Response Fund (QRF) of the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (MDRRMF) and exceeded by ₱ 27,000.00 for the months of July until December, 2021, contrary to Section 4 of DBM-DOH Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2021, henceforth, the propriety, legality and validity of the disbursement could not be ascertained.

The accuracy and reliability of some real accounts presented in CY 2022 Statement of Financial Position are doubtful due to “Undetermined/ Unidentified Balances” in various Assets and Liability accounts amounting to P30,377,023.50 and P725,122.66, respectively, inconsistent with Section 111 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 10, Chapter 1, Volume II of the NGAS Manual for LGUs. Moreover, the management failed to implement the reconciliation procedure for the one-time cleansing of Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts, inconsonant with COA Circular No. 2020-006. The abovementioned deficiencies affected the fair presentation of the financial statements as of December 31, 2022.

The Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivable balances of LGU Kitaotao as of December 31, 2022 reflected material discrepancies amounting to P4,110,020.25 and P3,913,948.25, respectively, as compared to the balances stated in the Summary of Delinquent Taxes as of year-end due to non-compliance with Section 20, Vol. 1 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs), thereby casting doubt on the reliability and accuracy of the said accounts in the financial statements.

Erroneous recording and account classification of transactions resulted in the overstatement and/or understatement of the Other Payables and Due to LGUs accounts, inconsistent with the mandate of PD No. 1445 – ‘Government Auditing Code and the Local Government Chart of Accounts thus affecting the fair presentation of the related accounts in the Financial Statements and moreover precludes the various stakeholders from monitoring and seeing accurate information which will be used in decision making.

Collective Negotiation Agreement (CNA) Incentive amounting totaling P3,650,000.00 were given to one hundred forty-six (146) officials and employees of the LGU despite non-compliance of the documentary requirements stated under DBM Budget Circular No. 2021-3 and Section 5.16 of COA Circular 2012-001, thus, hindering the team in the facilitation of the audit and may render the disbursement irregular as defined under Item 3 of COA Circular 2012-003.

The Municipality of Kitaotao still was not able to timely submit the year-end Financial Statements (FS) and its Supporting Schedules of the preceding year within the prescribed period, contrary to Section 347 of the Local Government Code of 1991, Section 41 of Presidential Decree (PD)1445 and COA Circular No. 2010-001, depriving the Auditors of ample time to review and render audit opinion on the fairness and presentation of the Financial Statements.

Paid Disbursement Vouchers, Liquidation Reports, Official Receipts and Deposit Slips and other reportorial documents were not submitted to the Office of the Auditor within the prescribed period, contrary to Section 100 and 107 of of PD No. 1445 and Section 7.2.1 of the 2009 Rules and Regulations on the Settlement of Accounts (RRSA) as prescribed for use under COA Circular 2009 -006 resulting to the delay in the review and verification of the propriety and validity of the transactions recorded in the books and precluding the rendering of the necessary and timely audit actions on these transactions. Moreover, the present condition exposes the unsubmitted transaction documents to either audit suspension or disallowance.

Appropriations worth P13 Million and Contracts amounting to P178 Million, all pertaining to Infrastructure Projects remained unimplemented and uncompleted, respectively, as of December 31, 2022 in relation to their target date of completion, inconsistent with PD No. 1445 – ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’ and contrary to the guidelines set forth in the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184 – ‘Government Procurement Reform Act’, thus depriving the end-users and/or the public from the benefits supposedly arising from the timely utilization of the subject infrastructures.

The agency failed to transfer its unexpended balance of the Local Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) totaling P12,632,852.35 as of December 31, 2022 to the Special Trust Fund, did not discuss the same in the Notes to Financial Statements and improperly accounted the unutilized LDRRMF for Calendar Year 2012-2014 amounting to P8,265,850.40 as “Other Payables”, contrary to Sections 5.1.10 and 5.1.16 of COA Circular No. 2012-002 and Section 21 of RA 10121 otherwise known as the “Philippines Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010”, thereby exposing the funds to risk of being used for purposes other than for which the LDRRMF was established and depriving its constituents of the benefits that could have been derived should the funds that remained unutilized for more than five (5) years were used for other social services.

The Municipality made acquisitions of Land in FY 2022 wherein P950,000.00 contained incomplete supporting documents and the related Disbursement Voucher of another acquisition worth P200,000.00 has not been submitted yet, inconsistent with the provisions provided under PD No. 1445 – ‘Government Auditing Code’, RA No. 7160 – ‘Local Government Code’ and its IRR, and COA Circular 2012-001 – ‘Prescribing the Revised Guidelines and Documentary Requirements for Common Government Transactions’, thus casting doubt as to the propriety and regularity of the transaction and precluding the auditor from the effective examination and verification thereof.

1. Advance Payments for Infrastructure Projects contained guaranties which were not in accordance with those provided for under the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184 - ‘Government Procurement Reform Act’ and COA Circular 2012-001 - ‘Prescribing the Revised Guidelines and Documentary Requirements for Common Government Transactions’, thus defeating the purpose for which the said guaranties were required, that is, as security for the re-payment of money upfront on the contract price.

Disbursements incurred for the period January to May 2022 covering payments of fuel as detailed below, were observed to contain incomplete supporting documents and were made thru reimbursement, inconsistent with the guidelines set forth in COA Circular No. 77-61 - ‘Prescribing the Use of the Manual on Audit for Fuel Consumption of Government Motor Vehicles’, PD 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’ and the Revised IRR of RA No. 9184 updated as of March 31, 2021, thus, casting doubt as to the validity and regularity of the subject transactions.

Several disbursements for Per Diems were observed to be paid in excess of the allowed Daily Travel Expenses (DTE) contrary to the guidelines set forth in Executive Order No. 77 – ‘Prescribing the Rules and Regulations and Rates of Expenses and Allowances for Official Local and Foreign Travels of Government Personnel’ and PD No. 1445 – ‘Government Auditing Code of the thus rendering the said excess payments prejudicial to the fiscal administration of the municipality and likewise deprives other programs/activities/projects from the use of such excess funds paid.

Repairs and Maintenance pertaining to Machinery and Equipment and Transportation Equipment could not be duly relied upon due to the inconsistent submission, attachment and filling up of the Request for Pre-Repair Inspection and Waste Materials report, inconsistent with the provisions provided under PD No. 1445 – ‘Government Auditing Code’, COA Circular No. 92-386 – ‘Prescribing Rules and Regulations on Supply and Property Management in the Local Governments’ and COA Circular 2012-001 – ‘Prescribing the Revised Guidelines and Documentary Requirements for Common Government Transactions’, thus casting doubt as to the propriety of the transactions, renders the internal procedures open to errors and precludes the auditor from the effective examination and verification of the subject transactions.

The disbursements of covid assistance totalling P6,137,500.00 during the previous year 2021 was not supported with any legal basis allowing its payment, contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, COA Circular No. 2013-003 dated January 30, 2013, Section 5.4.1 of Budget Circular No. 2006-1 dated February 1, 2006 and 9.1.5, Chapter 9, of the Manual on Position Classification and Compensation Scheme in Local Government Units, thereby casting doubt on the legality of the payments.

The validity and propriety of the COVID19-related disbursements in CY 2022 could not be established due to the following: (1) Liquidation for cash advances for Meal Allowances amounting to P604,250.00 were not properly supported with sufficient documents contrary to Section 4 (6) of Presidential Decree 1445 and COA Circular 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012; and (2) The grant of Meal Allowances to Vaccination Team Members exceeded P29,650.00 relative to the actual amounts earned contrary to COA Circular 2012-003 dated October 29, 2012.

The Municipality of Lantapan granted financial assistance to Philippine Red Cross Bukidnon Chapter totaling ₱600,000.00 which was erroneously recorded as an outright debit to “Donations” and credit to “Accounts Payable” during the setting up of the obligation in December 2021 prior to its payment in January 2022 contrary to COA Circular 2015-009 dated December 01, 2015, which bypassed the liquidation requirement as stated in Item B No. 4 of the Memorandum of Agreement dated December 14, 2021 and adversely affects the fair presentation in the financial statements.

The Municipal Accounting office failed to close Construction in Progress (CIP) accounts of various completed projects paid during the year with total project costs amounting to ₱34,110,870.88 to their appropriate asset accounts. This is not in accordance to IPSAS 1 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby overstating the CIP account and understating the proper asset accounts in the financial statements.

The Municipality credited “Other Payables” totaling ₱1,543,678.93 for the withheld retention money in the payment of the first billing of the contractor for the PRDP Project, “Concreting of Road and Drainage at Purok 3 to 5 Kulasihan, Lantapan, Bukidnon, of the Municipality of Lantapan,” instead of “Guaranty/Security Deposits Payable” contrary to COA Circular 2015-009; thereby overstating the “Other Payables” account and understating the “Guaranty/Security Deposits Payable” account.

Stored construction materials amounting to ₱1,017,095.00 for the Project Construction of water system @ Kinosuhan, Basac, Lantapan under the 20% Local Development Fund was directly recorded and reported in the Construction in Progress Account balance as of December 31, 2022. This is not in accordance to IPSAS 1 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby overstating the CIP account and understating the construction materials inventory in the year-end financial statements.

The Municipality of Lantapan granted Capital Assistances totaling ₱1,780,000.00 supported with ambiguous ‘Livelihood Agreements’ which were debited outright to “Donations” contrary to Section 123 and Section 4(8) of PD 1445, COA Circular 2015-009, and signed Livelihood Agreements, thus confusing the MSWDO and the recipients of the assistances of their duties and obligations, bypassing the liquidation of the provided support, and adversely affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The Municipality of Lantapan distributed food items to households affected by COVID-19 aggregating to ₱7,786,875.00 with various deficiencies contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree 1445 and COA Circular 2015-009, thereby casting doubt on the distribution process and resulting to unaccounted food items worth ₱64,138.92 which were erroneously debited expense outright.

Comparison between the financial statements of the Philippine Rural Development Project, “Concreting of Road and Drainage at Purok 3 to 5 Kulasihan, Lantapan, Bukidnon FMR”, revealed an overall variance of ₱118,800.86, contrary to Item a.1, Section 6.4.1, 6.7.1, and 6.7.2 of the PRDP Financial Management Operations Guidelines dated September 8, 2014 and Section 111(1) of PD 1445, thereby casting doubt on fair presentation of the financial reports.

The PRDP Project, “Concreting of Road and Drainage at Purok 3 to Purok 5 Kulasihan, Lantapan, Bukidnon”, with contract price of ₱93,635,000.00 had some data inconsistencies in its submitted documents and had some lacking supporting documents contrary to Section 34.3, Rule X of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 9184 dated March 31, 2021 and B.23 of the PRDP Module 1 Guidelines for the Procurement of Infrastructure Subprojects under PRDP Second Additional Financing with EU Grant co-financing, 2nd Edition dated November 2021, thereby casting doubt on the post-qualification procedure of the procurement process.

The procurement process of the PRDP Project, “Concreting of Road and Drainage at Purok 3 to Purok 5 Kulasihan, Lantapan, Bukidnon”, with contract price of ₱93,635,000.00 incurred 166 days of delay as compared to the suggested procurement timelines for National Competitive Bidding (NCB) under Item B.30 of PRDP Module 1 Guidelines for the Procurement of Infrastructure Subprojects under PRDP Second Additional Financing with EU Grant co-financing, 2nd Edition dated November 2021, thereby causing delay in the implementation of the project initiative.

The Municipality of Lantapan operates its Local Economic Enterprise(s) (LEE) with various deficiencies contrary to the Manual on the Setting Up and Operation of Local Economic Enterprises of 2016, Section 325 of the Local Government Code, and Section 107, Vol. I of the NGAS Manual; thereby casting doubt on the effectiveness and sustainability of the Local Economic Enterprises.

The Municipality of Lantapan paid salaries, PERA, and RATA to LGU Officials and Employees for CY 2022 totaling ₱47,924,990.37 that were not supported with the DTRs, minutes of the regular sessions, approved applications for leave, accomplishment reports, certificates of appearances, travel orders, and other pertinent supporting documents, in violation to Section 4 (6 & 7) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, COA Circular 2012-001, CSC Memorandum Circular No. 01, 2017, and Local Budget Circular No. 103 hence, the propriety of disbursements could not be determined.

The Municipality of Lantapan did not establish clear guidelines on the grant of Aid to Individual and Families in Crises Situations (AICS) for medical, burial and other purposes of CY 2022 aggregating ₱12,769,278.95 contrary to Section 123 and Section 4(6) of PD 1445, thus the validity, legality and propriety of the transaction could not be established and payment thereof may expose government funds to possible misuse.

Various procurement under the 20% Local Development Fund of the Municipality of Lantapan amounting to ₱16,521,040.00 were paid without subjecting the same with the prescribed form of warranty security in violation to Sec. 62.1 of RA 9184 which exposes the LGU to risk and difficulty of recovering damages in case of defects on procured goods.

Technical review of the Contract for the “Purchase of 2 units Dump truck-Isuzu QL3250U1 for the Municipality of Lantapan, Bukidnon” with contract price of ₱11,980,000.00 revealed that the technical specifications of the Ten-Wheeler Isuzu Dump Truck Manual offered by the winning bidder Jinyi Import and Export Trading Co. Inc., as shown on the submitted product technical specification sheet does not conform with the requirements Set forth on the Posted Bid requirements. Thus, casting doubt on the validity and legality of the contract as per technical aspect.

The Municipality of Lantapan paid “Productivity-Based Bonus” for CY 2021 totaling ₱1,974,689.60 to officials and employees with various deficiencies contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and Section 6.6, 6.7 & 6.8 of DILG-DBM Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2021-01 dated November 22, 2021; thereby casting doubt on the propriety of disbursements; validity of claims and the legality of PBB incentives received by thirteen (13) employees (totaling ₱277,394.00) with questionable eligibility.

The Municipality of Lantapan paid Service Recognition Incentive CY 2022 totaling ₱2,620,000.00 to officials and employees with various deficiencies contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and Sections 5 & 8 of Budget Circular No. 2022-4 dated December 20, 2022; thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of disbursement.

The Municipality of Lantapan paid gratuity pay totaling ₱606,500.00 to Job Orders with various deficiencies contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and Section 5.1 and 5.2 of DBM Budget Circular No. 2022-5 dated December 28, 2022, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of disbursement.

The Municipality of Lantapan cleared some employees with pending unliquidated cash advances totaling ₱129,690.00 contrary to Section 4(8) of PD 1445; thereby putting the interest of the government at a disadvantage.

The Municipality of Lantapan failed to optimally utilize their 20% Local Development (LDF) as shown by the existence of: a) Delayed implementation of 12 out of 17 ongoing projects at year-end funded out of the CY2022 20% LDF with total project cost of P8,500,000.00; and b) delayed implementation of all 10 uncompleted projects from CY2021 20% LDF with total project cost of P4,000,000.00. This is not in accordance to DILG-DBM Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2017-1 dated February 2, 2017, thereby depriving the constituents of the benefits from the timely completion of the said projects.

RPT/SET advance payments collected in CY 2022 totaling P15,658,445.92 were recorded as Other Deferred Credits instead of Deferred Real Property Tax/Deferred Special Education Fund Tax, contrary to COA Circular 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thereby, overstating the Other Deferred Credits account by a total of P15,658,445.92 in the Financial Statements and understating the Deferred RPT/SEF Tax by the same amount.

The current portion of the outstanding Loans Payable of the LGU amounting P2,516,666.68 was presented in the non-current portion of the Statement of Financial Position in CY 2022 instead in the current liability, contrary to Section 80 and 82 of IPSAS 1, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the financial statement.

The LGU failed to (1) restate the opening balances and the comparative amounts of the net/assets equity of the prior period due to change in accounting policy and prior period errors in the amount of P21,767,532.50 and P5,931,588.44, respectively, (2) present the effects of the restatement in the Statement of Changes in Net Assets/Equity in the appropriate period, and (3) provide the necessary disclosures related thereto, contrary to IPSAS 3, affected the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Fines and penalties resulting from delayed payments of RPT/SET by taxpayers were not recorded separately under the proper account but were lumped together with the RPT- Basic/SET and Due to LGUs contrary to Chapter 2 of PD 1445, thereby understating the Fines and Penalties account by P2,274,771.32 and overstating the RPT- Basic and SET accounts by the same amount.

The non-submission of the MTO of the Certified List of Taxpayers and Taxes Due caused the MAO to record the tax receivable and deferred credits at the beginning of the year based on estimates prepared by the Municipal Assessor’s Office, contrary to Section 20, Volume I of NGAS for LGUs which resulted to unreliable RPT and SET receivable balances as of year-end amounting to P12,605,324.35 each and hindering the proper monitoring of tax collections and delinquencies.

Fund transfers to the 14 barangays of the LGU totaling P1,287,500.00 in CY 2022 were recorded immediately as expense under the Due to Other LGU Account and released to the barangays without the complete documents required in Section 3.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thereby, exposing the said fund to misappropriation and affecting the proper determination of the accounting recognition to be used.

The payment of cash incentives totaling P231,000.00and monthly honorarium totaling P84,000.00 in CY 2022 to various national government personnel who are not among the personnel enumerated in Item 2 of the Compensation Policy Guidelines No. 98-1 resulted to disbursement of fund without legal basis.
