The payment of monthly honorarium to the GAD Focal Person, Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction Officer, Municipal Nutrition and Action Officer, all regular employees of the LGU, totaling P264,000.00 for CY 2022 is not among the honoraria enumerated in Local Budget Circular (LBC) 62 dated July 29, 1996, thus, validity of the said disbursement could not be ascertained.

Payment of leave monetization equivalent to 50% of the leave credits and those which are more than 10 days totaling P610,329.69 was not supported with the required documents per Section 5.14 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thus, reasonableness and validity of the claim could not be ascertained in view of the allowed circumstances to monetize leave credits at such quantity per Section 23 of the Omnibus Rules on Leave.

Prior years’ terminal leave benefit amounting to P138,328.81 was recorded as expense in the current year, contrary to the expense recognition principle, overstating the Terminal Leave Benefits Account by the said amount.

The Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) and its corresponding disclosures were submitted beyond the deadline and were not supported with the necessary reports such as the List of Not Yet Due and Demandable Obligations, among others, contrary to Section 4.1 of COA Circular No. 2010-001 dated March 2, 2010 and Section 3.5 of COA Accounting Circular No. 2007-02, thereby, affecting the fair representation of the figures reported.

The existence, completeness, and valuation of the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) account balance of P2.937 billion as of December 31, 2022 could not be ascertained due to: a) variance of P1.573 billion between the balances per books of accounts and the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE) and b) unsubmitted supporting documents to reclassification entries made to eliminate the unspecified/unidentified PPE items and adjusting entries on various identified PPE items aggregating P761.077million which are not in consonance with the provisions of Section 111(1) of PD No. 1445, IPSAS 17, and COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020.

The Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) was misstated due to error and differences in the manual and system generated calculation of the depreciation expenses and an incorrect manual entry resulting in an estimated overall understatement of Accumulated Depreciation by P28.405 million, an overvaluation by the same amount of its corresponding PPE accounts, and an overstatement of the Government Equity, casting doubts on the accuracy and reliability of the reflected carrying amount of these PPE and the Government Equity accounts in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2022.

The city’s adherence to the policies and procedures prescribed under COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022 and COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020 on the derecognition of Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) items with an aggregate net book value of P23,248,525.00 cannot be established and confirmed in the absence of approved JEVs and supporting documents, which casts doubt on its validity, propriety and legality, thereby affecting the reliability of the carrying amount of PPE in the year-end financial statements. The unsubstantiated derecognitions affected the evaluation of the city’s adherence to proper procedures and documentation in the extinguishment of the accountability for the derecognized properties.

The accuracy and reliability of the reported Real Property Tax Receivable and Special Education Tax Receivable including its corresponding Deferred Income accounts for CY 2022 is doubtful due to the non-reconciliation with the records of the City Treasurer’s Office and discontinued use of subsidiary ledgers which is not in consonance with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1 and 23, and Section 20 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS), thereby understating the affected accounts in the total amount of P191.225 million.

The balances of various Inventory accounts totaling P5,967,239.03 as of December 31, 2022 cannot be relied upon due to the (a) inconsistent application of the perpetual inventory method of accounting for Inventories, (b) improper maintenance of the inventory ledger cards, (c) non-adoption of the moving average costing method of inventories, (d) absence of documents supporting the recording of the expenses for supplies and medicines issued aggregating P26,580,936.38 (e) improper classification of inventory items totaling P814,071.00 and (f) discrepancies between the book balances and actual validation count of some inventory accounts, which are contrary to Sections 111 and 123 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, and pertinent Sections of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for LGUs.

Fund transfers recorded as Due to National Government Agencies (NGA) aggregating to P3,669,997.76 remained idle for 2 to 15 years. Moreover, erroneous recording amounting to P2,562,840.33 affected the reliability of the account balance presented in the year-end financial statements.

The City Government failed to submit on time copies of contracts and supporting documents of twenty- four (24) infrastructure projects funded out of the Local Government Support Fund- Support to Barangay Development Program (LGSF-SBDP) with a total contract amount of P91,509,296.53 and the submitted contracts and supporting documents of the other twenty (20) infrastructure projects were made beyond the reglementary period, contrary to COA Circular No. 2009-001 dated February 12, 2009, thus preventing the timely auditorial and technical review of the same.

Deficiencies were noted in the implementation of projects under the Local Government Support Fund- Support to Barangay Development Program (LGSF-SBDP) contrary to Section 2 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and pertinent GPPB issuances, thereby resulting to the non-completion of the project as programmed and depriving the constituents of the timely use of the projects/facilities.

The control and monitoring measures implemented by LGU Malaybalay in the utilization of fuel, oil and lubricants are not in consonance with the minimum internal control requirements provided under Sections 4 and 123 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 77-61 which exposed the LGU to possible wasteful, excessive and unnecessary expenditures for fuel consumption of government vehicles and further prevented the determination of the reasonableness of the reported fuel consumption totaling P65,375,700.26 for CY 2022.

There is no established internal control system over the receipt, disposition and utilization of the various Medical, Dental and Laboratory Supplies, Drugs and Medicines and Veterinary supplies which resulted to the improper reporting, monitoring and control over the inventory items in the possession of the custodians in contravention to the pertinent sections of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular 92-386 dated October 20, 1992, thereby impeding the verification and confirmation of the inventory items received and issued.

The liquidated damages imposed by the city government to the suppliers and contractors who failed to deliver goods and complete the infrastructure projects on time were not in accordance with Section 3.1- Annex D and Section 9- Annex E of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act No. 9184, due to incorrect formula adopted and limitation of up to a maximum 10% in its computation, resulting to an under- collection of P767,336.39, thereby failing to safeguard the interest of the government.

Advance payment to contractors totaling P1,579,910.98 were made without proper and complete supporting documents contrary to Section 4.2, Annex E of RA 9184 and its RIRR, Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thus, casting doubt on the legality and validity of the disbursements.

The City Government of Malaybalay (CGM) paid monetary awards en masse to elective officials and employees (casual and regular) as PRAISE – Personnel Motivation Incentive amounting to P40,279,359.86 and an Additional PRAISE Incentives to elective officials and selected office heads in the total amount of P4,100,000.00, without satisfying the basic documentary and qualification requirements set forth in Section 33 of the Civil Service Decree of the Philippines and Civil Service Commission (CSC) Memorandum Circular No. 01, s. 2001, which is contrary to Sections 2 and 4 (4) of Presidential Decree 1445, Section 33 of Presidential Decree No. 807 and CSC Memorandum Circular No. 01, s. 2001, thus the validity, propriety and legality of the disbursements cannot be ascertained.

The City’s compliance with the conditions in the grant and payment of CNA Incentives to 848 officials and employees totaling P20,133,332.32 cannot be established due to inconsistencies with the reported accomplishments as basis for its payment and absence of proof that the planned programs/ projects/activities (PPAs) have been implemented and completed in accordance with targets for the year and, contrary to DBM Budget Circular No. 2022-3 and Section 5.16 of COA Circular 2012-001, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the disbursement.

Projects that are not implementation ready totaling P262,881,835.20 were integrated into the 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) Programs, Projects, and Activities (PPAs) for CY 2022, inconsistent with the directive of DBM-DOF-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1 dated November 4, 2020, resulting to a low utilization rate of only 18.49% for the current year and 17% for the Continuing Appropriations- 20% LDF, thus, the fund was not optimally utilized which consequently deprived the public of the benefits that could have been derived from the immediate and maximum use of the funds.

LGU Malaybalay did not optimally utilize the appropriation under the 70% Mitigation Fund of the LDRRMF for CY 2022 with low utilization rate of 15.62% which is not in consonance with the purposes and intents of RA No. 10121 due to the inadequacy of planning and monitoring of the progress of the PPAs, thus, defeating the primary purpose of appropriating this fund and depriving the intended beneficiaries the benefits that can be derived therefrom.

Procurement of various Covid-19 supplies, equipment and meals by the City of Malaybalay through negotiated procurement under emergency cases totaling P8,380,800.00 were not compliant with the procedures under Section 53.2 of the Revised IRR of RA No. 9184 and the related GPPB issuances thus failing to ensure that suppliers were legally, technically, and financially capable. Moreover, inadequacies in the supporting documents to some transactions were apparent, thereby, preventing the determination on whether deliveries were made on a timely manner.

Twenty-five (25) reconciling items (comprising of unbooked stale checks, book errors and undeposited collections treated as deposits) remained unrecorded/unadjusted in the books of accounts while some dormant bank accounts were not prepared with Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS), amounting to ₱1,931,939.17 and ₱229,831.46, respectively, contrary to Section Sections 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the balances of Cash in Bank and the corresponding accounts reflected in the financial statements for calendar year 2022.

The improper issuance of official receipts and the journal entries made to transfer the 20% share of Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA) collections from GF-Proper to GF-LDF account are contrary to Volume 1 of NGAS Manual, thereby resulting in the inaccuracy and unreliability of the affected financial statement balances for CY 2022, which specifically overstated the “Subsidy to Other Funds” and “Subsidy from Other Funds” accounts amounting to ₱62.989 Million and ₱32.795 Million, respectively, and subsequently understated the “Surplus(Deficit) for the Period” and “Net Assets/Equity” accounts with net amount of ₱30.194 Million.
The municipality still failed to fully adhere with the guidelines set forth under COA Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012 for LDRRM funds, particularly on the following observations:

The Municipality did not prepare and submit the required year-end financial statements for its 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) account and improperly maintain numerous bank accounts under the same special account, contrary to Section 313(c) of RA 7160, New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual, and DOF-DBM-COA Permanent Committee Joint Circular No. 4-2012, thereby, the transparency and accountability in the receipt and usage of the 20% LDF could not be established and deprived the management and other stakeholders of the relevant information relative to the financial condition and results of operation of the 20% LDF that are vital in the making of well-informed and sound decision. Further, the monitoring and reconciliation of these multiple bank accounts provides additional and unnecessary burden to the management, specifically to the Municipal Accountant and Municipal Treasurer.

Three (3) bank accounts totaling ₱117,978.97 maintained by the LGU-Malitbog under Trust Fund-Philippine Rural Development Projects (PRDP) were not yet closed as to date despite that the related projects were already completed in CY 2020, while two (2) of these bank accounts became dormant with no Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS) since October 2022, inconsistent with DOF-DBM-COA Permanent Committee Joint Circular No. 4-2012 and COA Circular No. 96-011, thereby providing additional works and/or burden to the Municipal Treasurer and Municipal Accountant on the monitoring and reconciliation of these considered “unnecessary” bank accounts. Further, the non-submission of BRS and supporting documents for these dormant accounts for the said periods created doubt on the accuracy, reliability and existence of Cash in Bank account presented in the annual financial statements as of December 31, 2022 amounting to ₱76,309.01.

Various claims were paid in CY 2022 without bearing the approval of the proper officials on the disbursement vouchers, obligation requests and payrolls while some of these documents were signed by unknown representatives, aggregating to ₱35.397 Million, due to failure to implement a sound internal control system on obligations and disbursements, contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445, Section 344 of RA 7160, NGAS Manual and the Local Treasury Operations Manual, resulting in unauthorized transactions, weak internal control system and that the full accountability over the disbursed funds could not be established.
Disbursements related to infrastructure projects implemented thru straight contracts have various deficiencies, as follows:

The Bids and Awards Committee failed to submit the copies of twenty (20) perfected contracts procured thru competitive bidding, contrary to COA Circular No. 2009-001 dated February 12, 2009, hence, the reasonableness of the contract amount and the defects of the projects being implemented could not be readily determined/evaluated and communicated to management for appropriate action and that precluded the audit team in ascertaining the propriety and legality of the awarded contracts totaling ₱76.876 Million.
The controls on the granting and recording of cash advances for official travel expenses were inadequate and improper due to:

Registration fees paid in advance for trainings/seminars/conferences to be attended by some municipal officials and employees were improperly treated as an outright expense rather than as an individual cash advance aggregating ₱345,600.00, in violation to Section 2.0 of COA Circular No. 96-004, hence, the accountabilities over these supposed-to-be cash advances were not established at the time of payment and that various documents to substantiate the disbursed transactions were not attached. Moreover, with this current fiscal practice, the government funds are not properly safeguarded against possible wastage.

Improper obligation process was observed based on mobilization and progress billings rather than based on the awarded contract amount contrary to RA 7160, NGAS Manual for LGUs, and Manual on Procedures for the Procurement of Infrastructure Projects for Local Government Units, thus, the amount committed for the perfected contracts may be put at risk for possible use to other purposes.

The granting and recording of Assistance to Individuals and Families in Crisis Situations (AIFCS) payments charged against petty cash fund, instead to special cash advance, are inconsistent with COA Circular No. 97-002 and New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for LGUs, thereby affecting the propriety and regularity of the said transactions as to its accounting treatment and recording.

The related supporting documents of paid Disbursement Vouchers and payrolls were not stamped “PAID” in violation of COA Circular No. 92-389 dated November 03, 1992, thereby, opens the possibility of reusing the supporting documents for another claim of the same nature of expenditures and shows a weak internal control in the disbursement of government funds.

The LGUs failure to (1) restate the opening balances of the net/assets equity of the prior period in the Statement of Financial Position and Statement of Financial Performance, as may be applicable,(2) present the effects of the restatement in the Statement of Changes in Net Assets/Equity in the appropriate period, and (3) provide the necessary disclosures relative to the prior period errors reported at P39,047,993.51, contrary to IPSAS 3, affected the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Total unbilled balance of construction contracts with various contractors was recorded as Accounts Payable without proof of work accomplished as of December 31, 2022, contrary to Paragraph 19(a) of IPSAS 19, thereby, overstating the Accounts Payable and the overall Property, Plant, and Equipment Account of the LGU by an estimated amount of P16,56,861.61.

RPT/SET advance payments collected in CY 2022 totaling P116,657,603.71 were recorded as Other Deferred Credits instead of Deferred Real Property Tax/Deferred Special Education Fund Tax, contrary to COA Circular 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thereby, overstating the Other Deferred Credits account by a total of P116,657,603.71 in the Financial Statements and understating the Deferred RPT/SEF Tax by the same amount.

The LGU records RPT-Basic and SET accounts net of discounts for taxpayers who paid real property tax in advance contrary to Chapter 2 of PD 1445 thereby understating both the RPT-Basic and SET and Discount on Advance Payments account by P26,137,212.34.

The non-preparation of the MTO of the Certified List of Taxpayers and Taxes Due caused the MAO to record the tax receivable and deferred credits at the beginning of the year based on estimates prepared by the Municipal Assessor’s Office, contrary to Section 20, Volume I of NGAS for LGUs which resulted to unreliable RPT and SET receivable balances as of year-end amounting to P15,419,968.14 and P6,113,299.37, respectively and hindering the proper monitoring of tax collections and delinquencies.

The (1) non-maintenance of Supplies Ledger Cards (SLC), (2) inefficient procedure in the reporting of consumed inventories, and the (3) insufficient capacity to accommodate fuel inventory procured from various funds resulted in the failure to record as expense various inventory items, contrary to Paragraph 44 and 46 of IPSAS 12, thus, the Inventory reported at P90,070,365.78 in CY 2022 is overstated by at least P12,959,289.82, representing the amount of consumed/used inventories which remained unreported at year end.

Collections of RPT Receivable totaling 12,643,746.68 incorrectly recorded by the LGU as credit to Due to Other Funds instead of Due to LGU and RPT- Basic was subsequently erroneously corrected by debiting Due from Other Funds contrary to Chapter 2 of PD 1445, thereby overstating the Due to and Due from Other Funds Account by 12,643,746.68, respectively.

Eighteen Financial Aids and Awards to 11 Barangays which have not yet been released totaling P P9,314,968.60 was recorded as a Receivable and a Liability under the Due from LGU and Due to LGU accounts, respectively, contrary to the definition and description of Asset and Liability per Paragraph 5.6, 5.13, and 5.25 of IPSAS’ Conceptual Framework, thereby, overstating the said accounts in the financial statements.

Decided case by the Supreme Court regarding a certain Priority Development Assistance Fund transferred to the Bukidnon Vegetable Producers Cooperative (BVPC) booked at P5,500,000.00 remained recorded in the books of the LGU as Other Receivable and Due to NGAS, contrary to the definition of asset and liability per Section 5.6 and 5.14, respectively, of the IPSAS Conceptual Framework, thereby overstating the herein accounts in the financial statements.

Penalties resulting from delayed payments of RPT/SET by taxpayers were not recorded separately under the proper account but were lumped together with the RPT- Basic and SET contrary to Chapter 2 of PD 1445, thereby understating the Fines and Penalties account by P3,999,657.83 and overstating the RPT- Basic and SET accounts by the same amount.

Variation order for the Concreting of Mantibugao- Minsuro Farm to Market Road Project amounting P1,908,291.26 related to the Philippine Rural Development Project (PRDP) was performed by the LGU Economic Enterprise and was recognized as Accounts Payable in the General Fund books in the absence of an appropriation covering the same, contrary to Section 3.2 Annex “E”, thereby, incurring a liability and usage of government property without a valid legal basis.

The unexpended Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Fund (LDRRMF) from CYs 2014 to 2016 totaling P561,792.11 was not reverted to the General Fund contrary to Section 21 of RA 10121, thus, depriving the Municipality’s constituents to benefit from priority social services.

Procurement of 1-unit diesel tanker for motorpool amounting P500,000.00 was recorded to the Other Maintenance and Other Operating Expense (OMOOE) Account in the General Fund when the said item is expected to be used for more than one reporting period and cost thereof is more than P50,000.00, contrary to Par. 13 of IPSAS 17 and COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022.

Various cashbooks kept and maintained by the Municipal Treasurer have not been updated and reconciled with accounting records monthly in contrast to Section 27 of the Manual for New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs, Volume II, thus, the LGU funds were highly exposed to possible loss, misappropriation and major errors might not be averted immediately.

Completed projects under Trust Fund aggregated to ₱ 59,811,467.98 were still recorded under the ‘Construction in Progress (CIP) – Infrastructure Assets’ account in the books of the agency as of December 31, 2022 contrary to the provisions of COA Circular 2015-009 tainting the propriety, accuracy and reliability of the affected accounts.

The balance of the Due to LGUs account as of December 31, 2022 amounting to ₱ 110.176 million cannot be relied upon due to the (a) discrepancy of ₱ 56.645 million when compared to its reciprocal account Due from LGUs in the books of the Provincial Government of Bukidnon and (b) inclusion of the misclassified and unidentified sub-accounts totaling ₱ 996,099.35, contrary to Sections 111 and 123 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thus, affecting the correct and proper presentation of the “Due to LGU” account in the financial statements.

Refund to the Bureau of the Treasury for the unutilized Local Government Support Fund-Assistance to Municipalities (LGSF-AM) amounted to ₱ 1,631,480.20, as of December 31, 2021, of a Trust Fund project entitled Construction of Two-Storey Municipal Building in Barangay Anahawon, Maramag was taken from the General Fund without appropriation ordinance, inconsistent to Item 6.4.9.1 of DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2020-088 and Section 3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-003, thus, it possibly compromised the implementation of other projects, programs and activities under the General Fund and might fall under illegal/irregular disbursement of government funds.

The Municipal Mayor was granted with special cash advances, aside from travel, intelligence and confidential expenses, which accumulated to ₱ 900,000.00 in CY 2022 in contrast to Section 4.1.4 of COA Circular No. 97-002, thus, the propriety, legality and validity of the cash advances could not be ascertained.

A cash advance for Confidential Funds (CF) totaling ₱ 2 million was granted in CY 2022 without stating the duration of implementation of the CF and with the absence of the necessary supporting documents and liquidation reports at year-end, contrary to the provisions of Section 6.1.5, 6.1.7, 6.1.8.3, 6.1.8.4, and 6.2.2.7 of COA, DBM, DILG, Governance Commission for GOCCs and DND Joint Circular No. 2015-01 dated January 8, 2015, thus, it casted doubts as to the propriety and validity of the cash advances.

Honoraria totaling ₱ 206,500.00 were paid to various national government officials assigned to the Municipality of Maramag for the Calendar Year 2022 without legal basis contrary to pertinent provisions of R.A. No. 7160 clarified under DBM’s Compensation Policy Guideline No. 98-1 dated March 23, 1998,

Honoraria/incentives paid to officials and employees of the municipality and other designated members of various councils/boards amounting to ₱ 631,950.00 were not substantiated with a clear and definite legal basis contrary to Section 95 of RA No. 7160 and Section. 61 of General Provisions, General Appropriations Act 2022, thus, the validity, propriety, and legality of the disbursements cannot be ascertained.

Twenty (20) members of Liga ng mga Punong Barangay received monthly fuel and meal allowance at ₱ 2,000.00 each for a total amount of ₱ 432,000.00 on CY 2022 from LGU-Maramag without clear and definite legal basis contrary to Section 4(1) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 4.2 of Local Budget Circular No. 63 dated October 22, 1996, henceforth, it casted doubts as to the propriety, legality, and validity of the payments.

Payment of Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) honoraria in the total gross amount of ₱ 3,099,072.75 for CY 2022 was not in accordance to Section 5.7.1 of COA Circular 2012-001, Section 5.3 of DBM Budget Circular 2004-5A and Section 3.0 of DBM Budget Circular 2007-03, therefore, the propriety, legality and validity of the payments could not be ascertained.

The grant of monthly rice assistance to various officials and employees of LGU-Maramag in CY 2022 totaling to P 8,171,250.00, as of September 2022, was not substantiated with a clear and definite legal basis contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2013-003, henceforth, it casted doubts as to the propriety, validity, and legality of the payments.

The LGU still granted the allocation for hotel/lodging of daily travel expenses (DTE) to municipal officials and employees on their various local travels amounted to ₱ 399,100.00 despite the LGU paid the accommodation through payment to a travel and tours agency or additional cash advance by an employee, also, the LGU gave extra contingency/incidental funds for travel amounted to 1.435 million contrary to Sections 2 of PD No. 1445, and Section 5 and 7 of Executive Order No. 77, series of 2019 which resulted to double payments which was truly unfavorable to the interest of the government and raised doubts as to the validity, propriety, and regularity of the transactions.

Payment of relocation assistance for the displaced families at San Roque, Maramag, Bukidnon, mostly, due to road right-of-way for the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) -10 Concreting of Road Project totaling ₱ 660,000.00 was not properly and completely substantiated with pertinent documentary requirements in contrast to Section 4.6 of Presidential Decree 1445, thus, the propriety, validity and legality of the disbursement could not be ascertained.

Appropriation Ordinance No. 2022-02 entitled AN ORDINANCE APPROPRIATING SUPPLEMENTAL BUDGET NO. 3 OF THE GENERAL FUND FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022 OF THE MUNICIPALITY OF MARAMAG, BUKIDNON IN THE AMOUNT OF FIFTY SEVEN MILLION SIX HUNDRED FORTY THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED THIRTY NINE PESOS AND 80/100 (₱ 57,640,439.80) was not yet forwarded to Sangguniang Panlalawigan for mandatory review contrary to Section 56 and Section 327 of Republic Act No. 7160, thereby, precluded the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to identify possible appropriations that might be inoperative, disallowed or reduced.

There were incorrect recordings of payments for registration fees, membership dues, and other expenses under the “Travelling Expense” account, and some of the claims for registration fees were not supported by official receipts, a non-compliance of the Revised Chart of Accounts for LGUs and of Sec. 4 (6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thereby resulting to a misstatement of the traveling and other affected expense accounts by P1,285,900.72 as of October 2022 and casting doubt on the validity of the claims.

Disbursements for rehabilitation of barangay roads for the period January to October 2022 were capitalized instead of recording the same as an expense, and lacked sufficient supporting documentation, which are not in accordance with IPSAS 17 and Section 4(6) of the PD No. 1445, thereby misstating the asset and expense accounts of the financial statements as of December 31, 2022 by P477,624.00 and precluded the audit team from establishing the validity of the disbursements.

The Municipal Accountant does not forward the Report of Checks Issued and corresponding cancelled checks, if any, simultaneously with the Journal Entry Vouchers (JEVs) and Disbursement Vouchers (DVs), inconsistent with the procedures provided for in the NGAS Manual for LGUs, which poses difficulty in the monitoring of and accounting for all check issuances of the LGU.

The LGU failed to employ and implement sound management and fiscal administration in the distribution of financial assistance such that no specific guidelines were set, in violation of Section 4(8) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thus payments thereof exposes government funds to possible misuse.

There were erroneous computation of withholding taxes on payments to suppliers of goods and services for the period January to October 2022, contrary to Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) No. 23-2007, resulting to an under-remittance to the National Government totaling P241,305.76.

Transportation expenses were unsupported with receipts contrary to COA Circular 2021-001, and the practice of granting taxi allowances violates Executive Order (EO) No. 77, thereby casting doubt on the validity of the disbursements, totaling P696,301.00 for the period January to October 2022.

Disbursements for the labor component of construction projects totaling P3,905,307.75 lack complete documentation, in violation of Section 4(6) of the PD No. 1445, thus, the validity and propriety of the disbursements cannot be established.

There has been poor monitoring and implementation of various development projects, which is not in accordance with DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2019-188, resulting in delayed or incomplete projects, wasted resources, and funds being unutilized, all to the disadvantage of the government and particularly to the LGU’s constituents.

The LGU recorded 25 completed projects in the total amount of P31.496M, funded out of the financial assistance from Provincial Government of Bukidnon, as part of its Property, Plant and Equipment even if the ownership thereof is not of the LGU, inconsistent to the provisions set under IPSAS 17 and 23, thus, overstating the PPE and Government Equity Accounts in the General Fund by P31.496M.

Semi-expendable properties in the total amount of P351,437.00 and P5,224,108.88 that were issued were not properly supported with Inventory Custodian Slips (ICSs) and were not properly recognized as an expense, respectively, which is not in faithful compliance with COA Circular 2005-002 and paragraph 4 of COA Circular No. 2022-004 and dated May 31, 2022, thus, casts doubt as to the accuracy in the records of the Office of the General Services Officer and the fair presentation of the LGU’s Financial Statement as of December 31, 2022.

The LGU recognized fund receipts and interest income pursuant to DOE Energy Regulation No. 1-94 in the total amount of P10,377,776.71 as liabilities under the Due to NGAs account instead of recognizing the same as income under the Share from National Wealth account and Interest Income account, which is not in consonance with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 23, Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-006 and Annex A of the Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF) Memorandum Circular No. 03-01-2017, thereby adversely affecting the fair presentation of the LGU’s financial statements.

The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) of the Municipality failed to observe the required detailed evaluation of all bids using the non-discretionary criteria in conducting the same in the procurement of supplies and welfare goods for the LGU’s Peace and Order, Disaster, and Support to Indigency program aggregating to P1.798M, which is not in consonance with Sections 5.c, 32.2.1 and Annex H of the Republic Act 9184, thus, the propriety of the awarding of contracts cannot be established.

A total amount of P379,964,131.27 of Project Procurement Management Plans (PPMPs) based on the budget proposal were not prepared and submitted by the concerned departments and offices of the LGU for consolidation into an indicative Annual Procurement Plan (APP) contrary to Section 7, Rule II of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 9184, known as the “Government Procurement Reform Act”. Thus, procurement of goods, services and infrastructure projects in the total amount of P410,542,482.02 were undertaken without prior approved APP.

The LGU’s Annual Procurement Plan (APP) amounting to P3,481,219.73 and Supplemental APP amounting to P410,542,482.02 did not adhere to the correct format prescribed under GPPB Circular No. 07-2015 dated July 16, 2015, thus, relevant information in the effective and efficient conduct of the procurement of various goods, services, and infrastructure projects could not be ascertained.

Purchase of goods in the total amount of P3,127,796.00 and Purchase of office supplies in the total amount of P1,156,626.21 were done through Shopping and Small Value Procurement, respectively, without adhering to the requirements under Rule XVI of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 9184, known as the “Government Procurement Reform Act”, thus, resort to these alternative modes of procurement were not justified.

Unexpended Prior Year Appropriations for 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) – Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) in the total amount of P2.493M were not reverted to the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund in violation of Section 322 of R.A. No. 7160, known as the “Local Government Code of 1991”. Thus, the LGU disbursed a total of P2,212,675.00 without valid appropriations.

Supporting documents for the purchase of various goods in the total amount of P31.953M were not attached and government/accounting forms were not completely filled-up, which is not in consonance with Section 4 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 (P.D. 1445), known as the “Government Auditing Code of the Philippines”, while some supporting documents have unauthorized alterations/erasures and do not reflect actual dates, which may constitute Falsification under Articles 171 and 172 of Act No. 3815, known as “The Revised Penal Code” (RPC), as amended by R.A. 10951. Thus, delivery of purchased goods could not properly be monitored and liquidated damages in the amount of P81,688.37 for delayed deliveries were not properly imposed.

A total amount of P5,895,220.00 were allocated while a total amount of P2,515,135.55 were subsequently disbursed for the maintenance and other operating expenditures (MOOE) of the Municipal DRRM Office (MDRRMO) from the appropriations for Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) of the LGU contrary to Section 4.3 of the NDRRMC-DILG-DBM-CSC Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2014-1 dated April 4, 2014, Sec. 21 of R.A. 10121, known as the “Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010”, and Paragraph 5.0 of the NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC No. 2013-1 dated March 25, 2013. Thus, the fund was not fully utilized according to the purpose for which it was intended.

Payments for goods that were delivered late in the total amount of P2,874,350.85 were not deducted with liquidated damages in the total amount of P25,964.62 contrary to Section 68 of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act No. 9184, known as the “Government Procurement Reform Act” constituting undue prejudice to the government and depriving the LGU with income from liquidated damages.

Disbursement vouchers for payments of progress billings totaling to P27,426,116.83 did not have complete supporting documents and some have noted deficiencies, which is not in consonance with Section 4 (6) and 4 (7) of P.D. No. 1445, otherwise known as the “Government Auditing Code of the Philippines”, and COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thus, casting doubt as to the validity and propriety of the claims.

The LGU’s control and monitoring measures of its petroleum utilization is not in accordance with the minimum internal control requirements provided under COA Circular No. 77-61 which may have exposed to possible wasteful, excessive, and unnecessary expenditures the fuel consumption of government motor vehicles, machineries and equipment and further prevented determination of the reasonableness of disbursements in the amount of P3.818M in CY 2022.

The LGU made withdrawal of fuels to its supplier without undertaking first the necessary procurement process and despite non-issuance of Purchase Orders and Notice to Proceed, a non-compliance to the Procurement Manual for Local Government Units, thus, cast doubt as to the regularity of the transactions in the amount of P7.061M.

The material discrepancy between the “Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE)” accounts and its supporting schedules decreased by 8.04% or ₱10,773,668.30 significantly from CY 2021 to CY 2022, however thirteen (13) of the PPE accounts aggregating ₱123,145,838.13 remained to be unreconciled and unidentified which is not in consonance with Section 111(1) of PD No. 1445, Sections 4 and 70 of the Manual on NGAS for LGUs, and COA Circular 2020-006, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the Financial Statements.

The reported Receivable accounts of the LGU include accounts totaling ₱1,574,222.13 that have long been outstanding/uncollected, without available documents and/or dormant for more than ten years and where settlement could no longer be ascertained which is in contrary to IPSAS 1 and COA Circular 2016-005, thereby adversely affecting the reliability of the existence and valuation of reported receivable accounts.

The Municipal Accounting office erroneously recorded claims for Right-of-way against various individual amounting to Php1,431,555.00 as “Other maintenance and operating expenses” instead of recognizing the appropriate asset “Land” account. This is not in accordance to IPSAS I and COA Circular No. 2015-009, which overstated their expenses and understated their assets by the said amount, thereby affecting the fair presentation of year-end financial statements.

The Municipality of San Fernando provided local counterpart contributions for the DSWD KALAHI-CIDSS NCDDP initiatives totaling ₱1,459,973.00 which were recorded as outright debits to “Subsidy to other LGUs” account inconsistent with their Memoranda of Agreement contrary to COA Circular 2015-009; thereby casting doubt on the fair presentation of the financial statements and inadvertently bypassing the liquidation requirement in relation to the counterpart contribution.

The Municipality of San Fernando procured various food items for distribution/consumption totaling ₱8,176,123.92 with various deficiencies contrary to Section 4(6 &8) of Presidential Decree 1445 and Section 4.0 of COA Circular 2012-003; thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the project implementation and goods distribution and fairness of the presentation of the financial statements.

Payments of salaries and other personnel benefits totaling P54.9 million through Authority to Debit Accounts (ADA) were made without Disbursement Vouchers as required under the NGAS Manual for LGUs thus, leaving no proof that the procedural requirements under the pertinent provisions of RA 7160 relevant to disbursement of money were properly complied with prior to the approval of such payments.

The Municipality of San Fernando operates its Local Economic Enterprise(s) (LEE) with various deficiencies contrary to the Manual on the Setting Up and Operation of Local Economic Enterprises of 2016, Section 325 of the Local Government Code, and Section 107, Vol. I of the NGAS Manual; thereby casting doubt on the effectiveness and sustainability of the Local Economic Enterprises.

The Municipality of San Fernando paid salaries, PERA, and RATA to LGU Officials, Employees and Job Orders for CY 2022 totaling ₱110,473,560.65, that were not supported with the DTRs, minutes of the regular sessions, approved applications for leave, accomplishment reports, certificates of appearances, travel orders, and other pertinent supporting documents, in violation to Section 4(6 & 7) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, COA Circular 2012-001, and Local Budget Circular No. 103 hence, the propriety of disbursements could not be determined.

The Municipality of San Fernando automatically deducted the entirety of the 15% advance payment totaling ₱1,499,491.29 to the first payment of the project, Construction of Farm to Market Road from Purok 1 to New Terminal - Halapitan, unlike in other mobilization payments contrary to Section 4.3 of Annex E of the Revised IRR of RA 9184 and Section4(8) of PD 1445; thereby casting doubt on propriety of the progress payments which may raise a question on the principle of fairness.

The Municipality purchased a parcel of land (8,000 sqm) amounting to ₱300,000.00 with various deficiencies in violation to Section 10, 12, & 13 of Executive Order No. 1035, s. 1985 and 4(6 & 8) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, thereby casting doubt on validity and propriety of the purchase of the land property.

The Municipality of San Fernando paid Performance-Based Bonus for CY 2021 totaling ₱3,226,132.23 to officials and employees with various deficiencies contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and Section 6.6 & 6.8 of Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2021-01 dated November 22, 2021; thereby casting doubt on the propriety of disbursements and the legality of claims amounting of two (2) individuals totaling ₱64,819.30.

The Municipality of San Fernando paid gratuity pay totaling ₱2,013,000.00 to Job Orders with various deficiencies contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, Sections 5.1 to 5.3 of Budget Circular 2021-05 dated December 31, 2021, and Sections 5.1 to 5.3 of Budget Ciruclar 2022-05 dated December 28, 2022; thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of disbursements.

The Municipality of San Fernando paid Service Recognition Incentive CY 2022 totaling ₱3,996,000.00 to Two Hundred Six (206) officials and employees with various deficiencies contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and Sections 5 & 8 of Budget Circular No. 2022-4 dated December 20, 2022; thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of disbursement.

The Municipality of San Fernando failed to complete various ‘by-administration’ projects with a total project cost of ₱10,165,444.00 within their respective target dates of completion contrary to Section 4(8) of PD 1445 and Item 3.5 of Annex “A” of GPPB Resolution No. 09-2005, thereby casting doubt on the management capability of implementing by-administration project initiatives and, consequently, depriving the community of the benefits of their timely implementation.

The Municipality of San Fernando cleared some employees with pending unliquidated cash advances totaling ₱149,727.16 contrary to Section 4(8) of PD 1445; thereby putting the interest of the government at a disadvantage.

The presence of unreconciled amounts in the bank reconciliation statements (BRS) pertaining to CY 2013 backwards, the failure to adjust the identified bank reconciling items from CY 2016 up to present and the non-reversal of stale checks aggregating to a net overstatement of P6,157,880.53 resulted to unreliable Cash In Bank balance reported in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2022 which is contrary to the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 3.3 of COA Circular 96-11 dated October 2, 1996.

The collectability, existence and correctness of valuation of the Due from LGUs account is doubtful due to the inclusion of (a)dormant receivables totaling ₱1,803,945.18 and (b) long outstanding fund transfers to barangays ranging from three to six years totaling ₱951,483.29, contrary to IPSAS 1 and COA Circular Nos. 2016-005 and 94-013, resulting to unreliable account balance and delayed recognition of the appropriate Asset and/or Expense account for the utilization of funds transferred.

The balances of Intra-agency accounts “Due from Other Funds” and “Due to Other Funds” at year-end in the amount of P2.696M and P0.923M, respectively, showed a total difference of P1.774M, a non-compliance to paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, thereby casting doubt on the correctness and reliability of the balances in the financial statements.

Long outstanding Cash Advances granted to Officers and Employees from CY 2013 to CY 2018 totaling P347,532.57 remained unliquidated beyond the prescribed period for liquidation as of December 31, 2022, contrary to the provisions of Section 89 of P.D. 1445, Item 1.2 of COA Circular 2012-001, Item 5 of COA Circular 97-002 and CSC Memorandum Circular No. 23, s. 2019, resulting to the overstatement of Asset and Government Equity in the CY 2022 Statement of Financial Position and exposed the funds to possible loss, misuse or misapplication.

Payment of P330,065.64 insurance premiums for various insurable assets of the Municipality was directly recognized as insurance expense and some were erroneously recorded under the R & M - Transportation Equipment account in the amounts of P268,049.93 and P62,015.71 respectively, instead of recognizing the prepayments under the Prepaid Insurance, contrary to the accrual basis of accounting as defined in Paragraph 7 of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) I, and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thus understating the asset and overstating the expense account in the same amount of P195,743.30, rendering the affected accounts in Financial Statements as of December 31, 2022, unreliable and inaccurate.

The Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) account balance of P335.67 million is misstated and some could not be ascertained due to: (a) discrepancy of P21.467 million between the balances per books of accounts and the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE); (b) the presence of unspecified/unidentified PPE items aggregating P58.556 million; (c) various errors and lapses in the computation of accumulated depreciation, which overstated the PPE accounts by P1.363 million; and (d) the non-provision of depreciation to PPE accounts costing P10.727 million, overstating the carrying amount of PPE by an unquantified amount. Moreover, the correctness of the provided depreciation for PPE accounts aggregating P30.40 million cannot be validated due to (e) the non-preparation of Lapsing Schedules, thereby casting doubts on the accuracy and reliability of the reflected carrying amount of PPE and the Government Equity accounts in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2022.

The validity and legality of reported Accounts Payable balance in the aggregate amount of P567,395.12 could not be established due to the absence of valid proof to warrant payment of obligations which is not in consonance with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) No. 1 and Section 4(s), Volume I of the NGAS Manual, thus, affecting the true financial position of the municipality at the end of CY 2022.

Accuracy and reliability of the reported “Due to LGUs” account amounting P1,039,852.75 could not be established due to the presence of dormant and abnormal balances which is not in consonance with Sec. 111 (1) of PD 1445, IPSAS 1, COA Circular 2015-009 and Sections 9 and 10 of the Manual on NGAS for LGU, thus, affecting the true financial position of the municipality.

Allocation for discretionary funds in CYs 2022 exceeded the prescribed limitation, in contravention to Section 325 h of Republic Act No. 7160, thereby incurring expenditures in excess of what was authorized by law amounting to P802,980.51.

The lenient control of the LGU in deducting loan amortizations from the salaries of the LGU employees as mandated under Section 55 of the General Provisions of Republic Act 11639 or the General Appropriations Act of 2022 resulted in reduced take home pay of twenty-five (25) employees below the minimum amount of P5,000.00, thus failing to ensure them in bringing home decent portion of their earnings.

The submitted Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) for calendar year (CY) 2022 failed to present on its face the relevant information pertaining to continuing appropriation balances, including its obligations incurred during the year, a non-conformance with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) No. 1, thereby, affecting the reliability, accuracy and faithful presentation of the said financial statement (FS) and that it will then affect the attainment of the objectives of financial reporting which is to provide information useful to users of the FS for accountability and decision-making purposes.

Forty-eight (48) reconciling items (comprising of unbooked check disbursements, stale checks, book errors, interest income, and credit memo) remained unrecorded/unadjusted in the books of accounts, aggregating a net overstatement of ₱192,667.21, contrary to Section 83(I)(4) of Local Treasury Operations Manual and COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the Cash in Bank and the corresponding accounts reflected in the financial statements for calendar year 2022. Moreover, the non-submission to the audit team of the twenty-four (24) unrecorded check disbursements already encashed per bank statements totaling ₱283,959.19 may warrant the issuance of audit suspension or disallowance, as the case may be.

The PPSB Time Deposit with account number 0008-003478-231 amounting to ₱173,226.99 as of December 31, 2022 could not be verified due to the failure of the management to produce the related bank statements and Certificate of Time Deposit and its failure to prepare the required monthly Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS), contrary to Sections 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thereby affected the existence and the reliability of the Cash in Bank-Local Currency, Time Deposit account lumped to the Cash and Cash Equivalent account presented in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position.

The municipality did not prepare and submit the required year-end financial statements for its 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) account, contrary to New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual, thereby, the transparency and accountability in the receipt and usage of the 20% LDF could not be established and deprived the management and other stakeholders of the relevant information relative to the financial condition and results of operation of the 20% LDF that are vital in the making of well-informed and sound decision.

Various claims were paid in CY 2022 without bearing the approval of the proper officials on the disbursement vouchers, obligation requests and payrolls while some of these documents were signed by unknown representatives, aggregating to ₱69.127 Million, due to failure to implement a sound internal control system on obligations and disbursements, contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445, Section 344 of RA 7160, NGAS Manual and the Local Treasury Operations Manual, resulting in unauthorized transactions, weak internal control system and that the full accountability over the disbursed funds could not be established.

Various benchmarking activities conducted by the Municipality amounting to ₱5.017 Million were not duly supported with sufficient documentation and with other noted observations, contrary to DILG and DBM JMC No. 2 dated September 23, 2016, EO 77 dated March 15, 2019, and COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby affecting the regularity and propriety of such disbursements.

The municipality granted educational assistance totaling ₱3.008 Million to college and high school students as part of its scholarship program but supported with insufficient documentary requirements for failure to establish a clear-cut internal guidelines on the screening, approval, and release of such grant, which is not in consonance with the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thus, the audit team cast reservations on the propriety and validity of such assistance.

Fuel, grocery and other items considered as representation expenses were improperly paid to some LGU and national government personnel thru reimbursements without adhering to the proper procurement procedures and not supported with proper documentation, amounting to ₱345,000.00, inconsistent with the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA 9184 and some provisions of RA 7160, thereby, affecting the regularity and validity of the disbursed transactions.

Registration fees paid in advance for trainings/seminars/conferences to be attended by some municipal officials and employees were improperly treated as an outright expense rather than as an individual cash advance aggregating ₱598,500.00, in violation to Section 2.0 of COA Circular No. 96-004, hence, the accountabilities over these supposed-to-be cash advances were not established at the time of payment and that various documents to substantiate the disbursed transactions were not attached. Moreover, with this current fiscal practice, the government funds are not properly safeguarded against possible wastage.

The cash advance and the subsequent liquidation reports for travel expenses incurred during Comprehensive Development Plan (CDP) workshop were not supported with sufficient supporting documents and with other deficiencies totaling ₱726,700.00, contrary to COA Circular 1997-002 dated February 10, 1997, COA Circular 2012-001 dated June 14, 2021, and EO 77 dated March 15, 2019, thereby creating doubt on the propriety and validity of such disbursements.

Traveling expenses charged against 5% LDRRMF during the conduct of Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Plan (CBDRRMP) formulation at Libertad, Misamis Oriental were inadequately supported with relevant documentary requirements and with other noted deficiencies, contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445, COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012 and Executive Order No. 77, thereby casting doubt on the propriety and validity of said disbursements totaling ₱1,269,000.00.

The related supporting documents of paid Disbursement Vouchers and payrolls were not stamped “PAID” in violation of COA Circular No. 92-389 dated November 03, 1992, thereby, opens the possibility of reusing the supporting documents for another claim of the same nature of expenditures and shows a weak internal control in the disbursement of government funds.
Disbursements related to infrastructure projects implemented thru straight contracts have various deficiencies, as follows:

Improper obligation process was observed based on mobilization and progress billings rather than based on the awarded contract amount contrary to RA 7160, NGAS Manual for LGUs, and Manual on Procedures for the Procurement of Infrastructure Projects for Local Government Units, thus, the amount committed for the perfected contracts may be put at risk for possible use to other purposes.

The existence, validity and accuracy of the reported Inventories’ balances amounting ₱125,675,553.28 could not be ascertained due to the non-monitoring of their issuances, distribution and consumption and non-reconciliation between the records kept by the City Accounting Office (CAO) and the Report of Physical Count of Inventories by the City General Services Office (CGSO), in violation of section 111 (2) of PD 1445, par. 44 of IPSAS No. 12 and, sections 121, 122 and 124 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Vol. 1 thus, casting doubts on the accuracy and reliability of the Inventories presented in the CY 2022 Statement of Financial Position.

The Construction in Progress accounts’ balances totaling P182,784,976.12 could not be validated due to the failure of the City Accounting Office to prepare the Construction in Progress Ledger Cards (CIPLC), in violation of section 16 of the NGAS Manual Volume II, section 50 of the NGAS Manual Volume I and, COA Circular No. 2015-009 hence, completed projects were not properly classified to their appropriate asset accounts and not computed with depreciation which rendered the reported assets in the CY 2022 Statement of Financial Position as unreliable.

The CY 2022 General Fund Statement of Financial Position was understated by P44,836,728.64 due to the non-recording of the Trust Fund CY 2021 year-end closing entries thus, non-compliant to section 347 of R.A. 7160, section 123 of P.D. No. 1445 and sections 97, 103 and 104 of the Manual of the New Government Accounting System Volume 1, which render the CY 2022 Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as unreliable.

The Bank Reconciliation Statements from August to December 2022 for the twenty-nine (29) bank accounts were not submitted by the City Accounting Office thus, noncompliant to section 3 of COA Circular No. 96-011 hence, the accuracy, completeness and existence of the reported year-end Cash in Bank balances totaling ₱625,167,562.93 in the CY 2022 Statement of Financial Position could not be verified.

Cash Advances granted to Officers and Employees totaling ₱21,965,446.13 remained unliquidated hence, not in accordance to section 89 of P.D. 1445, section 1.2 of COA Circular 2012-001 and section 3.3 of COA Circular No. 96-004 thus, the accountability of the concerned officials and employees to strictly liquidate their cash advances within the prescribed period was not enforced. Moreover, the cash advances’ accounts had negative balances totaling P4,807,028.85 which cast doubts on the accuracy and reliability of the balances presented in the Statement of Financial Position.

The LGU recorded all its payments for insurance as outright expense totaling P22,464,427.02, in contrary to the Matching Principle of Accounting and Section 64 of the New Government Accounting System Manual Vol. 1 thus, overstating the Insurance Expense account by ₱13,359,324.18 and understating the Prepaid Insurance asset account by the same amount, thereby casting doubts on the reliability of the financial statements.

The City Accounting Office (CAO) failed to monitor the balances of some of the LGU’s Assets and Current Liabilities amounting P7,854,842.73 and P8,400,258.86 respectively, which remained inactive or non-moving for several years, in violation of section 123 of PD No. 1445 and section 7.0 of COA Circular 2016-005 thus, rendered the reported assets and current liabilities balances in the comparative Statement of Financial Position as unreliable.

The CY 2022 year-end closing entry for Trust Fund amounting P235,858,795.34 did not conform to the guidelines on the preparation of closing entries and was made without any supporting documents, in violation of Section 112 of P.D. 1445, sections 66 and 104 of the Manual of the New Government Accounting System Volume 1 and, COA Circular No. 2015-009 hence, maybe considered as an invalid transaction.

The procurement and distribution of the corn seeds amounting ₱6,224,628.00 sourced from the 30% Quick Response Fund (QRF) for Typhoon Odette affected farmers were not done in the quickest possible time, in contrary to the purpose of QRF. Moreover, the same amount was still recorded in full as inventory at year-end and not presented in the Notes to FS, in violation of par. 44 of IPSAS No.12 and sections IV, VI and VII of COA Circular No. 2014-002 which resulted to the overstatement and understatement of the LGU’s asset and expense accounts and, deprived the intended users of the effective understanding of the Financial Statements.

All final payments for 100% completed infrastructure projects were not supported with As-Built Plans, in violation of Section 9 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 thus, preclude the inspection of the completed projects if they were actually constructed based on plans and specifications.

The BAC failed to invite the duly recognized private groups for infrastructure and goods to observe in all stages of procurement, in violation of sections 3 and 13 of the IRR of R.A. 9184 hence, limiting the intention of the government in enhancing transparency in the government procurement process.

BAC Accreditation Certificate was required by the BAC for every supplier or contractor who shall participate in competitive bidding as an additional requirement in the LGU’s checklist of technical documents, in violation of sections 3 and 23.1 of R.A. 9184 hence, limiting the participation of other qualified supplier or contractor in the LGU’s procurement activities.

Mandatory documentary requirements on negotiated procurement under emergency cases for purchases of COVID – related goods totaling P13,643,042.80 were not attached to the vouchers and, postings of the NOA, PO, or NTP in the PhilGEPS website, LGU’s website and in any conspicuous place in the agency’s premises were not done by the LGU, in violation to COA – GPPB Joint Circular No. 01 dated March 26, 2020 thus, cast doubts as to the propriety and legality of the transactions and the procurement process undertaken.

The LGU’s accredited pharmacies undersupplied medicines to the recipients of medical assistance since the withheld taxes totaling P730,024.41 were not considered as part of the LGU’s payments, in violation to Section 113 of National Internal Revenue Code of 1997 hence, the LGU should be properly recompensed with medicines equivalent to the same amount of the withheld taxes.

The LGU had not implemented controls on the release of medicines from the accredited pharmacies/suppliers to its recipients of medical assistances, in violation to Sections 2, 123 and 124 of P.D. 1445 hence, the medical assistances were improperly disposed by some of the recipients and accredited pharmacies/ suppliers. Moreover, the Official Receipts issued by some of the accredited pharmacies/suppliers were not in detailed as to the quantity and actual medicines provided thus, cast doubts on what were actually provided to the recipients.

The LGU made disbursements for virtual training expenses totaling ₱433,500.00 that were not supported with official receipts and certificates that the participants completed the trainings, in violation to Section 4(6) of PD 1445 and item no. 5 of the General Requirements for all types of Disbursements as provided by COA Circular 2012-001, and Item 4.1.(b) CSC MC No. 3, s. 2021, thereby casting doubt on the propriety and validity of the transactions.

The LGU paid honoraria to its OSCA Head, CHO Pathologist and consultant in the codification of LGU’s ordinances totaling ₱505,575.00 which were not supported with their Approved Daily Time Records (DTRs) or duly verified/ accepted accomplishment reports thus, not in accordance to the documentary requirements set by COA Circular No. 2012-001 hence, cast doubts on the basis of the claims.

Multiple copies of accounting forms/ reports were unnecessarily attached in the LGU’s disbursements thus, not in accordance to section 2 of P.D. 1445, section 376 of R.A. 7160 and Volume II of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System for LGUs hence, such excess copies may be considered as wastage of the LGU’s office supplies.

Erroneous information was presented in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) and the Status of Appropriations, Allotments, Obligations and Balances (SAAOB) for CY 2023 for failure to disclose the correct amounts of obligation and unobligated appropriations for LDRRM-MOOE funds, materially deviating IPSAS 24, thus making the financial reports unreliable which would affect the rendition of auditor’s opinion on the prepared financial statement that would consequently affect the decision-making of its users.

Seventy-three (73) reconciling items still remained unrecorded/unadjusted in the books of accounts totaling ₱21,061,920.76; and three (3) closed PPSB bank accounts which were still recorded in the books of accounts with net amount of (₱64,920.50), contrary to Sections 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, resulting in a net understatement of ₱755,907.62 of Cash in Bank account, as reflected in the financial statements for CY 2023.

The reported balance of the “Due to NGAs” account under the Trust Fund’s books of accounts amounting ₱15.459 million pertaining to the two (2) projects funded by DILG-LGSF could not be relied upon due to the non-derecognition of the ₱14.848 million liabilities that have already been liquidated/settled, a deviation to COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the account balances presented in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2023 and the adequate disclosure in the Notes to Financial Statements for the same year.

Eleven (11) parcels of land are not supported with Transfer Certificates of Title (TCTs) under the name of the LGU-Baungon but mostly by Certificates of Tax Declaration (CTDs) and with various noted deficiencies, contrary to the provisions of Section 148 of COA Circular No. 92-386, RA 7160, and IPSAS 17, thereby casting doubt in determining the right to ownership over its properties and potentially exposing the agency to litigation risk and tainting the fair presentation and disclosure of said account in the financial statements that might affect the decision-making of its intended users.

The agency failed to adopt timely disposal procedures for twenty (20) fully depreciated unserviceable heavy equipment and other motor vehicles with carrying amount totaling ₱1.857 million, a nonconformance to Section 79 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 92-386 prescribing the Rules and Regulations on Supply and Property Management in the Local Governments, hence, the municipality could have generated greater benefits in terms of higher appraisal value for the property, lesser storage cost, and better management of limited storage space. Moreover, the proceeds to be derived from the sale of such properties could be an additional funding to finance various priority programs and projects of the municipality. Additionally, the inclusion of these fully depreciated properties tainted the valuation of the Property, Plant and Equity account balance presented in the Statement of Financial Position as at December 31, 2023.

Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts with net carrying amount of ₱495.469 million were not subjected to one-time cleansing and with other noted observations, a non-conformance to COA Circular 2020-006 and NGAS Manual for LGUs, thus, the accuracy and existence of the PPE accounts presented in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2023 are doubtful and unreliable, thereby depriving the government of reliable and useful information in decision-making and accountability for these assets.

The LGU Baungon transferred from its TF to GF’s books of accounts the two (2) completed projects in the total amount of ₱63.471 million funded out of the financial assistance from Provincial Government of Bukidnon (PGB), even if the ownership thereof are not yet conveyed to the LGU through the execution of Deeds of Donation, an infraction of the specific provisions set forth under the executed Memoranda of Agreement between LGU-Baungon and PGB and under IPSAS Nos. 17 and 23, resulting in an overstatement in the PPE and Government Equity Account in the General Fund with the same amount.

The LGU recorded eight (8) completed projects in the total amount of ₱7,822,538.22, funded out of the financial assistance from Provincial Government of Bukidnon, as part of its Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) even if the ownership thereof is not of the LGU and inadvertently recognized depreciation expenses during the year, inconsistent with the provisions set under IPSAS 17 and 23, thus, the reliability and accuracy of the PPE and Depreciation accounts are affected with overstatement of ₱7,822,538.22 and ₱142,235.99, respectively.

Various unnecessary and/or excessive travel expenses were incurred while some were supported with photocopies of Certificates of Appearance, contrary to Section 4(6) of PD 1445, COA Circular 2012-003, and existing CSC-COA-DBM Joint Circulars, thereby raising doubts to the propriety and validity of transactions which may warrant the issuance of notice of disallowance or suspension, as the case may be.

In the CY 2023, the municipality paid Hazard Pay in the amount of ₱1,553,936.98 and Subsistence Allowance in the amount of ₱321,000.00 to its public health and social welfare workers with inadequate documentation and paid on a predetermined fixed rate per month rather than on an actual service thru reimbursement basis, contravening COA Circulars Nos. 2012-01 and 2023-04, DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1 s. of 2018, and DBM-DOH JC No. 1, s. of 2012, as amended, thereby impairing the appropriateness and validity of the disbursed transactions and incurring overpayments of at least ₱12,883.87, which may warrant the issuance of audit suspension or disallowance, as the case may be.

The municipality disbursed communication expenses without an established internal guideline and with deficient documentation, while incurred unnecessary reimbursements for gadgets and other charges, totaling ₱331,037.21, ₱178,303.27, and ₱32,631.84, respectively, contrary to PD 1445, COA Circular Nos. 2012-001 and 2023-004, thereby casting doubt on the reasonableness and regularity of these transactions.

The municipality paid honoraria to the BAC Secretariat members rendering a full-time service and to the invited observers from Non-Government Organization (NGO) totaling ₱32,000.00 and ₱30,000.00, respectively, contravening Section 5.6 of DBM Budget Circular No. 2004-5A dated October 7, 2005 and Section 15 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184. Additionally, some disbursements were noted with incomplete supporting documents totaling ₱96,000.00, contrary to Section 4 of PD 1445 and COA Circular Nos. 2012-001 and 2023-004. Thus, raising concerns on the regularity and validity of the disbursed transactions.

The Municipality did not procure common-use supplies from the Procurement Service - Department of Budget and Management (PS-DBM) nor submit their Annual Procurement Plan-Common-Use Supplies and Equipment (APP-CSE) in the mPhilGEPS as required under Administrative Order No. 17 dated July 28, 2011, Appendix 30 of the Revised IRR of RA 9184, and GPPB Resolution No. 17-2020, thus, failing to ensure transparency, cost and time efficiency, and streamlined procurement process and depriving the national government of potential income due thereon.

The copies of perfected contracts were submitted delayed for 53 days in average and lacked basic supporting documents, contradictory to the pertinent provisions of COA Circular 2009-001, consequently precluded the audit team from undertaking the timely and relevant audit results on the propriety, legality and the technical aspect of the awarded contracts.

The existence, completeness and valuation of PPEs (excluding CIP) amounting P12,418,801,195.64 at year-end could not be ascertained due to the inability of the Inventory Committee to conduct the physical count at year end and to complete the PPE one-time cleansing process, property cards not updated, existence of unrecognizable items in the schedule, some acquired assets not recorded, presence of semi-expendable items, doubtful valuation of lands in the books contrary to existing rules and regulations.

The accuracy and reliability of the Construction -in Progress account at year-end amounting to P1,801,042,591.94 is doubtful due to the inclusion of completed projects, inconsistency of data in the CIP Ledger Card and the recognition the cost of on-going PGB funded projects implemented by other LGUs contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, Section 50 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System for LGUs, thus affecting the fair presentation of the affected account in the Financial Statement.

Prescribed policies and procedures for an effective control on the proper storage and accounting of inventories such as: perpetual inventory system, maintenance of stock cards, conduct of physical count of inventories, are not strictly adhered to contrary to Sections 112 and 122 of PD 1445, Section 4.s, 114, 120, 126 and 124 of the Volume 1 of the Manual of the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs, thus casting doubts on the existence and accuracy of the reported balance of the Inventories in the Financial Statement as of December 31, 2023.

Drugs and medicines dispensed by Bukidnon Provincial Hospitals amounting to P72 million and medical, dental and laboratory supplies amounting P92 million were not recorded as Cost of Sales and its inventory balances at year-end at P105.6 million and P340 million respectively in the Statement of Financial Position-General Fund, were erroneously classified under Inventory Held for Consumption contrary to Section 9 of IPSAS and COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thus misstating the affected account balances in the year end Financial Statement.

Error in recording the provincial share on SEF and GF real property tax resulted in the overstatement by P8.4 million for RPT-Basic, P12 million for Special Education Tax and Due from LGU accounts contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, Section 123 of PD No. 1445.

Deficiencies were observed on time deposits maintained by the Provincial Government of Bukidnon totalling P2,631,500,000.00 as of December 31, 2023 which include: a) total placements as of year end at P103M, P150M and P840M from Trust Fund, Special Education Fund and 20% Development Fund respectively; b)lack of proof of authority from the Sanggunian Panlalawigan ; c) non-submission of Certificate of Time Deposits to monitor placements made; and d) non-compliance to reversion of unexpended balances of Appropriations contrary to Sections 21 and 22 of COA Circular No. 92-382, and Section 322 of RA 7160 thereby affecting the regularity and propriety in the disposition of funds through the placements made.

The Provincial Government of Bukidnon (PGB) has still unsettled obligations with different source agencies for the unimplemented significant programs/projects aggregating to P98.241M, thereby depriving the intended beneficiaries the opportunity to avail timely the economic benefits the projects have to contribute in contrary to the objective of the government. At the same time, the foregoing unsettled obligations constitute unliquidated fund transfer of the source agencies to their disadvantage for violating pertinent provisions of COA Circular 94-013 dated December 13, 1994.

Unadjusted reconciling items affects the accuracy and reliability of the year-end balance of the Cash in Bank- Local Currency, Current Accounts contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, Section 3.3 of COA Circular No. 96-011, Section 74 of PD 1445.

Delay in issuing Deed of Donation, unrecorded liquidation reports and the failure of the PMIT to inspect completed projects funded by Provincial Government implemented by municipalities within the province resulted in the bloating of PPEs in the books and failure to effect transfer of ownership of the projects to the end user contrary to the Memorandum of Agreement signed by the parties.

The accounting office erroneously recorded 1) Training Expense in the amount of P87,000.00 as Traveling Expenses – Foreign; 2) Traveling Expenses – Local in the amount of P162,380.00 recorded as Other Maintenance and Operating Expenses contrary to the provision of Annex B, COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thus the accounts affected were understated and over stated by the same amount.

Deficiencies on the Premiums paid by PGB were observed for 1) not insuring all insurable properties of the province and 2) insurance premiums of various PGB properties were expense outright and no adjusting entries were recognized for the unexpired portion, contrary to IPSAS I and Section 62 of the MNGAS Volume 1, thus affecting the fairness of the balance reported in the FS at year end and put the properties at risk of not indemnified in case of loss or damage for those not insured contrary to RA No. 656.

Payments of Terminal Leave Benefits totaling P21,104,146.23 to the officials and employees of the Provincial Government of Bukidnon for the year ending December 31, 2023 were not supported with complete documents required under COA Circular No. 2023-004 dated June 14, 2023 to ensure that said payments are free from encumbrances, thus, affecting the validity thereof.

The agency incurred ₱ 2,056,269.51 for payment of leave credits to its officials and employees for CY 2023 without strict adherence to COA Circular 2023-004 and Sections 22 and 23 of the Omnibus Rules on Leave, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the disbursement.

The Notes to Financial Statements failed to provide adequate disclosures of the material and significant changes of account balances and noted deficiencies, contrary to the requirements of NGAS Manual and the pertinent disclosure requirements of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the Financial Statements.

The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) failed to submit back the seventy-six (76) endorsed contracts for deficient documentation to support the procurement activities aggregating an amount of P1.627B, contrary to the provisions of XOA Circular No. 2009-001 and Republic Act No. 9184 and its Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations, thus preventing the auditor to ascertain the compliance of the procurement process and the regularity of the awarded contracts to RIRR of RA 9184.
