The laxity of management in allowing deductions from loan amortizations and other obligations from the salaries of some LGU employees more than what is prescribed by Section 56 of the General Provisions of Republic Act 11936 or the General Appropriations Act of 2023 resulted in a take home pay below the minimum amount of P5,000.00 of some employees.

Registration Fees ranging from P10,000.00 to P25,000.00 for three days with no information as to its breakdown precludes the auditor from verifying whether the accommodation component is in accordance with the provisions of Executive Order No. 77.

Deposits of collections by field collectors to the depository bank were delayed contrary to Sections 29, 32, and 33 of the Manual on New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for LGUs, thereby exposing the funds to risks of loss or misuse.

The cashbooks maintained by the accountable officers did not bear the proper certification at the end of every month contrary to the provisions of Section 26, Chapter 3, Volume II of NGAS, thereby, affecting the integrity of the figures disclosed therein and impeding the efficient verification process of the collections.

The fidelity bonds of the eighteen (18) Accountable Officers were inadequate compared to the cash advances granted (Disbursing Officers) and collections received (Collecting Officers), contrary to Section 4.1 of Treasury Circular No. 01-2022 dated May 30, 2022, hence the risk of a limited indemnification from the Fidelity Fund in the event of defalcation, shortages or unrelieved losses in the account of the accountable officers.

Seventeen (17) accountable officers continued to perform their duties and responsibilities despite having an expired fidelity bond contrary to Section 101 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 7.2 of Treasury Circular No. 02-2009 dated August 6, 2009. Thus, the Provincial Government may not recover defalcations, shortages, and unrelieved losses.

Projects constructed and purchased by the Provincial Government of Bukidnon remained not operational as of year-end contrary Section 2 of P.D. No. 1445 thus depriving its target beneficiaries of its benefits.

Projects costing P236 million remain not completed, various projects worth P173 million are either terminated, and P6.8 million worth of projects are for termination or implementation has not yet started as of year-end contrary to Section 2 of P.D. No. 1445 and pertinent provisions of RA 9184 thus depriving its target beneficiaries to benefit in its immediate use.

Fund utilization and implementation of PPAs funded from the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) amounting to P654.706 M failed to observe guidelines particularly: (a) low utilization rate of implementation of PPAs; (b) improper charging of disbursements; (c) PPAs not included in LDRRMFIP; and (d) failure of Reports on Sources and Utilization of DRRMF to submit on time, all of those are contrary to the requirements under Sec. 21 of RA 10121, COA Circular No. 2012-002 and NDRRMC-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-1 which defeats its intended purpose and validity of the transactions made could not be ascertained.

Pertinent provisions embodied in the Implementation Management Agreement (IMA) in the implementation of the three (3) PRDP subprojects totaling P19.189M were not strictly adhered to by management could affect the continuity of its operations and possible cancelation of the IMA under Article VIII of the agreement.

Comparison between the financial statements of the Philippine Rural Development Project and the PRDP financial reports, revealed an overall variance of ₱903,616.32, contrary to Item a.1, Sections 6.4.1, 6.7.1, and 6.7.2 of the PRDP Financial Management Operations Guidelines dated September 8, 2014 and Section 111(1) of PD 1445, thereby casting doubt on fair presentation of the financial reports.

Several completed buildings and structures acquired through the financial assistance of the Provincial Government of Bukidnon totaling ₱63,650,000.00 were not yet recorded in the LGU books due to the absence of a fully executed Deed of Donation from PGB thus, non-compliant to IPSAS 17 which resulted to the understatement of LGU Assets by the same amount.

The reported Construction in Progress (CIP) accounts’ balances as of December 31, 2023 were unreliable due to the existence of the following material deficiencies: a) Various completed projects totaling ₱28,617,989.10 were still reported as CIP at year-end and b) Variance between the reported Construction in Progress accounts (per FS) and the reported actual cost incurred (per MEO report) of various ongoing projects amounted to ₱1,572,687.50 at year-end, which were not in accordance to IPSAS I, section 112 of PD 1445, and COA Circular No. 2015-009.

The Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts’ balances as of December 31, 2023 could not be ascertained due to (a) unidentified/no breakdown PPE items in the subsidiary/lapsing schedules with acquisition cost amounting to P73,208,035.14 and, (b) incomplete Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant, and Equipment (RPCPPE) with ₱657,673,921.36 or (96.57%) variance compared to accounting records hence, noncompliant to section 58 and 111 of PD 1445, IPSAS 1 and section 124 of the NGAS Manual for LGUs, thereby casting doubts on the accuracy, reliability, and existence of the reported assets in the CY 2023 Statement of Financial Position.

There were Two Hundred Fifty-Eight (258) recorded Property, Plant and Equipment totaling P5,409,131.70 with acquisition cost of below the P50,000.00 capitalization threshold, in contrary to COA Circular No. 2022-004, hence the PPE carrying amounts were overstated by P1,843,304.99 presented in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2023.

Previous years’ income from various sources which should have been recorded as other income for the period they were earned and, other funds due for remittance/liquidation to national government agencies/ other organizations were erroneously recorded in the Due to LGUs liability account in the General Fund and Trust Fund totaling ₱4,605,525.16, in violation to Sections 305(d) and 307 of RA7160 and, COA Circular No. 2015-009 which resulted to the overstatement of the reported liabilities and as well as the understatement of the Government Equity in the CY 2023 Statement of Financial Position.

Basic internal control on the segregation of duties was not properly observed when the Liquidating officer was also designated as a Special Disbursing officer allowing her to cash advance and disburse funds amounting to ₱4,653,980.00 thus, not in accordance to Section 50 of the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual (GAAM) Vol III and, Internal Control Standards for the Philippine Public Sector (ICSPPS) prescribed under COA Circular 2018-003, thereby exposing the government funds to risk of possible loss and misappropriation.

The BAC invited a private group and NGO which did not pass the criteria to be qualified observers in all the LGU’s procurement activities for infrastructure projects and goods, in violation of Section 13 of R.A. 9184 hence, limiting the intention of the government in enhancing transparency in the government procurement process.

All Purchase Orders for procurement of goods were improperly accomplished by the BAC personnel thus, noncompliant to the instructions in Appendix 29 of the NGAS Manual in accomplishing the form which casted doubts on the propriety of the transactions.

Various entries in the General Journals totalling P605M for the period January 2022 to December 2023 could not be verified due to the non-submission of journal entry vouchers (JEVs) and their supporting documents to the audit team, contrary to Section 4(6) of P.D. 1445, Section 347 of RA 7160, and Section 7.2.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009; thus, the validity, propriety, and regularity of the recorded transactions could not be ascertained and limits the scope of audit of the team.

The accuracy of the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) balances, including its accumulated depreciation as at December 31, 2023, and the related depreciation expenses for CY 2023 cannot be relied upon due to: a) retention in the Trust Fund of the acquisitions and completed projects initially recorded therein, amounting to P3,714,491.72, and non provision of the related depreciation expenses, b) various overstatements and understatements found in the computation of depreciation expenses, and c) non-compliance with the transitory provision on the phased recognition of the local road networks, contrary to Section 104, 1(i) of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs, Volume I and Philippine Public Sector Accounting Standards (PPSAS) No. 17, and COA Circular No. 2015-008; thereby, the accuracy of the Property, Plant and Equipment balances, including its accumulated depreciation as at December 31, 2023, and the related depreciation expenses for CY 2023 cannot be relied upon.

Collections of intra-agency fund transfers through check, totaling P76,482,766.91 for the period October 6, 2021 to December 1, 2022, were found with the following deficiencies: a) received without the issuance of official receipts, b) unrecorded in the cashbook of the accountable officer, and c) receipts totaling P8,912,350.40 were not recorded under the “Cash-Local Treasury” account, contrary to Section 68(1) of PD No. 1445 and Section 29 of Volume I of the NGAS Manual for LGUs, Section 90 of Book II of LTOM, and contrary to the Revised Chart of Accounts prescribed by COA Circular No. 2015-009. Therefore, it increased the difficulty in the examination and verification of the LGU’s collections, created the risk of the collection not being properly recorded and monitored, and understated the “Cash-Local Treasury” account by P1,550,000.00 and P7,362,350.40 for CYs 2021 and 2022, respectively.

The year-end balances of intra-agency accounts “Due from Other Funds” and “Due to Other Funds”, which are reciprocal in nature, could not be verified due to: a) a difference of ₱ 6,888,412.38 of the balances of the accounts, contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, b) non-submission and/or inadequate submission of supporting documents for various JEVs affecting the accounts amounting to P27,810,532.82, which is not in accordance with Sec. 111 (1) of P.D. 1445. Thus, the necessity, validity, propriety, and regularity of the recorded JEVs cannot be ascertained. It also limits the scope of the audit of the team and affects the correctness and fair presentation of the “Due to other funds” and “Due from other funds” account balances presented in the financial statements as of the year-end of CY 2023.

In CY 2023, erroneous adjusting entries were made for the outstanding checks that qualified to be considered stale checks, contrary to Section 59 and item 6 of Section 61 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual, thus affecting various accounts in the financial statements as of December 31, 2023.

Payments of Transportation Allowances (TA) for the Calendar Year 2023, aggregating P1,535,625.00, were not supported with certification that the official/employee did not use a government vehicle and was not assigned any government vehicle, moreover, various officials were paid with transportation allowances in full despite being assigned with government vehicles, a non-compliance to the requirements of Item 5.2 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 and a violation to Local Budget Circular (LBC) No. 103 and Annex B of COA Circular No. 2012-003, thus, the legality, validity, and propriety of the disbursements of TA cannot be established and resulting to overpayment of TA to various officials of the municipality.

The procurements of supplies and fuel by the LGU were not subjected to competitive bidding but through shopping or small value procurement due to the splitting of contracts, contrary to Section 26 of COA Circular 92-386 dated October 20, 1992, and Sections 7.3.4 and 54.1 of the revised IRR of RA No. 9184, thus affecting the validity, propriety, and legality of the procurement activities, and the municipality missed availing volume/wholesale discounts or lower prices associated with bulk purchases through competitive bidding.

Unutilized collection from proceeds of the sale of bidding documents and liquidated damages in the Trust Fund account at year-end amounting to ₱32,186.48 and ₱4,975.38, respectively, totaling ₱37,161.86 were not remitted to the General Fund account, which was not in conformity to Section 6.2 of Appendix 7 of the revised IRR of RA 9184, thus deprived the agency additional funds for its programs and projects. Moreover, the error resulted in an overstatement of “Other Payable” and an understatement of “Government Equity” accounts presented in the Consolidated Financial Statement, both by ₱37,161.86.

Payment of BAC honorarium in excess of the 25% basic monthly salary and honorarium for BAC Support staff totaling ₱42,636.00 is not consistent with Section 15 of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulation of R.A. 9184 and Section 5.9 of Budget Circular No. 2004-5A dated October 7, 2005; thus, the propriety, legality, and validity of the payments could not be ascertained.

Various road rehabilitation projects of the LGU were recorded in the “Road Networks” and “Construction in Progress—Infrastructure Asset” accounts, contrary to Sections 111.2 and 112 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Item IV-7 of COA Circular No. 2015-008, thereby overstating the Property, Plant, and Equipment and Government Equity accounts in the Financial Statement at year-end by ₱4,335,270.14.

The CY 2023 Financial Statements (FS) of the LGU did not disclose the required details of the LDRRMF with an unutilized balance of P8,550,710.49 as of December 31, 2023, contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-002. Moreover, the related Trust Liability – LDRRMF account has an unreconciled balance, which is not in conformity with Section 111 of PD No. 1445. Thereby depriving users of the FS of necessary information useful for decision-making, and casting doubt on the accuracy and reliability of the Trust Liability – LDRRMF account.

34 machinery and transportation equipment costing P30,175,729.05 were not recorded in the books of account of the municipality, a non-compliance to IPSAS 1 and IPSAS 17, thereby cast doubt on the correctness and reliability of the PPE account.

Incomplete recording, incorrect charging, and non-reconciliation of the disbursements charged against the current year 5% Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund is not compliant to COA Circular 2012-002, Annex B of COA Circular 2015-009, paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, and Volume 1 Chapter III Section 10 of the New Manual on Government Accounting System, thereby, affecting various accounts in the Financial Statements of the Municipality as of December 31, 2023 and cast doubt as to the validity of the charges against the LDRRMF for non-LDRRMF related disbursements.

Non-recording of CY 2023 unspent LDRRMF, incorrect amount transferred, and erroneous and incomplete recording of disbursements charged against the prior years’ 5% Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund, all in the Trust Fund books of accounts, is not in compliance to COA Circular 2012-002, Annex B of COA Circular 2015-009 and IPSAS 1 paragraph 27, thus, the account “Due from Other Funds” is understated by P3,656,616.15 and the account “Trust Liability – DRRMF” has a net overstated amount by P1,032,452.57.

The LGU did not recognize the uncollected business taxes and stall rents in the total amount of P1,101,598.40 as of December 31, 2023, which is not in consonance with Paragraph 14 of IPSAS 9 and Paragraph 106 of IPSAS 23, respectively, thus, corresponding receivable and income accounts were understated by P1,101,598.40.

Construction in Progress (CIP) totaling to P32,319,665.73 for the Construction of LGU Hotel were erroneously transferred to the Buildings Account although the project was not yet completed while phases/components constituting significant parts of the project totaling to P55,456,110.91 were not recognized in separate subsidiary ledgers in the CIP, which is not in consonance with Section 50, Volume I of Manual on The New Government Accounting System for Local Government Units and of the Paragraph 60 of IPSAS 17, respectively, thus, the Construction in Progress Account is understated by P32,319,665.73, and the Building Account is overstated by the same amount while the different phases/components of the project could not be properly identified for purposes of applying depreciation.

The OIC – Municipal Treasurer failed to maintain a complete and accurate record of the receipts, issuances, and transfers of accountable forms contrary to Sec. 24. of COA Cir. No. 92-382 dated July 3, 1992, thus, accountability for Accountable Forms (AFs) could not properly be established, and which resulted in the loss of one hundred (100) pieces of AF No. 51 (official receipts).

The Collectors and the OIC-Municipal Treasurer did not prepare the monthly Report of Accountability for Accountable Forms (RAAF) and monthly Consolidated Report of Accountability for Accountable Forms (CRAAF), respectively, contrary to Section 86 (G) Nos. (1) and (2), Book II, of the Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM) 2nd Edition. Thus, receipts, issuances, and returns of accountable forms were not properly accounted and monitored, which resulted to the non-presentation of 28,407 pieces of accountable forms at the time of cash examination conducted last September 18, 2023 exposing government funds to possible misappropriation.

Some Accountable Officers did not properly accomplish their cashbooks in accordance to the prescribed forms and required information under Book II of the Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM) 2nd Edition, thus, the cashbooks did not provide a complete and accurate record of all cash receipts, remittances/deposits, cash advances/disbursements and adjusting entries.

The Direct to Cashbook collections totaling to P50,247,130.19 of the OIC-Municipal Treasurer were actually collected by another bonded collector in the former’s behalf contrary to Sec. 25. COA Cir. No. 92-382 dated July 3, 1992 and Section 91, Book II of the Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM) 2nd Edition, thus, there is uncertainty in establishing accountability for cash and check collections and accountable forms.

The Municipality of Dangcagan failed to issue and maintain complete records of all Property Issue Slip, Acknowledgement Receipt for Equipment, or Property Acknowledgement Receipt for its 71 serviceable motor vehicles, a non-compliance to Section 143 and 158 of COA Circular No. 98-386, thus, the transfer of the said properties were not properly made and accountability for the motor vehicles could not be easily imposed.

Deficiencies in the registration of 46 vehicles and absence of registration documents of 3 vehicles of the Municipality were noted which is not compliant to Section 5 (a) and (b) of RA 4136, thus, the Municipality is remiss in its duty to abide by the law when it operated the said vehicles.

The municipality assigned vehicles to five (5) unbonded heads of office and paid a total of P297,600.00 transportation allowance to employees with assigned vehicle and with lacking supporting documents, a non-compliance to Section 101 of PD 1445, Section 8.2. of LBC 103, and COA Circulars 2012-001 and 2023-004, thus, propriety, legality, and validity of transactions cannot be ascertained.

The Municipality paid a total of P378,648.18 for reimbursement of communication expenses without sufficient basis and complete supporting documents, contrary to Section 447 of RA 7160 and COA Circulars 2012-001 and 2023-004, thus, casting doubt as to the propriety, legality, and validity of the payments.

Performance Securities totaling to P5,499,085.75 were not posted prior to the signing of the contract, and did not adhere to the correct validity period contrary to Section 39.1 and Section 39.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR of R.A. No. 9184, thus, validity of the infrastructure project contracts could not be established, the government was deprived of additional income from forfeiture of bid securities, and faithful performance by the winning bidder of its obligations under the contract could not be guaranteed.

The BAC did not submit some supporting documents to the infrastructure project contracts totaling to P31,448,162.74 while some supporting documents have patent error and deficiencies contrary to Paragraph 3.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-001 dated February 12, 2009. Thus, validity of the infrastructure project contracts could not be established.

The Municipality failed to revert to the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund the unutilized balance, in the amount of P345,914.82, of unspent LDRRMF five years after it was transferred to the Trust Fund books of accounts, a non-compliance to COA Circular 2012-002, thus depriving the LGU for a fund which could be used for other social services.

Payments for job order services not related to maternal and newborn care services in the total amount of P187,343.19 were charged against the funds received under the National Health Insurance Program (NHIP) for Women About to Give Birth and Their Newborns contrary to Sections 44 and 49 of IRR of R.A. No. 10606, otherwise known as “National Health Insurance Act of 2013”, Section 1 of Local Ordinance No. 10 Series of 2020, and Section 305(e) of R.A. 7160, resulting to the misappropriation of funds.

CY 2019 and CY 2021 savings under the 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) totaling to P1,031,671.00 were utilized without an approved Supplemental Budget enacted by valid ordinance contrary to Section 321 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the “Local Government Code of 1991” and Article 417 of A.O. No. 270 s. 1992 as amended by A.O. No. 47 s. 1993, thus, a contract agreement pursuant to the transfer of funds amounting to P1,026,675.88 was executed without valid and existing appropriations and subsequent disbursement in the same amount was made illegally.

The balance of the Land account amounting to P33,088,037.11 as of December 31, 2023 is deemed unreliable due to (a) land donated to a National Government Agency which still remained in the books of accounts (b) inclusion in the Land account of items which are in the nature of land improvements amounting to P1M, structures/buildings amounting to P8.6M and untitled land areas amounting to P1.8M and (c) non-reconciliation of a portion of the Land account amounting to P16.8M, all inconsistent with the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual and its corresponding Chart of Accounts, thus, casting doubt on the fair presentation of the amount presented in the financial statements.

School Fees of Don Carlos Polytechnic College (DCPC), an LGU-owned college, were not recorded using the Accrual Method of accounting resulting to an overstatement in revenues amounting to P36.9 Million for CY 2023, inconsistent with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), thus, affecting the fair presentation of the related accounts in the Financial Statements.

The balance of the Construction-in-Progress account as of December 31, 2023 is deemed unreliable due to (a) completed projects amounting to P22 Million that remained in the said account as of year-end; (b) labor component of projects implemented by Administration which were not taken up as Construction-in-Progress and (c) recognition of CIP for projects which have no requests for billing yet as of year-end, all inconsistent with the provisions of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual and its corresponding Revised Chart of Accounts, IPSAS 19 and COA Accounting Circular No. 2007-02, thus casting doubt on the accuracy, reliability and fair presentation of the amounts reflected in the financial statements.

The accuracy and reliability of Cash and Cash Equivalents balance as of December 31, 2023 could not be ascertained due to non-preparation and non-submission of Bank Reconciliation Statements of the Municipality for July to December 2023 within the reglementary period, a non-compliance with Section 74 of Presidential Decree 1445 and COA Circular No. 96-011, thus, affected the fair presentation of the Financial Statements for CY 2023.

The Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivable were setup not at the the beginning of the year and were not based on the Real Property Tax Account Register/Taxpayer’s Index Card due for CY 2023. Morever, advance payments for CY 2024 Real Property Tax received in CY 2023 were immediately recognized as income upon receipt despite being not yet due. The foregoing circumstances are all inconsistent with the provisions of Sections 20 and 22, Volume I of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) thereby casting doubt on the reliability and accuracy of the figures presented in the financial statements.

Loans Payable - Domestic amounting to P130,722,384.43 as of December 31, 2023 contained insufficient disclosures in the Notes to Financial Statements, inconsistent with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) thus, limiting significant financial information that can be available to various stakeholders and affecting the fair presentation of the of the said account in the Financial Statements.

The amount and details of the unexpended balance of the LDRRMF as of December 31, 2023 were not discussed in the Notes to Financial Statements, inconsistent with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) and COA Circular No. 2012-002, thus, limiting the information that can be available to various stakeholders and moreover, defeating the purpose for which the disclosure of the said balance is required to be made.

The Annual Procurement Plan (APP) of projects/programs/activities relating to infrastructure projects and other civil works for CY 2023 were not consolidated in the CY 2023 APP but were instead prepared separately per project and without following the prescribed format, inconsistent with the provisions of the Generic Procurement Manual Volume I of the GPPB, the Revised IRR of RA No. 9184 and GPPB Circular No. 07-2015, thus, affecting the effectiveness and efficiency of the overall procurement planning activities of the agency and more importantly, precludes the HoPE and/or other oversight bodies from seeing the entirety of the procurement plan of the agency for the budget year.

P366,600.00 worth of textile materials and polo shirts, released to Job Order employees for their uniform, were acquired without going through the proper procurement process and were not supported with adequate documents, inconsistent with the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Republic Act No. 9184 thus, depriving the agency from availing of the most advantageous price and moreover, casting doubt as to the validity, propriety and legality of the transaction.

The annual budget under the SEF for CY 2023 was not presented/supported with the DepEd-approved School Improvement Plan (SIP), the Division Education Development Plan (DEDP) and the DepEd and ECCD Council Budget, inconsistent with the provisions of Republic Act 716 and DepEd-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1, Series of 2017, thus, the conformity of the programmed disbursements thereof with the prescribed budgeting and utilization guidelines could not be verified.

Comparative amounts of the accounts in the LGUs Financial Statements were not restated to reflect the Prior Period Adjustments (PPA) with a total net effect in the Government Equity of P(63.9) million and corresponding disclosures related thereto were not provided, contrary to IPSAS 3, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants totaling P19.4 million were paid in advance, leaving at least a total of P2.2 million undelivered as of December 31, 2023 and P2.8 million with lacking supporting documents in violation of Section 88 of PD 1445 and paragraph 9.1.3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby, affecting the propriety of the transactions making the Fuel, Oil, and Inventory account balance of P20.5 million at year end doubtful.

Non-submission of the documents evidencing issuance of Construction Materials Inventory relative to the various projects and programs of the LGU, contrary to Section 116(c), Chapter 7, Volume I of LGU NGAS Manual, resulted to the failure of the LGU to reduce the said inventory account and allocate the cost thereof to the agency’s self-constructed assets per Paragraph 46 of IPSAS 12, thus, the reported Construction Materials Inventory totaling P33.9 million at year end, and Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) or appropriate expense could not be ascertained.

The LGUs Property, Plant and Equipment totaling P252.8 million were not depreciated, contrary to Section 58 of PD No. 1445 and Section 13 of IPSAS 17, thus, depreciation expense in CY 2023 is understated by an estimated amount of P14.5 million and the PPE overstated with amount thereof indeterminate due to unknown date of acquisition.

Completed projects amounting at least ₱82.4 million were not closed to the appropriate Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) account and were still included in the Construction in Progress (CIP) account contrary to Section 50 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS), Volume I, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the PPE accounts in the financial statements.

Issuance of other supplies and materials distribution totaling P8 million were not substantiated with appropriate Requisition Issue Slip (RIS) and Summary of Supplies and Materials Issued (SSMI), contrary to Section 116 and 121 of LGU NGAS Manual and distribution/recipient list attached contained various deficiencies, thus, the recorded expense totaling at least P8 million could not be ascertained.

The LGU land account includes a certain sub-ledger marked as “unreconciled amount” amounting P6,195,593.57, contrary to the definition of asset account per IPSAS 1, thereby, casting doubt on the correctness of the Land account reported.

Government Equity was credited upon reduction of liability (Due to NGA) due to fulfilment of condition relative to fund transfers totaling P3.5 million instead of crediting Subsidy from National Government contrary to Paragraph 45-47 and BC11 of IPSAS 23, thereby, understating the Subsidy from National Government account by the said amount.

The Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) account was not credited upon drawing of a reclassification entry (DR: Inventory, CR: PPA) in CY 2023 to correct a certain prior period error resulting from an erroneous recording of the payment of Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants amounting P2.4 million in the Construction in Progress – Infrastructure Assets account in CY 2022 instead of in the Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants Inventory account, contrary to sound accounting practice, overstating the PPE and Government Equity accounts of the LGU and failing to prepare appropriate disclosures, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Issued inventory in CY 2022 recorded as expense on the said year totaling P0.186 million was recorded again in CY 2023 as debit to prior period adjustment and credit to inventory, contrary to sound accounting and description of accounts per COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thereby, understating the Government Equity and Inventory Accounts of the LGU.

Issued inventory in CY 2023 totaling P0.290 million was erroneously recorded by debiting the inventory and crediting the expense account of the LGU, contrary to sound accounting and the description of accounts per Annex “B” of COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thereby, overstating/understating the inventory and expense accounts of the LGU.

Cash advances totaling P1.9 million drawn in CY 2019-2023 remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2023, contrary to Section 5.1.2 of COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997, thereby, exposing the funds to possible misuse and making the Asset and Expenses account unreliable.

Payment of progress billings totaling P20.5 million relative to 15 projects which were found to be beyond its estimated contract time were not substantiated by duly approved time extension and other supporting documents per Paragraph 11, Annex “E” of the revised RA 9184, thus, correctness of the payments made to the contractors could not be ascertained and liquidated damages estimated at P1.9 million may not have been imposed.

Documents relative to variation orders on least 5 infrastructure projects were not forwarded to the COA for review, contrary to Paragraph 3.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-001 dated February 12, 2009, thus, appropriate auditorial and technical review thereto were not conducted, casting doubt to the reasonableness of the variation cost and the additive/deductive period.

Fifty-one (51) progress and final billings totaling P50.6 million were not substantiated with the required documentary requirements enumerated in Section 9.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thus, validity and correctness of the payments could not be ascertained.

The LGU used the Purchase Order (PO) Form instead of Contract Agreement Form in its procurement of Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants totaling P15,470,961.04 procured thru public bidding, thus, various general and special conditions of the contract may be overlooked.

Expanded Withholding Tax (EWT) and withholding tax government money payments (GMP) were not withheld on payments totaling at least P254,018.45, contrary to Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 23-2007 thereby, depriving the government of its early collection of taxes.

The established amount of ₱1,500,000 for the “Real Property Tax Receivable” in the General Fund (GF) and ₱1,500,000 for the “Special Education Tax Receivable” in the Special Education Fund (SEF) at the beginning of CY 2023 were based on the Real Property Tax target in CY 2023 Annual Budget and not from the duly certified list showing the name of taxpayers and the amount due and collectible for the year provided by the Municipal Treasurer in contrast to Section 20 Volume I of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS), thereby, it tainted the accuracy and reliability of the said receivable accounts both in the GF and SEF.

Unexpended Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Funds in CY 2016 and CY 2017 which aggregated to ₱ 2.95 million was erroneously recorded in “Due from Other Funds” account in the General Fund book of accounts which was not in conformity to Section 21 of Republic Act No. 10121 and Section 5.1.10 and Annex C of COA Circular No. 2012-002, thus, it overstated the “Due from Other Funds” and “Government Equity” accounts as of December 31, 2023.

Biological Assets amounting to ₱ 911,113.01 as of December 31, 2023 remained dormant in the agency’s books for several years, and was not disclosed in the Notes to Financial Statements as to its nature, description and existence in contravention to IPSAS 27 paragraphs 16, 30 and 38-54 thereby casting doubts as to the existence and fair presentation of the said account in the financial statements.

Earned “Special Education Tax” amounted to ₱ 350,527.27 was erroneously transferred to General Fund and was recorded under “Real Property TaxBaasic” account contrary to Annex A of COA Circular 2016-004, thus, tainted the accuracy and reliability of the affected accounts both in the SEF and GF.

Various road rehabilitation projects of the LGU were capitalized and recorded in the “Road Networks” account contrary to Sections 111.2 and 112 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Item IV-7 of COA Circular No. 2015-008, thereby, overstating the Property, Plant and Equipment and Government Equity accounts in the Statement of Financial Position by ₱ 678,497.97 as of December 31, 2023.

Erroneous disclosure about the recording of one (1) unit pick-up truck under “Land Transportation Equipment” account in the Trust Fund book of accounts amounted to ₱ 1.582 million that was acquired in CY 2012 in Section 4.12.b of the Notes to Financial Statements (NTFS) for CY 2023 contrary to Section 128 of International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS) 1, thus, it affected the notes’ correctness and reliability.

Payment of ₱ 50,000.00 to Treasurer’s Office, Maramag, Bukidnon for the LGU’s cost sharing with the Southern Bukidnon Inter-Local Health Zone (SBILHZ) lacked updated or revised Memorandum of Agreement (MOA), guidelines or the like in contrast to Section 4.1 and 4.6 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 5 of General Requirements for all Types of Disbursement, thereby, the propriety, validity and legality of the transaction could not be ascertained.

Unexpended LGU counterparts for completed Trust Fund projects which accumulated to ₱ 494,561.11 remained under the “Trust Liabilities” account in the Trust Fund-LPRAP-BUB book of accounts in contrast to Section 99 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thereby, depriving the LGU of additional funds that could have been used to finance priority local government programs, projects and activities in CY 2023.

Erroneous accounting entries were made for recording the share of Internal Revenue Collections (IRC) of the 20% Development Fund Special Account and the related expenses thereof contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1 and Section 111(a) of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual, thus, the “Due From Special Accounts”, “Due to Special Accounts” and “Government Equity” accounts presented in the financial statements as of December 31, 2023, were not fairly stated.

The Municipal Budget Officer was unable to obligate the electricity expenses incurred in December, 2022 amounted to ₱ 618,415.50 contrary to Section 11 of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 24 and Section 306 of Republic Act No. 7160, thereby, they were charged to current or CY 2023 appropriations.

Procurement of sand and gravel for various infrastructure projects which accumulated to ₱ 0.972 million did not undergo public bidding in contrast to Section 10 and Section 8, Annex H of 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 9184, thereby the propriety, validity and legality of the disbursements could not be ascertained.

Contracts of lease between the lessees and the Municipal Mayor pertaining to the occupancy of the Kadingilan Memorial Park were not prepared and maintained by the Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO) in contrast to Section 16 of Ordinance No. 2010-09 or the Kadingilan Memorial Park Code (KMPC), thereby, tainted the propriety, legality and validity of the cemetery occupation and inferred high vulnerability of the LGU to possible infringements that would arise in the future.

The agency was not fully compliant with the guidelines relative to the reporting requirements of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) including the absence of disclosure of the ₱ 5.7 million unexpended balance in the Notes to Financial Statements contrary to the pertinent provisions of COA Circular No. 2012-002, hence, deprived users of a timely, complete, accurate and reliable information about the fund.

The unexpended LDRRMF recorded in the Special Trust Fund (STF) for years 2021 and 2022 totaling 4.4 million were charged with various expenses amounting to ₱ 808,306.30 per subsidiary ledgers without a revised AIP as approved by the local sanggunian and Local Chief Executive (LCE) contrary to Section 6.5 of NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC No. 2013-01, henceforth it casted doubts as to the propriety and validity of the disbursements.

LGU Kadingilan used 58% as the percentage rate in granting the FY 2022 Performance-Based Bonus (PBB) which was greater than the mandated maximum rate of 50% in contrast to the Notice of Eligibility issued by the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary, thereby, the propriety, validity and legality of the payment could not be ascertained and it resulted to an excessive payment totaling ₱ 225,898.64 which was unfavorable to the interest of the government.

The agency failed to submit within the prescribed period its year-end financial statements and supporting schedules for CY 2023, in violation of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2010-001, thereby hindering the audit team to render a reasonable audit opinion on management’s assertions that the financial statements are free from material misstatements, whether due to fraud or error, in accordance with IPSAS and precluded the users from its timely and useful information.

The agency failed to adopt timely disposal procedures for twelve (12) unserviceable heavy equipment and nine (10) motor vehicles with a carrying amount totaling ₱4.892 million, a nonconformance to Section 79 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 92-386 prescribing the Rules and Regulations on Supply and Property Management in the Local Governments; hence, the municipality could have generated greater benefits in terms of a higher appraisal value for the property, a lesser storage cost, and better management of limited storage space. Moreover, the proceeds to be derived from the sale of such properties could be additional funding to finance various priority programs and projects of the municipality. Additionally, the inclusion of these fully depreciated properties tainted the valuation of the Property, Plant, and Equitment account balance presented in the Statement of Financial Position as at December 31, 2023.

Office supplies inventory in the CY 2023 Statement of Financial Position totaling ₱4,767,985.98 included expendable and semi-expendable supplies worth ₱1,867,520.38 despite having been issued to end-users, due to the General Services Office’s infrequent preparation and submission of the Summary of Supplies and Materials Issued (SSMI) and Report of Semi-Expendable Property Issued (RSPI) to the Office of Municipal Accountant, a non-compliance to the provisions of the NGAS Manual for LGUs and COA Circulars No. 2015-009 and No. 2022-004, thus understating the operating expenses and overstating the government equity by ₱1,867,520.38.

The municipality paid honoraria to members of the BAC Secretariat rendering a full-time service whose positions are in the Procurement Unit totaling ₱37,716.84 contravening provisions of DBM Budget Circular No. 2004-5A dated October 7, 2005 and Section 15 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184. Additionally, the Accounting Office failed to withhold taxes from BAC honoraria payments totaling ₱399,149.45, contrary to BIR RR No. 2-98 implementing RA No. 8424. Thus, raising concerns on the regularity of the disbursed transactions and possible exposure to statutory penalties.

Payments of Transportation Allowances (TA) for Calendar Year 2023, aggregating ₱1,917,068.75, were not supported with certification that the official/employee did not use a government vehicle and was not assigned any government vehicle, moreover, various officials were paid with transportation allowances in full despite being assigned government vehicles, a noncompliance to the requirements of Item 5.2 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 and a violation to Local Budget Circular (LBC) No. 103 and Annex B of COA Circular No. 2012-003, thus, the legality, validity, and propriety of the disbursements of TA cannot be established and resulting to overpayment of TA to various officials of the municipality.

Disbursement of financial assistance to the 14 barangays of LGU Kalilangan totaling ₱420,000.00 for the conduct of various foundation day activities funded out of the General Fund were not supported with complete documentation and were erroneously recorded as an outright expense instead as Due from LGU, a non-compliance to Section 4 (8) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circulars No. 2012-001 and No. 94-013, thereby affecting the propriety and transparency of the disbursed transaction, as well as overstating the operating expenses and understating the government equity by ₱420,000.00 in the CY 2023 Financial Statements.

Extensions of contract time were granted to contractors without sufficient documentation, in violation of Sections 8.1 and 10.1-10.5 of Annex E of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act (RA) No. 9184 and Annex E of COA Circular No. 2009-001, thereby casting doubt on the validity of the time extension granted and precluding the LGU from collecting liquidated damages from the contractors.

Stale checks remained unadjusted in the books of accounts contrary to Section 59 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual and COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thus, understating the balances of Cash in Bank and Payable accounts presented in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2023 by ₱ 1,086,448.86.

The established amount of ₱ 5,235,831.68 for the “Real Property Tax Receivable” in the General Fund (GF) and ₱ 6,795,323.96 for the “Special Education Tax Receivable” in the Special Education Fund (SEF) in CY 2023 were based on the Real Property Tax target computed by the Municipal Assessor as of CY 2023 less the total actual collections for CY 2023, net of discounts and prior years collections including penalties from the report prepared by the Municipal Treasurer’s Office and not from the duly certified list showing the name of taxpayers and the amount due and collectible for the year provided by the Municipal Treasurer in contrast to Section 20 Volume I of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS), thereby, it tainted the accuracy and reliability of the said receivable accounts both in the GF and SEF.

LGU counterparts granted to Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) - Bukidnon Second District Engineering Office in years 2016 and 2018 totaling to ₱ 1.7 million remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2023 in contrast to Section 4.6 of COA Circular No. 94-013, therefore, the proper utilization and timely implementation of the identified or specific program, project or activity could not be determined and the “Due from National Government Agencies” and “Government Equity” were overstated.

Some items of the Property, Plant and Equipment of LGU Kibawe amounting to ₱ 35.78 million as of December 31, 2023 were not depreciated in contravention to Section 71 of International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS) 17, thus, it affected the fair presentation of the said accounts in the financial statements.

The Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2023 did not present the non-current portion of the Loans Payable – Domestic account with an outstanding balance of ₱ 19.4 million and its details were not fully disclosed in the Notes to the Financial Statements contrary to paragraphs 70, 80 and 127 of IPSAS 1, hence affecting the accuracy and reliability of the said account in the financial statements.

Unexpended LGU counterpart for completed KALAHI CIDDS Project amounted to ₱ 1 million remained under the “Trust Liabilities” account in the Trust Fund book of accounts in contrast to Section 99 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thereby, depriving the LGU of additional funds that could have been used to finance priority local government programs, projects and activities in CY 2023.

The purchases of Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricant (POL) by the agency amounting to ₱ 9.513 million were procured at a less advantageous price due to the non-utilization of available data for the prevailing retail-pump price from the Department of Energy (DEO) contrary to Section 2 of PD No. 1445 and GPPB Resolution No. 26-2019 dated October 30, 2019, thus, the propriety, legality and validity of the disbursements could not be ascertained.

Contracts of lease between the 1,278 lessees and the Municipal Mayor pertaining to the occupancy of the Kibawe Public Cemetery were not prepared and maintained by the Municipal Economic Enterprise and Development Office (MEEDO) in contrast to Section 6 and 7 of Ordinance No. 03 Series of 2020 or the Kibawe Public Cemetery Code, thereby, tainted the propriety, legality and validity of the cemetery occupation and inferred high vulnerability of the LGU to possible infringements that would arise in the future.

In-kind donations to Barangay Cabadiangan, Kadingilan, Bukidnon which aggregated to ₱ 193,266.00 lacked request letter and other pertinent supporting documents in contrast to Section 5 of General Requirements for All Types of Disbursements, thus, casted doubts as to the validity of the distribution of welfare/relief goods to the intended beneficiaries.

The LGU hired the service of a consultant amounted to ₱ 268,000.00 through negotiated procurement under Highly Technical Consultant without proper justification, likewise, the disbursement thereof lacked the complete supporting documents contrary to Section 48.2 and 53.7 of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 9184 and COA Circulars 2012-001, thus, casting doubts as to the propriety, legality, and validity of the disbursements and the LGU missed to avail discount or lower price associated with procurement through competitive bidding.

Payment of ₱ 100,000.00 to Southern Bukidnon Inter-local Health Zone (SBIHLZ) for the LGU’s cost sharing lacked Memorandum of Agreement (MOA), guidelines or the like in contrast to Section 4.1 and 4.6 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 5 of General Requirements for all Types of Disbursement, thereby, the propriety, validity and legality of the transaction could not be ascertained.

The LGU paid the Provincial Legal Officers and a private lawyer amounting to ₱ 27,000.00 and ₱ 8,000.00, respectively, for rendering legal services without definite legal basis contrary to the provisions of Section 95 and 481 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160 and COA Circular No. 98-002 dated June 9, 1998, thus, the validity, propriety, and legality of the disbursements cannot be ascertained.

Unexpended Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) of the agency was not transferred to the Special Trust Fund (STF) yearly contrary to Section 5.1.10 of COA Circular 2012-002, thereby might affect the assessment of the decision-makers and might mislead the users of the Financial Statements particularly relative to LDRRMF.

Unspent Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Funds (DRRMF) composed of the balances of Quick Response Fund (QRF) and DRRMF-MOOE in CY 2022 were transferred to the Trust Fund book of accounts in CY 2023 which was not in conformity to Section 5.1.10 and Annex C of COA Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012, thus, it overstated the total expenses in the General Fund and, subsequently, understated the total income by ₱ 4.87 million in CY 2023.

The unexpended LDRRMF totaling 7.1 million was charged with various disbursements amounting to ₱ 3.1 million without a (1) LDRRMFIP with a separate caption for the list of projects and activities charged to the unexpended LDRRMF, and (2) Revised AIP as approved by the local sanggunian and LCE, contrary to Section 5.1.2-3 of COA Circular 2012-002 and Section 6.5 of NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC No. 2013-01, respectively. Henceforth it casted doubts as to the propriety and validity of the disbursements.

The Municipality of Kitaotao incurred significant delays in the submission of their Disbursement Vouchers, Liquidation Reports, Collection Receipts and Deposit Slips for CY 2023, contrary to Section 100 and 107 of of PD No. 1445 and Section 7.2.1 of the 2009 Rules and Regulations on the Settlement of Accounts (RRSA) as prescribed for use under COA Circular 2009-006, thereby, precluding the conduct of the necessary and timely audit on the transactions recorded in the books of accounts and which may lead to the rendering of either a Qualified Opinion, Adverse Opinion or a Disclaimer of Opinion on whether the Financial Statements were fairly presented or not. Moreover, the present condition exposes the unsubmitted Disbursement Vouchers to audit suspension or disallowance.

The year-end balances of the intra-agency accounts, Due from Other Funds and Due to Other Funds, which are reciprocal in nature, yielded a discrepancy of P8,433,256.47, a departure from the provisions mandated by Presidential Decree No. 1445 and the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) thus, affecting the fair presentation of the related accounts in the Financial Statements.

The manner of recording Business Tax deducted from payments to suppliers is deemed unreliable due to (a) Business Tax which was initially recorded as Other Payables under the Trust Fund; (b) Business Tax initially recorded as Other Payables under the Trust Fund which were not consistently transferred to General Fund within the accounting period and (c) over recording of Business Tax in CY 2023 totalling P162,992.21 under the General Fund, all contrary to the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 1445, the New Government Accounting System Chart of Accounts and the International Public Sector Accounting Standards, which in effect exposes the amounts recorded under Other Payables to misappropriation and misuse and more importantly, casts doubt on the fair presentation of the amounts presented in the Financial Statements.

The unutilized balance of the Local Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) amounting to P8,265,850.40 was erroneously booked under the account Other Payables in the General Fund upon its reversion from the Special Trust Fund, inconsistent with the provisions of RA No. 10121 and Section 5.1.13 of COA Circular No. 2012-002, thus, exposing the funds to the risk of being used for purposes other than for which it was intended.

Disbursements amounting to P2,081,120.00 charged against the 5% Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) for CY 2022 and the Unexpended Balance of the LDRRMF disclosed (a) inappropriate charges/payments of expenses and (b) documentary deficiencies, all inconsistent with R.A. No. 10121, NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC No. 2013-1, NDRRMC-DILG-DBM-CSC JMC No. 2014-1, COA Circular No. 2012-001, COA Circular 2009-001 and R.A. No. 9184, thus depleting the funds that could have been used to finance activities that are within the thematic areas of DRRM and moreover, casts doubt as to the regularity of the aforesaid transactions.

The unexpended/unobligated balance of the Local Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) QRF and MOOE for CY 2023 was not transferred to the Trust Liability - DRRM account in the Trust Fund books as of December 31, 2023, contrary to Section 21 of RA No. 10121 and Section 5.1.10 of COA Circular No. 2012-002, thus, exposing the funds to the risk of being used for purposes other than for which the LDRRMF was established.

Collections pertaining to revenue and other receipts of the Municipality were not deposited intact and promptly to their appropriate bank accounts due to poor internal control and monitoring of collections and remittances of the Accountable Officers, with delays reaching a maximum of 116 banking days contrary to RA No. 7160, the Local Treasurer’s Manual and the Revised Cash Examination Manual, thereby exposing government funds to misappropriation and misuse by the accountable officers.

Six (6) accommodated checks totaling P18,625.00 were found on hand during the Cash Examination cut-off which indicated the practice of encashing private checks using collected funds of the Accountable Officers, a deviation from the provisions of PD 1445 and the Revised Cash Examination Manual, thereby exposing the government funds to risk of misappropriation and misuse.

Cash advances totaling P9,146,584.40 granted in CY 2023 and in prior years remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2023 and moreover, additional cash advances were granted to municipal officials and employees despite having unliquidated balances, all contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 97-002, thus, exposing government funds to risk of possible misuse, casting doubt as to the regularity and propriety of the related transactions and prevents the recording of the related expenses in the proper period.

Cash Advances totaling P61,612,201.54 were granted without the stated specific legal purpose for which it was disbursed and without the required supporting documents, contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445, COA Circular No. 97-002 and COA Circular No. 2023-004, thereby exposing government funds to risk of misuse and misappropriation and furthermore, the legality, validity and propriety of the disbursements on which the cash advances were applied could not be readily determined.

The grant and liquidation of Cash Advances for Confidential and/or Intelligence Funds is deemed non-compliant with the prescribed rules and regulations in view of a) Unliquidated Cash Advances for CF and/or IF b) Non-designation of a Special Disbursing Officer or the Head of Agency for the drawing of Cash Advances for CF and/or IF c) Cash Advances granted without supporting documents and d) Non-submission to the COA Audit Team Leader of the Cash Advance Disbursement Vouchers within seven (7) days from release thereof, all in violation of the provisions stated in PD No. 1445 and COA-DBM-DILG-GCG-DND Joint Circular No. 2015-01, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the related transactions.

Payments of BAC Honoraria amounting to P350,400.00 were not supported with sufficient and relevant documents and were not recorded using the prescribed account, inconsistent with the provisions set forth in COA Circular No. 2012-001 and DBM Budget Circular No. 2004-5A, thus precluding a timely and effective examination of thereof and moreover, casts doubt as to the regularity of the aforesaid transactions.

The agency made disbursements for honoraria amounting to P229,000.00 for services which are deemed part of the inherent duties and responsibilities of the recipients and of the agency in general, inconsistent with the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 1445, DBM Budget Circular No. 2007-1 and the General Appropriations Act of 2022, thus, casting doubt on the the legality, propriety and validity of the related disbursements and moreover, may be considered irregular as these are expenditures incurred without adhering to the established rules and regulations.

Salaries, honoraria and other allowances totaling P16,184,289.85 were granted without the complete documentary evidence, contrary to PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2012-001, thus, casting doubt on the validity, propriety and regularity of the related transactions and moreover, exposes the aforesaid transactions to audit suspension or disallowance.

Reimbursements for transactions with amounts ranging from P1,500.00 to P35, 010.00 which totaled P311,081.50 were only supported with Reimbursement Expense Receipts as proof of payment, contrary to COA Circular 2012-003 and and COA Circular No. 2021-001, thus, casting doubts on the validity, propriety and regularity of the transactions.

Various procurement transactions totaling P6,889,483.29 were made through reimbursement which is not one of the allowed alternative modes of procurement, a departure from the provisions of the Revised IRR of Republic Act 9184, otherwise known as the Government Procurement Reform Act, thus, depriving the municipality from availing of the most advantageous prices of the goods and services subjected to reimbursement and moreover, casts doubt as to the legality, validity and propriety of the related procurement transactions.

The annual budgets under the SEF for CYs 2022 to 2023 were not presented/supported with the DepEd-approved School Improvement Plan (SIP), the Division Education Development Plan (DEDP) and the DepEd and ECCD Council Budget, inconsistent with the provisions of Republic Act 716 and DepEd-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1, Series of 2017, thus, the conformity of the programmed disbursements thereof with the prescribed budgeting and utilization guidelines could not be verified.

The Petty Cash Fund totaling ₱80,000.00 had various deficiencies contrary to Sections 48 and 52 of the New Government Accounting System Manual for LGUs (NGAS for LGUs) and the DOF-BLGF Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM), thereby casting doubt on the propriety of the establishment and utilization of the petty cash fund and the correctness of the accounting treatment of all transactions related to petty cash.

The Municipality of Lantapan granted Capital Assistances totaling ₱2,815,000.00 which were supported with ambiguous ‘Livelihood Agreements’ that were debited outright to “Donations” contrary to Section 4(8) and Section 123 of PD 1445, COA Circular 2015-009, and the signed Livelihood Agreements, thus confusing the MSWDO and the recipients of the assistances of their duties and obligations, bypassing the liquidation of the provided support, and adversely affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Comparison between the financial statements of the Philippine Rural Development Project, “Concreting of Road and Drainage at Purok 3 to 5 Kulasihan, Lantapan, Bukidnon FMR”, revealed an overall variance of ₱8,742,896.44 between the SSAF and the other financial reports, contrary to Item a.1, Section 6.4.1, 6.7.1, and 6.7.2 of the PRDP Financial Management Operations Guidelines dated December 7, 2021 and Section 111(1) of PD 1445, thereby casting doubt on fair presentation of the financial reports.

The Municipality purchased and distributed inventories totaling P10,257,599.60 with various deficiencies contrary to Sections 2 and 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and Paragraph 44 of IPSAS 12; thereby casting doubt on the propriety of the distribution of inventories and correctness of the balance of the Inventory Accounts.

The Municipal Accounting Office failed to submit Journal Entry Vouchers (JEV) and their supporting documents on accounting entries aggregating to P466,375,375.90 as well as updated Subsidiary Ledgers (SL) which is contrary to Section 347 of Republic Act (RA) 7160, Section 7.2.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009 and Paragraph Two (2), Section 114 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 which casts doubts on validity, propriety and regularity of recorded transactions, and the reliability and fair presentation of financial statements.

Fund transfers, that are recorded as liability, totaling ₱12,991,824.61 from the Department of Interior and Local Government have no Memorandum of Agreement contrary to Section 3.1.2 of COA Circular 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012 and IPSAS 15; thereby creating difficulty in determining the responsibilities of the LGU, and casting doubt on the propriety of its recognition as financial liability in the accounting records.

The Municipal Accounting Office failed to submit Journal Entry Vouchers (JEV) and their supporting documents on various adjustments aggregating to P 466,375,375.90 as well as updated Subsidiary Ledgers (SL) which is contrary to Section 347 of Republic Act (RA) 7160, Section 7.2.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009 and Paragraph Two (2), Section 114 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 which casts doubts on validity, propriety and regularity of recorded transactions, reliability and fair presentation of financial statements.

Cash Examination of the Disbursing Officer revealed various deficiencies contrary to the DOF-BLGF Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM), thereby affecting monitoring and accuracy of records of the said officer and creating difficulty in the conduct of audit activities.

The Municipality of Lantapan granted financial assistance to Barangay Kulasihan and Bugcaon totaling P2,000,000.00 to purchase parcels of land with estimated of value of P1,000,000.00 each with various deficiencies contrary to Section 2 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445; thereby casting doubt on the propriety of the fund transfers and creates a huge risk on the part of the LGU.

The Municipality of Lantapan submitted their quarterly report on Projects, Programs, and Activities (PPAs), which reflected that the project, Construction/Improvement of Water System at Purok 5 Balila, with contract price of P2,911,281.60, was 100% complete despite the fact that project was still actually ongoing contrary to Section 2 of Presidential Decree 1445, thereby casting doubt on the reliability of project accomplishment reports.

The Municipality of Lantapan failed to comply the lacking documents noted in relation to the auditorial/technical review of the returned project contracts with a total contract price of P5,809,926.79 contrary to Section 3.1.1 and 3.1.4 of COA Circular 2009-001; thereby creating difficulty in facilitating the completion of technical review and inspection by the COA-TSO.

The Municipality purchased various parcels of land totaling P8,409,519.19 with lacking documents contrary to Sections 10 of the Executive Order (EO) No. 1035, s. 1985, Section 4 (6&8) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and Paragraph 13.1 of COA Circular 2012-001, thereby casting doubt on the validity, and propriety of the purchase of the land.

The Municipality procured various goods under Negotiated Procurement – Two Failed Biddings totaling P8,145,526.00 with lacking eligibility documents contrary to Section 23, Items D & G of Annex “H”, and of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (R-IRR) of RA 9184 which creates difficulty in ascertaining the eligibility of the winning bidders and casts doubt on the regularity of the procurement process.

Various projects with contract prices totaling P26,187,692.87 had physical dimension variances contrary to approved As Built Plans; thereby casting doubt on the submitted/declared accomplishments in relation to the project initiatives.

The Municipality of Lantapan incorrectly computed the recoupment deductions of various billings totaling ₱55,058,148.36 from two (2) project initiatives contrary to Section 5.3(b) of the 2023 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 9184, which resulted to a billing variance totaling ₱657,853.71 and increased the risk of the unrecouped portion.

Cash Advances totaling P39,307,202.13 were granted without supporting documents contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445; thereby casting doubt on the regularity of the grant of cash advances.

Various government initiatives totaling ₱162,028,472.54 were extended beyond their target date of completion with lacking documentary requirements contrary to Section 11.1 and 11.5 of Annex “E” of the 2023 Updated Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 9184, thereby creating unnecessary risk for the projects under extended work duration and casting doubt on the validity of the approval of the work extension.

The accuracy, completeness, and existence under the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) account with book value totaling P550.362 million as of December 31, 2023 could not be ascertained due to: a) non-conduct of physical count of majority of its PPE accounts for CY 2023; b) incomplete details of Report on Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE); and c) existence of unreconciled balances of movable properties between General Services Office and the Municipal Accounting Office, in disregard of COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020, affecting the fairness of presentation of the PPE accounts in the financial statements.

The accuracy and reliability of Property, Plant and Equipment balances as of December 31, 2023 could not be ascertained due to non-provision of accumulated depreciation and depreciation expense in some PPE items totaling P30.196 million thereby, contrary to Section 58 of PD no. 1445, Section 13 of IPSAS 17 and could lead to misstatement of CY 2023 depreciation expense and overstatement of PPE carrying amounts as of December 31, 2023.

The Land account balance of P9.690 million is understated due to non-application of revaluation model as accounting policy contrary to the provision of IPSAS 17, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the CY 2023 Financial Statements balances.

Comparative amounts of the accounts in the LGUs Financial Statements were not restated to reflect the Prior Period Adjustments (PPA) with a total net effect in the Government Equity of P8.846 million and corresponding disclosures related thereto were not provided, contrary to IPSAS 3, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The uncollected receivables account as of December 31, 2023, consisting of Due from NGOs/POs, Loan Receivables, and Other Receivables totaling P6.090 million from CYs 2000 to 2013, and the lack of comprehensive details of Other Receivables balances amounting to P10.054 million in the Financial Statements Schedules, is contrary to Section 58 of Presidential Decree 1445 and Section 6.1 of COA Circular No. 2016-005, rendering the Financial Statement unreliable.

Investment properties costing P5.398 million were erroneously recorded as Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE), contrary to International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 16, understating both the Investment Property Account and its corresponding Accumulated Depreciation by P5.398 million and P1.504 million, respectively and overstating the Property, Plant and Equipment and the corresponding Accumulated Depreciation by the same amount, affecting fair presentation of Financial Statements thereof.

The LGU did not credit revenue upon the utilization of funds, despite liabilities being deemed reduced upon utilization, contrary to Paragraphs 45-47 and BC11 of IPSAS 23, thereby, overstating the Due to NGA and understating the revenue and net income of the LGU by at least P3.955 million.

Seven (7) stale checks amounting to P1.039 million remained outstanding for more than six months in contrary to Section 59, Chapter 3 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System for LGUs Volume I, thereby understating the Cash-LCCA and the affected payable account.

Training Expenses in CY 2023 totaling P2.129 million was erroneously recorded by debiting the Membership Dues and Contributions to Organizations expense account of the LGU, contrary to sound accounting and the description of accounts per Annex “B” of COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thereby, overstating the Membership Dues and Contributions to Organizations expense account and understating the Training Expense account of the LGU.

Reconciling items totaling P22,006.97 identified in the Bank Reconciliation Statements were not adjusted in the agency’s book of accounts, contrary to Item 3.3 of COA Circular No. 96-011 dated, October 2, 1996, thus affecting the reliability of Cash in Bank account – LCCA totaling to P141.189 million thus, the accuracy and veracity of the amount is doubtful.

The remaining balance of the Bayanihan Grant to Cities and Municipalities (BGCM) of the LGU amounting P3.6 million was not reverted to the National Treasury, contrary to DBM Local Budget Circular No. 125 dated April 7, 2020 and DBM Circular Letter No. 2021-13 dated December 31, 2021, thereby, depriving the Government of the Philippines of the opportunity to reallocate and utilize these funds for other essential programs and services.

The procurement of drugs and medicines totaling P3.1 million in CY 2023 were not substantiated with the required documentary requirements prescribed under Section 9.1.3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, thus, propriety and safety of the procured medicines could not be ascertained.

The grant of Other Bonuses and Allowances through PRAISE Incentives to fifty-one (51) officials and employees at P60,000.00 each totaling P3.06 miliion were paid without proper distinction, criteria and evaluation as prescribed by CSC Memorandum Circular No. 1, s. 2001 on PRAISE guidelines thereby, cast doubts on the propriety of claims.

Payment of various expenses totaling to P1.058 million was not supported with Charge Sales Invoice from the seller contrary to Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 2-2014, thus, casting doubt on the validity of the transaction.

Technical specifications for the procurement of goods for “maternal and child pack for newly delivered mothers” totalling P0.199 million were not stated in the Purchase Request (PR) and Request for Quotation (RFQ), and complete item name and brand name in the Purchase Order (PO), contrary to Section 8(b)(i), Annex “H” of the 2016 revised IRR of RA 9184 and Item B(1)(h)(i)(m) of COA Circular No. 96-010 dated August 15, 1996, respectively, thus, correctness of the items delivered and price worthiness thereof could not be ascertained.

Payment of various money claims has no assigned Disbursement Voucher (DV) Number contrary to Section 32 Chapter 2 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System for LGUs Volume 2, thereby causing difficulty in identifying and tracing the same to the respective journals and related reports and documents.

Financial reports and other documents for audit were not submitted within the prescribed period as required under Section 122 of PD 1445 and Sections 7.1 and 7.2 COA Circular 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009, thus, precluding the timely audit of the financial transactions, and preparation and submission of the required audit reports.

Unutilized balances of LDRRMF under the Trust Fund for CY 2018 and below of Approximately P15.736 million, were not transferred to the General Fund (GF) contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012, thus, the amount was not made available to fund projects or programs which the Municipality and its constituents could benefit.

The accuracy and reliability of Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) is doubtful due to (a) unreconciled material variance of P81.052 million between the actual amounts reported therein versus the amounts in the Statement of Financial Performance due to the inability to provide and complete the reconciliation reports and (b) lack of disclosures of the reasons for material differences, contrary to Paragraphs 21 of the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) No. 1 and Paragraphs 14, 47 and 29 of IPSAS No. 24.

The discrepancy between the City Treasurer's Office records and the reported Real Property Tax Receivable, Special Education Tax Receivable, and their corresponding Deferred Income accounts decreased by 11.59%, or ₱22.163 million, between CY 2022 and CY 2023. However, a material understatement totaling ₱169.063 million remained, primarily due to the incomplete reconciliation and discontinued use of subsidiary ledgers, which is not in accordance with Sections 4, 20, and 70 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) and International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1 and 23.

The non-adoption of the perpetual inventory method in recording all receipts and issuances of welfare goods and lack of regular coordination, contrary to Section 114, Chapter 7, Volume I of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual, COA Circular 2014-002, and COA Circular No. 2015-009, understated the Inventory account and overstated the expense and correspondingly the Government Equity account by approximately P1.700 million as of year-end.

The accuracy and existence of the reported Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) account balance as of December 31, 2023 totaling P2.815 billion could not be ascertained due to the doubtful existence of PPE items with an aggregate net book value of P114.21 million; non-inclusion in the RPCPPE of PPE items with carrying amounts totaling P2.15 million; non-submission of RPCPPE for accounts with a total net book value of P467 million, thereby casting doubt on the reliability of the balance presented in the Statement of Financial Position at the end of CY 2023.

The Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) was misstated due to error and differences in the manual and system generated calculation of the depreciation resulting in an estimated net overstatement of Accumulated Depreciation by P134.726 million, resulting to the undervaluation of corresponding PPE accounts and understatement of the Government Equity by the same amount, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the Financial Statements as of December 31, 2023.

Livestock associated with the City’s livestock dispersal program with a carrying value of P6.321 million was erroneously recorded as Work/Zoo animals under the Property, Plant, and Equipment account instead of the proper biological assets account, contrary to Section 2 of PPSAS 27. The existence of the recorded assets cannot be determined and validated due to the non- submission of the report on the physical count of biological assets, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements as at reporting date.

The balance of the Due to National Government Agencies (NGA) account for the implementation of projects/programs/activities in the total amount of P39.013 million as of December 31, 2023 is unreliable due to the (a) existence of dormant balances totaling P1.125 million; (b) unliquidated and/or unrefunded and unremitted balances aggregating P2.222 million; (c) inclusion of funds received that do not meet the criteria for recording of liability amounting to P0.726 million; (d) erroneous adjustments amounting to P1.204 million; and (e) unidentified subsidiary accounts totaling P1.863 million.

The utilization/liquidation of Trust Liabilities, fund transfers made by National Government Agencies (NGA) and other trust receipts in the Trust Fund books were not recognized as revenue despite that conditions thereof have already been met, contrary to Paragraphs 44, 45 and 46 and Basis For Conclusion (BC) No. 11 of IPSAS 23, thereby understating the revenue account of the LGU and caused the Trust Fund to report a deficit totaling P41.526 million.

Variance aggregating P22.09 million was noted between the Report on Sources and Utilization of the DRRMF and the accounting and budget records due to non-reconciliation, contrary to Sections 111 and 123 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thereby creating doubt on the accuracy of both report and records and affecting the correctness and accuracy of the disclosure made in the Notes to Financial Statements.

Unutilized balance totaling P7.078 million from the CY 2017 DRRM Special Trust Fund (STF) was not reverted to the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund with total utilization amounting P2.58 million for CY 2023, contrary to the various provisions under COA Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012, which could have been used as additional funding source for other social services of the LGU. Moreover, the CY 2015 and 2016 DRRM STF unutilized balance aggregating P37.02 million reverted to the General Fund on January 19, 2023 was not made available for other social services despite availability of funds.

The utilization of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) of the LGU could not be judiciously evaluated due to the non-preparation of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund Investment Plan/ Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Plan (LDRRMFIP/LDRRMP) for the Special Trust Fund (STF) from CY 2017 to 2022 and Supplemental Budget No. 1 with disbursements aggregating P22.617 million, not in consonance with the various provisions required under COA Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012, and the Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-01 of the NDRRMC, DBM and DILG dated March 25, 2013.
