The delayed implementation and inclusion of projects that are not implementation ready into the 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) Programs, Projects, and Activities (PPAs) for CY 2023 resulted to a low implementation and utilization rate of the current year and Continuing Appropriations, thus, impeding the optimum utilization of the fund which consequently deprived the public of the benefits that could have been derived from its immediate implementation and maximum utilization.

The City Government of Malaybalay failed to fully utilize the financial assistance for Typhoon Odette victims totaling P12.479 million with minimal utilization rate of 11.68% due to the absence of coordinated efforts between and among City Officials and with the Source Agency which is not in consonance with DBM Local Budget Circulars No. 141 and DILG-DSWD-DND Joint Memorandum Circular no. 4 series of 2021, thereby defeating the purpose by which the financial assistance was given and depriving the intended beneficiaries the benefits that can be derived therefrom.

Terminal leave benefits granted to thirty-three (33) officials and employees aggregating ₱4.398 million as of November 30, 2023 were paid despite having incomplete documentation which is not in consonance with the requirements under COA Circular 2012-001 and CSC Memorandum Circular No. 06, s. of 2003, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the disbursements.

Travelling expenses were paid in excess of the maximum Daily Travel Expense (DTE) allowed under Executive Order No. 77 dated March 15, 2019 which constitutes excessive expenditures. Moreover, transactions with inadequate supporting documents were found, thereby casting doubt on its propriety and validity.

The City Government of Malaybalay’s government share of the monthly Pag-IBIG premium is in excess of the maximum mandatory contribution of P100.00 for each employee as required in Republic Act No. 9679 otherwise known as the Home Development Mutual Fund Law of 2009 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations, resulting to an over-remittance to the Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF) totaling P4.418 million.

Inter-agency payables representing withheld taxes, premium contributions and loan amortizations for the BIR, GSIS, Pag-ibig and Philhealth aggregating ₱7.192 million as of December 31, 2023 were not remitted in full within the prescribed period, contrary to Section 4 of BIR Revenue Regulation No. 4-2002, Sections 5 and 11 of BIR Revenue Regulation No. 11-2018, Sections 14.1 to 14.3 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act (RA) No. 8291, Section E.4 of HDMF Circular No. 275 dated January 22, 2010 and Section 18 of the IRR of the National Health Insurance Act of 2013, thereby exposing the City Government and the employees to the possible imposition of penalty and surcharges for the late remittance thereof.

Erroneous information was presented in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) and the Status of Appropriations, Allotments, Obligations and Balances (SAAOB) for CY 2023 for failure to disclose the correct amounts of obligation and unobligated appropriations for LDRRM-MOOE funds, while the unspent balance of LDRRM-Capital Outlay appropriations totaling ₱14,964.70 have been erroneously transferred to the Trust Fund, materially deviating IPSAS 24 and Section 5.1.11 of COA Circular No. 2012-002, thus making the financial reports unreliable which would affect the rendition of auditor’s opinion on the prepared financial statement that would consequently affect the decision-making of its users.

Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivable accounts in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position for Calendar Year 2023 had unreliable and inaccurate balances due to the agency’s improper method of establishing receivables based on “collection target” for the year, instead of the certified list based on Real Property Tax Account Register (RPTAR) or Taxpayer’s Index Card, inconsistent with the provisions of PD 1445 and NGAS Manual for LGUs, hence, the said accounts were understated by ₱3.008 million and ₱4.061 million, respectively. Further, the corresponding Deferred RPT and Deferred SET accounts were understated by ₱3.210 million and ₱4.273 million, respectively.

The LGU’s computation of depreciation expense is inconsistent to the IPSAS 17, NGAS Manual for LGUs, and COA Circular 2004-003, due to its non-provision of depreciation for all PPE additions in CY 2023, thereby, the related Depreciation Expense and Accumulated Depreciation accounts were both understated by ₱2.033 million, affecting the reliability and accuracy of the financial statements.

Twenty-three (23) parcels of land are not supported with Transfer Certificates of Title (TCTs) under the name of the LGU-Malitbog but mostly by Certificates of Tax Declaration (CTDs), contrary to the provisions of Section 148 of COA Circular No. 92-386 and RA 7160, thereby casting doubt in determining the right to ownership over its properties and exposing the agency to a possible risk of court litigation. Moreover, incomplete/unidentifiable subsidiary ledgers were maintained for Land account costing ₱11.105 million as at December 31, 2023 while relevant disclosure requirement was not presented in the Notes to Financial Statements as prescribed by IPSAS 17, thus, creating doubt on the completeness and fair disclosure of said account in the financial statements that might affect the decision-making of its intended users.

The agency failed to adopt timely disposal procedures for twenty-one (21) unserviceable heavy equipment and other motor vehicles, a nonconformance to Section 79 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 92-386 prescribing the Rules and Regulations on Supply and Property Management in the Local Governments, hence, the municipality could have generated greater benefits to the municipality in terms of higher appraisal value for the property, lesser storage cost, and better management of limited storage space. Moreover, the proceeds to be derived from the sale of such properties could be an additional funding to finance various priority programs and projects of the municipality.

Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts with net carrying amount of ₱700.536 million were not subjected to one-time cleansing and with other noted observations, a non-conformance to COA Circular 2020-006 and NGAS Manual for LGUs, thus, the accuracy and existence of the PPE accounts presented in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2023 are doubtful and unreliable, thereby depriving the government of reliable and useful information in decision-making and accountability for these assets.

Unnecessary surcharges due to delayed payments were incurred and paid against government funds on top of the monthly electric bills in calendar year 2023 totaling ₱127,983.22, contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular 2012-003 dated October 29, 2012, thus, depleting government funds which could have been allocated to valuable programs and projects benefiting the constituents.

LGU-Malitbog improperly hired the services of consultants in calendar year 2023 without adhering to the proper procurement procedures as prescribed by the Revised IRR of RA 9184 and COA-DBM JC No. 2, s. 2020, thereby precluded the transparency, competitiveness, and accountability as envisioned by the said law and regulations and that the audit team cast reservation on the regularity and validity of the disbursed transactions totaling ₱1,931,177.

The municipality paid procurement-related honoraria both to GSO personnel rendering full-time service and to the invited observers from Non-Government Organization (NGO) totaling ₱36,000.00 and ₱19,600.00, respectively, contravening provisions of DBM Budget Circular No. 2004-5A dated October 7, 2005 and Section 15 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184. Additionally, some disbursements were noted with incomplete supporting documents totaling ₱417,000.00, contrary to Section 4 of PD 1445 and COA Circular Nos. 2012-001 and 2023-004. Thus, raising concerns on the regularity and validity of the disbursed transactions.

Motor vehicles procured in calendar year 2023 totaling ₱13.662 million were not supported with complete documentation, inconsistent with PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 2023-004, hence, the validity and propriety of the disbursements are doubtful.

Some procurements of Supplies & Materials Inventory and Diesel Fuel amounting ₱1,945,867.74 and ₱2,246,205.06, respectively, were presumed splitted, in violation of the proper procurement procedures as prescribed by the Revised IRR of RA 9184, thereby circumventing the necessity of competitive bidding and the requirements for the alternative methods of procurement.

Similar procurement items included in the Annual Procurement Plan (APP) of LGU-Malitbog were not consolidated on a quarterly basis and were improperly presented in generic terms and per department basis instead as one procuring entity, caused by the non-preparation and non-consolidation of the PPMPs by end-users, in violation to the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, thereby defeating the main purpose of consolidation procedure and the numerous unnecessary purchases had been undertaken by the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) throughout the year.

The copies of perfected contracts were submitted delayed for 160 days in average and lacked basic supporting documents, contradictory to the pertinent provisions of COA Circular 2009-001, consequently precluded the audit team from undertaking the timely and relevant audit results on the propriety, legality and the technical aspect of the awarded contracts.

The hiring of job order workers in calendar year 2023 were not supported with contracts duly signed/consented by said workers, contravening Article 1305 of the Civil Code of the Philippines, CSC-COA-DBM JC No. 1, s. 2017, COA-DBM JC No. 2, s. 2020, and various DILG Legal Opinion, thus, the audit team cast reservation on the propriety of hiring job order workers, including the disbursements thereof made by LGU Malitbog..

The accuracy, reliability, and existence of the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts as of December 31, 2023 with book value of ₱1.427 billion could not be ascertained due to: (a) non-conduct of complete physical count of its PPE for CY 2023; (b) existence of unreconciled balances between General Services Office and the Municipal Accounting Office; (c) presence of bulk acquisitions without specifying quantities in Property Cards and PPE Ledger Cards; (d) capitalization of costs of Repairs and Maintenance; and (e) not completely adopting the Uniform Property Identification System for PPE, in disregard of COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020 and COA Circular 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022, affecting the fairness of presentation of the PPE accounts in the financial statements.

Investment properties costing P27.703 million were erroneously recorded as Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE), contrary to International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 16, understating both the Investment Property Account and its corresponding Accumulated Depreciation by P27.703 million and P6.608 million, respectively and overstating the Property, Plant and Equipment and the corresponding Accumulated Depreciation by the same amount, affecting fair presentation of Financial Statements thereof.

Retrospective treatment of prior period errors was not adequately complied and applied by the LGU on Prior Period Errors totaling P19.131 million and corresponding disclosures related thereto were not sufficiently provided, contrary to IPSAS 3, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Donations in CY 2023 totaling P8.611 million was treated and recorded as direct adjustment (debit) to the Government Equity account instead of expense, contrary to the definition of expense per Paragraph 7 of IPSAS 1, thus, the CY 2023 expenses of the LGU and overall net income is understated by the same amount, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Various issued inventories totaling P3.856 million were either not charged to expense or Prior Period Adjustment but were recorded under Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE), contrary to COA Circular 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022, affecting the fairness of presentation of the PPE accounts in the financial statements.

Borrowing costs incurred in CY 2023 totaling P2.515 million relative to the construction of various qualifying assets were not capitalized but instead recorded as interest expense, contrary to Paragraph 3.11 of the LGUs Notes to Financial Statements and Paragraph 18 to 20, IPSAS 5, thereby, overstating the expense of the LGU and understating the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) by the same amount, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Cash in Bank - Local Currency, Current Account and Trust Liabilities accounts were both overstated by P1.997 million as at December 31, 2023 representing erroneous recording of the release of LBP Loan proceeds to the LGU from the year 2021, contrary to sound accounting and description of accounts per COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thereby affecting the fairness of the presentation of Financial Statements at year-end.

The balance of the Due to PhilHealth account as presented in the financial statements of the LGU is overstated by P1.559 million as at December 31, 2023 representing the variance of the account on the LGU’s books and the Statement of Premium Account (SPA) from PhilHealth which is not in accordance with Paragraph 27 of International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS), affecting the fair presentation of the Financial Statements thereof.

The LGU reduced its liability (Due from NGAs) and increased its Government Equity in relation to its fund utilization and liquidation of the P1.5 million fund transfer from DA-RFO for the “Enhancement of Municipal Food Terminal Project” despite that the condition attached thereto has not been met, contrary to Paragraph 47 and BC 11 of IPSAS 23, thereby, understating the Due to NGA and overstating Government Equity account by P1.5 million.

The reliability and accuracy of the Cash in Bank -Local Currency, Current Account and Cash in Bank - Local Currency, Time Deposits Due accounts of the LGU are doubtful as: 1) identified reconciling items initially totaled at P(0.379 million)(net) for its eight (8) bank accounts were not adjusted in the agency’s book of accounts as at December 31, 2023, and 2) non-submission of copies of Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS) for its fifteen (15) bank accounts totaling P8.025 million, contrary to Item 3.3 of COA Circular No. 96-011 dated, October 2, 1996.

The LGU imposed only a maximum of 10% liquidated damages on the delayed delivery of 4 units 4x4 multi-purpose vehicles from the contract cost less of tax, contrary to Section 3.1, Annex “D” of RA 9184, thus, the imposed liquidated damages was short of P0.380 million, understating the Miscellaneous Income of the LGU.

Disposal of unserviceable properties with a total cost of P P33.366 million was not facilitated due to the non-submission of the Inventory and Inspection Report of Unserviceable Property (IlRUP), contrary to COA Circular 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020 and Section 379 of Republic Act (RA) 7160, instigating the properties to further deterioration and causing the saleable value thereof to decline.

Disbursement Vouchers, Payrolls and Official Receipts including its supporting documents were not submitted, as of this writing, to the Office of the Auditor, contrary to COA Circular 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009 and Section 6.05 of COA Circular 95-006 dated May 18, 1995, thus, the validity, propriety and legality of these transactions could not be validated.

The LGU’s payments of the GSIS premium contributions and loans for CY 2023 totaling ₱25.655 million were only supported with validated deposit slips instead of Official Receipts, in violation of COA Circular 2004-006 dated September 9, 2004, thus, failed to support the same with acceptable evidence that the liability arising from the claim has indeed been extinguished or reduced in the amount received by the payee.

Check Register was not prepared by the Municipal Treasurer which is not in consonance with the provisions of Section 42 of NGAS Manual for LGUs, Volume I, hence, the presentation, accounting and monitoring of the release of checks to the rightful claimants cannot be facilitated, exposing risks of possible claim disputes thereof.

The a) delays in remittances of premium contributions for the year 2023 to PhilHealth and b) unresolved deficiencies appearing on the PhilHealth Statement of Premium Account (SPA) of the LGU totaling P0.475 million pertaining to nonpayment of premium for the prior year 2015 are not in consonance with Section 19 of the “Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA 7875” as amended, which may result to penalties and other liabilities under the pertinent provisions of the Revised Penal Code.

Stale checks remained unadjusted in the books of accounts contrary to Section 83(I)(4) of Local Treasury Operations Manual and COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thus, understating the balances of Cash in Bank and Payable accounts presented in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2023 by ₱ 304,092.94.

The inclusion of unreconciled/unidentified balances in the subsidiary ledgers in the amount of ₱ 80.558 million in the General Fund (GF) and ₱ 559,177.39 in the Trust Fund (TF) or totalling ₱ 81.117 million was inconsistent to Section 111 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 10, Chapter 1, Volume II of the NGAS Manual for LGUs thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of some real accounts presented in CY 2023 Statement of Financial Position.

Financial assistance granted to various barangays of the Municipality of Maramag from the years 2015 to 2022 totaling to ₱ 3,498,454.72 remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2023 in contrast to the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between the Municipal Mayor and Punong Barangay, therefore, the total assets was overstated as of December 31, 2023 and proper utilization and timely implementation of the identified or specific program, project or activity could not be determined.

10% LGU counterpart amounted to ₱ 3 million for the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) project entitled “Concreting of Purok 9 to Purok 9A, North Poblacion Farm to Market Road” was recorded in “Subsidy – Others”, an expense account, instead of “Due from NGAs”, a receivable account, in contrast to Section 7 of Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between the District Engineer of DPWH-Bukidnon Second District Engineering Office and the Municipal Mayor of LGU Maramag and COA Circular 2015-009, thus, tainted the accuracy and reliability of the affected accounts.

Road networks account amounting to ₱ 206,252,659.12 as of December 31, 2023 did not include computation for depreciation in contravention to Section IV-12, IV-13 and VII-a.4 of COA Circular No. 2015-008, thus, it affected the fair presentation of the said account in the financial statements.

Completed Bottoms-Up Budgeting (BUB) Project from the Department of Agriculture (DA) entitled “Concreting of JCT. National Highway to Panadtalan-Sabacajan-San Roque Farm to Market Road” was unrecorded in the General Fund book of accounts contrary to the Certificate of Acceptance and Commitment issued by the Municipal Mayor dated May 3, 2019, therefore, the total assets and total government equity were understated by ₱ 8.18 million as of December 31, 2023.

Completed projects aggregated to ₱ 16.938 million were still recorded under the “Construction in Progress” (CIP) accounts in the General Fund book of the agency as of December 31, 2023 contrary to the provisions of COA Circular 2015-009 tainting the propriety, accuracy and reliability of the affected accounts.

Two (2) completed infrastructure projects turned-over by LGU Maramag to the recipient barangays were already derecognized in the Trust Fund book of accounts without the necessary deeds of transfer, certificate of project turn-over and acceptance by the recipient barangay and the like contrary to Section B.5 and C of the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between LGU Maramag and the Provincial Government of Bukidnon, therefore, the propriety, validity and legality of the derecognition and transfer of the previously constructed project could not be ascertained and casted doubts as to the full implementation and completeness of the rehabilitation project .

“Intangible assets” account amounting to ₱14.686 million as of December 31, 2023 was not amortized in contravention to Section 73 and 88 of IPSAS 31 and COA Circular 2015-009, thus, it affected the fair presentation of the said account in the financial statements.

Unpaid financial assistance to various barangays totalling to ₱ 18.4 million was recorded in the “Accounts Payable” account instead of “Due to LGUs” account contrary to Annex A of COA Circular 2016-004 and Section 11 and 48 of IPSAS 24, thus, it tainted the correctness, accuracy and reliability of the affected accounts as of December 31, 2023.

The unutilized amount of ₱ 2.372 million financial assistance received from the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) was not reverted to the National Treasury as of December 31, 2023 contrary to Section 3.8 of the DBM LBC No. 141 and depriving the National Government of the timely usage of this fund to finance various priority programs and projects.

The LGU paid a total of ₱ 1,023,979.79 for reimbursement of communication expenses without sufficient basis and complete supporting documents contrary to Section 447 of RA 7160 and COA Circulars 2012-001 and 2023-004, thus, casting doubts as to the propriety, legality, and validity of the payments.

The purchases of Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricant (POL) by the agency amounting to ₱ 4.7 million were procured at a less advantageous price due to the non-utilization of available data for the prevailing retail-pump price from the Department of Energy (DEO) contrary to Section 2 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Item 10 of Negotiated Procurement under Annex H of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act 9184, thus resulted in an overpayment, initially computed, to the suppliers totaling ₱ 603,119.71. Likewise, the procurement of POL was not under GPPB Resolution No. 26-2019, dated October 30, 2019, hence, the Municipality missed to avail volume discounts or lower prices associated with bulk purchases through competitive bidding.

The lease of venue for the technical budget hearing totaling ₱ 498,750.00 was not supported with complete documentation, contrary to Section 4(6) of PD 1445 and Annex H of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 9184, likewise, the disbursement might be extravagant under Annex E Item No. 2 and 3 of COA Circular 2012-003 dated October 29, 2012, thus, casting doubts to the propriety, legality, and validity of the disbursements.

Five percent (5%) Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) share of building permit fees collected by LGU Maramag from calendar year 2012 to November 2023 totaling to ₱ 1.479 million was remitted directly to DPWH Bukidnon 2nd District Engineering Office (DEO) contrary to Section 2.3 to 2.5 of DPWH DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 001, thus, the propriety, validity and legality of the payment could not be ascertained.

The grant of Personnel Motivation Incentive (PMI) to various officials and employees of LGU-Maramag totaling to ₱ 8,685,390.14 was not substantiated with a clear and definite legal basis contrary to Section 4.1 & 4.6 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2013-003, henceforth, it casted doubts as to the propriety, validity, and legality of the payment.

Check and cash disbursements, cash receipts, and general journal transactions, including their supporting documents, involving the amount of not less than P48M for the month of December 2023, were not submitted within the reglementary period in violation of Section 107 of PD No. 1445 and Item 6.05 of COA Circular No. 95-006 and, thereby limiting the extent of audit, preventing the audit team to establish fully the validity of the underlying transactions, and forfeiting the benefit of, among others, timely detecting errors and deficiencies; identifying areas for improvement; having input to assessments of accountability and decisions that need to be made, and limiting the review and verification of the submitted financial statements.

Management failed to submit a Monthly Report of Official Travels and a complete and reliable Monthly Report of Fuel Consumption, contrary to the provisions of COA Circular No. 77-61, thereby preventing the audit team from verifying and determining the reasonableness of fuel consumed for the year 2023 and the correctness of the reported fuel expenses amounting to P11,491,712.34 in the year-end Financial Statements, and defeating one of the main utilities of the reports, which is to aid the management in the prevention of wasteful, excessive, and unnecessary expenditures of fuel.

Payments of Transportation Allowances (TA) for the Calendar Year 2023, aggregating P2,049,750.00, were not supported with certification that the official/employee did not use a government vehicle and was not assigned any government vehicle, moreover, various officials were paid with transportation allowances in full despite being assigned with government vehicles, a non-compliance to the requirements of Item 5.2 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 and a violation to Local Budget Circular (LBC) No. 103 and Annex B of COA Circular No. 2012-003, thus, the legality, validity, and propriety of the disbursements of TA cannot be established and resulting to overpayment of TA to various officials of the municipality.

The fidelity bonds of the accountable officers (AOs) were inadequate, as some of their collections and cash advances at a given time exceeded the maximum cash accountability. Additionally, one (1) AO was allowed to continue drawing cash advances and performing disbursing functions despite the expiration and non-renewal of his fidelity bond, contrary to Section 305(f) of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160 and Item 5.1 of Treasury Circular No. 02-2009. Thus, there is an increased risk that defalcations, shortages, and unrelieved losses of the AOs beyond the maximum cash accountability of the fidelity bonds might not be recovered.

The Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO) lacks proper control over the management of LGU’s collections, contrary to Section 69 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, Section 26 of COA Circular No. 98-382, and Sections 29 and 30 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual for LGUS, resulting in significant delays in collectors’ remittance of up to 211 days, deposits of collections of only four (4) times a month, increased the difficulty in the audit and verification of collections, and exposed the LGU’s funds to misappropriations or losses.

There were procedural errors, lapses, and improper presentation/recording of data in the cashbooks, which were not in consonance to the prescribed format and instructions as provided in the Forms and Annexes of Book II of the Local Treasurer Operation’s Manual (LTOM) 2nd Edition, thereby creating difficulties in the verification and tracing of collections and deposits, and cash-in-treasury balances cannot be immediately determined as of a given time.

Management’s inadequacy during the conduct of the preliminary study and detailed engineering stage, contrary to Items 1 and 2 of Annex A and Section 17.6 of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act (RA) No. 9184, resulted in delays in project implementation of up to 323 calendar days (CD), affecting the timely delivery of services to the constituents. Moreover, extensions of contract time were granted to contractors without sufficient documentation, contrary to Annex E of COA Circular No. 2009-001, thereby casting doubt on the validity of the time extensions granted.

One disbursement for equipment rental, amounting to P60,000.00, was not supported with complete documentation, contrary to Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445 and Annex N of COA Circular No. 2009-001; thereby, the legality, validity, propriety, and reasonableness of the disbursement cannot be determined.

The grant of honoraria to the officials and employees who are members of the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (MDRRMC), totaling P156,000.00 for the year 2023, was bereft of legal basis in violation of Section 4(1) of PD No. 1445, Section 30(a) of R.A. No. 7160, and Sections 3.1.1 and 4.7 of Local Budget Circular No. 62, thereby may fall under an illegal disbursement of government funds.

Two completed projects in the total amount of P16.753 million, funded out of the Bottom-up-Budgeting fund from Department of Interior and Local Government for the Quezon Water District are recorded as part of the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) of the Municipality, inconsistent to the provisions set under IPSAS 1, 17 and 23, thus, affecting the balances of the financial statements of the Municipality as of December 31, 2023.

Inclusion of the cost of the residential houses at Paglaum Village, in the amount of P6.476 million, as part of the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) account of the Municipality is not in accordance with paragraph 13 of IPSAS 17 and the COA Circular 2015-009, thus, affecting the financial statements of the Municipality as of December 31, 2023.

There were deficiencies noted between the inventory report and the records in the books of accounts of the Municipality for its vehicles and heavy equipment, a non-compliance to IPSAS 1 and IPSAS 17, thereby cast doubt on the correctness and reliability of the “Machinery and Equipment” and “Transportation Equipment” accounts under the Property, Plant and Equipment.

Absence of relevant documents to establish the transactions in the amount of P59.797 million recorded in Accounts Payable is not in accordance to Section 4 (6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, Section 157 Volume 1 of Government Accounting and Auditing Manual, and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby, precluding the auditor to validate the existence and validity of transactions and affects the accuracy of the financial statements as of December 31, 2023.

The LGU did not recognize the uncollected business taxes and stall rents in the total amount of P0.431 million as of December 31, 2023, which is not in consonance with Paragraph 14 of IPSAS 9 and Paragraph 106 of IPSAS 23, respectively, thus, corresponding receivable and income accounts were understated by P430,985.59.

Performance Securities totaling to P27.123 million did not adhere to the correct form and validity period contrary to Section 39.1 and Section 39.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR of R.A. No. 9184, thus, validity of the infrastructure project contracts could not be established, and faithful performance by the winning bidder of its obligations under the contract could not be guaranteed.

Four (4) contracts totaling to P1.636 million for the implementation of infrastructure projects were terminated contrary to Annex I of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of R.A. No. 9184 and Section 8.XV.C. of the Local Government Units (LGU) Procurement Manual, thus, validity of the four (4) new contracts could not be established, implementation of the priority development projects was unreasonably delayed, and the government was deprived from claiming liquidated damages due to such delay.

Thirty (30) infrastructure project contracts totaling to P73.957 million were not supported with complete documents and did not strictly follow the procedure for competitive bidding contrary to Paragraph 3.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-001 dated February 12, 2009 and the provisions of R.A. No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations. Thus, validity of the infrastructure project contracts could not be established.

Project billings totaling to P8.502 million were not supported with complete documents contrary to Section 4(6) of P.D. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2023-004 dated June 14, 2023, thus, validity and propriety of the disbursements could not be established.

Honoraria totaling P0.707 million were paid to various national and provincial government personnel assigned to the Municipality of Quezon for the Calendar Year 2023 contrary to pertinent provisions of R.A. No. 7160 clarified under DBM’s Compensation Policy Guideline No. 98-1 dated March 23, 1998, thus, casting doubt as to the propriety, legality, and validity of the payments.

The Municipality revised the programmed expenditure of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund for the calendar year 2023 by re-appropriating the amount of P1.319 million initially appropriated as maintenance and other operating expenses to capital outlay without the required Appropriation Ordinance covering a Supplemental Budget, not compliant to Section 1 of Administrative Order No. 47, thus, cast doubt as to the validity of the re-appropriation.

The Municipality failed to prepare and maintain complete and proper records of all Acknowledgement Receipt for Equipment (ARE) or Property Acknowledgement Receipt (PAR) for the issuances of its vehicles and heavy equipment, a non-compliance to Sections 142, 143 ,158, and 167 of COA Circular No. 98-386, which resulted to difficulty in the imposition of accountabilities.

Fund transfers totaling ₱53,500,000 from the Department of Interior and Local Government have no Memorandum of Agreement contrary to Section 3.1.2 of COA Circular 2021-001 dated June 14, 2012 and IPSAS 15; thereby creating difficulty in determining the responsibilities of the LGU and casting doubt on the propriety of its recognition as financial liability in the accounting records.

The Due to LGUs account of the Municipality of San Fernando to the Province of Bukidnon had various deficiencies contrary to Section 111 of the Presidential Decree 1445 of the Government Auditing Code of the Philippines and Section 29 paragraph 16 of the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) casting doubts on the Rights and Obligations, and correctness of records and resulting to a variance of P34,370,523.22 when compared against the Due from LGUs account of the Provincial Government.

The balance on the “Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants Inventory” on the Financial Statement of the calendar year 2023 and the ending balance provided by the General Service Office of the Municipality of San Fernando has a discrepancy amounting to P420,380.09 which is contrary to Section 111(1 &2) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 which casts doubt on the correctness of the financial statement balance of the aforementioned account.

Various deficiencies were found in relation to the Local Counterpart Contribution (KALAHI-CIDSS PMNP) totaling P3,053,492.00 contrary to COA Circular 2015-009 and the signed Sub-Project Agreement, thereby casting doubt on the fair presentation of the financial statements and the faithful compliance of the LGU of their roles expressed in the agreement.

The Municipality of San Fernando implemented a Low-Cost Housing Project totaling P961,650.00 with various deficiencies contrary to Sections 2 and 4(6 & 8) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and COA Circular 2015-009, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the implementation and distribution procedures of the project and the fair presentation in the financial statements.

The selected items on the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE – Equipment and other PPE) record with net book value totaling P 5,502,512.02 have already been distributed to Barangays for their use but are still in the accounts of the Municipality which is contrary to Paragraph 14 (a and b) of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 17 cast doubts on the fair presentation of PPEs in the financial statements.

The selected items on the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE - Buildings) record with net book value totaling P 7,829,148.66 have already been distributed to Barangays for their use but are still in the accounts of the Municipality which is contrary to Paragraph 14 (a and b) of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 17 cast doubts on the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The Municipality of San Fernando had various unidentified ‘TBD’ Property, Plant, and Equipment Assets totaling P32,222,983.07 without details contrary to Section 111 (1) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445; thereby casting doubt on the fair presentation of the PPE accounts in the financial statements.

Municipality purchased various parcels of land totaling P 6,462,355.00 with various deficiencies contrary to Sections 10, 12, & 13 of the Executive Order (EO) No. 1035, s. 1985 and 4 (6&8) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, and Sections 50 and 52 of the New Government Accounting System Manual for LGUs (NGAS for LGUs) thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the purchase of the land and the correctness and reliability of the accounting records.

A portion (6,369 sqm) of a parcel of land (16,444 sqm) with a market value of P434,991.00, was allocated for Housing Units a resettlement site for distribution, was not properly recorded in the accounting books which is contrary to the definition of Land and Property and Equipment for Distribution according to Annex B of COA Circular 2015-009 Prescribing the Revised Chart of Accounts for Local Government Units, Paragraph 11 of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 12 which results in the overstatement of PPEs and understatement of Inventories.

Various donated land properties with an approximate value of P1,092,420.00 were not record as Land contrary to Paragraph 14 (a & b) of IPSAS 17, thereby casting doubt on the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The supply and delivery of Construction Materials for the construction of the PNP (mobile force) Concrete Fence, Landscaping & Duty Post, costing P1,412,884.06, as compared to the actually erected project, Construction of PNP (Mobile Force) Building, with an Approved Budget for the Contract of P2,000,000.00 had various deficiencies contrary to Section 4.1, 4.8 of PD 1445 and Section 10 of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulation of RA No. 9184; thereby casting doubt on the validity and legality of the procurement process and raises skepticism on the effectiveness of the BAC.

Various government initiatives totaling ₱129,032,423.00 were extended beyond their target date of completion with lacking documentary requirements contrary to Section 11.1 and 11.5 of Annex “E” of the 2023 Updated Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 9184, thereby creating unnecessary risk for the projects under extended work duration and casting doubt on the validity of the approval of the work extension.

The project, Concreting of Farm to Market Roads in 24 Brgys @ 2Million/Barangay, with contract price of P47,815,792.68 by Angel and Sam Construction and General Merchandise had various physical dimensions variances when compared to the Program of Works of LGU San Fernando contrary to Section 2 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and the Definition of As Built Plans under DPWH Department Order 38, Series 2016; thereby casting doubt on the cost-effectiveness of payments made and declared accomplishments of the LGU.

The LGSF-SBDP project, Opening Concreting of Farm to Market Road at Barangay Little Baguio, San Fernando, Bukidnon, with a total contract price of P3,992,726.40 had physical deficiencies as compared to its approved Program of Works despite being declared as 100% complete contrary to Section 2 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445; thereby casting doubt on the cost-effectiveness of payments made and declared accomplishments of the LGU.

The Municipality of San Fernando failed to comply the lacking documents noted in relation to the auditorial/technical review of the returned project contracts with a total contract price of P78,248,292.86 contrary to Section 3.1.1 and 3.1.4 of COA Circular 2009-001; thereby creating difficulty in facilitating the completion of technical review and inspection by the COA-TSO.

Procurement of goods totaling P54,939,877.16 were not supported by warranty securities contrary to Section 62.1 of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act (RA) 9184, thereby resulting to risks of unattended manufacturing defects and/or possible contract breaches.

The Municipality erroneously charged expenditures relating to the Rehabilitation of the Executive and Legislative Building totaling P930,310.00 against the 20% Local Development Fund contrary to DBM-DOF-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 1 dated November 4, 2020; thereby casting doubt on the legality of the charged expenditure.

The Municipality of San Fernando granted cash advances totaling P10,668,204.99 with various deficiencies contrary to Sections 4(6) and 89 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the grant of cash advances.

The pre-printed ‘Totals’ figure in the Requests for Quotation of Forty-Eight (48) shopping transactions of the Municipality of San Fernando totaling P4,894,538.10 were equal to the lowest supplier quotation contrary to Volume 2 of the Manual of Procedures for the Procurement of Goods and Annex “H” of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act (RA) 9184, thereby casting doubt on the propriety of procurement process.

Various deficiencies were noted regarding the land property under TD No. 22-019-0013-00793 owned by the Municipality of San Fernando with a total market value of P1,406,023.00 contrary to Sections 2 and 4(2) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445; thereby casting doubt on the faithfulness of the management in its commitment to safeguard its assets and risking possibility of losing actual possession of the Land.

The Municipality of San Fernando does not regularly release wages of Job Orders on time as prescribed under Art. 103, Chapter III, Book III of the Labor Code, thereby adversely affecting the quality of life of Job Orders.

The final payments for infrastructure projects of the Municipality of San Fernando totaling P 4,753,612.12 have lacking documents which is contrary to paragraph 9.1.1.4 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 of June 14, 2012, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the final payments made for infrastructure projects.

Cash Assistances totaling P3,700,000.00 were distributed to beneficiaries with various deficiencies contrary to the Section 2 and 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, DSWD Memorandum Circular No. 06 Series of 2023, and the Signed Memorandum of Agreement; thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the implementation and release of the cash assistance to some beneficiaries.

Irregularities were found in the receipts and deposits of revenue collections which resulted to untraced and unaccounted income collections of approximately P1.187 million due to the lack of adequate internal control measures on the LGUs collection system that prevented the detection of irregularities, hence, created an avenue for fraud which may result to possible loss of government funds and income.

The balances of Intra-agency accounts “Due from Other Funds” and “Due to Other Funds” at year-end in the amount of P3.815 million and P1.460 million, respectively, remained unreconciled which resulted to a total variance of P2.355 million, a non-compliance to paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, thereby casting doubt on the correctness and reliability of the balances in the financial statements.

Cash advances totaling P0.308 million, granted to the Special Disbursing Officer, remained unliquidated at the end of CY 2023, contrary to Section 89 of P.D No. 1445 and pertinent provisions of COA Circular No. 2007-002, resulting to non-recognition of the related expenses in the proper accounting period, thereby understating the related expense accounts and overstating the assets of the LGU as of December 31, 2023 by a maximum amount of P0.232 million.

Cash advance for Confidential Fund amounting to P0.200 million remained unliquidated for a period of two (2) years, contrary to Section 89 of P.D No. 1445 and pertinent provisions of COA Circular No. 2007-002 and COA-DBM-DILG-GCG-DND Joint Circular No. 2015-01 dated January 8, 2015, resulting to non-recognition of the related expenses in the proper accounting period, thereby understating the related expense accounts and overstating the assets of the LGU as of December 31, 2023 by the same amount of P0.200 million.

The existence, completeness, and valuation of the Property and Equipment (PPE) account balance of P345.37 million as of December 31, 2023 could not be ascertained due to: a) the presence of unspecified/unidentified PPE items aggregating P61.885 million and (b) a discrepancy of P14.968 million between the balances per books of accounts and the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE) which are not in consonance with the provisions of Section 111(1) of PD No. 1445, IPSAS 17, and COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020.

The Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) account was misstated due to (a) various errors and lapses in the computation of accumulated depreciation, which overstated the Assets and Government Equity accounts by P2.465 million as a result of understated provision of depreciation by the same amount; (b) non-provision of depreciation to PPE accounts costing P10.978 million; and (c) non- provision of additional depreciation to and absence of Lapsing Schedules of PPE accounts with an aggregate cost of P36.34 million, which overstates the carrying amount of PPE by an unquantified amount, thereby, casting doubts on the accuracy and reliability of the reported carrying amount of PPE and the Government Equity accounts in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2023.

The validity and legality of reported Accounts Payable balance in the aggregate amount of P9.706 million could not be established due to the (a) presence of dormant accounts aggregating P0.57 million, (b) non-reversal of liabilities resulting to overstatement of various accounts by P3.628 million and (c) recording of liabilities in the absence of proof to warrant obligations totaling P1.613 million, which is not in consonance with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) No. 1 and Section 4(s), Volume I of the NGAS Manual, thus, affecting the true financial position of the municipality at the end of CY 2023.

Misstatements of Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) and related expenses totaling P2.932 million was found as a result of the inadequate accounting control and monitoring and inconsistencies in the recording of expenditures for various infrastructure projects which is not in conformity with the requirements of IPSAS No. 17, thereby understating the assets and overstating the expense accounts of the LGU as of December 31, 2023.

Misstatement of Trust Liabilities- DRRM and related assets accounts amounting to P1,619,388.00 was identified and material discrepancy was noted between the Report on Sources and Utilization of the DRRMF and the accounting records due to the non-reconciliation of the reports and non-maintenance of subsidiary ledgers, contrary to Sections 111 and 123 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, and Section 5.1.5 of COA Circular No. 2012-002, thereby creating doubt on the accuracy of both report and records and affecting the correctness and accuracy of the disclosure made in the Notes to Financial Statements.

The LGU failed to observe the frequency of preparation and submission of reports to identified offices relative to the Report of Sources and Utilization of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Fund (LDRRMF) for CY 2023 and the preparation of the LDRRMF Investment Plan/ LDRRM Plan (LDRRMFIP/LDRRMP) for the Special Trust Fund (STF) from CY 2020 to 2022, which is not in consonance with the various provisions under COA Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012, and the Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-01 of the NDRRMC, DBM and DILG dated March 25, 2013, thereby precluding the audit team in the assessment of the accuracy of the reports and the efficiency, propriety and validity in the utilization of the fund.

Purchase of copier machines totaling P423,776.00 were charged against the CY 2023 LDRRMF and Special Trust Fund despite not being related to Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) activities, contrary to the provisions of Republic Act No. 10121 otherwise known as “Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010”, NDRRMC-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2013-1 dated March 25, 2013, thereby resulting to improper utilization of said funds.

The Municipality incurred expenses in connection with the Benchmarking activity in Bacolod City and Legislative Inquiry in Manila in the aggregate amount of ₱0.865 million which were deficient of supporting documents and which may be deemed unnecessary pursuant to COA Circular No. 2012-003, DILG Memorandum Circular 2011-059 and DILG-DBM Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2 dated September 23, 2016.

Erroneous information was presented in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) and the Status of Appropriations, Allotments, Obligations and Balances (SAAOB) for CY 2023 for failure to disclose the correct amounts of obligation and unobligated appropriations for LDRRM-MOOE funds, materially deviating IPSAS 24, thus making the reports unreliable which would affect the rendition of auditor’s opinion on the prepared financial statement that would consequently affect the decision-making of its users.

The inadvertent accounting entries made by the Municipal Accounting Office relating to LDRRMF transactions and the non-maintenance of corresponding subsidiary ledger accounts under “Trust Liabilities- DRRMF” account are inconsistent with the specific provisions of NGAS Manual for LGUs and with COA Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012, resulting in the overstatement of accounts “Transfers of Unspent Current Year DRRM Funds to the Trust Funds” and “Subsidy from General Funds Proper/Special Accounts” presented in the Statement of Financial Performance for CY 2023 by ₱16.549 million and ₱11.995 million, respectively, and might affect the decision-making of the would-be users of the financial statements.

Proceeds from liquidated damages and bank interest income were lodged to Other Payables account under the Trust Fund (TF) books of accounts totaling ₱2.820 million, a non-conformance to some provisions of PD 1445, thereby affecting the reliability, accuracy and faithful presentation of certain balances presented in the financial statements for the period ending December 31, 2023.

Forty-eight (48) recorded parcels of land are not supported with Transfer Certificates of Title (TCTs) under the name of the LGU-Talakag but mostly by Certificates of Tax Declaration (CTDs) and with various noted deficiencies, contrary to the provisions of Section 148 of COA Circular No. 92-386, RA 7160, and IPSAS 17, thereby casting doubt in determining the right to ownership over its properties and potentially exposing the agency to litigation risk and tainting the fair presentation and disclosure of said account in the financial statements that might affect the decision-making of its intended users.

The agency failed to adopt timely disposal procedures for twenty (20) fully depreciated unserviceable heavy equipment and other motor vehicles with carrying amount totaling ₱4.370 million, a nonconformance to Section 79 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 92-386 prescribing the Rules and Regulations on Supply and Property Management in the Local Governments, hence, the municipality could have generated greater benefits in terms of higher appraisal value for the property, lesser storage cost, and better management of limited storage space. Moreover, the proceeds to be derived from the sale of such properties could be an additional funding to finance various priority programs and projects of the municipality. Additionally, the inclusion of these fully depreciated properties tainted the valuation of the Property, Plant and Equity account balance presented in the Statement of Financial Position as at December 31, 2023.

Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts with net carrying amount of ₱624.999 million were not subjected to one-time cleansing and with other noted observations, a non-conformance to COA Circular 2020-006 and NGAS Manual for LGUs, thus, the accuracy and existence of the PPE accounts presented in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2023 are doubtful and unreliable, thereby depriving the government of reliable and useful information in decision-making and accountability for these assets.

Various expenses totaling ₱84.458 million were misclassified to Other Maintenance and Operating Expenses account due to accounting treatments that are considered as departures from IPSAS and COA Circular 2015-09, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the account balances presented in the Statement of Financial Performance for the period ending December 31, 2023.

In CY 2023, the LGU Talakag improperly disbursed various additional allowances/benefits totaling ₱22.006 million to its municipal officials and employees, job order workers, barangay and SK officials and volunteers, and other personalities, contrary to RA 6758, RA 11466, House Joint Resolution No. 4, s. 2009, and Supreme Court jurisprudence, thereby casting doubt on the propriety, legality and validity of the disbursed transactions exposing the scarce government funds to improper disposition which could have been appropriated to other priority programs, projects and activities and may consequently warrant the issuance of audit disallowance.

Payments for legal services were incurred bereft of legal basis totaling ₱370,000.00, inconsistent with the specific provisions of Section 4 of PD 1445, COA Circular 2012-001, DBM’s Compensation Policy Guidelines No. 98-1, and RA 7160, thereby affecting the propriety, validity and legality of these transactions.

The municipality paid Hazard Pay and Subsistence Allowance to its MHO and MSWDO personnel with inadequate supporting documents and improper computations resulting in underpaid Hazard Pay for MSWDO personnel amounting to ₱69,502.87 and overpaid Subsistence Allowance for both offices amounting to ₱146,400, contravening COA Circulars Nos. 2012-001 and 2023-04, DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1 s. of 2018, and DBM-DOH JC No. 1, s. of 2012, as amended, thereby impairing the appropriateness and validity of the disbursed transactions and depriving the said personnel of the correct amount of benefits rightfully due to them.

The municipality still reimbursed communication expenses in the total amount of ₱1.169 million either treated as office supplies or telephone expenses, without an established internal guideline, and with improper/deficient documentation, while inclusive of the total amount are unnecessary payments for gadget cash-outs and other charges of at least ₱64,447.79, respectively, contrary to PD 1445 and pertinent COA circulars, thereby casting doubt on the reasonableness and regularity of these transactions and may warrant issuance of audit suspension or disallowance, as the case may be.

LGU-Talakag improperly paid monthly representation expenses in favor to the twenty-eight (28) members of the Liga ng mga Punong Barangay aggregating ₱245,500.00 without clear and definite legal basis, contrary to Section 4(1) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 4.2 of Local Budget Circular No. 63 dated October 22, 1996, hence, the audit team cast reservation on the propriety and validity of said disbursements.

RATA for OICs of regular positions were improperly paid/obligated on commutable basis rather than on reimbursable basis and with lacking documentary requirements, contradictory to DBM Local Budget Circular No. 103 and COA Circular Nos. 2012-001 and 2023-004, thus, affecting the propriety and validity of the disbursed transactions aggregating to ₱168,750.00.

The municipality failed to revert to the National Treasury the unutilized fund received from Bayanihan Grant to Cities and Municipalities (BGCM) in CY 2020 with reported cash balance of ₱452,965.04, on the account of the pending reconciliation with the records of the concerned offices as to the correct amount to be remitted, inconsistent with DBM Circular Letter No. 2021-13 dated December 31, 2021, thereby depriving the National Government of the timely usage of this fund to finance various priority programs and projects.

The hiring of job order workers were noted with various deficiencies, contravening Article 1305 of the Civil Code of the Philippines, CSC-COA-DBM JC No. 1, s. 2017, COA-DBM JC No. 2, s. 2020, and various DILG Legal Opinion, thus, the audit team cast reservation on the propriety of hiring job order workers, including the disbursements thereof made by LGU -Talakag.

The copies of perfected contracts were submitted delayed for 71 days in average and lacked basic supporting documents, contradictory to the pertinent provisions of COA Circular 2009-001, consequently precluded the audit team from undertaking the timely and relevant audit results on the propriety, legality and the technical aspect of the awarded contracts.

The City Accountant could not provide the breakdown/ details of the reverted accounts payable amounting P75,240,000.00 as the source of fund for Supplemental Budget No. 02 due to the non-availability of the accounting records from CY 2019 and below thus, noncompliant to Section 111 of PD 1445 hence, the validity of the reverted accounts payable could not be substantiated.

The City has Accounts Payable (A/P) from CYs 2020 to 2022 amounting ₱5,195,042.76 for salaries, wages, honoraria, salary differential, hazard pay, gratuity pay, year-end bonus, cash gift, and reimbursements of travelling expenses of several regular, casual and job order employees which are still outstanding as of December 31, 2023 due to improper booking and poor monitoring, in violation of Section 40, Book VI of the Administrative Code and Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-006 hence, the existence and validity of the A/P balance is doubtful.

The validity and accuracy of the Cash-in-Bank account amounting to ₱583,853,343.15 as of December 31, 2023 could not be relied upon due to: a) book reconciling items totaling to ₱98,089,818.4(additions) and ₱69,544,536.19(deductions) to book balances remained unadjusted at year-end; b) Prior-years’ deposits in transit with a total amount of ₱22,224,903.53 still not credited by the bank; and c) non-adjustment of stale checks totaling to ₱279,771.36 which were inconsistent with Section 74 and 112 of PD 1445, Sec. 3.3 COA Circular No. 96-011, and Sections 32 and 59 of the Manual on the New Government accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs.

The balances of the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts at year end totaling P4,196,736,456.76 did not reconcile with the balance of the Report on Physical Count of PPE amounting P2,482,451.047.19, in violation of Sections 58, 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and COA Circular 2020-006, making the balances of the accounts unreliable.

The Property, Plant, and Equipment Ledger Cards (PPLEC) contained incomplete and inaccurate details thus, noncompliant to Sections 114 and 120 of New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for Local Government Units, Sections 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 2020-006 which cast doubts on the accuracy and reliability of PPE accounts’ balances in the CY 2023 Statement of Financial Position.

The CY 2023 depreciation expenses totaling P27,149,041.24 pertaining to several Property, Plant and Equipment (PPEs) could not be ascertained since: a) beginning balances, loan proceeds, LGU equity and assets which do not meet the definition of PPE were subjected to depreciation, b) there were incomplete details such as date of acquisition, name and location of PPEs in the PPE ledger cards, c) only the name of the contractor/ supplier was indicated as the description of the PPE of the depreciation schedule and, d) various completed assets transferred from Trust Fund directly to equity and, furniture and fixtures were depreciated without breakdown, in contrary to the provisions of Section 13 of IPSAS 17 which rendered the CY 2023 Financial Statements as unreliable.

There were Seven Hundred Sixty-Two (762) recorded Property, Plant and Equipment totaling P15,599,428.90 with purchase costs below the P50,000.00 capitalization threshold, in contrary to COA Circular No. 2022-004, hence the PPE accounts’ balances were overstated by the same amount.

The existence, validity and accuracy of the reported Inventories’ balances amounting ₱152,462,982.40 could not be ascertained due to non-reconciliation between the records kept by the City Accounting Office (CAO) and the Report of Physical Count of Inventories by the City General Services Office (CGSO) with a variance totaling of ₱115,796,121.40, in violation of section 111 (2) of PD 1445, par. 44 of IPSAS No .12 and, sections 121, 122 and 124 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Vol. 1 thus, casting doubts on the accuracy and reliability of the Inventories presented in the CY 2023 Statement of Financial Position.

The Notes to Financial Statements did not provide adequate disclosures of the material and significant changes of account balances, contrary to the requirements of NGAS Manual and the pertinent disclosure requirements of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), thereby depriving the intended users of the effective understanding of the Financial Statements.

The City Accounting Office and City Budget Office did not install the COA e-NGAS and e-Budget systems after their training held last October 19 to November 4, 2021 thus, noncompliant to COA Circular No. 2004-007 hence, the LGU could not automatically generate the required financial statements and reports when immediately needed by the management and other users of information.

The CY 2023 Report on Utilization of Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund had the following errors/discrepancies: a) no breakdown of the continuing appropriation, b) undeducted trust fund expenses and, c) different unutilized balance compared to the balance in the trust fund books thus, non-compliant to Section 111 (2) of PD 1445, thereby casting doubt on the accuracy and reliability of the report.

The financial assistance for livelihood projects totaling to ₱800,000.00 granted by the City Government of Valencia to eight (8) NGOs/POs had various deficiencies in violation to Section 4(6) of PD 1445, COA Circular 2012-001, and the executed Memorandum of Agreements governing the transactions which casted doubt on the effectiveness and propriety of granted livelihood assistance.

The City Government of Valencia paid salaries to its regular employees amounting to ₱170,122,048.19 until September 2023 with various deficiencies on their supporting Daily Time Records (DTRs) which was noncompliant with Section 4 (6 & 7) of PD 1445, CSC Memorandum Circular No. 21, series of 1991 and Sec. 194 of the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual Vol. I, thereby casting doubt on the accuracy and validity of the salaries paid for that period.

Basic internal control on segregation of duties was not properly observed by allowing the HR department to handle both the creation of payroll and at the same time given the access to upload payroll data for the crediting of salaries and other employee benefits through Landbank weAccess for CY 2023 amounting to ₱491,254,403.58, which was not in accordance to Section 50 of the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual (GAAM) Vol III, and Internal Control Standards for the Philippine Public Sector (ICSPPS) prescribed under COA Circular 2018-003, thereby exposing the government funds to risk of possible losses and misappropriation.

CY 2023 Terminal Leave Benefits claims totaling P4,930,708.09 were incompletely supported with the required documents thus, noncompliant to Section 51.13 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 thereby casting doubt on propriety of the claims.

Employees who monetized fifty percent (50%) or more of their accumulated leave credits did not provide justification for their claims thus, non-compliant to CSC Memorandum Circular No. 16, s. 2002 and COA Circulars No. 2012-001 which cast doubt on the propriety of the claims.

CY 2023 procurements totaling ₱122,258,110.58 were unsupported with various required documents, in violation to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree 1445 and Republic Act 9184, thereby casting doubts on the regularity of the transactions.

Various goods procured by the City Government of Valencia totaling to ₱20,710,334.50 were paid without warranty security, in violation to Sec. 62.1 of RA 9184 which exposes the city to the risk and difficulty of recovering damages in case of defects on the procured goods.

The CY 2023 procured drugs and medicines totaling P5,376,620.13 were unsupported with the required documents prior to disbursement thus, noncompliant to COA Circulars No. 2012-001 and 2023-004, thereby casting doubts on propriety of the transactions.

All 100% completed projects with approved time extensions were not supported with the written consent of the bondsmen for the extension of the validity of the performance security, in violation of Section 39.5 and Section 11 of Annex E of the Revised IRR of R.A. 9184 thus, all performance securities for the faithful performance of the contractors’ obligations may not fully cover the approved time extensions.

Inaccurate and unreliable balances of the Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivable accounts were presented in the Statement of Financial Position at December 31, 2024 due to: (1) the non-reconciliation of financial reports versus the certified list of all real property tax delinquencies and (2) the ongoing inventory and unverified existence of real property units (RPUs), inconsistent with the provisions in Presidential Decree No. 1445 and NGAS Manual for LGUs, thereby overstating the RPT/SET receivables and deferred accounts by ₱6.527 million.

Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts could not be relied upon due to the following deficiencies: (1) two unrecorded items of Motor Vehicles costing ₱3.539 million; (2) still failed to conduct physical inventory resulting to non-submission of RPCPPE on some items of PPE; (3) still not subjected to one-time cleansing, and (4) still failed to update property tagging and Property Cards per category of PPE, a non-conformance to IPSAS 1 and 23, NGAS Manual for LGUs and COA Circular 2020-006, thus, the accuracy and existence of the PPE accounts presented in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024 aggregating ₱507.356 million are doubtful and unreliable, thereby depriving the government of reliable and useful information in decision-making and accountability for these assets.

The non-compliance to the accrual basis of accounting for insurance and fidelity bond premiums resulted in the overstatement of the Prepaid Insurance and Fidelity Bond Premium accounts by ₱206,894.99 and ₱122,023.22, respectively, contrary to IPSAS No. 1, Section 4.a of Vol. 1 of the Manual on NGAS for LGUs and the Revised Chart of Accounts for LGUs, thereby, casts doubt as to the accuracy and reliability of the figures of related accounts presented in the financial statements.

Financial assistance granted in CY 2023 to four barangays of the Municipality of Baungon totaling ₱4 million remained unliquidated despite project completion as of December 31, 2024 in contrast to the Memoranda of Agreement (MOA) between the Municipal Government of Baungon and said component barangays, therefore, proper utilization and timely implementation of the identified program, project or activity could not be determined while compromising the reliability of the financial statements by overstating Due from LGU and Equity accounts, aside from hindering the said barangays to receive any additional financial assistance for developmental projects.

The failure of the LGU management to properly account for, monitor, and document fuel transactions resulted in the unreliable reporting of the Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants Inventory balance of ₱2,668,717.00 and the Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants Expenses of ₱5,929,564.20, contrary to IPSAS No. 12, COA Circular No. 2015-009, and COA Circular No. 77-61, which casts doubt on the accuracy and reliability of the affected balances reported in the financial statements, as well as showing weakness of internal control employed by management on its fuel transactions.

Inventory accounts amounting to ₱10.666 million were not subjected to semestral physical inventory and with other noted observations, a non-conformance to NGAS Manual for LGUs, thus, the accuracy, reliability and existence of the Inventory accounts presented in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024 are doubtful and unreliable, thereby indicating a weak internal control on inventory management and depriving the government and would-be users of essential information for decision-making and accountability over these assets.

The Municipal Accounting Office failed to submit Disbursement Vouchers and General Journal accounts, including various Journal Entry Vouchers recorded in CY 2024, totaling ₱712.415 million, contrary to Section 347 of RA 7160 and Section 7.2.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009, thus, the propriety and legality of the transactions could not be ascertained and may affect the rendition of auditor’s opinion on the financial statements due to audit scope limitation.

The Municipality improperly granted honoraria for BAC and TWG members amounting to ₱456,000 with the following deficiencies: (1) ) incomplete supporting documents, (2) failure to adhere to the prescribed maximum honorarium rate per procurement project, and (3) lack of established internal rules and procedures in consideration of the attendance/participation of individuals in procurement activities and meetings involving competitive bidding, contrary to Section 4 of PD 1445, COA Circular No. 2012-001, and Section 4.0 and 5.3 of DBM Budget Circular No. 2004-5A, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the disbursed transactions.

Foreign travel-related expenses incurred during benchmarking activities in South Korea and Japan have various noted deficiencies totaling ₱1.447 million, contrary to DILG-DBM JMC No. 02, series of 2016, DILG MC No. 2022-147, EO No. 77, and COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby raising doubts as to the validity, propriety and regularity of the travel claims.

Foreign travel-related expenses incurred during LMP-Bukidnon’s Economic and Cultural Mission Tour in USA on September 12-25, 2024 have various noted deficiencies totaling ₱200,000.00, contrary to COA Circular Nos. 2012-01 and 2015-009, and AO No. 6 (s. 2017), hence, the validity, propriety and accountability over the disbursed government funds, including its judicious and prudent use, were not properly established and attained.

Meals and snacks served during regular sessions of the SB and other activities undertaken by the LGU-Baungon have various noted observations, inconsistent with PD 1445 and COA Circular Nos. 2012-003 and 2012-001, thereby raising doubts about the reasonableness and propriety of the disbursed transactions aggregating ₱1,008,460.00.

The Municipality granted Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) for the period August 2021 to July 2023 totaling 6,105,750.00 with various deficiencies contrary to the executed Memorandum of Agreement, DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01, DOH AO No. 2022-001 and Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, thereby creating doubt on the validity and propriety of the release of the HEA.

Confidential Fund (CF) amounting to ₱813,720.00 which is equivalent to its annual appropriation for calendar year 2024 was withdrawn once and not on a quarterly basis, contrary to the provisions of Section 6.1.5 of COA, DBM, DILG, GCG and DND Joint Circular No. 2015-01 dated January 8, 2015 which provides that cash advance for CF shall be limited to a three-month requirement, thus, casting reservation on the propriety and validity of the disbursed transaction which is also considered an “excessive” expenditure pursuant to COA Circular No. 2012-003.

The Municipality of Baungon failed to submit the semestral Procurement Monitoring Reports (PMR), Annual Procurement Plans (APPs) and Agency Procurement Compliance and Performance Indicator (APCPI) Results to the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) as mandated under Section 12.2 of the Revised IRR of RA 9184 and reiterated by GPPB Circular Nos. 03-2015 and 02-2020, hindering the GPPB’s ability to properly monitor the procurement activities of the municipality during the year.

The balance of the Cash in Bank – Local Currency, Current Account in the total amount of P1.651 billion is unreliable due to: (1) unadjusted reconciling items in a total (net) amount of P4.535 million in the books of accounts; and (2) the non-reversion of various unreleased checks aggregating P132.895 million to the cash in bank balance and incorrect recording of unpaid obligations identified as “outstanding ADA” aggregating P32.643 million contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1 and Section 3.3 of COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thereby affecting the accuracy, reliability, and correctness of account balance reported in the Financial Statements as at year end.

The Cash in Bank- Local Currency Savings Account and Interest Income were understated by P151.143 million and P1.144 million, respectively, and the Treasury Bills account was overstated by P149.999 million due to the non-recording of the receipt of the maturity value of the investments made, thereby affected the fairness of the presented account balances in the Financial Statements as of December 31, 2024.

The reported balance of the “Due from GOCCs” account aggregating P222.485 million cannot be relied upon due to the (i) significant discrepancy amounting to P67.946 million between the subsidiary records and the complementary detailed records; and (ii) presence of long outstanding receivables from GOCCs totaling P3.354 million which have remained unliquidated for approximately 4-11 years, thus, the amount reflected in the Province’s Financial Statements as of December 31, 2024 may not reflect the accurate value of the account.

An aggregate variance of P138.993 million was arrived at between the confirmed amount by the LGUs and the balances reported in the PGB’s year-end financial statements, which is not in conformity with pertinent Sections of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the balances of affected accounts presented in the financial statements as of December 31, 2024.

The accuracy and reliability of the Inventory accounts totaling P1.140 billion could not be verified and ascertained due to (i) the inability to conduct a physical count resulting to non-submission of the Report on the Physical Count of Inventories (RPCI); (ii) discrepancies in the reports of the custodians/end users; (iii) non-submission of monitoring and accountability reports of the custodians/end-users; and (iv) the presence of unidentified inventory items, contrary to Sections 111 and 123 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 and Section 124, Chapter 7, Volume 1 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS).

The balance of the “Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants Inventory” account in the Financial Statement at the end of Calendar Year (CY) 2024 does not accurately reflect the actual inventory levels due to the (i) presence of non-moving and unidentified lumped amount totaling P9.311 million; (ii) improper recognition of inventories and liabilities amounting to P3.218 million; (iii) accounting errors aggregating P0.564 million; and (iv) discrepancies between the SL balance and the confirmed balances stored at the gasoline stations as confirmed by the various offices of the Provincial Government amounting to P17.393 million, which are contrary to Section 111 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 casts doubt on the reliability and fair presentation of the Financial Statements.

The “Land” account balance as of December 31, 2024 is misstated due to the (i) non- recognition of unpaid obligations; and (ii) undervaluation of recorded parcels of land, contrary to existing standards and guidelines, which in effect, understated the “Land”, “Accounts payable” and other affected accounts by an estimated amount of P67.231 million, thereby affecting the accuracy, reliability, and correctness of account balances reported in the Statement of Financial Position as at year end.

The “Property, Plant and Equipment” account balances as of December 31, 2024, are misstated due to the (a) unrecorded donated properties with a value of at least P13.998 million; (b) undervalued PPEs items; (c) non-provision of depreciation on PPE items amounting P82.505 million; (d) improper recognition of PPE items arising from financial assistance to other LGUs aggregating P813.625 million; (e) unidentified PPE items in lump amounts and presence of negative book values totaling P42.702 million and (P0.309 million), respectively; (f) inconsistent classification of PPE items; and (g) non-completion of one-time cleansing reports and failure to conduct annual physical count of PPE. These are all contrary to existing standards and guidelines, thereby affecting the accuracy, reliability, and correctness of the account balances reported in the Statement of Financial Position as at year-end.

The balance of the Due to National Government Agencies (NGAs) account in the Trust Fund books as of December 31, 2024 is overstated due to the inclusion of P79.942 million, as liability for the funds received for the implementation of projects/programs/activities, which have been fully liquidated and the projects terminated due to the reversion of undisbursed funds to the National Treasury after the end of its validity period, thereby affecting the accuracy, reliability, and correctness of the account balances reported in the Statement of Financial Position as at year end.

Non-recording of revenue from uncollected rentals and non-forfeiture of rental deposits upon termination of lease contract amounting to P960,000.00 and P180,000.00, respectively, resulted in the understatement of “Rent Income”, “Accounts Receivable”, and “Government Equity” accounts and overstatement of the “Guaranty Security/Deposits Payable” account, contrary to the provisions of paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, paragraph 5 and 14 of IPSAS 9, and in the Contract of Lease thereby casting doubts on the completeness, reliability, accuracy and disclosures of the affected accounts in the Financial Statements.

Deficient documentations were observed to support the Contract Agreement executed for the PRDP Scale Up sub-project “Construction of Iba-Cabulohan- Paradise FMR” with a total project cost of P309,332,908.40.
