Moreover, inconsistencies in the “start date” and the provisions between the technical specifications and Program of Work was noted, thereby raising doubts on the management's preparation and review process of the approved POW, technical specifications, the contract agreement and its integral parts.

The balance of the “Accounts Payable” cannot be fully verified and validated due to the incomplete submission and documentation deficiencies upon recognition of liability across all funds totaling P30.615 million, contrary to the provisions of Section 347 of Republic Act No. 7160, Section 7.2.1.a of COA Circular No 2009-006 and Section 122 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, thereby casting doubts on the reliability, accuracy and the rights and obligations related to the Accounts payable in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024.

The PGB made payments for the purchase of Four (4) parcels of land totaling P55,252,714.68 net of tax and other assessment fees as of October 31, 2024, with lacking documentary requirements contrary to Section 4 (6&8) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 and Paragraph 13.1 COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby casting doubt on the completeness, validity, and propriety of the land purchased.

Deficiencies were found on the (i) bulk procurement and payments of staggered deliveries of diesel fuel; and (ii) mode of payments to various local fuel suppliers, contrary to Paragraphs 7, Appendix 22 of the Revised IRR for Republic Act (RA) No. 9184 dated April 15, 2024 and Section 88 of the Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 – Government Auditing Code of the Philippines, which cast doubt on the completeness, accuracy, propriety and validity of the transactions.

Inter-agency payables representing withheld taxes, monthly contributions and loan amortizations to Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF) / Pag-IBIG, and Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PHIC) aggregating P13,980,289.15 as of December 31, 2024 were not remitted in full within the prescribed period and there were delinquent repayments of loans and underpayment of premium dues with HDMF and GSIS, contrary to governing rules issued by the concerned National Government Agencies, thereby exposing the Provincial Government and the employees to the possible imposition of penalties and surcharges for the late remittance thereof.

Foreign travel expenses incurred in CY 2024 totaling P13.059 million were not completely supported with approved travel authority from the DILG and relevant documents specifically required by applicable DILG Memorandum Circular, COA Circular and pertinent provisions of Executive Order No. 77, thereby raising concerns on the validity, propriety, and regularity of the travel expenses.

The existence and accuracy of the PPE accounts, with carrying costs totaling ₱638.959 million, as presented in the CY 2024 financial statements, are doubtful due to: (i) an unreconciled cost amounts aggregating ₱677.391 million compared to the RPCPPE, which persisted because the LGU failed to utilize the one-time PPE account cleansing; (ii) the inclusion of 547 items costing below the PPE capitalization threshold of ₱50,000.00 in the RPCPPE totaling ₱10.832 million; and (iii) the conduct of physical count, preparation of the RPCPPE and reconciliation of records were not properly made, in violation of Sections 58, 111, and 112 of PD No. 1445, COA Circular No. 2020-006, and COA Circular No. 2022-004, thereby compromising the fair presentation of accounts, leaving property accountabilities unresolved and unaccounted for, and failing to safeguard assets against loss and misappropriation.

Seven completed PPE, used and/or occupied by the LGU and funded through the financial assistance of the PGB, with a total costs of ₱62.487 million, have not yet been recorded in the LGU’s books of accounts due to the absence of executed Deeds of Donation transferring ownership thereof, contrary to Section 111 of PD No. 1445 and the IPSAS No. 17, resulting in non-compliance with applicable accounting regulations and led to the understatement of the PPE accounts, Depreciation Expenses, and equity accounts by ₱51.331 million, ₱2.558 million, and ₱51.331 million, respectively.

The accuracy and existence of the “Receivable – Disallowances and Charges” account amounting to ₱1.838 million could not be ascertained due to lack of details, supporting schedules, and adequate disclosures in the financial statements contrary to Section 111 of PD No. 1445 and IPSAS No. 1, thereby affecting fair presentation of the account in the year-end financial statements.

The accuracy and reliability of depreciation expenses for several PPE items amounting ₱1.203 million could not be ascertained due to the absence of detailed information and itemized breakdowns in the depreciation lapsing schedule contrary to Section 111 of PD No. 1445 and Section 13 of IPSAS No. 71, thereby, casting doubt on the correctness of the net book value of PPE presented in the financial statements and impairing the fair presentation of the LGU’s financial position and performance.

Registration Fees for the Cultural Mission Tour at the USA and the Benchmarking Activity at Japan, totaling ₱0.620 million, were: (a) erroneously recorded as “Training Expenses” account, and (b) not properly substantiated by the required documents for foreign travel, contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009 and COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby rendered the propriety and reasonableness of the payment of registration fees doubtful, overstated the “Training Expenses” account by ₱0.620 million, and omitted Traveling Expenses – Foreign account in the year-end financial statements.

The LGU paid honoraria amounting to ₱0.336 million for services rendered by a part-time doctor holding a permanent position in another LGU, without the necessary authorization, contrary to Section 7(b)(2) of RA No. 6713, or the “Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees”, and Section 136 of Civil Service Commission (CSC) Resolution No. 1800692, or the “2017 Omnibus Rules on Appointments and Other Human Resource Actions (Revised 2018)”, thereby constituting double compensation and casted doubt on the propriety and regularity of the transactions.

The LGU disbursed “loyalty awards” or incentives totaling ₱0.140 million to fourteen (14) Barangay Tanods of various barangays, based on their length of service, anchored on Municipal Ordinance No. 2019-05, however both are inconsistent with DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2024-086 which requires that incentive and awards must be based on meritorious performance, thereby casting doubt on the regularity of the transactions.

The Municipality did not fully comply with the monitoring and reporting requirements related to the SEF, due to the delayed, undocumented and/or non-provision of copies of the CY 2024 Annual and Supplemental Budget to concerned LGU officials, and the non-submission of quarterly and annual SEF Utilization Reports to the DepEd, DBM, and DILG Regional Offices contrary to Item 6.1 DepEd-DBM-DILG JC No. 1, s. 2017, thereby undermining transparency and accountability in the use of SEF funds.

The agency failed to submit within the prescribed period its year-end financial statements and supporting schedules for CY 2024, in violation of Section 41(2) of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2010-001, thereby hindering the audit team to render a reasonable audit opinion on management’s assertions that the financial statements are free from material misstatements, whether due to fraud or error, in accordance with IPSAS and precluded the users from its timely and useful information.

The MTO reports all checks drawn on the RCI, even if not actually released to claimants, and the MACCO records the unreleased checks in the Check Disbursement Journal, which is contrary to Sections 42 and 43 of the MNGAS for LGUs; thus, it contributed to the delayed submission of DVs to the audit team and resulted in the understatement of the Cash in Bank account by P4,347,156.56, overstatement of receivables by P495,624.35, and understatement of liabilities by P2,169,680.98 of the CY 2024 financial statements.

The MSWDO failed to execute a contract between the municipal government and the SEA-Kaunlaran beneficiaries of capital assistance intended to be repaid, which totaled P990,000.00 for the years 2022-2024, in violation of Section 2 of PD No. 1445, thus weakening the enforceability of the intended repayments and limiting availability of funds to future beneficiaries. Moreover, the Municipal Accountant failed to disclose the transactions as required by IPSAS 19, which may result in the understatement of potential resources available to the municipal government.

Foreign travel-related expenses incurred during LMP-Bukidnon’s Economic and Cultural Mission Tour in the United States of America (USA) on September 12-25, 2024, totaling ₱400,000.00, had multiple deficiencies, contrary to Section 2 of PD No. 1445 and various provisions of EO No. 77, COA Circular Nos. 96-004, 2012-001, and 2015-009, and COA Resolution No. 2021-044; thus, the legality, validity, propriety, and accountability over the disbursed government funds were not properly established and attained.

The LGU paid monthly subsidies to punong barangays who are also receiving monthly honoraria from their respective barangays, totaling P132,667.80 for the period January to October 2024, in violation of Section 8, Article IX(B) of the 1987 Constitution; thereby, it casts doubt on the legality, validity, and propriety of the disbursements, as they may be tantamount to additional, double, or indirect compensation, and may warrant the issuance of audit disallowance.

Subsidies to Damulog Women’s Federation (DAWFED) and Persons with Disability (PWD) Federation Presidents, totaling P89,500.00 for the period January to October 2024, intended for food and/or transportation during federation meetings, were paid in the form of allowances and were not supported with complete documentation, contrary to Sections 4(6)-4(8) of PD No. 1445, thereby casting doubt on the legality, validity, and propriety of the disbursements.

Payments of various financial assistance and subsidies, totaling P732,500.00 for the period January to October 2024, do not adhere to the LGU’s established internal guidelines, sound management and fiscal administration, and were not supported with complete documentation, which is not in accordance to Sections 4(6) and 4(8) of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2012-003; thereby, casting doubt on the legality, regularity, validity, and propriety of the disbursements.

Disbursements for traveling expenses and registration fees, amounting to P860,750.00 and P1,156,896.00, respectively, for activities outside the province were noted with various deficiencies and inconsistencies, in violation of Section 3(a) of EO No. 77 and COA Circular No. 2012-003; consequently, the legality, validity, propriety, and regularity of these disbursements could not be established. Moreover, the improper accounting of cash advance refunds, contrary to the Revised Chart of Accounts for LGUs, resulted in an overstatement of expenses amounting to P29,600.00.

The Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO) failed to segregate cash receipts by fund, and improperly attached RCDs and other supporting documents to the appropriate JEVs. This is contrary to Annex 41 and Section 49 of Volume II of the MNGAS for LGUs and the Revised Cash Examination Manual; thereby, created difficulties in verifying and tracing the proper fund classification and accuracy of recording of cash receipts, as well as establishing the accountability and transparency of the cash receipts.

The classification of personnel under “Contracts of Service” does not align with the definition provided in COA-DBM JC No. 2, s. 2020, leading to confusion in the proper treatment and required supporting documents for payments. Moreover, payments to “Contracts of Service” and “Emergency Hires” were not supported with biometric-generated DTRs, accomplishment reports, and sufficient documentation, contrary to Items 1.1.1 and 1.2.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001; thereby, the transparency, necessity, validity, and propriety of the disbursements cannot be established.

Disbursements related to various artistic works, totaling P197,000.00, did not undergo with the required procedures provided in Annex H of the 2016 IRR of RA No. 9184 and were not supported with complete and sufficient documentation contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-001; thus, there is no assurance that the government obtained the most advantageous price or terms for the services, and the transparency, validity, and propriety of the disbursements cannot be established.

The attendance sheets, distribution sheets and activity designs attached to the disbursement vouchers for meals and food supplies, totaling P4,118,908.41 from January to October 2024, showed inconsistencies and deficiencies, contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-001 and Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445; therefore, the validity and propriety of the meals and food supplies cannot be established.

The non-specification of item descriptions in the LGU’s procurement documents for meals and snacks does not adhere to the principles of transparency, accountability, efficiency, and economy, contravening Sections 2 and 7.3.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA No. 9184; thereby, it creates possible ambiguity and misunderstanding between the supplier and the LGU, and undermines the integrity of the procurement process.

Semi-expendable properties in the total amount P931,299.00 and P988,203.02 were not supported with Inventory Custodian Slips (ICSs) and were improperly recorded as part of Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts, respectively, a non-compliance to Paragraph 4.1 of COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022, which resulted to difficulty in identifying the accountable person for the semi-expendable properties and an overstatement of the PPE account of the Municipality as of December 31, 2024.

Collections from the spring resort operations of the LGU totaling to ₱1,012,405.00 were recorded in the Trust Fund under the Due to LGUs Account contrary to Section 313 of the Local Government Code (LGC), resulting to misstatements on the recorded collections in the General Fund and Trust Fund cashbooks of the Municipal Treasurer, deposits of General Fund collections in the Trust Fund bank account, and overstatement of the Due to LGUs Account in the Trust Fund totaling to ₱207,734.14.

Various receipts without specific purpose totaling to ₱543,698.66 were treated as receipts with specific purpose and recorded in the Due to LGUs account of the LGU contrary to Sections 305(d) and 308 of the Local Government Code (LGC), thus, income earned from these receipts were not recorded in the General Fund, cash received were not included in the unappropriated surplus of the LGU, and subsequent disbursements against the receipts were made without valid appropriations.

Financial transactions not related to the LGU’s liability to other LGUs were recorded in the Due to LGUs account contrary to the proper account classifications prescribed under COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, resulting to the following misstatements:

Non-identification of specific projects/programs and improper and erroneous recording of disbursements funded out of the 20% Development Fund were not compliant to Section 4 (7) and (8) of PD 1445 which resulted to inclusion of non-capitalizable expenditure totaling P357,155.85 and difficulty in reconciling the obligations against recorded assets amounting to P5,029,331.00 which cast doubt as to the correctness of the Property, Plant, and Equipment Account.

Completed programs, projects, and activities, dormant/unreconciled balances exist under the Due to LGUs account of the LGU totaling to ₱2,875,986.60, ₱769,173.12 of which was recorded in the General Fund while the remaining ₱2,106,813.48 was recorded in the Trust Fund, contrary to the Par. 22 of IPSAS 19, thus, fairness of presentation of the account in the consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024 could not be established.

Recording of the receipts and transfer of the Share from the Internal Revenue Collection in the General Fund Proper to the Special Account in the General Fund - 20% Development Fund was not in accordance with Volume 1 of the Manual on New Government Accounting System which resulted to an overstatement of the accounts “Subsidy to Other Funds” and “Subsidy from Other Funds” in the amount of P42,833,891.00 in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Performance of the Municipality for the calendar year ended December 31, 2024.

Advance payments of Special Education Tax (SET) were recorded in the General Fund contrary to Sections 235 and 310 of the Local Government Code (LGC), thus, the advance SET collections for CY 2024 totaling to ₱1,026,626.16 were erroneously deposited in the bank account of the General Fund. Moreover, the Due to Other Funds account in the General Fund is understated by ₱1,026,626.16 while the Deferred Special Education Tax and Due from Other Funds account in the Special Education Fund are understated by the same amount. Finally, an unidentified account in the General Fund may be misstated by ₱1,640,544.99.

The Municipal Treasurer and the Municipal Accountant did not follow the correct accounting procedures in recording real property and special education taxes, discounts, and penalties contrary to Sections 20, 22, 23 and 64, Chapter 3 of The New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual, resulting to unrecorded discounts totaling to ₱147,767.04 and unrecorded penalties totaling to ₱73,130.06 while fairness of presentation of the Real Property Tax Receivable and Special Education Tax Receivable both amounting to ₱4,118,874.40 as well as Deferred Real Property Tax and Deferred Special Education Tax amounting to ₱7,876,459.05 and ₱6,490,340.82, respectively, could not be established.

The imposition of the public cemetery fees and charges was not equitably applied to all individuals contrary to Section 130(b)(1) of the Local Government Code of 1991, thus, unpaid balances exist totaling to ₱7,100,600.00. Moreover, The LGU did not follow the correct accounting treatment for receipts of various public cemetery fees and charges, which is not in consonance to Paragraphs 19 and 28 of IPSAS 9, thus, uncollected receivables totaling to ₱5,500,600.00, revenues totaling to ₱2,250,600.00, unearned income totaling to ₱3,250,000.00, and cost of goods sold were not recognized while operating expenses were not properly segregated under the General Fund.

The Municipality disbursed the appropriation for “Other Maintenance and Operating Expenses” in the total amount of P23,435,794.90 without the required prior Sanggunian Authorization, a non-compliance to section 22 (c ) and 336 of RA 7160, thus, the legality of the disbursements cannot be established.

The disbursements for repairs and maintenance of government vehicles and equipment in the total amount of ₱2,514,899.12 is not compliant to Section 9.1.3.4 of COA Circular 2012-001 and operating procedures provided under Chapter IV of the Training Handbook on Property & Supply Management System, thus, cast doubt as to the validity and propriety of the disbursements and adequacy of the internal control for the same.

Procurement of Supplies and Materials in the total amount of ₱4,282,940.46 for the implementation of various programs, projects, and activities of the LGU were not in accordance with RA 9184 and its IRR, resulting to ineffective and inefficient procurement activities and doubt exist as to the validity and regularity of the disbursements.

Disbursements for meals and snacks in the total amount of ₱4,865,813.86 were not properly and completely supported with required information and documents, inconsistent with the provisions of PD No. 1445, thus, the legality and validity transactions cannot be established.

Deficiencies were noted in the appointments and payrolls of job orders in the total amount of ₱24,035,278.01 a non-compliance to CSC-COA-DBM Joint Circular No.1, s. 2017, and COA Circular 2012-001, thus, cast doubt as to the accuracy, validity and appropriateness of the disbursements.

Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) items that were found to be non-existing/missing and with identified accountable persons, in relation to the conduct of the “One-time Cleansing” activity totaling P2,715,652.00, were still included in the year-end balances due to incomplete implementation of the required procedures and which information were not accordingly disclosed in the Notes to the Financial Statements, contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2020-006, thus, rendered the accuracy, reliability and faithful presentation of balances reflected in the Financial Statements as of December 31, 2024 doubtful.

The accuracy of the Cash in Bank accounts cannot be relied upon, in view of the following deficiencies, to wit, (a) delayed submission of Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS); (b) stale checks still included as bank reconciling items under outstanding checks aggregating to P110,795.33 and (c) presence of unadjusted long-standing book and bank reconciling items, all contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445, COA Circular No. 96-011, and the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for LGUs, thus affecting the reliability of the Cash in Bank account and casting doubt on the amounts presented in the Financial Statements for as of December 31, 2024.

Procedural errors that occurred in the preparation of the year-end financial reports led to misstatements in the individual accounts in the Statement of Financial Performance, the understatement of the ending Cash and Cash Equivalents in the Statement of Cash Flows, both by a total P12,212,891.62, and finally erroneous information presented in the Notes to Financial Statements, all inconsistent with Section 111 of P.D. 1445 and Section 19 of IPSAS 1 - Presentation of Financial Statements, thus, casting doubt as to the reliability and accuracy of the figures presented in the Financial Statements for CY 2024.

The accuracy and reliability of Accounts Payable as of year-end could not be ascertained due to the inclusion of recorded payables amounting to P8,681,696.15 with only a List of Accounts Payable as supporting document, inconsistent with the principles mandated in PD No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’, the Administrative Code of the Philippines and the New Government Accounting Manual System (NGAS) for Local Government Units, thus casting doubt as to the existence and validity of the reported Accounts Payable in the Financial Statements as of December 31, 2024.

The CY 2024 year-end balances of the accounts “Due to GSIS” and “Due to Pag-IBIG” amounting to P2,672,830.87 & P635,673.87 respectively, could not be relied upon, in view of the following deficiencies noted, to wit, (a) existence of variances in the monthly deductions and remittances ranging from P1,890.41 to P2,557,168.25; (b) payments for premiums and loan amortization refunds which were not attached with complete supporting documents; and (c) the “Due to Pag-IBIG” account for Job Order Employees containing a negative beginning balance of P341,664.22, all contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’ and the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual thus causing inaccurate monthly balances in the related accounts, and non-reconciliation of the intra-agency transactions, inability to ascertain the legality, propriety and validity of the disbursements, and moreover, casts doubt on the reliability and accuracy of the figures presented in the financial statements.

The manner of recording transactions under the account Due to PhilHealth is deemed insufficient in view of (a) the existence of variances in the monthly deductions and remittances aggregating P277,330.00; (b) delayed transfers to the General Fund of intra-agency liabilities involving PhilHealth deductions with a total amount of P636,857.17 and (c) unrecorded remittance amounting to P277,387.05, all inconsistent with the principles mandated in PD No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’ and the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual, thus causing inaccurate monthly balances in the related accounts, non-reconciliation of the intra-agency transactions and moreover, casting doubt on the propriety, existence, accuracy of the amounts presented in the Financial Statements.

The Municipality has not consistently complied with the applicable BIR withholding tax regulations and accounting principles in view of the noted deficiencies and procedural errors in relation to the withholding and remittance of taxes on compensation, all inconsistent with PD No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines and the relevant BIR Revenue Issuances, thus exposing the Agency to possible penalties that might accrue in view of the possible under/non remittances, compromising the operations of the GF’s Programs, Projects and Activities in view of the utilization of its cash for tax liabilities of other funds with no transferred cash yet and moreover, casting doubt on the propriety, existence and accuracy of the “Due to BIR” and Intra-Agency accounts as of December 31, 2024.

The procedures employed by the agency in the grant of Hazard Pay is deemed non-compliant with relevant rules and regulations in view of the following: (a) grant of Hazard Pay to Public Health Workers (PHWs) using criteria which were declared invalid and (b) payment of Hazard Pay to Public Social Workers (PSWs) and Public Health Workers (PHWs) with incomplete supporting documents, all inconsistent with Presidential Decree No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’, DBM-DOH Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2016 , DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2018 , COA Circular No. 2012-001 and COA Circular 2012-003 , thus casting doubt as to the validity and propriety of the said disbursements and further, may render the same irregular and be subjected to audit suspension or disallowance, if warranted.

The procedures being employed by the agency in its Cemetery Operations is deemed insufficient in view of the following: (a) inconsistent application/implementation of the cost of cemetery products/services; (b) non-presentation/non-filing/non-preparation of copies of Burial Contracts and Certificates of Ownership of fully paid cemetery products/services as well as the non-maintenance of a systematic and orderly record keeping process and (c) non-functioning of the office designated to exercises supervision and administration over cemetery operations, all inconsistent with Municipal Ordinance No. 2019-026 or the Don Carlos Public Eternal Garden Ordinance, thus affecting the efficiency of cemetery revenue collection, exposing the agency to disputes on ownership rights/details and rendering ineffective the management of the cemetery operations of the Agency.

The procedures employed by the Agency in accounting and reporting related to the Local Risk Reduction and Management Fund are deemed non-compliant with the related rules and regulations in view of the following deficiencies noted, to wit: a) non-submission of the monthly Report on the Utilization of Disaster Risk Reduction & Management Fund to the COA Auditor on or before the 15th day of each month and b) failure to prepare the Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Fund Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP) for CY 2024 in the prescribed format, all inconsistent with RA No. 10121 and COA Circular No. 2012-002 , thus, preventing the Audit Team from timely reviewing the disbursements charged to the LDRRMF and depriving the intended users of the LDRRMFIP from the information provided by the prescribed format.

The (a) non-conduct of complete physical count of its PPE for CY 2024; (b) presence of bulk acquisitions without specifying quantities aggregating P0.260 million in Net Book Value (c) inclusion of doubtful PPE items with a total Net Book Value of P1.052 million; and (d) erroneous and unreliable computation of Accumulated Depreciation which are not in consonance with COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020, COA Circular 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022 and Section 13 of the International Public Sector Accounting Standards, affected the reliability of the reported Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts as of December 31, 2024 with book value of ₱994.624 million as existence and accuracy thereof could not be ascertained, affecting the fairness of presentation of the PPE accounts in the financial statements.

The LGU did not submit the required Report on the Physical Count of Inventories (RPCI) as mandated by Section 124, Chapter 7 of LGU NGAS Manual, hindering the verification of the existence and condition of the inventories totaling P114.866 million as of December 31, 2024, affecting the accuracy of the LGU’s reported balances.

Completed projects from prior years totaling P94.899 million, funded through conditional fund transfers, erroneously recognized as completed only in CY 2024 were recorded as a direct debit to Government Equity instead of being routed through the Prior Period Adjustment account and was not accompanied by the necessary disclosures, contrary to Paragraph 54 of IPSAS 3 and Annex “B” of COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The LGU recorded in its Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts a total of P48.134 million representing previously unrecorded Construction in Progress (CIP) without complete supporting documents, contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, thus, the validity, accuracy, and reliability of the recording could not be ascertained, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The LGU did not recognize revenue upon fulfillment of the conditions attached to the P17.640 million fund transfers, contrary to Paragraph 44-45 of IPSAS 23 which requires revenue recognition when conditions are satisfied, thereby, understating its revenue account by the aforementioned amount.

Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants of the LGU totaling P15.014 million was still carried in the inventory despite absence thereof due to delayed submission of fuel consumption reports, contrary to the definition of asset per Paragraph 7 of IPSAS 1, thereby overstating the Fuel, Oil and Lubricants Inventory account by the same amount.

Uncollected taxes initially recorded under Real Property Tax Receivable and Special Education Tax Receivables totaling P14.952 million were closed at year-end, contrary to the Modified Accrual accounting policy prescribed by the NGAS and to Paragraphs 59–60 of IPSAS 23, resulting in the understatement of receivables and deferred real property and special education tax by the same amount in the LGU’s financial statements as of December 31, 2024.

The inefficient inventory management of the LGU due to the absence of a dedicated property or supply management unit, resulted in a decentralized and ineffective control system that contravenes the supply and property management standards outlined in Sections 116 to 124, Chapter 7, Volume I of the NGAS for LGU, leading to unclear accountability and the non-recording of property consumption/ distribution amounting to at least P9.599 million, understating the inventory balance by at least the said amount.

The LGU’s erroneous recording of (a) the receipt of unspent CY 2023 DRRMF amounting to P7.777 million as a credit to the “Transfers from General Fund of Unspent DRRMF” account instead of the “Trust Liability – DRRM” account, and (b) the disbursement of P2.138 million as a debit to the same revenue account and P1.494 million to the “Trust Liability – DRRM” account—without appropriately crediting the “Transfers from General Fund of Unspent DRRMF” account—contrary to the provisions of COA Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012, resulted in the overstatement of the “Transfers from General Fund of Unspent DRRMF” account by P2.006 million and the understatement of the “Trust Liability – DRRM” account by P5.639 million.

The (a) non-reclassification of semi-expendable properties to the appropriate accounts, with a Net Book Value of ₱5.027 million, along with the (b) non-maintenance of prescribed forms and the (c) non-conduct of physical count, contrary to COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022, resulted in the overstatement of the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) account by the same amount, and cast doubt on the reliability of the reported semi-expendable properties, as their existence and accuracy could not be ascertained, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The Reconciliation between the ‘Actual Amounts’ in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) for the year ended December 31, 2024 showed amounts of ‘entity differences’ without the proper disclosures required under Paragraphs 7 and 46 of IPSAS 1 and Paragraphs 14, 39 and 47 of IPSAS 24, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the Notes to Financial Statements (NTFS) and the SCBAA.

A total of P0.608 million procured thru Direct Retail Purchase was erroneously recorded under the Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants Inventory account, contrary to the IPSAS Description of Accounts, thereby overstating the said account as of December 31, 2024.

A foreign travel-related expense amounting to ₱160,000.00 was erroneously recorded under the Membership Dues and Contributions to Organizations account instead of the appropriate Travelling Expenses – Foreign account, contrary to the account classification prescribed under Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015 due to the absence of adequate control mechanisms in the posting process, thereby overstating the former and understating the latter account in the financial statements.

Fuel consumption recorded in CY 2024 amounting P12.476 million representing current and prior year consumptions, respectively, lacked the necessary data and documents required per COA Circular No. 75-6 dated November 7, 1975, thereby affecting the transparency, validity, and proper authorization of the said expenses.

Fuel, Oil and Lubricants procured by the LGU through public bidding amounting to P10.429 million were paid in full despite the LGU’s insufficient capacity to receive and stock the same, contrary to Section 88 of PD 1445 and paragraph 9.1.3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, thus, may indicate irregular disbursement.

The LGU’s procurements of Petroleum Fuel, Oil, and Lubricant (POL) products through Direct Retail Purchase, totaling P1.032 million were found to have documentary deficiencies contrary to the pertinent provisions of RA 9184 and GPPB Resolution No. 24-2019 dated October 30, 2019, which may have undermined the competitiveness, transparency, and overall integrity of the procurement process.

Foreign travel expenses incurred in CY 2024 totaling P0.672 million were not completely supported with the relevant documents specifically required by applicable DILG Memorandum Circular, COA Circular and pertinent provisions of Executive Order No. 77, thereby raising concerns on the validity, propriety, and regularity of the travel expenses.

The non-maintenance of inventory subsidiary ledger cards of the LGU contrary to Section 114 and 120, Chapter 7, Volume I of the NGAS for LGUS, resulted in the inability to accurately track and reconcile inventory items, quantities and costs, undermining the reliability of inventory records and compromising the integrity of the LGUs financial reporting.

The LGU granted Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) to Health Care Workers and Non-Health Care Workers for the period covering CYs 2021-2023 totaling P11.459 million without complete supporting documents, contrary to DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01, DOH AO No. 2022-001, and DOH AO No. 2022-039, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the payment.

(a) LGU counterpart amounted to ₱ 1.5 million granted to Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) - Bukidnon Second District Engineering Office in calendar year 2024 was expensed outright in contrast to COA Circular No. 2015-009; (b) LGU counterparts granted to Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) - Bukidnon Second District Engineering Office in years 2015 and 2021 totaling to ₱ 4.25 million remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2024 in contrast to Section 4.6 of COA Circular No. 94-013 therefore, affecting the financial statements of the LGU as of December 31, 2024 and the proper utilization and timely implementation of the identified or specific program, project or activity could not be determined.

Thirty-five (35) units of residential houses at Kadingilan Paglaum Village were accounted as part of “Buildings” account in the books of accounts of the LGU contrary to paragraph 13 of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 17 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby, affecting its Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024.

Six (6) old structures owned by LGU-Kadingilan that were demolished in CY 2024 with a total acquisition cost of ₱ 5.228 million were not derecognized in its books of accounts contrary to Section 62 of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 45, thereby, affected the fair presentation of the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024.

Completed trust fund project entitled “Concreting of Roads from Poblacion to Salvacion, Kadingilan, Bukidnon” amounted to ₱ 14.995 million remained in the “Construction in Progress – Infrastructure Assets” account and was not reclassified to “Road Networks” account as of December 31, 2024 contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby, the accuracy and reliability of the affected accounts could not be ascertained.

Twelve (12) unserviceable properties and three (3) missing equipment, claimed to be disposed by management, with total acquisition costs of ₱ 15.1 million and ₱ 2.7 million, respectively, were still carried in the books of accounts of the LGU contrary to Sections 379 of Republic Act No. 7160, thus, the “Construction and Heavy Equipment” and “Motor Vehicles” accounts did not accurately reflect the actual serviceable properties of the Municipality and the total assets and total equity were overstated as of December 31, 2024.

The Municipal Engineer missed to immediately notify COA about the damaged four-wheel service vehicle (pick-up truck) with an acquisition cost of ₱ 1.5 million directly accountable to him after it met an accident and missed to present his application for relief of accountability with the required supporting documents within the reglementary period of 30 days from its occurrence in contrast to COA Circular No. 1992-751, thereby, he was not relieved of his liability for the loss or damage of the LGU’s property.

The Local School Board (LSB) was not fully compliant with the reporting requirements for the Special Education Fund (SEF), as indicated in Section 6.1 of the DepEd-DBM-DILG Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2017, thereby undermining transparency and accountability in the allocation and utilization of the SEF.

The 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) was utilized for COVID-19-related expenses amounting to ₱ 1,046,245.00 despite the cessation of the State of Calamity in the Philippines, contrary to Section 6.0 of DILG-DBM Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1, s. 2020, and resulting in an irregular disbursement.

The purchases of Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricant by the agency totalling ₱ 5.195 million were procured through negotiated procurement and at a less advantageous price due to the non-utilization of available data for the prevailing retail-pump price from the Department of Energy contrary to Appendix 22 of the Revised IRR of RA 9184 dated October 15, 2023, thus, resulted in an initially computed overpayment to the suppliers amounted to ₱ 325,732.70.

Payment of terminal benefits to four (4) retirees which aggregated to ₱ 2.412 million were not properly and completely substantiated with documentary requirements inconsistent to Section 5.13 of COA Circular No. 20212-001, hence, the propriety, validity and legality of the disbursements could not be ascertained.

The storekeeper of the Municipal Food Terminal who received its sales revenue was not bonded and missed to issue official receipts to its buyers in contravention to Sections 21 and 23 of the Revised Cash Examination Manual, thereby, the propriety, accuracy and reliability of the “Sales Revenue-Municipal Food Terminal” account amounted to ₱ 213,541.00 for the year ended December 31, 2024 could not be ascertained and highly exposed the public funds to possible cash misappropriation or, worse, theft.

Municipal officials and employees were paid travel allowances for foreign travel totaling ₱ 2,465,640.00 without the approval from the DILG and clear-cut computation of the daily subsistence allowance contrary to Section 4.3 of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2022-147 dated November 22, 2022, and Section 14 of Executive Order No. 77 thus raised doubts as to the validity, propriety, and regularity of the travel claims.

Foreign travel-related expenses incurred by the agency amounting to ₱365,335.00, have various noted deficiencies, contrary to DILG MC 2022-147, DILG MC 2019-83, EO 77 and COA Circular 2012-001, hence, the validity, propriety and regularity over the disbursed government funds, including its judicious and prudent use, were not properly established and attained.

Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) amounting to ₱ 5,703,812.50 for the period August 2021 to November 2022 was granted by the LGU in CY 2024 with various deficiencies contrary to the executed Memorandum of Agreement, DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01 and Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, thereby creating doubt on the validity and propriety of its release

Non-recording and proper monitoring of breeding stocks received from Department of Agriculture is inconsistent with Section 2 of PD 1445 and Memorandum of Agreement entered into by and between the Municipality of Kalilangan and the Department of Agriculture Regional Field Office 10 (DA RFO 10), thereby, created risks of assets that may deprive other constituents of future benefits and doubts as to the reliability of the balances of the “Breeding Stocks” account shown in the financial reports of the LGU as of December 31, 2024.

Various deficiencies related to Food Supply transactions in CY 2024, such as (1) non-attachment of Acknowledgement Receipts (AR) and list of beneficiaries, (2) mismatched supporting documents to transaction vouchers, and (3) late recording of expenses, contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-001 and Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445; therefore, the correctness, validity, and propriety of recorded “food supply expense cannot be established.

Irregular procurement of Fuel Oil and Lubricant (FOL), inconsistency in the documentation of the actual withdrawal of FOL to align the details with the mode of delivery indicated in the contracts and purchase orders, improper recording of FOL inventory, and erroneous entry of recording FOL expense deviate from GPPB Resolution No. 26-2019, COA Circular No. 2012-001, and Section 111 (2) of PD 1445; thus, they are considered irregular and cast doubt on the reliability of FOL expense and inventory account balances as of December 31, 2024.

The recording of expenses upon the transfer of custody of drugs and medicines inventory and medical, dental, and laboratory supplies inventory from General Services Office (GSO) to the Municipal Health Office deviates from Section 4 (5 & 8) of PD No. 1445; therefore, the correctness, validity, and propriety of recorded “Drugs and Medicines Inventory, and Medical, Dental, and Laboratory Supplies Inventory” and its related expenses both as of December 31, 2024 cannot be established.

The monthly remittances of taxes withheld, premium and loan payments, and other mandatory deductions from all Special Accounts maintained under General Fund (GF), including other funds such as Special Education Fund (SEF) and Trust Fund (TF) accounts, were remitted on a monthly basis to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Pag-IBIG, and Philhealth using the Funds from the GF Proper account; however, no definite timeline for actual cash fund from these funds were transferred to GF, which is not in consonance with Sections 2 of Presidential Decree (P.D.) No. 1445, thus may disrupt the smooth operations/implementation of the scheduled projects, programs, and activities (PPAs) under the GF Proper account.

The Municipality has substantially complied with the rules and regulations on the monthly premium contributions and loan amortizations of its personnel and remittance thereof to the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF)/Pag-IBIG, and Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth), respectively. However, the following exceptions were noted, to wit: (a) remittance of the full amount of withheld funds was not consistently observed; (b) clerical errors in payroll preparation; (c) an un-updated GSIS portal; and (d) an outdated HDMF and PhilHealth remittance master file, contrary to the provisions of R.A. No. 8291, Section 3 of the IRR of R.A. No. 9679, and Section 19 of the IRR of R.A. No. 7875, which resulted in the accumulation of unremitted balances under the Inter-Agency Payables accounts as of December 31, 2024.

Disbursements for CY 2024 salaries, PERA, and RATA paid to employees and elected officials were not properly supported due to lacking daily time records, certification from the HRMO of the posting of deductions to individual leave ledgers, non-attachment of travel documents for out-of-office duties, and attendance sheets on Sanguniang Bayan’s regular sessions, which is inconsistent with item 6 of section 4 of PD 1445 and section 1.2.1 of COA Circular 2012-001, thus casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the payments.

Leave applications of employees without leave balances were approved by the management with pay and excessive Special Privilege Leave which is inconsistent with item 8 of section 4 of PD 1445 and the Omnibus Rule on Leave, thereby resulting in irregular transactions and creating doubt of the reliability in the affected expense accounts.

Procurement of Common-Use Supplies and Equipment (CSE) and Inventory Items was delayed for an average of 59 days compared to the scheduled timeline in the Annual Procurement Plan (APP), due to late transmittal of Project Procurement Management Plans (PPMPs), differences in the PPMP format used by different offices, erroneous entries in the PPMP, and the false presumption of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) secretariat, which deviates from the Budget Operations Manual (BOM) for Local Government Units (LGUs) and Section 4 (4) of PD 1445, resulting in inefficient utilization of government funds.

Foreign travel-related expenses incurred during LMP-Bukidnon’s Economic and Cultural Mission Tour in the United States of America (USA) on September 12-25, 2024, and VMLP-Bukidnon’s Benchmarking Activity on Agricultural Technologies in Japan on October 30-November 4, 2024, totaling ₱360,000.00, had multiple deficiencies, contrary to Section 2 of PD No. 1445 and various provisions of EO No. 77, COA Circular Nos. 96-004, 2012-001, and 2015-009, and COA Resolution No. 2021-044; thus, the legality, validity, propriety, and accountability over the disbursed government funds were not properly established and attained.

The Municipal Accounting was unable to record the unpaid lease/rental fees of delinquent lessees of market stalls in the “Accounts Receivable” account amounted to ₱ 41,375.00 and their corresponding surcharges in contrast to International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS) 1 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby, the total assets and total government equity were understated as of December 31, 2024.

Various land improvements not related to fishery and marine structures amounted to ₱ 19.335 million were erroneously recorded under “Land Improvements – Aquaculture Structures” account in contrast to COA Circular 2015-009, thereby, affected the fair presentation of the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024 and possibly misled its end users.

Five (5) old structures owned by LGU-Kibawe that were demolished in CY 2024 with a total acquisition cost of ₱ 5.577 million were not derecognized in its books of accounts contrary to Section 62 of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 45, thereby, affected the fair presentation of the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024.

Two (2) construction and heavy equipment under the custody of the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) were not recorded in the books of accounts of the LGU contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby, the total assets and total government equity were understated as of December 31, 2024.

Various rehabilitation/repair projects of LGU-Kibawe were capitalized and recorded under “Construction in Progress – Infrastructure Assets” in the General Fund instead of treating them as outright expenses in contravention to COA Circular 2015-009, thereby, overstated the total assets and total government equity by ₱ 310,836.00 as of December 31, 2024.

Loans granted by Landbank of the Philippines, Malaybalay City Branch to LGU-Kibawe aggregating to ₱ 39,987,451.09 was erroneously recorded in full in the books of accounts of the LGU by a debit entry “Loans Receivable-Government Owned and/or Controlled Corporations (GOCCs)” and credit entry “Loans Payable-Domestic” accounts without actual receipt of the loan proceeds contrary to COA Circular 2015-009, thereby, presenting misleading information in the Statement of Financial Position and eventually overstated the total assets and total liability in the net amount of ₱ 17,656,183.09 as of December 31, 2024.

Interest income amounted to ₱ 55,487.99 were recorded as “Other Payables” and was not classified as general income in CY 2024 contrary to Section 65 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 17 of Volume I, Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS), thus, it affected the fair presentation of the financial statements as of December 31, 2024 and deprived the LGU to augment its local revenues to finance its priority projects.

LGU Kibawe missed to return the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) booked in the General Fund amounted to ₱ 69,000.00 to the Bureau of the Treasury as of December 31, 2024 which was not in conformity to the Philippine Supreme Court Decision G.R. No. 208566 dated November 19, 2013, thus, continuous possession might result to legal charges which is truly detrimental to the interest of the LGU.

The Local School Board (LSB) was not fully compliant with the reporting requirements for the Special Education Fund (SEF), as indicated in Section 6.1 of the DepEd-DBM-DILG Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2017, thereby undermining transparency and accountability in the allocation and utilization of the SEF.

LGU-Kibawe granted “Yuletide Social Assistance” amounted to ₱ 66,000.00 to the twenty-two (22) Punong Barangays of the Municipality of Kibawe in CY 2024 without a clear and legal basis in contrast to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, No. 5 of General Requirements for all types of disbursements of COA Circular No. 2012-001 and COA Circular 2013-003, thereby, tainted the propriety, validity and legality of the said payment.

Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) amounting to ₱ 3,627,687.50 for the period August 2021 to July 2023 was granted by the LGU in CY 2024 with various deficiencies contrary to the executed Memorandum of Agreement, DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01 and Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, thereby creating doubt on the validity and propriety of its release.

Foreign travel-related expenses incurred by the agency amounting to ₱360,000.00, have various noted deficiencies, contrary to DILG MC 2022-147, DILG MC 2019-83, EO 77 and COA Circular 2012-001, hence, the validity, propriety and regularity over the disbursed government funds, including its judicious and prudent use, were not properly established and attained.

Unpaid remittances of mandatory contributions, claims of LGU officers and employees, fund transfer and barangay financial assistance which aggregated to ₱ 2,879,415.62 were recorded under the “Accounts Payable” account contrary to COA Circular 2015-009, thereby, tainted the correctness, accuracy and reliability of the affected accounts as of December 31, 2024.

The accuracy of the Cash in Bank accounts cannot be relied upon, in view of the (a) delayed submission of Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS); (b) inclusion in Cash in Bank - LCCA of alleged closed bank accounts with a total balance amounting to P2,926,829.37; and (c) presence of unadjusted long-standing book and bank reconciling items, all contrary to PD No. 1445, COA Circular No. 96-011 and New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual for LGUs, thus casting doubt on the amounts of Cash in Bank - LCCA presented in the Financial Statements as of December 31, 2024.

Cash Shortages totaling P317,380.13 were incurred by the agency’s Accountable Officers and Forty-nine (49) stubs and Four Hundred Ninety-six (496) pieces of accountable forms could not be determined as to whether they were issued or not, due to their non-recording in the cashbooks and non-submission of the corresponding Report of Collections and Deposits, all contrary to the Local Treasury Operations Manual and COA Memorandum 2013-004, thereby, exposing government funds to risk of misappropriation by the Accountable Officers and moreover, adversely affecting the collection of projected income intended for the programmed expenditures of the agency.

The agency has not submitted to the Office of the Auditor within the prescribed period the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) for CY 2024 and the Agency’s paid Disbursement Vouchers, Liquidation Reports, Official Receipts and Deposit Slips and other reportorial documents, contrary to PD No. 1445 and the 2009 Rules and Regulations on the Settlement of Accounts, resulting to the delay in the review and verification of the propriety and validity of the transactions recorded in the books and precluding the rendering of the necessary and timely audit actions on these transactions. Moreover, the non-submission of the SCBAA precludes the Office of the Auditor from Rendering an Opinion in view of the incomplete Financial Statements.

The Municipality has not consistently complied with the rules and regulations on the proper withholding of monthly contributions and loan amortizations of its personnel and remittance thereof to the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) and Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF)/Pag-IBIG, by incurring the deficiencies noted, to wit, (a) existence of variances in the monthly deductions and remittances aggregating P218,226.67; (b) HDMF remittances totaling P1,816,727.05 were not made on time; (c) payments for premiums, loan amortizations and refunds were not attached with complete supporting documents; and (d) non-recording of withheld amounts in their appropriate liability accounts, contrary to RA No. 9679, RA No. 8291 and PD No. 1445. Consequently, the existence, legality, propriety and validity of the related disbursements could not be ascertained. Moreover, the aforementioned deficiencies expose the municipality to interests and penalties imposed by the GSIS and HDMF for delayed remittances. Lastly, the reliability and accuracy of the figures presented in the financial statements at year-end are deemed doubtful.

The manner of recording transactions under the account Due to PhilHealth is deemed insufficient in view of a) the existence of variances between the amount of monthly deductions and actual remittances aggregating P411,245.18; b) delayed recording of remittances in the books of accounts; c) attachment of inadequate supporting documents in the Journal Entry Voucher for remittances and d) non-recording of withheld amounts in their appropriate liability accounts, all inconsistent with the principles mandated in PD No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’ and the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual, thus causing inaccurate monthly balances in the related accounts, inability to ascertain the existence, legality, propriety and validity of the related disbursements and lastly, casting doubt on the reliability and accuracy of the amounts presented in the Financial Statements.

Receipts of advance payment for Real Property Tax (RPT) – Basic & SEF aggregating P1,097,266.06, net of discount, were erroneously recorded under Accounts Payable instead of Deferred Real Property Tax (RPT), Deferred Special Education Fund (SEF) Tax and Discount on Advance Payments contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby understating the aforementioned RPT related accounts and overstating Accounts Payable as of year-end, precluding the effective monitoring of unearned RPT, its corresponding discount and the eventual recognition of the same as income and more importantly, exposing the subject amount to misuse and misapplication as it is recorded under the wrong account title.

Loans Payable Domestic amounting to P204,475,208.44 as of December 31, 2024 was not separately presented in the Statement of Financial Position and did not contain sufficient disclosures in the Notes to Financial Statements, inconsistent with the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for LGUs and the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) thus, limiting significant financial information that can be available to various stakeholders and affecting the fair presentation of the of the said account in the Financial Statements.

The Municipality has not consistently complied with the applicable BIR withholding tax regulations and accounting principles in view of the noted deficiencies and procedural errors in relation to the withholding and remittance of taxes from suppliers, all inconsistent with Presidential Decree No. 1445, the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual, and Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 23-2012, thus exposing the Municipality to possible penalties that might accrue in view of the possible under remittances, compromising the operations of the GF’s Programs, Projects and Activities in view of the utilization of its cash for tax liabilities of other funds with no transferred cash yet and moreover, casting doubt on the propriety, existence, accuracy of the accounts “Due to BIR” and “Due from Other Funds” as of December 31, 2024.

The Municipality has not consistently complied with the applicable BIR withholding tax regulations and accounting principles in view of the noted deficiencies and procedural errors in relation to the withholding and remittance of taxes on compensation, all inconsistent with Presidential Decree No. 1445, the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual, and the relevant BIR Revenue Issuances, thus exposing the Municipality to possible penalties that might accrue in view of the under-remittances and non-compliance with the prescribed method of computing withholding taxes and moreover, casting doubt on the propriety, existence and accuracy of the “Due to BIR” account as of December 31, 2024.

The procedures being employed by the agency in its Cemetery Operations is deemed insufficient in view of the following: (a) non-maintenance by the Municipal Treasurer’s Office of a register in account of the cemetery and (b) erroneous recording of collections from cemetery operations, all inconsistent with PD No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’, Municipal Ordinance No. 07 (15th SB) series of 2022 or the Revised Local Revenue Code of the Municipality of Kitaotao, the Local Treasurer’s Manual and related issuances, thus rendering ineffective the management of the cemetery operations of the Agency leading to inefficiency in cemetery revenue collection and casting doubt on the reliability of the related revenue accounts in the Financial Statements.

The procedures employed by the agency in the grant of Hazard Pay is deemed non-compliant with relevant rules and regulations in view of the following: (a) grant of Hazard Pay to Public Health Workers (PHWs) using rates other than that prescribed; (b) grant of Hazard Pay to Public Social Workers (PSWs) based on a formula other than that prescribed and (c) payment of Hazard Pay with incomplete supporting documents, all inconsistent with Presidential Decree No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’, DBM-DOH Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2016, DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2018, COA Circular No. 2012-001 and COA Circular 2012-003, thus casting doubt as to the validity and propriety of the said disbursements and further, may render the same irregular and be subjected to audit suspension or disallowance, if warranted.

The procedures, practices and internal control of the Municipal Treasurer’s Office is deemed unreliable in view of the following: a) Non-maintenance of Cashbook and non-sequential issuance of pre-numbered official receipts for collections aggregating P729,561,392.02; b) Issuance of Accountable Forms to unbonded collectors; and c) Improper recording in the cashbook and Report of Collections and Deposits of issued accountable forms, all contrary to the Presidential Decree No. 1445, the Local Treasury Operations Manual and the Revised Cash Examination Manual, thus, exposing collections of revenue and trust funds to the risk of loss and misappropriation.

The Municipality has not consistently complied with the rules and regulations on the utilization of the Local Government Support Fund - SBDP for funds received in CY 2024 in view of the non-maintenance of a separate Subsidiary Ledger under the Trust Fund for each barangay beneficiary and project(s) to be implemented inconsistent with PD No. 1445 and Local Budget Circular No. 154, thus, preventing the efficient and effective monitoring and report generation of the transactions under each barangay project and moreover, exposes the Agency and the persons responsible to penalties under existing laws.

‘Construction in Progress – Infrastructure Assets’ account totaling P93.6 million representing the Philippine Rural Development Project – Concreting of Road and Drainage at Purok 5, Kulasihan, Lantapan, Bukidnon, was not depreciated and reclassified to Road Networks contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009 and DPWH Department Order No. 176, Series of 2015, which resulted to an overstatement of the PPE account by P4.68 million and an understatement of the depreciation expense by P4.68 million.

Various items totaling P11.22 million were erroneously recorded under the ‘Land’ account contrary to IPSAS 17 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby casting doubt on the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Various expenditures totaling P3.03 million relating to the Rehabilitation of Barangay Roads were recorded under Construction in Progress – Infrastructure Assets instead of posting it under its appropriate expense account contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009 and Section 111(2) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445; thereby casting doubt on the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The Municipality granted Barangay Alanib P1 million in financial assistance to purchase a lot for the Cemetery and failed to monitor the barangay's utilization and liquidation contrary to Section 1.2 of Article 1 of the signed Memorandum of Agreement. This cast doubt on the LGU's diligence in the observance of the provisions of the Memorandum of Agreement and results to overstatement of the ‘Due from LGUs’ account.

The Municipality granted financial assistance to 275 farmers affected by the dry spell totaling P0.825 million without proper guidelines contrary to Section 16 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160 and Section 4(2) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, Section 5.8 of COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997, and COA Circular No. 2015-009; thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the release of the said financial assistance and overstates the expense account by P93,000.00.

The Paglaum Village Project, with unpaid dues of P1.77 million by the vendees, had various deficiencies contrary to the perfected Conditional Contracts to Sell, Paragraph 9 of IPSAS 15, Section 94 of New Government Accounting System Manual for LGUS, and Sections 2, 112, & 114 (2) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445; thereby casting doubt on the propriety and effectiveness of the collection efforts of the LGU and adversely affects the fair presentation of the financial statements.

BUSECO Poles affected by two (2) FMR PRDP Projects incurred relocation costs of P224,415.57. The relocation cost was erroneously debited under the ‘Other MOOE’ account contrary to Paragraph 30 of IPSAS 17 and Paragraph 11 of Part IV of COA Circular No. 2015-008 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby understating the property, plant, and equipment account by the same amount.

Foreign travel expenses totaling P0.733 million in CY 2024 had various deficiencies contrary to COA Circular 2012-001, COA Circular No. 2012-003, DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2022-147, Executive Order (EO) No. 77, and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby raising concerns about the validity, propriety, and regularity of the travel expenses. Due to these deficiencies, the asset is understated by P220,494.07.

The Municipality granted BAC Honoraria totaling P0.674 million to BAC Members and the Technical Working Group without established internal rules and procedures in consideration of the attendance and participation of individuals in procurement activities and meetings contrary to Section 4.0 of DBM Budget Circular No. 2004-5A; thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the final computation of BAC Honoraria.

Certificates of Acceptance related to the PRDP Project, Concreting of Road and Drainage at Purok 3 to Purok 5 Kulasihan, Lantapan, with a contract price of P93.6 million were issued before the lapse of the defects liability period and attached to final payments contrary to Section 62.2.2 of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (R-IRR) of RA No. 9184, which is consistent with the DPWH DO No. 99, Series of 2015; thereby indirectly allowing any possible defects to remain uncorrected.

The Municipality granted Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) for CY 2021 totaling P6.45 million (net amount received totaling P6.16 million) with various deficiencies contrary to DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01, DOH AO No. 2022-01 & 039, Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, and the signed Memorandum of Agreement; thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the release of the HEA.

The Municipality implemented and liquidated the TUPAD Project with a total project cost of P467,000.00 with various deficiencies contrary to DOLE Department Order No. 239-23 and the signed Memorandum of Agreement, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the implementation and liquidation of the program.

The Municipality released Social Pensions to Senior Citizens totaling P12.2 million with various deficiencies contrary to the signed Memorandum of Agreement and DSWD Memorandum Circular No. 06, Series 2024, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the implementation and liquidation of Senior Citizens' Social Pensions.

Improper planning and inventory management of LGU Lantapan manifested in the procurement of some goods (i.e. Drugs & Medicines for Distribution, Medical, Dental and Laboratory Supplies for Distribution) contrary to Section 2 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, thereby casting doubt on the propriety of the inventory management.

Progress payments totaling P19 million were paid and supported by Statements of Work Accomplishment prepared by the agency management without the ‘conforme’ of the contractors contrary to Item 5 of Annex “E” of 2016 of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (R-IRR) of Republic Act (RA) No. 9184, thereby casting doubt on the propriety of the said payment processes.

Various unused projects of other agencies were erected on LGU land properties with market value totaling P15.86 million without supporting Memoranda of Understanding/Agreement and Sangguniang Bayan Resolutions contrary to Sections 2 & 4(2) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, Sections 22(c ) & 447 (2) Republic Act (RA) No. 7160, and DILG-NEDA-DBM-DOF Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 1, Series of 2016, dated November 18, 2016; thereby casting doubt on the regularity and propriety of the use of LGU land properties.

The Municipality distributed inventories totaling P11.82 million with various deficiencies contrary to Sections 2 and 4(6) of the Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, thereby casting doubt on the propriety of the procurement process and the implementation of distribution initiatives.

The Municipality erroneously charged expenditures relating to the Construction/Improvement of Multi-Purpose Building (Admin Bldg.) totaling P11.42 million against the 20% Local Development Fund contrary to DBM-DOF-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 1 dated November 4, 2020; thereby casting doubt on the legality of the charged expenditure.

The (a) existence of unreconciled balances aggregating ₱1.51 million between the General Services Office and the Municipal Accounting Office and the (b) under-recording of Accumulated Depreciation by at least P2.577 million which are contrary to COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020 and IPSAS No. 17, affected the reliability of the reported Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts as of December 31, 2024 by ₱1.51 million as existence and accuracy thereof could not be ascertained and overstating the PPE account by P2.577 million, affecting the fairness of presentation of the PPE accounts in the financial statements.

The (a) non-reclassification of issued Semi-Expendable Properties aggregating P2.5 million to expense account, along with the (b) non-maintenance of prescribed forms, report and registry on semi-expendable properties which are contrary to COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022, casted doubt on the proper accountability over the semi-expendable properties and the fair presentation of the year-end financial statements as the Inventory Account is overstated by the same amount.

Absence of an established process flow and uniformity in record keeping resulted to the dormancy of recorded projects totaling P84.304 million that remained recorded in the Construction in Progress (CIP) account since at least the CY 2022, contrary to the qualitative characteristics of financial information as provided under the IPSAS Conceptual Framework, thereby, diminishing the relevance, reliability, and fair presentation of the financial statements.

The validity and accuracy of the Due to PhilHealth account cannot be ascertained due to the discrepancy of P119,222.43 noted between the Financial Statements and the supposedly adjusted Statement of Premium Account (SPA) from Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PHIC) which is not in accordance with Paragraph 27 of International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS), affecting the fair presentation of the Financial Statements thereof.

The Reconciliation between the ‘Actual Amounts’ in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) for the year ended December 31, 2024 showed material amount of ‘entity differences’ without the proper disclosures required under Paragraphs 7 and 46 of IPSAS 1 and Paragraphs 14, 39 and 47 of IPSAS 24, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the Notes to Financial Statements (NTFS) and the SCBAA.

The LGU granted Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) to Health Care Workers and Non-Health Care Workers for the period covering CYs 2021-2023 totaling P6.783 million without complete supporting documents, contrary to DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01, DOH AO No. 2022-001, and DOH AO.

Foreign travel expenses incurred in CY 2024 totaling P374,568.00 were not completely supported with approved travel authority from the DILG and relevant documents specifically required by applicable DILG Memorandum Circular, COA Circular and pertinent provisions of Executive Order No. 77, thereby raising concerns on the validity, propriety, and regularity of the travel expenses.

The Reconciliation between the ‘Actual Amounts’ in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) and the Statement of Financial Performance for the year ended December 31, 2024, showed material items without proper disclosures regarding the breakdown and information of the aforementioned items, contrary to Section 111 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, Paragraphs 7 and 46 of IPSAS 1 and Paragraphs 14, 39 and 47 of IPSAS 24; thereby adversely affecting fair presentation of the Notes to Financial Statements and the SCBAA.

The discrepancy between the City Treasurer's Office records and the reported Real Property Tax Receivable, Special Education Tax Receivable, and their corresponding Deferred Income accounts decreased by 51.83 per cent, or ₱87.621 million, between CYs 2023 and 2024, however, a material understatement totaling ₱81.441 million remain, due to the incomplete reconciliation, and recording of the interests/penalties in the aforementioned Receivable accounts which is not in accordance with Section 111 of PD 1445, Sections 20 and 70 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS), and International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1 and 23.

The non-submission of the report to the accounting office on uncollected rental fees from the stallholders of the Malaybalay City Public Market amounting to ₱0.973 million as of December 31, 2024 resulted to the non-recognition of Income and Receivable, an indication of lapse in internal control of the management, thus affecting the fairness of the affected accounts in the Financial Statement contrary to IPSAS 1 and Sections 123 and 124 of PD 1445, respectively.

The accuracy and existence of the reported Inventory account balance as of December 31, 2024 totaling P88 million could not be ascertained due to the doubtful existence of items with an aggregate amount of P39 million; semi-expendable properties were not reclassified in the appropriate account; and the inclusion of Semi-Expendable items already issued to end users amounting to P36 million, thereby casting doubt on the reliability of the balance presented in the Statement of Financial Position at the end of CY 2024.

The balance of the “Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants Inventory” account in the Financial Statement at the end of Calendar Year (CY) 2024 do not accurately reflect the actual inventory levels due to the (i) improper recognition of prior year expenses amounting to P6.189 million; (ii) presence of unsubstantiated journal entry voucher for adjustments; and (iii) discrepancies between the SL balance and the confirmed balances stored at the gasoline stations amounting to P21.661 million, which are contrary to Section 111 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, and paragraph 37 of IPSAS 12-Inventories, casting doubt on the reliability and fair presentation of the account in the Financial Statements.

The accuracy and existence of the reported Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) account balance as of December 31, 2024 totaling P3.206 billion could not be ascertained due to the doubtful existence of PPE items with an aggregate net book value of P93.5 million; non-submission of RPCPPE for accounts with a total net book value of P768 million; failure to complete the one-time cleansing; non-recognition of depreciation to some items; and non-reclassification of items costing below P50,000.00 in an aggregate amount of P5.93 million, thereby casting doubt on the reliability of the balance presented in the Statement of Financial Position at the end of CY 2024.

The accuracy and reliability of the PPE account “Road Networks” amounting to P1.069 billion (net of depreciation) as of December 31, 2024 could not be relied upon due to (1) properties not found, damaged or no longer existing as reported in the physical count; (2) non-maintenance of records; (3) absence of road network component/s; and (4) incomplete disclosure in the Notes to Financial Statements, contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-008, thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the amount of Road Networks presented in the Statement of Financial Position at the end of CY 2024.

The utilization/liquidation of Trust Liabilities, fund transfers made by National Government Agencies (NGA), and other trust receipts in the Trust Fund books were not recognized as revenue even though the conditions for recognition have already been met, contrary to Paragraphs 44, 45 and 46 and Basis for Conclusion (BC) No. 11 of IPSAS 23, thus causing a deficit of P40.143 million in the Trust Fund for the period ending December 31, 2024.

Error in recording the collection for the sale of bidding documents and non-recording of excess amount collected as part of local government funds resulted to misstatement of the affected accounts in the financial statement amounting to P2.221 million, contrary to International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1 in presentation of FS and COA Circular No. 2015- 009, and DOF-DBM-COA Permanent Resolution No. 2005-2.

Disbursement vouchers (DVs) and the accompanying supporting documents were belatedly submitted ranging from 7 to 191 days after the reglementary period due to manpower constraint in the City Accounting Office handling the submission and scanning of vouchers, contrary to Section 347 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160, Section 122 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, COA Circular No. 2009-006, COA Circular No. 95-006, and Section 44 of the Manual on New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGU), thereby adversely affecting the timely review of the City’s financial transactions and noted deficiencies, if any, could not be immediately communicated to the management.

Accuracy and correctness of the City’s Report on Sources and Utilization of the DRRMF and the Accounting and Budget records and related disclosures for CY 2024 could not be ascertained due to the: a) non-preparation of the LDRRMF Investment Plan for the CY 2024 PPAs; b) noted variance aggregating P40.336 million between the utilization report and the related records and disclosures; and c) unspent 30% QRF and DRRMF-MOOE totaling P40.095 million not transferred to the “Trust Liabilities-DRRMF” account, contrary to the pertinent provisions of Presidential Decree No. 1445, COA Circular No. 2012-002, COA Circular 2015-009, and JMC No. 2013-01.

Disbursements totaling P13.987 million were charged against the LDRRMF of the City Government of Malaybalay despite not being related to Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) activities, contrary to several provisions of Republic Act No. 10121 otherwise known as “Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010”, and NDRRMC-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2013-1 dated March 25, 2013, thereby defeating the purpose of the fund as well as decreasing its availability for disaster related use.
