The non- implementation and inclusion of projects that are not implementation ready into the 20% Local Development Fund (LDF), General Fund-Proper, Economic Enterprise and Special Education Fund’s Programs, Projects, and Activities (PPAs) for CY 2024 and prior years resulted to a low implementation and utilization rate of the current year and Continuing Appropriations, thus, impeding the optimum utilization of the fund which consequently deprived the public of the benefits that could have been derived from its immediate implementation and maximum utilization.

Various deficiencies were observed in the utilization by the City Government of Malaybalay of the DOH funds for Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) in CY 2024 totaling ₱28.152 million, contrary to the executed Memorandum of Agreement, DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01, DOH AO No. 2022-001 and Section 4(6) of PD 1445, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the release of the HEA and deprived the intended personnel of the timely receipt of the HEA benefits.

Various deficiencies were noted in the monetization of leave credits, such as (a) monetization of Sick Leave (SL) credits without exhausting Vacation Leave (VL) credits first; (b) employees availed of leave monetization more than once; (c) monetization of more than ten (10) days or 50 percent or more of leave credits without valid supporting documents; and (d) other deficiencies, contrary to Sections 22 and 23 of Rule XVI of the Omnibus Rules on Leave, CSC-DBM Joint Circular No. 2-97, COA Circular 2012-001, and CSC Resolution No. 00-0034 dated January 5, 2000, thereby casting doubt on the regularity and propriety of the disbursement.

The payment, control and monitoring measures implemented by the City Government of Malaybalay in the utilization of fuel, oil and lubricants are not in consonance with Sections 88, 4 and 123 of the Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 77-61 which exposed the LGU to possible wasteful, excessive and unnecessary expenditures for fuel consumption of government.

Deficiencies were observed in the payments of honoraria to BAC and TWG members amounting to P1.203 million due to non-submission of some of the documentary requirements and non-submission of one payroll, contrary to Item 6, Section 4 of PD No. 1445 and Section 5.7.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 and DBM Budget Circular NO. 2004-5A.

Inter-agency payables representing withheld premium contributions and loan amortizations for the GSIS, Pag-ibig and Philhealth aggregating ₱7.43 million as of December 31, 2024 were not remitted in full within the prescribed period, contrary to Sections 14.1 to 14.3 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act (RA) No. 8291, Section E.4 of HDMF Circular No. 275 dated January 22, 2010 and Section 18 of the IRR of the National Health Insurance Act of 2013, thereby exposing the City Government and the employees to the possible imposition of penalty and surcharges for the late remittance thereof.

Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts could not be relied upon due to the following deficiencies: (1) adjusting entry reclassifying PPE accounts was made without proper supporting documents; (2) non-reconciliation of the RPCPPE and accounting records; (3) PPEs are lumped and described as “Beginning Balances”, temporary accounts, and without appropriate description amounting to ₱396.173 million, and (3) still not subjected to one-time cleansing, a non-conformance to IPSAS 1 and 23, NGAS Manual for LGUs, and COA Circular 2020-006, thus, the accuracy and existence of the PPE accounts presented in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024 aggregating ₱704.781 million are doubtful and unreliable, thereby depriving the government of reliable and useful information in decision-making and accountability for these assets.

Costs incurred for dredging project at Malitbog River totaling ₱999,399.76 were improperly capitalized instead as a direct expense, a clear deviation to IPSAS No. 1, COA Circular Nos. 2015-009 and 2020-006, thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the specific asset, expense and equity accounts presented in the financial statements.

The non-compliance to the accrual basis of accounting and proper recording for insurance and fidelity bond premiums resulted in the overstatement of the Insurance Expense and Fidelity Bond Premium accounts by ₱523,748.73 and ₱82,257.53, respectively, contrary to IPSAS No. 1, Section 4.a of Vol. 1 of the Manual on NGAS for LGUs and the Revised Chart of Accounts for LGUs, thereby, casts doubt on to the accuracy and reliability of related account balances presented in the financial statements.

The Municipal Accounting Office failed to submit some Disbursement Vouchers and General Journal accounts, including various Journal Entry Vouchers recorded in CY 2024, totaling ₱981.876 million, contrary to Section 347 of RA 7160 and Section 7.2.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009, thus, the propriety and legality of the transactions could not be ascertained and may affect the rendition of auditor’s opinion on the financial statements due to audit scope limitation.

Various labor payments for projects implemented by administration charged against 20% LDF appropriations were incompletely substantiated with relevant documentary requirements and with other noted deficiencies such as the labor payments exceeded the allocated labor cost per Program of Work (POW), improper recording of labor cost for regular road maintenance to an asset account and misleading information reflected in the SWA, all runs counter to IPSAS Nos. 1 and 17, Section 4 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thereby casting reservations on the validity and propriety of the disbursed transactions aggregating ₱9.979 million, including the accuracy and reliability of CIP accounts presented in the Statement of Financial Position.

LGU-Malitbog hired and paid the services of a highly technical consultant for a total of ₱600,000.00 in calendar year 2024 without adhering to the proper procurement procedures and documentary requirements as prescribed by the revised IRR of RA 9184 and COA Circular 2012-001, thereby precluded the transparency, competitiveness, and accountability as envisioned by the said law and regulations and that the audit team cast reservation on the regularity and validity of the disbursed transactions.

The grant of 5-day Union Leave, made available to employees under the 2024 Collective Negotiation Agreement (CNA) between the LGU and the Employees’ Association, resulted in indirect additional compensation payments while availing such leave totaling ₱284,117.58 but is devoid of legal basis and inconsistent with Omnibus Rules on Leave, Rule XVI of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order (EO) No. 292 and Public Sector Labor-Management Council (PSLMC) Resolution No. 13, s. 2023, thereby casting doubt on its legality and validity.

The municipality failed to: (1) remit intact the withheld Expanded Withholding Tax (EWT) and Value Added Tax (VAT) to the BIR; (2) timely transfer the remittance shares of LDF, SEF and TF in favor of GF Proper; (3) draw acceptable journal entries in recording BIR-related transactions; and, (4) timely remit, collect and deposit checks in favor of BIR and GF Proper, inconsistent with the provisions of PD 1445 and existing BIR rules and regulations, consequently impairing the adequacy of the LGU management’s internal control which might render them susceptible to any imposition of tax assessment and penalties, the possibility of inaccurate or misleading financial information, and compromising the GF fund’s operation due to a reduced cash position caused by belated transfer, non-transfer and/or delayed collection/deposit of remittance shares from said funds.

The municipality paid Hazard Pay and Subsistence Allowance to its MHO and MSWDO personnel totaling ₱2.069 million with inadequate supporting documents and improper computations resulting in overpaid Hazard Pay and Subsistence Allowance for the said personnel, contravening COA Circular Nos. 2012-001, DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1 s. of 2018, and DBM-DOH Joint Circular No. 1, s. of 2012, as amended, thereby impairing the appropriateness and validity of the disbursed transactions.

Some travelling expenses paid for the calendar year 2024 contained deficiencies, such as: (1) inadequate supporting documents for liquidation; (2) non-compliance with the prescribed rates and allowable expenses, (3) improper cash advances granted to a single accountable officer instead of each official or employee processing their own advances which are contrary to the provisions of COA Circular 2012-001, Executive Order No. 77, and COA Circular 97-002, thereby raise doubt on the propriety and validity of the transactions and might pose risks of irregular, unnecessary, or excessive expenditures.

The Municipality granted Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) in November 2024 totaling ₱6.678 million with various deficiencies contrary to the executed Memorandum of Agreement, DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01, DOH AO No. 2022-001 and Section 4(6) of PD 1445, thereby creating doubt on the validity and propriety of the release of the HEA.

The municipality disbursed communication expenses without clear guidelines on granting of communication allowances to its officials and employees while also incurring unnecessary payments for gadgets and other charges, totaling ₱1.446 million and ₱0.172 million, respectively, contrary to Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and COA Circular 2012-003, thereby casting doubt on the reasonableness and regularity of these transactions.

Foreign travel-related expenses incurred during LMP-Bukidnon’s Economic and Cultural Mission Tour in USA on September 12-25, 2024 have various noted deficiencies totaling ₱200,000.00, contrary to COA Circular Nos. 2012-01 and 2015-009, and AO No. 6 (s. 2017), hence, the validity, propriety and accountability over the disbursed government funds, including its judicious and prudent use, were not properly established and attained.

Payroll payments in favor of DOLE TUPAD Program recipients released by LGU Malitbog aggregating ₱1.713 million have insufficient documentation, a non-conformance to specific provisions of PD 1445 and DOLE DO No. 239, series of 2023, consequently, the audit team could not validate the propriety and validity of such disbursed transactions.

The (a) existence of unreconciled balances between General Services Office and the Municipal Accounting Office and the (b) presence of bulk acquisitions without specifying quantities in Property Cards and PPE Ledger Cards contrary to COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020 and COA Circular 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022, affected the reliability of the reported Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts as of December 31, 2024 by ₱375.579 million as existence and accuracy thereof could not be ascertained, affecting the fairness of presentation of the PPE accounts in the financial statements.

Prior Period Adjustments totaling P111.884 million was presented in the “Adjustment of Net Revenue Recognized Directly in Net Assets/Equity” in the Statement of Changes in Net/Assets Equity (SNAE), contrary to Paragraph 118 of IPSAS 1, indicating non-compliance with the prescribed presentation of prior period errors and potentially impairing the understandability and faithful representation of the financial statements.

Completed projects totaling at least P49.251 million were not closed to appropriate asset accounts and were not provided with the corresponding depreciation contrary to Section 50 of Volume I of the NGAS Manual and the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) Description of Accounts, hence, affected the reliability of the year-end Financial Statements.

Revenue from non-exchange transactions arising from completed projects funded through fund transfers was not uniformly recognized by the LGU, as portions amounting to P4.653 million and P12.160 million were recorded under “Grants and Donations in Kind” and “Transfers from National Government”, respectively, contrary to the qualitative characteristics of financial reporting, thereby impairing the understandability and comparability of the financial statements.

Twenty-seven (27) road lots of the Local Government Unit (LGU) totaling P17.785 million were credited and presented in the Statement of Financial Performance as ‘Other Gains’ instead of ‘Prior Period Adjustment’ and the required disclosures were not provided in the Notes to Financial Statements, contrary to the illustrative accounting entries prescribed under Annex "E" of COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020, Section 51 of IPSAS 3, and the disclosure requirements under Paragraph 54 of the same IPSAS, thereby, overstating the ‘Other Gains’ account, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The (a) non-reclassification of issued Semi-Expendable Properties aggregating P29.4 million to expense account, along with the (b) non-maintenance of prescribed Registry of Semi-Expendable Property Issued (RegSPI) for issued semi-expendable properties which are contrary to COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022, casted doubt on the proper accountability over the semi-expendable properties and the fair presentation of the year-end financial statements as the Inventory Account is overstated by the same amount.

Construction in Progress totaling P3.656 million was derecognized without supporting documentation, contrary to Paragraph 82 of IPSAS 17 and Paragraphs 27 of IPSAS 1, thereby impairing the faithful representation and reliability of the financial statements, understating the Property, Plant, and Equipment account by the said amount, and adversely affecting their fair presentation.

The Reconciliation15 between the ‘Actual Amounts’ in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) for the year ended December 31, 2024 showed material amounts16 of ‘entity differences’ without the proper disclosures required under Paragraphs 7 and 46 of IPSAS 1 and Paragraphs 14, 39 and 47 of IPSAS 24, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the Notes to Financial Statements (NTFS) and the SCBAA.

Reconciling items totaling (P0.200) million (net) from the eleven (11) bank accounts were not adjusted in the LGUs books of accounts as of December 31, 2024, contrary to Sections 3.2 and 3.3 of COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thereby, overstating the Cash in Bank – Local Currency, Current Account in the financial statements.

A foreign travel-related expense amounting to ₱160,000.00 was erroneously recorded under the Training Expenses account instead of the appropriate Travelling Expenses – Foreign account, contrary to the account classification prescribed under Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thereby overstating the former and understating the latter account in the financial statements.

The LGU granted Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) to Health Care Workers and Non-Health Care Workers for the period covering CYs 2021-2023 totaling P13.536 million without complete supporting documents, contrary to DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01, DOH AO No. 2022-001, and DOH AO No. 2022-039, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the payment.

Foreign travel expenses incurred in CY 2024 totaling P4.234 million were not completely supported with approved travel authority from the DILG and relevant documents specifically required by applicable DILG Memorandum Circular, COA Circular and pertinent provisions of Executive Order No. 77, thereby raising concerns on the validity, propriety, and regularity of the travel expenses.

Donations of Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) totaling P2.140 million to various barangays and institutions were not supported with complete documentation, contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thereby, affecting the validity of the recorded transaction.

The budget for a foreign travel-related expense totaling P310,000.00 was erroneously charged to the appropriations for Training Expenses account instead of the appropriate Travelling Expenses – Foreign account, inconsistent with Section 305(a) of the R.A. No. 7160, thereby, constituting irregular expenditure.

The non-submission by the LGU of the copies of its Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS) for its four (4) bank accounts with an aggregate book balance of P5.035 million contrary to Section 3.4 of COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, hindered the timely verification of the accuracy and completeness of the recorded cash balances.

Seal of Good Local Governance (SGLG) Incentive in CY 2022 funded project entitled “Concreting of Municipal Street Portion of Quezon Avenue & Portion of Felix Manalo Street (from Jct. Maramag-Maradugao Road to Jct. Daniel Rumualdez street)” with a total project cost of ₱ 4.994 million was not recognized and recorded in the General Fund book of accounts of the LGU in contravention to Section 6.5.2 of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2023-019, thereby, understated the total assets, total income and total government equity as of December 31, 2024.

Repair of 73 units Classrooms Elementary School/Central Elementary School and National High School-Bukidnon National School of Home Industries Annex Project at Maramag, Bukidnon funded by the Provincial Government of Bukidnon with a total project cost of ₱ 3.632 million was lodged in “Construction in Progress-Buildings and Other Structures” account in the Special Education Fund (SEF) book of accounts instead of “Repairs and Maintenance-Buildings and Other Structures” account in the Trust Fund contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009 and Section 94 Chapter 5 Volume I of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual for LGUs, thereby, the correctness and validity of recording in the Special Education Fund book of accounts could not be ascertained and it overstated the total assets and total government equity of the said fund as of December 31, 2024.

Reciprocal accounts “Due to LGUs” and “Due from LGUs” between the Municipality of Maramag and the Province of Bukidnon had a material discrepancy amounting to ₱ 33,116,492.44 which was not in consonance with International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS) 1 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby, affecting the accuracy, propriety and reliability of the reported balance of the said account in the financial statements as of December 31, 2024.

To implement a systematic and timely approach to updating the “Due to LGUs” account upon submission of liquidation reports, in compliance with IPSAS and COA regulations. This will ensure the financial statements accurately reflect the Municipality's obligations and maintain consistency in inter-agency transactions.

Interest income/earnings of Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP) – Valencia City Branch, Special Savings Account No. 0831-04078A-160 amounted to ₱ 1.988 million in CY 2024 was not accrued thereto but was directly credited to DBP – Valencia Current Account No. 0831-04078A-030 contrary to Section 23 of COA Circular No. 92-382, thus, monitoring and accounting of its interest income/earnings were difficult.

Advance payments aggregating to ₱ 3,114,889.50 were made to suppliers for the procurement of “goods” despite the lack of prior approval of the President contrary to Item 4.1, Annex D of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 9184 which resulted to irregular disbursements.

Payment of terminal benefits to five (5) retirees and one (1) resignee which aggregated to ₱ 1.486 million were not properly and completely substantiated with documentary requirements inconsistent to Section 5.13 of COA Circular No. 20212-001, hence, the propriety, validity and legality of the disbursements could not be ascertained.

Out of the five hundred fifty two (552) lessees of LGU’s stalls, four hundred thirteen (413) lessees have no contracts of lease and one hundred thirty nine (139) lessees have expired contracts of lease in contravention to Ordinance No. 2015-110 or an Ordinance enacting the Local Economic Enterprise Code of the Municipality of Maramag, Bukidnon, thereby, tainted the propriety, legality and validity of the leases and the LGU was vulnerable to being aggrieved from possible infringements by the lessees.

(a) The Municipal Treasurer collected the various LGUs’ cost sharing in the Southern Bukidnon Inter-local Health Zone (SBILHZ) which aggregated to ₱ 4,650,489.21 as of December 31, 2024 but without an available legal and written authority contrary to the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) among the Provincial Government of Bukidnon, Municipal Governments of Maramag, Quezon, Pangantucan, Kalilangan, Kadingilan, Don Carlos, Kitaotao, Dangcagan, Kibawe and Damulog, Department of Health Region 10 and the Bukidnon Provincial Hospitals that include Kibawe, Kalilangan and Maramag; (b) LGU-Maramag recognized and recorded the collections of the cost sharing of the members of the SBILHZ as “Trust Liabilities” in the General Fund book of accounts inconsistent to Section 94, Chapter 5, Volume I of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual for LGUs and Section 1 of COA Circular No. 92-382, thus, the propriety, validity and legality of the collections and the recording of the “Trust Liabilities” in the General Fund could not be ascertained.

Financial subsidies to component barangays with specific purpose totalling ₱ 700,000.00 were not supported with complete documentation and were treated as outright expenses contrary to Section 3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, which created no basis for monitoring the compliance of the implementing agency in the utilization of the funds for its intended purpose and exposing such funds to the risk of possible misuse.

The twenty (20) Punong Barangays of the Municipality of Maramag received financial subsidy and assistance from LGU-Maramag at ₱ 18,000.00 each for a total amount of ₱ 360,000.00 in CY 2024 without clear and definite legal basis contrary to Section 95 of RA No. 7160 and Section 4.2 of Local Budget Circular No. 63 dated October 22, 1996, thus, it casted doubts as to the propriety, legality, and validity of the payments.

The payment of BAC honoraria amounting ₱ 285,747.66 was not supported by a Notice of Award, and the payment in excess of the 25% basic monthly salary totaling ₱ 53,709.71 was not in accordance with Section 5.7.1 of COA Circular 2012-001 and Section 5.3 and 5.4 of DBM Budget Circular 2004-5A, thus, the propriety, legality, and validity of the payments could not be ascertained.

Foreign travel-related expenses have various noted deficiencies totaling ₱838,020.19, contrary to COA Circular Nos. 2012-01 and 2015-009, and AO No. 6 (s. 2017), hence, the validity, propriety and accountability over the disbursed government funds, including its judicious and prudent use, were not properly established and attained.

Municipal officials were paid travel allowances for foreign travel totaling ₱490,600.00 without the approval from the DILG and lacking supporting documents contrary to Section 4.3 of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2022-147 dated November 22, 2022, and COA Circular 2012-001 thus raised doubt as to the validity, propriety, and regularity of the travel claims.

Failure of the Inventory Committee to conduct a physical count of all the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts owned by the Municipality, aggregating to P927,434,578.11 net of accumulated depreciation, or 73.32% of the total assets as of December 31, 2024; non-maintenance of property cards per category of PPE by the General Services Office; incomplete provision of allowances for depreciation; and failure to initiate actions related to the required One-Time Cleansing of PPE accounts were not in compliance with the provisions of Section 111 (1) of P.D. 1445, Sections 119 and 124 of the MNGAS for LGUs, Volume 1, COA Circular No. 2020-006, and Paragraph 71 of IPSAS No. 17. Thus, the existence, correctness, and valuation of the accounts cannot be ascertained.

Balances of various inventory accounts cannot be relied upon due to inconsistent application of the Perpetual Inventory Method (PIM), non-conduct of the semestral physical inventories, presence of various nonmoving accounts, failure to drop inventories already issued, bloating the inventory account balances as of December 31, 2024, erroneous dropping of accounts, unreliable supporting documents attached to dropping of accounts, and incorrect recording of a purchase. Moreover, the inadequate internal control system of the General Services Office (GSO) for inventory management, reporting, and recording was not in compliance with Section 111(2) of P.D. No. 1445, Paragraph 44 of PPSAS 12, various provisions of the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs) Volume I, and COA Circular No. 2022-004, thereby, inventories were exposed to theft or loss and mismanagement. Moreover, the accuracy, completeness, and existence of the inventory account balance of P64,295,932.64 as of December 31, 2024.

Various disbursement vouchers for meals and food supplies, totaling P4,118,908.41 from January to December 2024, showed inconsistencies and deficiencies, contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-001, Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445, Section 343 of R.A. 7160, COA Circular No. 2015-009, COA Circular No. 1992-386 and Section 54.1 of R.A. No. 9184; therefore, the validity and propriety of the expenses related to meals and food supplies cannot be established.

Various intra-agency fund transfers affecting the accounts “Due to Other Funds” and “Due from Other Funds”, amounting to P26,179,765.09 in calendar year (CY) 2024, could not be verified due to inadequate attachment of supporting documents, which is not in accordance with Sec. 111 (1) of P.D. 1445, thus the necessity, validity, propriety, and regularity of the recorded JEVs cannot be ascertained. It also limits the scope of the audit of the team. Moreover, it created doubt as to the correctness of the “Due to other funds” and “Due from other funds” account balances as of the year-end of CY 2024.

Foreign travel-related expenses incurred during the League of Municipalities of the Philippines (LMP)-Bukidnon’s Economic and Cultural Mission Tour in the United States of America (USA) in September 2024 and the Vice Mayors’ League of the Philippines (VMLP) Bukidnon Chapter Benchmarking Activity from October 29 to November 5, 2024, totaling ₱329,383.00, had multiple deficiencies, contrary to Section 2 of PD No. 1445 and various provisions of EO No. 77, COA Circular Nos. 96-004, 2012-001, and 2015-009; thus, the legality, validity, propriety, and accountability over the disbursed government funds were not properly established and attained.

The grant of honoraria to the officials and employees who are members of the Board of Trustees of the Pangantucan Bukidnon Community College (PBCC) and the PBCC Administration, totaling P314,000.00 for the year 2024, was bereft of legal basis in violation of Section 94 of R.A. No. 7160, Section 63 of the general provisions of R.A. 11975, COA Circular 2012-003, and Section 4.0 of the National Budget Circular No. 2007-510, thereby may fall under an irregular disbursement of government funds.

Payments for monetization of leave credits were not in accordance with Sections 22 and 23 of Rule XVI of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order (E.O.) No. 292, COA Circular Nos. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, and 2012-003 dated October 29, 2012; thus, the legality, validity, and propriety of the disbursements could not be established, and the disbursements may be considered irregular.

Regular and casual employees' individual leave card entries have a number of errors that violate Section 11(2) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and various provisions of Executive Order No. 292, raising questions about the accuracy and dependability of balances of leave credits of each employee and of monetization payments that have been computed using employee leave card balances.

Disbursements for CY 2024 salaries and PERA paid to employees were not properly supported due to lacking daily time records, certification from the Human Resource Management Office (HRMO) of the posting of deductions to individual leave ledgers, approved leave applications, travel documents for out-of-office duties, and requests for manual entries; payment of salaries for unauthorized absences; and deficiencies in various entries in the DTRs, which is inconsistent with item 6 of section 4 and item 2 of Section 111 of PD 1445, E.O. No. 292, or the Omnibus Rules on Leave, and section 1.2.1 of COA Circular 2012-001 and Section 191(c) of the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual (GAAM), cast doubt on the accuracy, validity, and propriety of the payments of salaries and PERA made to regular and casual employees in CY 2024 amounting to P82,292,999.34, as well as on the correctness of salaries expense and PERA recognized in CY 2024.

The Municipality failed to observe the intact remittance of the withheld taxes both from compensation and suppliers, contributions, and loan repayments from the salaries and wages of its personnel to the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF), Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PHIC), and Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), contrary to Section 4.114.C of BIR Revenue Regulation 2-98, Section 6b of RA No. 8291, Section 3, and Rule VII of R.A. No. 9679, and Section 20 (b), Rule III of the IRR of the National Health Insurance Act of 1995, resulting in under- and over-remittance of the amounts withheld and creating doubts on the reliability and completeness of the remittances made. Consequently, the Municipality accumulated unremitted balances of P18,980.96 to HDMF and P6,574.48 to BIR, P188,588.59 to GSIS and P12,022.70 to PHIC as of October 31, 2024.

Monthly remittances of taxes withheld, premium and loan payments, and other mandatory deductions from all Special Accounts maintained under General Fund (GF), including other funds such as Special Education Fund (SEF) and Trust Fund (TF) accounts, were remitted on a monthly basis to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Pag-IBIG, and Philhealth using the Funds from the GF Proper account; however, the actual cash fund from these funds were transferred to GF Proper only after the remittance to the various government agencies, which is not in consonance with Sections 2 of Presidential Decree (P.D.) No. 1445, thus may disrupt the smooth operations/implementation of the scheduled projects, programs, and activities (PPAs) under the GF Proper account.

Unutilized collection from proceeds of the sale of bidding documents in the Trust Fund account at year-end amounting to ₱470,818.00 was not remitted to the General Fund account, which was not in conformity to Section 6.2 of Appendix 7 of the revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA 9184, thus depriving the agency of additional funds for its programs and projects. Moreover, the error resulted in an overstatement of “Other Payable” and an understatement of “Government Equity” accounts presented in the Consolidated Financial Statement, both by the same amount.

The grant of a cash advance for a Confidential Fund of P200,000.00 to the Former Municipal Mayor his physical incapacity to perform his duties and functions due to his absence is contrary to Section 2 of P.D. No. 1445, Commission on Audit (COA), Department of Budget and Management (DBM), Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG); Governance Commission for GOCCs (GCG), Department of National Defense (DND) Joint Circular No. 2015-01, Section 46(a) of R.A. No. 7160, and the bounds of good faith; thereby, created a loss or wastage of government funds through illegal or improper disposition.

Deficiencies were noted in the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) of the Municipality a non-compliance to IPSAS 1 and 17, COA Circular Nos. 2020-006 and 2022-004, thus, cast doubt as to the fairness of presentation of the PPE Account in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024.

Receipts from PhilHealth for professional fees were recorded as Other Payables instead of Trust Liabilities, a non-compliance to IPSAS 1 and Annex B of COA Circular 2015-009 which resulted to an overstatement of the account “Other Payables” and understatement of the account “Trust Liabilities” in the amount of P10,073,609.31 in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024.

Doubt exists as to the correctness of depreciation expenses in the amount of P10,686,683.84 for “Buildings and Other Structures” of the LGU due to deficiencies noted in the recording of its related Property, Plant, and Equipment, a non-compliance to IPSAS 3 and 17, thereby cast doubt as to the fairness of the presentation of Non-cash Expenses reported in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Performance for the year ended December 31, 2024.

The municipality failed to facilitate the proper disposition of dormant receivable aging more than 10 years totaling ₱4,742,249.38, inclusive of unidentifiable and unverifiable balances totaling ₱291,270.28 million, a non-compliance to International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS) No. 1, COA Circulars Nos. 2023-008, thereby, affecting the reliability of the account “Receivables” presented in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024.

The rehabilitation of cottages amounting to P1,097,088.73 was recorded as an expense, and individual subsidiary ledgers were not maintained for each cottage constructed at the LGU-owned spring resort, a non-compliance with IPSAS 1 and Section 10, Chapter I, Volume II of the New Government Accounting System Manual, resulting in an understatement of the Property, Plant, and Equipment of the LGU and potentially causing inaccuracies in recording subsequent costs and in determining the carrying amount of property upon derecognition.

Fully liquidated fund transfers in the total amount of ₱38,531,361.03 from the Provincial Government of Bukidnon were still recorded in the accounts “Due to LGUs” and “Property, Plant, and Equipment” in the Trust Fund books of accounts of the Municipality, a non-compliance to IPSAS 1 and Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-009, which resulted to an overstatement of the said accounts in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2024.

Changes in the annual budget for the project “Installation of Street Lighting System at Poblacion and San Jose” to “Installation of LED Streetlights along Municipal Road – Poblacion” in the amount of P3,000,000.00 was made without adhering to the guidelines set forth under Republic Act No. 7160, thus, cast doubt as to the propriety and legality of the disbursements in the total amount of P2,793,769.00.

Deficiencies were noted in the appointments and payroll payments of job orders, a non-compliance to CSC-COA-DBM Joint Circular No.1, s. 2017, and COA Circular 2012-001, thus, cast doubt as to the validity and appropriateness of the disbursements.

Payrolls of Regular and Casual Employees in CY 2024 were not supported with applications for leave of absences, minutes of session, and certificates of appearance, contrary to Section 4(6) of P.D. No. 1445, Sections 21, 51 and 53 of CSC MC No. 41, s. 1998, thus, employees may have undertaken unauthorized absences and validity, propriety and legality of the disbursements for salaries and wages in the total amount of ₱91,601,224.92 could not be established. Moreover, the HR in-charge could not record the leave credits consumed in a timely manner and accuracy of the leave balances as of year-end could not be ascertained.

Multiple procurement activities were undertaken by the Municipality for supplies and materials which are needed at or about the same time and for the same purpose, contrary to Sections 7 and 54.1 of IRR of R.A. 9184, and Section 26 of COA Circular 92-386 dated October 20, 1992, which cast doubt as to the propriety of the procurements and indicate the potential occurrence of splitting of government contracts.

Twenty-Two (22) infrastructure project contracts totaling to P47,653,535.30 were not supported with complete documents and did not strictly follow the procedure for competitive bidding contrary to Paragraph 3.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-001 dated February 12, 2009, and the provisions of R.A. No. 9184 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations. Thus, validity of the infrastructure project contracts could not be established.

The existence, accuracy, and valuation of the LGUs’ reported inventories’ ending balance of P33.65 million as of December 31, 2024, could not be ascertained due to various deficiencies in handling the inventories accounts. This is contrary to Sections 2 and 4(6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 124 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Volume 1 for Local Government Units.

Insurable properties of the LGU for CY 2024 amounting to P334.135 million were not covered with property insurance from the General Insurance Fund (GIF) of the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) and the payments of insurance premiums of the selected insured properties of the LGU were expensed outright amounting to P0.591 million thus, incompliant to Property Insurance Law, COA Circular No. 2018-02, and Section 64 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual Volume I, thereby exposing some of the LGU’s properties to risk of non-indemnification for possible damages of losses of PPEs on account of fortuitous event and overstating the insurance expense account by P325,959.61 and understating the Prepaid Insurance asset account by the same amount which cast doubts on the reliability of the CY 2024 financial statements.

There were deficiencies noted in keeping the accounts of the LGU due to accounting errors plus lacking details of the reports made by the LGU inspectorate team, inconsistent with Section 111 of PD 1445, Section 141, Volume III, Section 4 (a) of Chapter 2, Volume I of the New Government Accounting System Manual for Local Government Units and Item 71 of International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS), thereby resulting to financial misstatement totaling P0.947 million.

The absconded project, “Construction of Multi-Purpose Building/Barangay at Barangay Bonacao, Bulalang, Dao, San Jose & Sto. Domingo (Phase 2),” with a contract price of P7.995 million had various deficiencies contrary to Section 28, Article II and Section 7, Article III, of the 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines, COA Circular Nos. 2015-009 & 2013-004, Sections 39.1, 39.2, 68 and Annexes ‘E’ & ‘I’ of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (R-IRR) of Republic Act (RA) 9184, and the Uniform Guidelines for Blacklisting of Manufacturers, Suppliers, Distributors, Contractors, and Consultants of the GPPB; thereby casting doubt on the transparency of the monitoring reports of the LGU and exposing the interests of the LGU to risks. Fair presentation in the financial statements is also adversely affected due to the understatement of Asset by P2.45 million, understatement of liability by P2.021 million, understatement of income by P397,897.44, and a noted need for prior period adjustment to equity of P35,876.00.

Fund transfer of BIR remittance amounting to P1.545 million from Trust Fund (TF) to General Fund (GF) was not supported by Disbursement Voucher (DV) and proper supporting documentation showing the necessary information to verify the validity of the transaction made; thus, non-compliance to Item a.1 of Section 7.4.1 and Item a, b, & f of Section 8.1 of PRDP Scale Up Financial Management Operation Guidelines of April 2024 Edition, thereby casts doubt on the validity and reliability of the transaction made and affects the fair presentation of the submitted financial reports.

Disbursements relating to the LGU PRDP Project, “Concreting of Mahayag, Namnam-Iglugsad-Kibongcog Farm-to-Market Road,” totaling P24.725 million had various deficiencies contrary to the approved Financing Mix Table as stated in the Implementation Management Agreement (IMA) and Section 4.3.4 and 7.6 of PRDP Scale Up Financial Management Operation Guidelines of April 2024 Edition; thereby casting doubt propriety of the cost sharing scheme implemented by the LGU San Fernando and the fairness of the presentation and disclosures in the Notes to Financial Statements.

The Reconciliation between the ‘Actual Amounts’ in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) – General Fund and the Statement of Financial Performance – General Fund for the year ended December 31, 2024, showed entity differences P23.605 million under MOOE and Capital Outlay without proper disclosures regarding the breakdown of the afore-cited differences contrary to Section 1 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 and Paragraphs 7 and 46 of IPSAS 1; thereby adversely affecting fair presentation of the Notes to Financial Statements.

The Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and the disbursement vouchers along with the corresponding supporting documents related to the utilized amount of P416,874.58 (out of the total fund transfer of P3.103 million) of the Philippine Multisectoral Nutrition Project (PMNP) implemented by the LGU in CY 2024 were not submitted to the Office of the Auditor contrary to Section 26 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, Section 7.2.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-006, and Paragraph 27 of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1 and item 13 of Annex 1 of the Philippine Multisectoral Nutrition Project World Bank guidelines dated May 31, 2022, thereby casting doubts on the validity and propriety of the implemented project and affects the fair presentation of CY 2024 Financial Statements.

The BAC failed to invite a duly recognized private group in a sector or discipline related to the PRDP infrastructure project, “Concreting of Mahayag, Namnam-Iglugsad-Kibongkog Farm-to-Market Road,” with an ABC of P260 million and, an NGO which pass the criteria in sections 13.2(a) and 13.2(b) of the IRR, in violation of R.A. 9184 hence, limiting the intention of the government in enhancing transparency in the government procurement process.

The LGU released the first progress payment to the contractor without securing Contractor’s Affidavit on payment of laborers and materials with PRDP Infrastructure project name Concreting of Mahayag, Namnam – Iglugsad – Kibongcog Farm to Market Road amounting to P24.725 million, thus contrary to Section No. 4 of PD 1445 and Section 9.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby cast doubt on the propriety of the released payment.

The procurement process of the PRDP Project, “Concreting of Mahayag, Namnam – Iglugsad – Kibongcog Farm-to-Market Road,” with a contract price of ₱241.051 million incurred 16 days of delay as compared to the suggested procurement timelines set by A.31. Milestones for Request for Bids (RFB) of Module 1: Guidelines for the Procurement of Infrastructure Subprojects under PRDP Scale Up of March 2024 Edition, thereby causing a delay in the implementation of the project initiative.

The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) failed to scrutinize the technical components of the Contractor’s capability in providing sufficient equipment for the PRDP Infrastructure Project named “Concreting of Mahayag, Namnam – Iglugsad – Kibongkog Farm-to-Market Road, with a contract price of P241.051 million wherein the List of Equipment for the Contract declared by the Contractor does not collaborate with the Equipment Utilization Schedule (EUS) and Program of Works (POW) conformed to by the Procuring Entity and the winning Contractor/Bidder, thus contrary to Section 12.1 of 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of R.A. 9184, thereby cast doubts on diligence of the BAC during the conduct of the bid evaluation and the winning bidder’s technical capability to perform and consummate the project initiative.

The program of Works (POW) for the PRDP Project "Concreting of Mahayag, Namnam-Iglugsad-Kibongkog Farm-to-Market Road" with an approved budget for the contract of P260 million does not collaborate with the Specifications that are integral parts of the contract agreement contradictory to Paragraph 3 (i) of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations—Annex A of the R.A 9184 and the Signed Contract Agreement, thereby raising doubts on the management's preparation and review process of the approved POW, technical specifications, and the contract agreement.

Certificates of Acceptance were issued to completed infrastructure projects with contract amounts aggregating to P53.2 million, which were subjected to final payment in CY 2024, even before the lapse of the defects liability period, contrary to Section 62.2.2 of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (R-IRR) of RA 9184, which is consistent with the DPWH DO No. 99, Series of 2015; thereby indirectly allowing defects to remain uncorrected.

Cash advance for Confidential Funds totaling P2.6 million was submitted along with the bulk of the monthly disbursement vouchers of the LGU and was noted to lack a necessary supporting document contrary to COA-DBM-DILG-GCG-DND Joint Circular No. 2015-01 dated January 8, 2015; thereby casting doubt on the regularity of the grant and liquidation of the cash advance and adherence of the LGU on the procedures of the Joint Circular, which risks the confidentiality of the transaction.

The Municipality submitted the liquidation of fund transfers totaling P35.233 million with unconscionable delay of 936 days on average per disbursement voucher and without any supporting Memoranda of Agreement, contrary to Section 4.6 of COA Circular 94-013 and Section 3.1.2 of COA Circular 2012-011. Thus, the municipality created bottlenecks in audit and embraced operational inefficiency.

Various goods procured by the Municipality of San Fernando, Bukidnon, totaling ₱6.99 million were paid without warranty security, in violation of Sections 54.5 and 62 of RA 9184, which exposes the LGU to the risk and difficulty of recovering damages in case of defects in the procured goods.

The Municipality granted Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) for CY 2021 to 2023 totaling P4.187 million with various deficiencies contrary to DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01, DOH AO No. 2022-01 & 039, Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, Section 344 of RA No. 7160, and the signed Memorandum of Agreement; thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the release of the HEA.

The salary and RATA claims of the LGU’s employees and officials in CY 2024 were not supported with DTRs, minutes of regular sessions, approved applications of leave, accomplishment reports, certificates of appearances, travel orders and other necessary supporting documents, in violation to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, Section 52 of Republic Act No. 7160, CSC Memorandum Circular No. 21 s. 1991, COA Circular No. 2012-001, and Local Budget Circular No. 103; hence, the propriety of the paid salaries could not be ascertained.

Foreign travel expenses totaling P200,000.00 in CY 2024 were not supported with adequate documents contrary to Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, COA Circular 2012-001, DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2022-147, and Executive Order (EO) No. 77, thereby raising concerns about the validity, propriety, and regularity of the travel expenses.

The Municipality purchased an agricultural land with an area of (51,992 sqm) amounting to ₱7 million with various deficiencies in violation of COA Circular 2012-001, Section 10 & 13 of Executive Order No. 1035, s. 1985 and 4(6 & 8) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, thereby casting doubt on validity and propriety of the purchase of the land property.

The Municipality granted CNA Incentives totaling P4.336 million without disbursement voucher and lacking supporting documents contrary to the CSC Amended Rules and Regulations Governing the Exercise of the Right of Government Employees to Organize CY 2005, Sections 1 & 2 of Article IV, Sections 1 & 2 of Article XII, and Section 1 & 2 of Article XIII of the Rank and File Employees Union of San Fernando Constitution and By-Laws, DBM Budget Circular No. 2024-4 dated November 11, 2024, Section 344 of RA 7160, and Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445; thereby raising concerns on the validity and propriety of the grant of CNA Incentives.

The Municipality of San Fernando failed to comply with the documents required by COA TSO and/or the local auditors in relation to the auditorial and technical review of projects with contract prices totaling P155.371 million, contrary to Sections 3.1.1 and 3.1.4 of COA Circular 2009-001 and Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445; thereby creating difficulty in facilitating the completion of the post-audit of COA.

Infrastructure Projects funded under 20 per cent Local Development Fund (LDF) administered by the LGU with a total amount of P12.174 million were delayed, temporarily suspended, and un-updated in the quarterly engineering reports thus, these deficiencies are inconsistent with Section 4 (8) & 58 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, Item 3.5 of Annex “A” of GPBB Resolution No. 09-2005, and Section 477 (3) of Republic Act No. 7160, thereby casting doubt on the management capability of implementing by-administration project initiatives and, consequently, depriving the community of the benefits of their timely implementation.

The Financial Assistance (FA) guidelines prescribed by the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) Resolution to the Municipality's needing constituents do not harmonize with national standards/guidelines, which raises questions as to the proper use of resources and whether the FA claims faithfully adhere to existing national guidelines consistent with Sections 2 and 4 (7) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 305 (h) of Republic Act No. 7160, also known as the Local Government Code of 1991.

The Land property owned by the LGU situated in Barangay Bonacao, San Fernando, Bukidnon, under TD No. 22-019-0002-05013 with a market value of P226,850.00, which was intended for evacuation center, was occupied by locals without legal documents or agreement to reside and erect temporary dwellings in the area thus, contrary to Sections 2 and 4(2) of Presidential Decree No. 1445; thereby casting doubt on the faithfulness of the management in its commitment to safeguarding its assets and risking the possibility of losing actual possession of the Land.

The accuracy and reliability of the year-end balances of the Cash Local Treasury and Cash in Bank- Local Currency, Current Accounts in the amount of ₱40,118.37 and ₱84.425 million, respectively are doubtful due to: a) recording of ₱122,265.79 worth of check payments released in the ensuing year; b) deposits in the ensuing year amounting ₱3.630 million were recorded as deposits in the cashbooks and in the books of accounts and treated as deposit in transit in the bank reconciliation statement as of December 31, 2024; c) reconciling items that remain unadjusted; and d) other deficiencies noted, contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, Section 43 and 44 (i) of Chapter 1 of MNGAS, Section 3.3 of COA Circular No. 96-011, Section 74 of PD 1445.

The balances of Intra-agency accounts “Due from Other Funds” and “Due to Other Funds” at year-end in the amount of ₱8.89 million and ₱7.158 million, respectively, remained unreconciled which resulted to a total variance of ₱1.732 million, a non-compliance to paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, thereby casting doubt on the correctness and reliability of the balances in the financial statements.

The non submission of the report to the accounting office on uncollected rental fees from the stallholders of the public market and housing unit owners at Paglaum Village of LGU-Sumilao amounting to ₱4.348 million as of December 31, 2024 resulted to the non-recognition of Income and Receivable, an indication of lapse in internal control of the management, thus affecting the fairness of the affected accounts in the Financial Statement contrary to of IPSAS 1 and Sections 123 and 124 of PD 1445, respectively.

The collectability, existence and correctness of valuation of the “Due from LGUs” account is doubtful due to the inclusion of (a) dormant receivables totaling ₱1.803 million and (b) long outstanding fund transfers to barangays aging eight years totaling ₱0.600 million, contrary to IPSAS 1 and COA Circular Nos. 2016-005 and 94-013, resulting to unreliable account balance and delayed recognition of the appropriate Asset and/or Expense account for the utilization of funds transferred.

The accuracy and existence of the reported Inventory account balance as of December 31, 2024 totaling ₱251,748.73 could not be ascertained due to the 1) inconsistency in the computation of shortage/overage in the RPCI; 2) non submission of RPCI of other items, 3) non-recording of receipt of vaccines, 4) purchases of accountable forms expensed outright and unaccounted unissued items, and other deficiencies observed, thereby casting doubt on the reliability of the balance presented in the Statement of Financial Position at the end of CY 2024.

The accuracy and reliability of the PPE account “Road Networks” amounting to ₱57.569 million (net of depreciation) as of December 31, 2024 could not be relied upon due to (1) non-maintenance of records, (2) RPCPPE submitted not the prescribed format, (3) absence of road network component/s, and (4) incomplete data of the lapsing schedule and erroneous computation of depreciation expense, and (5) non-disclosure in the Notes to Financial Statements contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-008, thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the amount of Road Networks presented in the Statement of Financial Position at the end of CY 2024.

The validity and legality of reported Accounts Payable balance in the aggregate amount of ₱5.601 million could not be established due to the presence of dormant accounts and absence of valid proof/information to warrant recognition of obligations which is not in consonance with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) No. 1 and Section 4(s), Volume I of the NGAS Manual, thus, affecting the true financial position of the municipality at the end of CY 2024.

Inter-agency payables representing withheld premium contributions and loan amortizations for the accounts Due to BIR and Due to Philhealth in the aggregate amount of ₱219,009.99 were not remitted in full within the prescribed period contrary to pertinent BIR Revenue Regulations and Section 18 of the IRR of the National Health Insurance Act of 2013, thereby exposing the Municipality and the employees to the possible imposition of penalty and surcharges for the late remittance thereof. Moreover, the Due to GSIS and Due to PAG-IBIG accounts reported a negative ending balance in the aggregate amount of ₱496,546.90 as of December 31, 2024, thus casting doubt on the reliability of the affected balances as reflected in the Financial Statement contrary to IPSAS 1, and its compliance to the Republic Act (RA) No. 8291, Section E.4 of HDMF Circular No. 275 dated January 22, 2010.

Deficiencies were noted with the accounting records in relation to the “Trust Liabilities-DRRMF” account which is not in consonance to Sections 111 and 123 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, and Sections 4.4, 5.1.12, and 5.1.13 of COA Circular No. 2012-002.

Various lacking supporting documents were observed in the utilization by the Municipality of Sumilao of the DOH funds for Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) in CY 2024 totaling ₱1.519 million contrary to the executed Memorandum of Agreement, DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01, DOH AO No. 2022-001 and Section 4(6) of PD 1445, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the release of the HEA.

Foreign travelling expenses totaling P460,000.00 in CY 2024 had various deficiencies contrary to COA Circular 2012-001, COA Circular No. 1996-004, DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2022-147, Executive Order (EO) No. 77, and COA Circular 2015-009, thereby raising concerns about the validity, propriety, and recording of the travel expenses.

Deficiencies were observed in the payments of honoraria to BAC and TWG members amounting to P427,312.50 due to the absence of some of the documentary requirements, contrary to Item 6, Section 4 of PD No. 1445, Section 5.7.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 and DBM Budget Circular NO. 2004-5A.

Pertinent guidelines in the monitoring and reporting of the LGU’s Special Education Fund were not complied with due to the late and/or non-submission of the approved SEF Budget, and the quarterly and annual SEF Budget Accountability reports to the concerned offices, which is inconsistent with Items 5.5 and 6.1, DepEd-DBM-DILG Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2017, thereby undermining transparency and accountability over these funds.

Eighteen (18) completed projects aggregating ₱75.247 million were still recorded under the Construction in Progress accounts as of December 31, 2024, owing to the non-reconciliation of engineering and accounting reports and pending turnover from source agencies, contrary to Paragraphs 14 and 71 of the IPSAS No. 17 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby, overstated the Property, Plant and Equipment and Government Equity accounts both by ₱5.087 million, while understated the Depreciation Expense and overstated the Surplus/(Deficit) accounts both by ₱3.202 million in the consolidated financial statements.

LGU Talakag improperly recognized worth ₱15.794 million of family food packs donated by DSWD as Welfare Goods for Distribution and Grants and Donations in Kind in the CY 2024 Statements of Financial Position and Financial Performance, respectively, instead of: (1) recording them in the Registry of Donated Relief Goods for DRRM, (2) complying with the reportorial requirements in prescribed formats, and (3) disclosing the same in the Notes to the Financial Statements, inconsistent to the accounting and reporting guidelines of COA Circular 2014-002, thereby, compromising the transparency and accountability in the use of disaster relief donations while potentially affecting the decision making of users of financial statements.

Drugs and Medicines Inventory and Medical, Dental and Laboratory Supplies Inventory accounts presented in the CY 2024 Statement of Financial Position were inaccurate stemming from the improper recording of inventories as an outright expense and non-reconciliation of pertinent records/reports, inconsistent with Paragraph 44 of IPSAS No. 12, COA Circular No. 2015-009, and Sections 114 and 121, Volume 1 of the NGAS Manual for LGUs, thus misstated the Inventories, Expenses, and Government Equity accounts by ₱7.551 million presented in the consolidated financial statements as at year-end.

The non-compliance to the accrual basis of accounting and proper recording for insurance and fidelity bond premiums resulted in the overstatement of the Insurance Expense and Fidelity Bond Premium accounts by ₱324,139.78 and ₱54,055.15, respectively, contrary to IPSAS No. 1, Section 4.a of Vol. 1 of the Manual on NGAS for LGUs and the Revised Chart of Accounts for LGUs, thereby, casts doubt on to the accuracy and reliability of related account balances presented in the financial statements.

The municipality failed to formulate guidelines for the effective collection of rent income from heavy equipment totaling ₱1.018 million in CY 2024, inconsistent with Section 70 (D) of Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM), 2nd Edition, Section 3 of SB Ordinance No. 026, s. 2014, and corresponding Memorandum of Agreement, thereby exposing the LGU to the risk of delayed collection, inaccurate computation of rent income, and non-accrual of income for November and December 2024 rentals amounting ₱0.218 million.

The municipality failed to facilitate the proper disposition of dormant receivable accounts aging 10 to 34 years totaling ₱7.580 million, inclusive of unidentifiable and unverifiable “beginning balances” totaling ₱7.332 million, inconsistent to the International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS) No. 1, COA Circulars Nos. 2023-008 and 2016-005, thereby, compromising the reliability of the financial statements by overstating receivables and equity accounts.

Financial assistance granted to various barangays of the Municipality of Talakag from the years 2013 to 2023 totaling ₱11.145 million, inclusive of unidentifiable and unverifiable “beginning balances” totaling ₱0.263 million remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2024, in contrast to the Memoranda of Agreement (MOA) between the Municipal Government of Talakag and its component barangays, therefore, proper utilization and timely implementation of the identified program, project or activity could not be determined while compromising the reliability of the financial statements by overstating Due from LGU and Equity accounts, aside from hindering barangays with unliquidated balances to receive additional financial assistance for developmental projects.

The Municipal Accounting Office failed to submit Disbursement Vouchers, Liquidation Reports, General Journal accounts, including various Journal Entry Vouchers for the month of December 2024, totaling ₱999.685 million, contrary to Section 347 of RA 7160 and Section 7.2.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009, thus, the propriety and legality of the transactions could not be ascertained and may affect the rendition of auditor’s opinion on the financial statements due to audit scope limitation.

Various deficiencies totaling ₱5.593 million were noted in relation to local travel expenses incurred during the LGU’s Annual Team Building Activity in Metro Manila, contrary to DILG-DBM JMC No. 02 dated September 23, 2016, DILG MC No. 2011-59 dated April 25, 2011, EO 77, AO No. 6 (s. 2017), and COA Circular No. 2012-003, thereby, the validity, propriety, and the judicious and prudent use of government funds were not properly established and attained.

Foreign travel-related expenses incurred during benchmarking at Cheonan Dairy Cooperatives, Farms and other Agricultural Sites in South Korea have various noted deficiencies totaling ₱1.696 million, contrary to DILG and DBM JMC No. 02 dated September 23, 2016, DILG MC No. 2022-147 dated November 22, 2022, EO 77, and COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby raising doubts as to the validity, propriety and regularity of the travel claims.

Benchmarking activities conducted by the Municipality amounting to ₱1.008 million were not duly supported with sufficient documentation and with other noted observations, contrary to DILG and DBM JMC No. 2 dated September 23, 2016, EO 77 dated March 15, 2019, and COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby affecting the regularity and propriety of such disbursements.

Foreign travel-related expenses incurred by certain LGU officials during their respective trips in USA and Japan have various noted deficiencies totaling ₱586,185.00, contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-01 and AO No. 6 (s. 2017), hence, the validity, propriety and accountability over the disbursed government funds, including its judicious and prudent use, were not properly established and attained.

The Municipality improperly granted honoraria for BAC, TWG members, and BAC Secretariat amounting to ₱650,500 with the following deficiencies: (1) failure to adhere to the prescribed maximum honorarium rate per procurement project, and (2) lacking Notices of Award (NoA) to the winning bidders of procurement activities being claimed, contrary to Section 4 of PD 1445, COA Circular No. 2012-001, and Sections 4.0 and 5.3 of DBM Budget Circular No. 2004-5A, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the disbursed transactions.

The Municipality granted Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) in November 2024 for the period August 2021 to December 2022 totaling ₱6.577 million with incomplete documentation contrary to the executed Memorandum of Agreement, DOH-DBM JAO No. 2023-01, DOH AO No. 2022-001 and Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the release of the HEA.

The Municipality of Talakag failed to submit the semestral Procurement Monitoring Reports (PMR), Annual Procurement Plans (APPs) and Agency Procurement Compliance and Performance Indicator (APCPI) Results to the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) as mandated under Section 12.2 of the Revised IRR of RA 9184 and reiterated by GPPB Circular Nos. 03-2015 and 02-2020, hindering the GPPB’s ability to properly monitor the procurement activities of the municipality during the year.

The existence and accuracy of the Cash-in-Bank, Local Currency accounts, amounting to ₱621.422 million, presented in the CY 2024 financial statements could not be relied upon due to the unadjusted or uncorrected 466 bank and book reconciling items presented in the BRSs as of December 31, 2024, which include: a) 413 book balance reconciling items, comprising ₱93.841 million for addition and ₱61.058 million for deduction, with a net balance of ₱32.783 million; b) 27 items presented as “Deposits in Transit” totaling ₱19.749 million aging from five months to over 19 years; and c) 26 stale checks presented as outstanding checks, totaling ₱0.414 million, aging from one year to over nine years, which were inconsistent with Sections 74 and 112 of PD No. 1445, and Section 3 of COA Circular No. 96-011, and Sections 32 and 59 of the NGAS Manual for LGUs, Volume I, thereby impairing the reliability and accuracy of financial reporting, increasing the risk of misstatements in the financial statements, and resulting in potential non-compliance with established regulations.

The accuracy and reliability of the Advances to SDOs and O&Es accounts in the CY 2024 Consolidated Financial Statements, totaling ₱50.468 million and ₱11.344 million, respectively, could not be ascertained due to an unreconciled balance of ₱10.674 million between the financial statements and the supporting schedules for the General Fund, contrary to the IPSAS No. 1, Section 111 of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby casting doubts on the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The existence and accuracy of the reported inventory balances, totaling ₱188.695 million, could not be fully verified due to: a) the non-completion of the physical count and non-submission of the RPCI for the 13 out of the 21 inventory accounts, and b) the variance totaling ₱92.481 million between the records maintained by the CAO and the submitted RPCI prepared by the CGSO for eight inventory accounts, contrary to Section 111(2) of PD No. 1445, Section 124 of the NGAS Manual for LGUs, Volume 1, and Chapter Three of the NGICS, thereby, the inventory account balances in the CY 2024 Consolidated Statement of Financial Position may not be fairly presented and may not accurately reflect the true condition of the LGU’s assets, while the reliability of financial reporting and the effectiveness of internal controls over inventory management were rendered doubtful.

The existence and accuracy of the PPE accounts, with carrying costs totaling ₱3.418 billion, as presented in the CY 2024 financial statements, are doubtful due to an unreconciled balance of ₱125.521 million compared to the RPCPPE, which persisted because the LGU failed to utilize the one-time PPE account cleansing, in violation of Sections 58, 111, and 112 of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2020-006, thereby compromising the fair presentation of accounts, leaving property accountabilities unresolved and unaccounted for, and failing to safeguard assets against loss and misappropriation.

Accounts Payable recognized for various transactions in the LGU’s books of accounts under the General Fund as of year-end, totaling ₱11.705 million, were not properly substantiated with duly accomplished Acceptance and Inspection Reports (AIR) and/or any proof of receipt or delivery of purchased items contrary to Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445, COA Circular No. 2015-009, and Section 118 of the NGAS Manual for LGUs, Volume I, thereby casting doubts on the occurrence, existence, and validity of claims to or obligations of the LGU, and affecting fair presentation of the account in the year-end financial statements.

The Accounts Payable for the unpaid portion of the contract costs of three completed PRDP Projects were not accrued and recognized at year-end, while the paid portion remained in the CIP accounts, thus total project costs amounting to ₱138.999 million were not reclassified to the appropriate PPE accounts, derecognized and transferred to the General Fund books of accounts, and provided with depreciation contrary to the IPSAS Nos. 1, 17, and 29 and the NGAS Manual for LGUs, Volume I, which resulted to the overstatement of the CIP accounts and understatement of the Accounts Payable account in the PRDP Trust Fund year-end financial statements by ₱134.095 million and ₱4.904 million, respectively, and the understatement of the PPE accounts and the Depreciation Expense in the General Fund year-end financial statements by ₱136.442 million and ₱2.558 million, respectively.

The existence, accuracy, and reliability of Loans Payable account balance of ₱570.654 million presented at year-end is doubtful due to the inability of the LGU to: a) classify and present the current portion of the loan balance; b) submit amortization schedules and other relevant documentation for all existing loans payable; and c) retain and provide copies of all executed loan contracts and agreements of the LGU, contrary to IPSAS No. 1 and Section 111 of PD No. 1445, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the year-end financial statements and precluded further analysis and review of the account.

Management fees totaling ₱2.650 million from the operations of the PS-LGU Depot for CYs 2020 to 2024 were not collected, recognized as income, nor recorded as receivables due to: a) delays in billing, caused by the expiration of the previous Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and the delay in the approval of the subsequent MOA between the LGU and the PS-DBM, and b) the non-submission of the billing statements to the CAO, contrary to the IPSAS No. 1 and the provisions in the MOA, thereby understating the relevant revenue, receivable, and equity accounts of the LGU by ₱0.870 million, ₱2.650 million, and ₱1.780 million, respectively, and deprived the LGU of the income and funds it could have used for its programs, projects, and activities.

Expenses for foreign travel of 29 LGU officials and employees to Incheon, South Korea, for benchmarking on several dates, totaling ₱4.534 million, were: a) erroneously recorded as Traveling Expenses – Local and b) not properly substantiated by the required documents, including a duly approved travel authority from the DILG Regional Director, supporting computation of the DSA, and other necessary documentation, contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009, Section 4.3 of DILG MC No. 2022-147, Sections 9 and 14 of EO No. 77, and COA Circular No. 2012-001 , thereby rendered the validity, propriety, and regularity of the travel claims doubtful, overstated the Traveling Expenses – Local account, and omitted Traveling Expenses – Foreign account by ₱4.534 million in the year-end financial statements.

Registration Fee for the Benchmarking Activity at Japan, amounting to ₱0.160 million, was: a) erroneously recorded as “Traveling Expenses – Local” account, and b) not properly substantiated by the required documents for foreign travel, contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009 and COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby rendered the propriety and reasonableness of the payment of registration fees doubtful, overstated the Traveling Expenses – Local account by ₱0.160 million and omitted Traveling Expenses – Foreign account in the year-end financial statements.

The accuracy and reliability of the SCBAA are doubtful due to the non-reconciliation of variances totaling ₱341.240 million, resulting from the difference between the actual amounts reported therein and those in the SFPer which stems from the failure to provide and complete reconciliation reports, contrary to Paragraphs 47 and 48 of IPSAS No. 24, thereby hindering the LGU's ability to effectively discharge its accountability obligations by identifying major sources of variance between budgeted and recognized financial amounts.

Comparison between the CY 2024 Financial Statements and the SSAF as of December 31, 2024 for the PRDP revealed an overall variance of ₱0.198 million, contrary to Section 111(1) of PD No. 1445 and Item 6.4.1(a)1 of the PRDP Financial Management Operations Guidelines, thereby casting doubt on fair presentation of the financial reports.

Cash advances totaling ₱4.287 million granted to LGU’s officers and employees remain outstanding and unliquidated for periods ranging from six months to over ten years, due to: a) the non-implementation of the internal control measures in the grants and liquidations, b) non-imposition of the prescribed sanctions, and c) erroneous recording of liquidations as reflected by negative balances in the report, contrary to Section 89 of PD No. 1445, Section 1.2 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, and COA Circular No. 97-002, thereby precluded the determination of the propriety of fund utilization for their intended purposes, left government funds vulnerable to misuse, and rendered the report on the status of unliquidated cash advances inaccurate and unreliable

Cash advances for Confidential Expenses totaling ₱22.300 million remained outstanding and unliquidated for over ten years due to lack of proof that liquidation reports were submitted to and Credit Notices were issued by the COA Chairman’s Office, contrary to the provisions of COA Circular No. 2003-003, thereby actual rendition of liquidation reports is doubtful, propriety of the utilization of Confidential Funds could not be ascertained and government funds are exposed to risk of loss or wastage.

The CNA Incentives for CYs 2023 and 2024 were granted to LGU officials and employees at ₱30,000.00 per personnel, which was not in conformity with the ₱25,000.00 limit stipulated in the Agreement, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the disbursements.

The validity and propriety of disbursements totaling ₱7.900 Million against the Support to Peace and Order Budget Allocation could not be ascertained due to: a) incomplete documentation for expenses incurred during the peace and order monitoring of the 23rd Charter Day Celebration, amounting to ₱1.500 million, and b) payments made to eight uniformed personnel totaling ₱0.800 million per month for services rendered from September 2023 to April 2024 which may constitute double compensation and lack of legal basis, contrary to Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445, Section 8, Article IX-B of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, and COA Circular No. 2013-003, thereby casts doubts whether funds allocated for Peace and Order projects, programs, and activities were utilized as intended.

Approved contract time extensions due to bad weather condition, attached to the disbursement vouchers for payments of PRDP Projects’ progress billings, were not sufficiently supported by extended performance securities, nor by other documents justifying the time extensions granted to the contractors, contrary to Section 4 of PD No. 1445 and Items 7.5 and 47 of Section IV – General Conditions of the Contract of the Philippine Bidding Documents prescribed under PRDP Module 1 – Infrastructure Project Procurement Guidelines, raising doubts about their validity; furthermore, any resulting unjustified delays may deprive the public of the immediate use of the projects, and the safeguard of the LGU’s financial interest against contractor’s noncompliance with its contractual obligations could not be ascertained.

The “Three-Strike” rule and contract termination for the ongoing project “Concreting of Jct. Brgy Mabuhay to Brgy Banlag proper to Sitio Pantaron FMR” costing ₱238.528 million were not enforced despite the negative slippage exceeding 15% contrary to Item 3.6.5 of the PRDP Intensified Building-Up of Infrastructure and Logistics for Development (I-BUILD) Operations Manual and Section 5.10.c of the PRDP Implementation Management Agreement (IMA), to the detriment of both the LGU and the national government, as the negative slippage hampers critical infrastructure, disrupts public service delivery, and undermines the effective use of government funds.

The turnover of furniture, fixtures, equipment, and other PPE from contractors to the LGU upon completion of PRDP projects was not adequately documented and accounted for in accordance with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) DO No. 7, series of 2006, thus, these LGU properties are at risk of loss, misappropriation, or unauthorized use.

Salaries paid to the LGU’s casual employees amounting to ₱64.641 million for the payroll periods from January to September 2024 were inadequately supported by the required documentation contrary with Sections 4(6) and 4(7) of PD No. 1445 and Item 4.1.3 of Commission on Audit (COA) Circular No. 2012-001, thereby raising doubts on the propriety of the salaries paid during that period.

Unrelated expenditures amounting to ₱0.743 million were paid from the 5% LDRRMF contrary to Section 21 of RA No. 10121 and the guidelines on the allocation and utilization of the said fund prescribed in National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) – DBM – DILG Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2013-01, thereby defeating the purpose of the fund to develop and improve the City’s disaster risk management capacity.

The LGU has allocated ₱94.982 million, or 5% of the total CY 2024 budget, and has utilized ₱91.764 million, or 97% of the allocated amount, for the implementation of various Gender-Responsive Programs, Activities, and Projects (PAPs), thereby fulfilling the requirements set forth in Section 35 of the General Provisions of the GAA of FY 2024.

Fifty-seven (57) reconciling items (comprising of unbooked stale checks, debit memo, outstanding bank transfers, bank and book errors) remained unrecorded/unadjusted in the books of accounts while three (3) PPSB bank accounts that were already closed but still had book balances, totaling ₱0.737 million and ₱0.130 million, respectively, contrary to Sections 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, resulting in a net understatement of ₱0.589 million which affected the accuracy and reliability of the Cash in Bank and the corresponding accounts reflected in the financial statements for CY 2025, aside from the doubtful existence of those bank accounts already closed with a net negative balance in the books of accounts amounting ₱64,920.50.
