Inaccurate and unreliable balances of the Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivable accounts were presented in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025 due to: (1) the non-establishment of receivables at the beginning of the CY 2025 for failure of MTO to submit a certified list of tax dues to MAccO and (2) the non-reconciliation of the accounting, treasury, and assessor's records, inconsistent with the provisions of PD No. 1445 and NGAS Manual for LGU, thereby understated the said accounts by ₱8.425 million each, while the Deferred RPT and Deferred SET payable accounts were understated by ₱8.425 million, and ₱10.226 million, respectively.

The municipality failed to facilitate the proper disposition of dormant receivable accounts aging 10 to 35 years totaling ₱3.298 million inconsistent to the International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS) No. 1, COA Circulars Nos. 2023-008 and 2016-005, thereby, compromising the reliability of the financial statements by overstating receivables and equity accounts.

The non-reconciliation among records of the GSO, MAccO and the Inventory Committee, along with other noted observations is contrary to the NGAS Manual for LGUs, thereby indicating weak internal control over the inventory management and casting doubt on the accuracy, reliability and existence of the inventory accounts reported in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025.

Absence of verifiable documents to establish the transactions in the amount of ₱11.186 million recorded in Accounts Payable is not in accordance to Section 4 (6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, Section 37 Volume 1 of Government Accounting and Auditing Manual, and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby, precluding the auditor to validate the existence and validity of transactions affecting the accuracy and reliability of the financial statements as of December 31, 2025.

The Municipality did not prepare and submit the required year-end financial statements for its 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) account and unnecessarily maintains two (2) bank accounts under the same special account with a total balance of ₱33.472 million per bank statements, contrary to NGAS Manual for LGUs and DOF-DBM-COA Permanent Committee Joint Circular No. 4-2012, thereby, the transparency and accountability in the receipt and usage of the 20% LDF could not be established depriving the intended users of relevant financial information that are vital in the making of well-informed and sound decision, while the monitoring and reconciliation of these multiple bank accounts provides additional and unnecessary burden to the management, specifically to the Municipal Accountant and Municipal Treasurer.

The failure of the Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO) to submit nine (9) disbursement vouchers (DVs) aggregating ₱0.565 million and to prepare the Report of Checks Issued (RCI), as well as the premature recording by the Municipal Accounting Office of these unsubmitted DVs in the Check Disbursement Journal prior to their submission to the audit team, constitute a clear deviation from Sections 43 and 44, Chapter 3, Volume I of the NGAS Manual for LGUs, resulting in unreliable accounting records, hampering audit verification of check disbursement transactions, indicating weak internal control over check disbursements, and posing accountability/legal risks to the Municipal Accountant for conclusively recording transactions in the books of accounts without any supporting document as basis.

The timely and proper remittance and deposit of collections, as well as the timely submission of monthly collection reports, were not strictly observed incurring delays of up to 16, 15, and 104 calendar days, respectively, contrary to the provisions under PD No. 1445, Local Treasury Operations Manual, and NGAS Manual for LGUs, thus resulted in weak internal control system over cash management, exposing government funds to risks of loss, misuse, or misappropriation due to undeposited cash balances, and adversely affecting the timeliness of audit procedures and the prompt verification of reported collections.

The maintenance of the unnecessary bank accounts for the Special Education Fund and Trust Fund is contrary to the One Fund Concept of accounting and the provisions of DOF-DBM-COA Permanent Committee Joint Circular No. 4-2012 dated September 11, 2012, thereby, the monitoring and reconciliation of these bank accounts provides undue burden to the Management.

The Unexpended Balance of the prior years’ LDRRMF totaling ₱21.198 million for CY 2020–2024 was not incorporated in the CY 2025 LDRRMF Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP) and Annual Investment Program as an additional fund source, while unspent CY 2018-2019 Special Trust Fund totaling ₱0.351 million was not reverted to the General Fund, inconsistent to COA Circular No. 2012-002 and NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC No. 2013-1, thus constrained the proper utilization of available funds for LDRRM programs/projects/activities and exposed the LGU to possible risks due to non-compliance with prescribed procedures in utilizing the Unexpended LDRRMF.

Salaries and wages paid to all regular and casual employees of LGU Baungon in CY 2025 have various noted deficiencies, contrary to the provisions of PD 1445, COA Circular 2012-001, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292 and 2025 Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service, thus, weakened internal controls over employee attendance and payroll processing, diminished accountability of supervisors, undermined the reliability of attendance records and leave balances, and cast doubt on the validity and propriety of incurred disbursements aggregating ₱60.733 million.

The Local School Board (LSB) of LGU Baungon failed to submit the required SEF Utilization Reports to the DepEd, DBM, and Sangguniang Bayan, contrary to Item 6.1 of the DepEd-DBM-DILG Joint Circular no. 1 s. 2017, thus, the intention of such guidelines to promote and enhance transparency and accountability over the utilization of SEF was not properly achieved due to its omission in providing relevant information to the intended users of said reports.

The balance of the “Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants Inventory” account in the Financial Statement at the end of Calendar Year (CY) 2025 does not accurately reflect the actual inventory levels due to the: (i) presence of non-moving and unidentified lumped balances totaling ₱10.312 million; (ii) improper recognition of inventories and liabilities amounting to ₱1.171 million; (iii) accounting errors aggregating ₱0.564 million; and (iv) discrepancies amounting to ₱4.409 million between the Subsidiary Ledger (SL) balances and the confirmed balances stored at the fuel suppliers as confirmed by the various offices of the Provincial Government, which are contrary to Section 111 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, affecting the fair presentation of the Financial Statements.

The Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) account balances as of December 31, 2025, are misstated due to: (a) non-recording and under recording of donated properties amounting to at least ₱3.098 million; (b) undervaluation of PPE items recorded at nominal amounts; (c) improper recognition of PPE items arising from financial assistance to other LGUs with an aggregate net book value of ₱828.478 million; (d) unidentified PPE items recorded in lump sums totaling ₱42.285 million; and (e) improper preparation of the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE). These conditions are contrary to existing accounting standards and guidelines, thereby adversely affecting the accuracy, reliability, and correctness of PPE balances reported in the Statement of Financial Position as at year-end.

The Construction-in-Progress (CIP) Account includes: (a) unidentified and non-moving lump-sum items totaling to ₱78.849 million, and (b) completed projects totaling to ₱28.329 million, which are not in strict adherence to Sections 111 and 112 of PD No. 1445, otherwise known as “Government Auditing Code of the Philippines”, COA Circular No. 2002- 003 dated June 20, 2002, and COA Resolution No. 2014-003 dated January 24, 2014, thus, the CIP balance in the Statement of Financial Position of the PGB amounting to ₱1.504 billion as of December 31, 2025 could not be relied upon.

The financial statement balances of the PPE and other affected accounts as of December 31, 2025, are unreliable due to the inclusion of completed projects under the CIP accounts, including those with unrecognized project costs arising from non-recognition of liability for unbilled amounts, and non-recording of utilized construction materials inventory, contrary to Sections 111 and 112 of PD No. 1445, pertinent provisions of IPSAS 1, 17 and 27, and section 50, Chapter 3 of Volume 1 of the Manuals of the New Government Accounting Systems (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGU), thereby affecting the accuracy, reliability, and correctness of account balance reported in the Financial Statements as at year-end.

CY 2022 and CY 2024 tax payables in the total amount of ₱4.049 million were charged against the CY 2025 current appropriations and recorded as expense in the CY 2025 books of accounts of the PGB, while CY 2023-2025 tax payables were not obligated and recognized in the books contrary to Section 119 of PD No. 1445, thus, the accounting entry for the disbursements totaling ₱4.049 million is erroneous, the total Taxes, Duties and Licenses Expense as of December 31, 2025 in the amount of ₱5.137 million is unreliable, and the Due to BIR Account is understated by approximately ₱2.723 million.

The reported balance of the “Due from GOCCs” account aggregating ₱319.579 million cannot be relied upon due to the: (i) significant discrepancy of ₱20.317 million between the subsidiary records and the complementary detailed records maintained by the provincial hospitals; and (ii) existence of long outstanding receivables from GOCCs totaling ₱1.3 million which have remained unliquidated from 5-12 years, affecting the fairness of presentation of the Province’s Financial Statements as of December 31, 2025.

A total amount of ₱250 million were placed in time deposits without sufficient proof that the funds were idle, which is not in consonance with Sections 21 and 22 of the COA Circular No. 92-382 dated July 3, 1992, thus there is no assurance, that the funds placed into time deposits were indeed idle and would not affect the implementation of programs, activities and projects lined-up for the year.

The Guaranty/Security Deposits Payable Account includes dormant and/or unreconciled amounts totaling to ₱40.733 million, which is not in adherence with Sections 4(4) and 4(8) of PD No. 1445, Section 62.1 and Item 6 of Annex E of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA No. 9184, thereby affecting the accuracy, reliability, and correctness of the account balance reported in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025.

The Provincial Government made final payments for completed infrastructure projects totaling ₱25.483 million (net of taxes and other deductions) as of December 31, 2025, despite the absence of required supporting documents, contrary to Sections 4(6) and 4(8) of PD No. 1445 and Item No. 9.1.1.4 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thereby casting doubt on the validity and propriety and regularity of the final payments.

Progress billing payments for the Concreting of Iba-Cabulohan-Paradise Farm-to-Market Road (FMR) at Cabanglasan, Bukidnon totaling to ₱129.321 million were not supported with complete documents, which is not in consonance with Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445 and Item No. 9.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thus, validity, propriety, and legality of the disbursements cannot be ascertained. Moreover, the Performance Bond and Contractor’s All Risk Insurance (CARI) did not cover the entire period required to be covered, which is not in adherence to Section 62.2.2.2 of the RIRR of RA No. 9184, and Clause No. 14.1 of the General Conditions of the Contract (GCC) for the project, thus, exposing the government to risk of unrecoverable losses and additional costs in the event of contractor default or project damage during the uninsured period.

Leave Credit Cards were given to separated employees without adhering to the disposal procedures prescribed in the National Archive of the Philippines (NAP) General Circular No. 5 dated October 10, 2023, thus, audit of disbursements for payment of terminal leave benefits in the total amount of ₱37.427 million could not be completed.

Salaries and wages of regular employees without sufficient accumulated leave credits were not carefully monitored by some payroll clerks in coordination with the PHRMO and PAccO, hence, leaves of absence without pay were not properly considered in the preparation of payrolls contrary to Civil Service Commission (CSC) Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 08, s. 2014, Section 5 of RA No. 8291, and Item No. 5.4 of Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Budget Circular (BC) No. 2009-3, resulting in overpayments in the total amount of ₱151,772.84.

Absences of casual employees were not supported with approved applications for leave, office order/travel orders, certificates of appearance, and/or driver’s trip tickets (for drivers), while leave credit cards of casual employees show inaccurate accumulation of leave credits contrary to the provisions of CSC MC No. 41, s. 1998, Executive Order No. 77, s. 2019, COA Circular No. 2012-001, and COA Circular No. 77-61, which may result in the overpayment of salaries and wages, carrying over of utilized leave credits to the succeeding periods, payment of salaries and wages without sufficient leave credits, monetization in excess of actual leave credits earned, and/or payment of terminal leave benefits based on overstated leave balances.

Personnel Motivation Incentives (PMIs) totaling to ₱84.146 million were paid to its appointive and elective officials and employees without adhering to the policies and other requirements of Section 33 of PD No. 807, s. 1975, CSC MC No. 01, s. 2001, the CSC-approved Program on Awards and Incentives for Service Excellence (PRAISE) of the PGB, and such other pertinent laws, rules and regulations on Employee Suggestions and Incentive Awards System, thus, validity, propriety, and legality of the disbursements could not be ascertained.

In CY 2025, honoraria totaling ₱1,893,185.24 net of tax, were paid to the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) Secretariat Section Heads and Members, who are performing procurement-related duties as part of their regular functions, for their participation in the procurement activities, contrary to Item 4 of DBM Circular No. 2004-5A and Section 45 of RA 12009 otherwise known as the New Government Procurement Act, casting doubt on the validity, propriety and regularity of the payments.

The Programs, Projects, and Activities (PPAs) identified in the CY 2025 Gender and Development (GAD) Plan and Budget (GPB) amounting to ₱360.827 million may not constitute GAD interventions while the GAD database was not prepared in accordance with pertinent guidelines, contrary to the provisions of RA No. 9710, PCW-DILG-DBM-NEDA Joint Circular (JC) No. 2013-01 and PCW Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2018-04, thereby creating doubt on whether the PPAs contributed in achieving the intended objectives of promoting gender equality and women’s empowerment.

Inter-agency payables representing withheld taxes, monthly premium contributions and loan amortizations aggregating ₱111.634 million as of December 31, 2025 were not remitted in full and within the prescribed period to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF) / Pag-IBIG, and Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth), which is not in consonance with Section 305(l) of RA No. 7160 as well as the governing rules issued by the concerned National Government Agencies (NGAs), thereby, exposing the PGB and its employees to the possible imposition of penalties and surcharges due to late remittances, delinquent repayments of loans, and underpayment of premiums.

The PGB was not able to insure all its insurable properties and to prepare and submit the Property Inventory Form (PIF), contrary to Sections 5 and 11 of RA No. 656, otherwise known as “Property Insurance Law”, and the COA Circular No. 2018-002 dated May 31, 2018, respectively, thereby exposing the PGB to the risk of significant financial losses in case of fortuitous events.

The existence, accuracy, and correctness of the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts as at December 31, 2025 could not be ascertained due to: a) the unreconciled variance amounting to ₱21.472 million between eight (8) PPE accounts in the accounting records and the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant, and Equipment (RPCPPE); b) Twelve (12) PPE items recorded in the books but not included in the RPCPPE with net book value totaling ₱676.239 million; and c) non-maintenance of Stock Cards and PPE Ledger Cards contrary to Paragraph 27 of the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1, Volume I; COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020; Sections 114, 119, and 120 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs), Volume I; and Section 491(b) of the Generally Accepted Accounting Manual (GAAM), Volume I, thus, affecting the fair presentation of the PPE balances in the financial statements.

Depreciation expense for various completed PPE, used and/or occupied by the LGU and funded through the Financial Assistance (FA) of the Provincial Government of Bukidnon (PGB), in the previous years, was not recognized in the LGU’s books, contrary to Section 111 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 and the IPSAS No. 17 resulting in non-compliance with applicable accounting regulations and led to the understatement of Depreciation Expenses by ₱1.981 million and overstatement of PPE and equity account by ₱13.018 million.

The deficiencies in the recognition, reclassification, and recording of completed CIP projects totaling ₱15.458 million, including the non-recognition of related liabilities amounting to ₱1.489 million and depreciation expense, resulted in the overstatement of the CIP accounts and understatement of the related PPE, Liability, Depreciation Expense, and Accumulated Depreciation accounts, contrary to PD No. 1445, the MNGAS, and IPSAS.

The existence, accuracy, and correctness of the Inventories accounts as at December 31, 2025 could not be ascertained due to: a) the variance amounting to ₱1.099 million between accounting and actual Inventory records; b) non-inclusion in the Report on the Physical Count of Inventories (RPCI); c) delayed and non-submission of the RPCI; and d) non- preparation and non-maintenance of Supplies Ledger Cards (SLCs) and Stock Cards (SCs), contrary to Section 111(2) of PD No. 1445, Section 114 and 124 of the MNGA) for LGUs Volume I, and Item V (1) of COA Circular No. 80-124, thereby, the inventory account balances in the CY 2025 Consolidated Statement of Financial Position may not be fairly presented and may not accurately reflect the true condition of the LGU’s assets.

The accuracy, validity, and existence of the “Receivable – Disallowances and Charges” account amounting to ₱1.838 million could not be ascertained due to the absence of supporting schedules and documentary basis to the nature and composition of the account, contrary to Section 111 of PD No. 1445 and IPSAS No. 1, thereby affecting the reliability and fair presentation of the account balances in the year-end financial statements.

There were twenty-two (22) pre-signed blank checks in the hands of the Municipal Treasurer during the physical count of accountable forms which is not in accordance to various fundamental principles for financial transactions under Section 4 of PD No. 1445, Sec 344 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160, and COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby exposing public funds to risk of misuse.

The grant of cash advances to the Disbursement Officer (DO) and Special Disbursement Officers (SDO) had the following deficiencies: a) cash advances intended for wages were not supported with approved payrolls at the time of grant; and b) cash advances granted exceeded the maximum accountability authorized under their Bond Certificates, contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-001, PD No. 1445 and Treasury Circular No. 1-2022, thereby exposing government funds to potential risk of loss and misuse and potential unrecoverable losses.

The planning, recording, and reporting of the Municipality’s 5% Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) disclosed the following deficiencies: a) the unexpended/unobligated balances of unimplemented projects chargeable against the 5% LDRRMF (General Fund) – Current and Continuing Appropriation for Capital Outlay (CO) totaling ₱1.500 million were incorrectly transferred to the Special Trust Fund; and b) the prior years’ unexpended LDRRMF balances were not incorporated in the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP) for CY 2025. These are inconsistent with Sections 4.4, 5.1.2, 5.1.11, and 5.1.12 of COA Circular No. 2012-002, thus, the propriety and legality of the LDRRMF transactions cannot be ascertained.

Planning and implementation of programs, activities, and projects (PPAs) on Gender and Development (GAD) could not be ascertained due to the following deficiencies: (a) Non-formulation of GAD Agenda; (b) No established GAD Focal Point System Technical Working Group (GFPS TWG); (c) GAD Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Team was not established; and (d) The DILG-endorsed GAD Plan and Budget and GAD Accomplishment Report for CY 2025 were not submitted to the COA Audit Team within the prescribed period, hence the direction in setting and monitoring the GAD initiatives towards the achievement of its gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE) goals were affected contrary to the provisions in Item 4.0 of PCW-DILG-DBM-NEDA Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-01, Section 9, Chapter VI, Section 36 (a) & (c) of the Magna Carta for Women, and Item V of COA Circular No. 2014-001 dated March 18, 2014.

The agency failed to submit within the prescribed period its year-end financial statements and supporting schedules for CY 2025, in violation of Section 41(2) of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2010-001, thereby hindering the audit team to render a reasonable audit opinion on management’s assertions that the financial statements are free from material misstatements, whether due to fraud or error, in accordance with IPSAS and precluded the users from its timely and useful information.

Balances of various inventory accounts cannot be relied upon due to inconsistent application of the Perpetual Inventory Method (PIM). Moreover, the inadequate internal control system of the LGU for inventory management, reporting, and accounting was not in accordance with the provisions of Sections 114 and 119 of the Manual on New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs) Volume I, thereby increasing the risk of undetected errors, misstatements, and possible loss, misuse, or misappropriation of government resources. And they greatly affect the reliability of balances of inventory accounts presented in the financial statements.

Several Journal Entry Vouchers (JEVs) prepared by the Municipal Accounting Office and submitted to the audit team did not reflect the same accounting entries in the corresponding journals, contrary to Section 111(2) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 and Section 2, Volume II of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs. Consequently, the accounting entries and other data reflected in the JEVs were rendered unreliable, the audit trail was weakened, and the required consistency in the keeping of accounts was not observed, resulting in misleading information.

Payments for prizes, repairs of motor vehicles, and financial assistance were recorded under “Other Maintenance and Operating Expenses” instead of the appropriate specific accounts, contrary to Sections 111(2) and 112 of Presidential No. 1445 and the Revised Chart of Accounts for LGUs prescribed under COA Circular No. 2015-009, resulting in inaccurate classification of expenses and misleading financial information.

The handling and recording of the cash advances and liquidations of the Disbursing Officer were found with various deficiencies and errors, in violation of Section 111(2) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, the Revised Chart of Accounts for LGUs prescribed under COA Circular No. 2015-009, and Item 4.1.7 and 6.3 of COA Circular No. 97-002, resulting in the overstatement of the “Due from Officers and Employees” account by ₱56,534.00 and the misstatement of other related accounts, an inaccurate or misleading presentation of the status of the DO’s cash advance, and the use of funds for purposes other than those for which it was granted.

The grant and recording of cash advances for travel, registration fees, and membership dues are not in accordance with COA Circular No. 97-002 and Sections 4(8) and 111(2) of Presidential Decree No. 1445; therefore, the accountabilities of cash advances were not clearly established, weakened controls over the grant and liquidation of cash advances, resulted in inaccurate accounting records, and exposed public funds to inefficient handling and increased the risk of mismanagement.

The municipality’s Annual Budget for FY 2025 was not forwarded to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review within three (3) days after its approval and contained lump-sum appropriations for certain non-office PPAs that were not supported with Supplemental AIP, in violation of Sections 56 and 447 of RA No. 7160 and Article 454(d) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA No. 7160, thereby reducing the time available for the LGU to address any observations or required modifications arising from the review and increasing the risk of unauthorized or improperly classified expenditures.

Travel expenses were paid to non-LGU personnel, not supported with sufficient documents, and improperly recorded under the account “Travel Expenses-Local”, violating Executive Order (EO) No. 77, Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, and the Revised Chart of Accounts for LGUs prescribed under COA Circular No. 2015-009; thereby, casting doubt on the legality, validity, and propriety of the disbursements, and resulting in the misclassification of the recorded expenses.

Various payments for travel expenses were found with incomplete supporting documentation and unapproved by the proper officials, in violation of Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, Section 4b of the Executive Order (EO) No. 77, and Items 1.1.4.1 and 1.2.4.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001. Thus, the audit team casts doubt on the legality, validity, and propriety of the travel expenses.

Several construction projects completed beyond the original contract period were not properly deducted with liquidated damages (LD), in violation of Item 8.1 of Annex E of the Revised IRR of RA No. 9184 and Item 71.2.4 of the IRR of RA No. 12009, resulting in potential losses to the LGU and adversely affecting the intended beneficiaries of the projects.

Payments for monetization of leave credits were not in accordance with Sections 22 and 23 of Rule XVI of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order (E.O.) No. 292, COA Circular Nos. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, and 2012-003 dated October 29, 2012, thus casting doubt on the legality, validity, and propriety of the disbursements, and the disbursements may be considered irregular.

The LGU’s existing staffing pattern shows significant reliance on job order personnel for functions that appear regular and continuing, contrary to Section 76 of Republic Act No. 7160, DOLE Wage Order No. RX-23, and Items 7.2 and 9.0 of CSC–COA–DBM Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2017, thereby posing risks to workforce stability and the effective delivery of government services.

The ‘Land’ account with a total balance of ₱10.862 million presented under Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position of the Municipality as of December 31, 2025 was found to have deficiencies, a non-compliance with Section 111 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 148 of COA Circular No. 92-386, thus, the accuracy, completeness, and reliability of the ‘Land” account cannot be reasonably assured.

Completed projects funded from fully liquidated fund transfers totaling ₱17.014 million were not properly recorded in the books of accounts of the Municipality, a noncompliance with Section 3 Chapter 1 Volume 3 of the New Government Accounting System Manual and DILG Memorandum Circular Nos. 2020-088 and 2023-063. Consequently, the accounts “Property, Plant, and Equipment” was understated by ₱17.014 million and the “Inter-agency Payables” was overstated by ₱16.929 million in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025.

Deficiencies were noted in the sale and accounting of municipal lands, including the failure to derecognize sold land from the “Land” account, the non-recognition of deferred income totaling ₱3.511 million, and the absence of complete and readily verifiable data for the land sold by the Municipality, which is not compliant to RA No. 7160, PD 1445, and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thus, raise doubts regarding the propriety and legality of the transactions and the accuracy of the affected accounts in the Municipality’s financial statements for Calendar Year 2025.

Four (4) completed infrastructure projects amounting to ₱22.464 million, funded through transfers from local and national government agencies were still recorded under “Construction in Progress (CIP)” in the Trust Fund books of accounts, which is not in compliance with Section 50 Chapter 3 Volume 1 of the New Government Accounting System Manual and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thus, the “Road Networks” account is understated by ₱22.464 million, while the CIP account is overstated by the same amount.

The Municipality implemented the Second Tranche of the Updated Salary Schedule pursuant to Executive Order No. 64 but without the required SB authorization from the Sanggunian, a non-compliance to Section 5.0 of Local Budget Circular (LBC) No. 165, thus, cast doubt on the legality and correctness of the salary increase granted to its regular employees.

A total of 1,660 accountable forms were used and remitted by personnel other than the original Accountable Officers (AO) to whom they were issued, a non-compliance to Section 25 of COA Circular No. 92-382, thereby weakening established protocols on the transfer of accountability and complicating the systematic tracking of collections and deposits.

Some Accountable Officers did not properly accomplish their cashbooks in accordance with the prescribed forms and required information under Book II of the Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM) 2nd Edition, as a result, the cashbooks did not provide complete and accurate record of all cash receipts, remittances or deposits, and cash advances or disbursements which caused the delay in the reconciliation of accounts and increase the risk that errors or issues involving public funds might not be timely identified.

The Collectors failed to accurately prepare the monthly Report of Accountability for Accountable Forms (RAAF), and the Municipal Treasurer is delayed in the submission of the Consolidated Report of Accountability for Accountable Forms (CRAAF), contrary to Section 86 (G) Nos. (1) and (2), Book II, of the Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM), 2nd Edition. As a result, the receipt, issuance, and return of accountable forms were not properly monitored which led to the non-presentation of 27,938 pieces of accountable forms during the cash examination conducted on November 03, 2025, exposing government funds to possible misappropriation.

Fuel consumption of the LGU were not properly monitored and reported by the General Services Office (GSO) and were not properly supported with complete documentary requirements, contrary to Section 4 (6) and Section 123 of P.D. 1445, Section 9.3.1 of COA Circular 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012 and the provisions of the Manual on Audit of Fuel Consumption of Government Motor Vehicles as prescribed by COA Circular No. 77-61 dated September 26, 1977, thus, transparency, accountability, equity, efficiency, and economy in the procurement of fuel could not be guaranteed thereby exposing the Government to possible wasteful, excessive, unnecessary, and irregular expenditures for fuel consumption.

Disbursement vouchers for payments of progress billings totaling to ₱39.125 million did not have complete supporting documents which is not in accordance with Section 4 (6) and 4 (7) of P.D. No. 1445, otherwise known as the “Government Auditing Code of the Philippines,” and COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thus, cast doubt on the validity and propriety of the claims.

Cash Advances granted to 28 LGU officials/employees and other individuals totaling ₱2.501 million remained unliquidated beyond the prescribed period for liquidation contrary to Section 89 of P.D. 1445, Item 1.2 of COA Circular 2012-001, Item 5 of COA Circular 97-002 and CSC Memorandum Circular No. 23, s. 2019 which exposed the funds to possible loss, misuse or misapplication that calls for LGU’s immediate attention and decisive actions.

Procurement of supplies, materials and equipment in the total amount of ₱4.215 million for the implementation of various programs, projects, and activities of the LGU were not in accordance with Section 4(6) of P.D. 1445, Section 9.1.3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, Section 53 of Chapter 2, Volume II of the NGAS Manual for Local Government Units and Section 4.7.3 of COA Circular 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022 and RA 9184 and its IRR, resulting to ineffective and inefficient procurement activities and doubt exist as to the validity and regularity of the disbursements.

Irregular and unnecessary travel expenditures totaling ₱1.798 million were incurred in CY 2025, in violation to Sections 2 and 4 of P.D. No. 1445, COA Circular No. 2012-003, and R.A. 9184 (as amended by R.A. 12009), which resulted in a significant breakdown of internal controls and a disregard on the Principles of Economy and Efficiency, thereby impairing the legality and propriety of public fund utilization.

The Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) balances of the agency could not be relied upon in view of the following deficiencies: a) Variances in the cost of PPE and depreciation expense reflected in the Financial Statements vis-a-vis the corresponding amounts in the supporting schedules; b) Incorrect residual value rate used in computing depreciation; and c) Recognition of full-year’s depreciation for PPE items regardless of acquisition/completion dates, all contrary to the provisions provided for in PD No. 1445, the NGAS Manual for LGUs, COA Circular No. 2003-007 and COA Circular No. 2015-008, thereby casting doubt on the accuracy, reliability and the faithful representation of the PPE balances presented in the Municipality’s Financial Statements as of December 31, 2025.

Adjustments to the accounts Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE), Accumulated Depreciation, and Government Equity totaling P85.294 million were not supported with adequate documentation, contrary to the provisions prescribed in PD No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines” and the New Government Accounting System Manual for LGUs, thus precluding the effective examination of the said transactions and furthermore, casts doubt on the corresponding balances presented in the Financial Statements as of year-end.

The Municipality failed to collect and record earned space rentals totaling P3.389 million as of December 31, 2025 from its Municipal Economic Enterprise operations due to the lack of proper monitoring and coordination among the concerned offices, contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445 and the Don Carlos Market Code of 2022. Consequently, the Municipality was deprived of additional funds that could have been used for various projects and activities beneficial to its constituents and moreover, the receivables and revenue accounts are understated as of year-end thereby casting doubt on the accuracy and reliability of the figures presented in the Financial Statements as of December 31, 2025.

The Performance Bond for various contracts with an aggregate value of P25.154 million did not cover the period until the last date of the Defects Liability Period, inconsistent with the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA No. 9184, otherwise known as “Government Procurement Reform Act”, thus, may expose the government to unrecoverable losses and additional costs in the event there are discovered damages to the infrastructure on account of the use of materials of inferior quality and there is no guarantee posted for the contractor to undertake the repairs thereof or for the agency to forfeit incase the contractor fails to comply with its obligations.

The procedures employed by the Municipality in relation to its LDRRMF are deemed non-compliant with relevant rules and regulations in view of the following: (a) The Unexpended Balance of the prior years’ LDRRMF totaling P29.060 million was not incorporated in the CY 2025 Annual Investment Program as additional fund sources wherein P20.073 million was not supported with a LDRRMF Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP); and (b) The amount recognized as LDRRMF Unexpended Balance covering CY 2025 and subsequently transferred to the 5% LDRRMF Special Trust Fund (Unexpended Balance) includes the amount allocated for Capital Outlay - Continuing Appropriations, all inconsistent with COA Circular No. 2012-002 and NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC No. 2013-1, thus resulted in the limited fund source to support LDRRM programs/projects/activities, exposes the disbursements sourced from the unexpended balances of the LDRRM Fund which are not supported with an approved LDRRMFIP and approved AIP to consequences in view of its non-adherence to the mandated procedures in the utilization of the Unexpended Balance of the LDRRMF, exposes the continuing appropriation to the risk of being used for new expenditure items, and lastly, overstating the Trust Liability – DRRM account as of year-end.

The Municipality obligated and paid Terminal Leave Benefits totaling P5.946 million with incomplete and non-compliant supporting documents, inconsistent with Presidential Decree No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’, Item 5.13 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, GSIS Memorandum Circular No. 005, s. 2018 and Section 7 of CSC Omnibus Rules on the Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), thus casting doubt as to the validity and propriety of the said disbursements and further, may render the same irregular and be subjected to audit suspension or disallowance, if warranted.

The Municipality paid full monthly RATA to Sangguniang Bayan (SB) officials notwithstanding the non-rendering of the required full service or actual work performance, resulting to a total overpayment of P0.250 million, contrary to the provisions embodied in PD No. 1445, DBM Local Budget Circular No. 157 and COA Circular No. 2012-003, thus casting doubt as to the validity and propriety of the said disbursements and further, may render the same irregular and be subjected to audit suspension or disallowance, if warranted.

The Fidelity Bond of Revenue Collection Clerks and the Disbursement Officer under the Municipal Treasurer’s Officer was insufficient to cover the maximum amount of cash accountability handled, contrary to Section 101 of PD 1445, Bureau of Treasury Order No. 01-95 dated December 5, 1995, Bureau of Treasury Circular No. 02 – 2019 dated April 11, 2019 and Bureau of Treasury Circular No. 01 – 2022 dated May 30, 2022, thereby exposing government funds to potential risk of non-recovery in cases of loss, shortage, misuse, or defalcation.

Infrastructure projects charged to the 20% Local Development Fund (LDF), with a total appropriation of P23.433 million, were implemented belatedly as compared to the targeted month of implementation per AIP and were not procurement-and-implementation ready, contrary to DBM-DOF-DILG JMC No. 1, and in effect, precluded the LGU from achieving optimal utilization of the funds, caused the completion dates of projects to be later than what should have been, and deprived its constituents of the desirable socio-economic benefits that could have been realized had the projects been completed at an earlier time.

Expenditures amounting to P0.278 million were inadvertently charged to the 5% Local Disaster Reduction and Management Fund (LDRMMF) instead of charging them to regular Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) and Capital Outlay appropriation of the General Fund, contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012, NDRRMC-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-1 and NDRRMC-DILG-DBM-CSC Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2014-1, thus depleting the funds that could have been used to finance activities that are within the thematic areas of DRRM.

Transfers to and from the Easy Savings Plus (ESP) accounts with the Landbank of the Philippines (LBP), totaling P273.226 million and P33 million respectively, were not supported with sufficient documents to determine the basis of the amounts transferred and withdrawn, inconsistent with the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Republic Act No. 7160 - ‘Local Government Code of 1991’, thus, the regularity and propriety of the placement of funds under such accounts could not be established and further, exposes Programs, Projects and Activities to the risk of delayed payments in view of the risks in the transfer process being employed by the Municipality.

Environmental Fee collections totaling ₱15.310 million were recorded under “Other Payables” account instead of the appropriate income/revenue accounts, contrary to the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1- Presentation of Financial Statements and the Local Government Chart of Accounts, overstating the Other Payables account and understating the Agency’s income/revenue, thereby, affecting the fair presentation of the Financial Statements.

Unidentified and unrecorded bank deposits and disbursements totaling ₱9.204 million and ₱1.092 million, respectively, were noted from the LGU’s five (5) bank accounts as of December 31, 2025, contrary to the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 1445, IPSAS, and Sections 3.2 and 3.3 of COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thereby understating the Cash in Bank - Local Currency, Current Account by a net amount of ₱8.112 million, exhibiting control weakness over its cash management, particularly in the recording and reconciliation process.

Various Inventories- Semi-Expendable accounts in the total amount of ₱6.683 million remains outstanding as of December 31,2025, which should have been expensed in accordance with COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022, overstating the Inventory and Government Equity accounts by the same amount, affecting the fair presentation of the year-end financial statements.

Various consumed/distributed supplies and materials remained recorded under Inventory accounts at year-end due to inadequate supply management controls, including the absence of an effective and centralized property and supply management system, inadequate monitoring of inventory issuances and utilization, delayed submission of consumption/distribution reports, and the non-conduct of physical inventory count, contrary to Sections 116 to 124, Chapter 7, Volume I of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for LGU, thereby, overstating the Inventory and Government Equity account by at least ₱5.983 million, affecting the accuracy and reliability of the year-end financial statements.

Fuel, Oil, and Lubricants inventory account as of December 31, 2025 totaling ₱1.975 million still includes a total amount of ₱1.178 million which are already consumed, hence, should have been expensed, contrary to Paragraph 7 of IPSAS 1, thereby overstating the Fuel, Oil and Lubricants Inventory account by ₱1.178 million.

The LGU incurred obligations for the period ended June 10, 2025 in excess of the authorized appropriations under reenacted budget or under the CY 2024 Final Approved Appropriation, totaling ₱2.438 million contrary to the pertinent provisions under Section 305 and 323 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991.

Prior Period Adjustments recorded in CY 2025 totaling ₱13.836 million representing prior year consumptions of Fuel, Oil and Lubricants (FOL) products lacked the necessary data and/or the necessary documents required per COA Circular No. 75-6 dated November 7, 1975, thereby affecting the transparency, validity, and proper authorization of the said expenses.

Disposal of unserviceable properties with a total cost of at least ₱6.984 million was not facilitated due to the non-preparation and submission of the Inventory and Inspection Report of Unserviceable Property (IlRUP), contrary to COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020 and Section 379 of RA No. 7160, depriving the Municipality of its other income from sales on unserviceable properties if found valuable.

The utilization of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) under the Special Trust Fund (STF) in CY 2025 totaling ₱4.550 million was not supported by an approved LDRRMF Investment Plan, contrary to the pertinent provisions under COA Circular No. 2012-002, thus, affected the validity of the utilization of the LDRRMF.

The grant of financial assistance to indigent constituents totaling ₱4.181 million was made without established policies/specific criteria on the determination of the qualified beneficiaries and the amount to be granted for a particular condition/case, contrary to Section 305 of the Local Government Code of 1991, resulting in inconsistent and discretionary distribution of financial aid.

The (a) unreconciled variance amounting to ₱237.850 million between the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE) and the balances in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025, and (b) non-submission of CY 2025 RPCPPE for Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) classifications totaling ₱666.406 million, contrary to COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020, affected the reliability of the reported PPE accounts in the Financial Statement as of December 31, 2025 as existence and accuracy thereof could not be ascertained.

The Construction in Progress (CIP) account totaling ₱276.097 million as of December 31, 2025 includes completed and operational infrastructure projects totaling at least ₱66.576 million, contrary to the provisions of IPSAS 17- PPE, resulting in the misclassification of assets and non-recognition of its respective depreciation, thereby affecting the accuracy, reliability and fair presentation of the year-end Financial Statement.

The Municipal Accounting Office erroneously and excessively recorded the total receivables amounted to ₱ 9.645 million in the books of accounts and noted other deficiencies relative to the turned-over thirty-two (32) housing units and lots at the Kadingilan Paglaum Village contrary to the provisions of the Contract to Sell between LGU-Kadingilan and the vendee, thus, affected the fair presentation of the financial statements as of December 31, 2025, possibly misled the end-users and affected the propriety, validity and legality of the sale of government properties.

The LGU was not able to implement the prescribed controls over its semi-expendable properties totaling ₱ 3.334 million, contrary with Section 123 of PD 1445 dated June 11, 1978, Section 1 of the Administrative Code of 1987 and COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022, as supplemented by COA Circular No. 2024-006 dated March 14, 2024, thereby affecting the reliability of records and accountability over semi‑expendable properties; exposing government assets to risks of loss, misuse, and mismanagement.

Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) insurance proceeds and subsequent repair expenses of a Toyota Hilux were recorded in the “Due to LGU” account inconsistent to Sections 111 and 112 of PD 1445, Section 305(a) of RA No. 7160 and Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015‑009, as a result, the “Due to LGU” account was overstated by ₱ 0.244 million, while “Government Equity” was understated by the same amount at year‑end and it affected the propriety, validity and legality of the pertinent disbursements amounted to ₱ 0.334 million.

Disbursements amounting to ₱ 0.995 million for procurement of goods for distribution unrelated to calamity or disaster relief operations were charged to the Welfare Goods Expense account, contrary to Section 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-009. Moreover, the remaining goods for distribution at year-end were not recognized as inventory, resulting to an overstatement of expenses by ₱ 0.137 million and a corresponding understatement of the LGU’s inventory account by the same amount as of December 31, 2025.

Various deficiencies were noted in the grant and payment of Hazard Pay and Subsistence Allowance to the LGU’s Public Health Workers and Social Workers with an initial computation of overpayment of ₱ 0.460 million, contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-001, DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1 s. of 2018, DBM-DOH JC No. 1 s. of 2012 and DBM-DOH JC No. 1 s. of 2016, thereby affecting the reliability, validity and accuracy of the disbursed funds, depleted the funds for its purpose and loss on the part of the government.

Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants amounting to ₱ 6.497 million were procured through Small Value Procurement instead of consolidating the LGU’s quarterly fuel requirements and subjecting them to Competitive Bidding in violation of Section 26 of COA Circular 92-386 dated October 20, 1992 and Section 54 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, as amended by RA 12009, thus, affected the validity, propriety and legality of the procurements and the municipality missed the opportunity to avail volume or wholesale discounts and lower prices associated with bulk purchases through competitive bidding. In addition, disbursements totaling ₱ 1.109 million for fuel payments were processed prior to complete delivery and issuance of the fuel contrary with Section 88 of PD 1445, thereby exposing the LGU to weak procurement controls, the risk of incomplete delivery, and potential loss of public funds.

Incomplete installation of Cassava Dryer Center accessories, a sub-project in the Trust Fund, amounted to ₱ 2.999 million was paid in full in contrast to Section 5.2, Annex E of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations and Section 3.1 of COA Circular 2012-003, hence, it was detrimental to the interest of the government, represented a major loss on the part of LGU-Kadingilan and its constituents and could be treated as an irregular disbursement.

The processing of the Transfer Certificates of Title (TCT) to LGU-Kadingilan of the newly procured lands which aggregated to ₱ 16.704 million was not fully facilitated as of December 31, 2025 contrary to Section 16 of Executive Order No. 1035 which was prejudicial to the interest of the government and exposed LGU-Kadingilan to future infringements, land disputes, loss of property or the like.

LGU Kadingilan missed to immediately notify COA about the damaged four-wheel service vehicle (pick-up truck, 4x4 Nissan Navara, color black) with an acquisition cost of ₱ 1.56 million directly accountable to the Municipal Mayor after it met a road crash incident and to present his application for relief of accountability with the required supporting documents within the reglementary period of 30 days from its occurrence in contrast to COA Circular No. 1992-751, thereby, he was not relieved of his liability for the loss or damage of the LGU’s property.

Three (3) completed Trust Fund projects amounted to ₱ 79.597 million were already recorded to their appropriate asset accounts in the General Fund books of accounts with the absence of Deeds of Donation (DOD) contrary to the Memoranda of Agreement (MOA) between LGU-Kadingilan and the source agency, thus, tainted the propriety, validity and legality of the donations and the transfer of ownership of the assets.

The 77 lessees of LGU’s market stalls have expired contracts of lease in contravention to Municipal Ordinance No. 2024-26 (16th SB) or Market Code of the Municipality of Kadingilan, Province of Bukidnon, thereby, tainted the propriety, legality and validity of the leases and made the LGU vulnerable to possible infringements by the lessees.

A variance between the General Ledger (GL) and the Subsidiary Ledgers (SL) amounting to ₱116.271 million was observed as of December 31, 2025. This discrepancy is inconsistent with the provisions of Sections 111, 114, and 123 of P.D. No. 1445, thereby casting doubt on the accuracy, reliability, and fair presentation of the account balances.

Several Journal Entry Vouchers (JEVs) prepared by the Office of the Municipal Accountant (OMA) and submitted to the audit team did not reflect the same accounting entries in the corresponding journals. In addition, some JEVs were prepared and/or signed simultaneously with, or prior to, the completion and approval of the corresponding Disbursement Vouchers (DVs). These practices were contrary to Section 111(2) of P.D. No. 1445, Section 02 of Volume II, and Section 05 of Volume I of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs. Consequently, the accounting entries and other data reflected in the JEVs were rendered unreliable, the audit trail was weakened, and the required consistency in the keeping of accounts was not observed, resulting in misleading information.

The Municipality failed to recognize certain parcels of land in its Books of Accounts and to transfer the corresponding titles in the name of the Government, contrary to Section 39 of P.D. No. 1445 and Article 47 of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code. Consequently, the Land account and Government Equity were understated. Moreover, the absence of formal titling exposes the Municipality’s properties to potential third-party claims and creates uncertainty regarding its absolute ownership rights.

The inadequate monitoring of market rental accounts resulted in the non-recognition of unpaid rental fees totaling ₱0.304 million, plus its corresponding surcharges and interest, as well as overpayments amounting to ₱55,223.50 for CY 2024 and 2025. This is contrary to Section 4 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual for LGUs, Volume I, and Sections 112 and 123 of P.D. No. 1445, thereby the accuracy in the recognition of actual revenues and receivables from market rentals is not established and is affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements as a whole as of December 31, 2025.

Stale checks totaling ₱0.753 million remained uncancelled and unadjusted in the books of accounts as of December 31, 2025, contrary to Section 59 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual for LGUs, Volume I and Item 3.2 of COA Circular 96-011. This resulted in the understatement of both Cash in Bank and Liability accounts, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The Municipality paid Hazard Pay and Subsistence Allowance to its personnel based on improper computations and with incomplete supporting documents, resulting in overpayments. These disbursements were non-compliant with relevant rules and regulations and are inconsistent with DBM-DOH Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2012, as amended; DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2018; and COA Circular No. 2012-001, thus casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the disbursements.

The collections of the Collecting Officers were not remitted immediately to the Liquidating Officer. Moreover, the Liquidating Officer did not deposit the collections turned over to her daily or on the next banking day. In some instances, collections were not deposited intact, contrary to Sections 26, 31, and 28 of COA Circular No. 92-382 and Section 69 of P.D. No. 1445. These practices deprived the government of the timely use of its funds and exposed government funds to possible loss, misuse, or misappropriation.

The fidelity bonds of the Accountable Officers (AOs) were inadequate, as some of their collections at a given time exceeded the maximum cash accountability, contrary to Sections 5.1 and 7.3 of Bureau of the Treasury Circular No. 02-2009, thereby exposing government funds to the risk of non-recovery in the event of loss.

The Municipality failed to maintain a separate Trust Fund account and prepare the required Program of Work (POW) for the 15% share of the Office of the Building Official (OBO) derived from collected building permit fees and other charges, contrary to Section 208 of P.D. No. 1096 and DPWH-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 001, thereby hindering the proper disposition and utilization of funds intended for building regulatory functions.

Insurable properties of the Municipality for CY 2025 were not covered with property insurance from the General Insurance Fund (GIF) of the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS); and the Property Inventory Form (PIF) was not prepared and submitted to the Office of the Auditor on or before April 30, 2025; these deficiencies constitute non-compliance with the provisions of the Republic Act No. 656 or Property Insurance Law, COA Circular No. 2018-002, and COA Circular No. 92-390; thus exposing some of the Municipality’s properties to risk of non-indemnification for damages or losses due to fortuitous events.

The Municipal Agriculture Office failed to properly safeguard, monitor, and distribute the fertilizer assistance from the Department of Agriculture (DA). This is contrary to Section 123 of P.D. 1445; thereby exposing government property to the risk of loss or wastage and resulting in the inequitable distribution of agricultural inputs to farmer-beneficiaries.

The LGU missed to implement the prescribed controls over its semi-expendable properties contrary to Section 123 of PD 1445 dated June 11, 1978, Section 1 of the Administrative Code of 1987 and COA Circular No. 2022-004 dated May 31, 2022, as supplemented by COA Circular No. 2024-006 dated March 14, 2024, thereby affecting the accountability over semi‑expendable properties; exposing government assets to risks of loss, misuse, and mismanagement.

Various deficiencies were observed relative to the “Land” account of LGU-Kibawe in contravention to COA Circular No. 2015-009 and Section 3.1 of COA Circular No. 2024-006, thus, it affected the fair presentation of the financial statements as of December 31, 2025.

Various structures unrelated to markets, totaling P17.291 million, were erroneously recorded under the “Markets” account in violation of COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby tainting the propriety, accuracy, and reliability of the affected accounts as presented in the Financial Statements and potentially misleading end-users.

The LGU was not able to recognize it in its books one (1) Patient Transport Vehicle (PTV) donated by the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO), contrary to Sections 111 and 112 of PD 1445, resulting in the understatement of both the Transportation Equipment and Government Equity accounts and affecting the faithful presentation of the LGU’s financial statements as of December 31, 2025.

The Municipal Accounting Office was unable to recognize and record “Accounts Payable” and “Construction in Progress – Building and Other Structures” for the unpaid final billing of the completed project under the Trust Fund titled “Construction of Trading Post at West Kibawe” amounted to ₱ 4.987 million and was not able to reclassify the said project to its appropriate asset account contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009, thus, understated the total assets and total liability by ₱ 487,762.02 and affected the fair presentation of the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025.

The absence of complete documentation for the ₱2.59 million Accounts Payable set up at year-end, in violation of Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 157, Volume 1 of the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual, precluded independent verification of the validity of obligations and affected the reliability and accuracy of the reported Accounts Payable balance in the LGU’s financial statements as of December 31, 2025.

The transfer of unspent CY 2025 Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) amounting to ₱7.145 million from the General Fund to the Trust Fund was not recorded in the Trust Fund books as of December 31, 2025 contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-002, resulting to the understatement of the “Cash” and “Trust Liability - DRRMF” accounts.

Various deficiencies were noted in the grant and payment of Hazard Pay and Subsistence Allowance to the LGU’s Public Health Workers and Social Workers with an initial computation of overpayment of ₱0.157 million, contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-001, DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1 s. of 2018, DBM-DOH JC No. 1 s. of 2012 and DBM-DOH JC No. 1 s. of 2016, thereby affecting the reliability, validity and accuracy of the disbursed funds, depleted the funds for its purpose and loss on the part of the government.

Completed Trust Fund project entitled “Concreting of Municipal Streets (Malvar, Carlos Fortich, Lakandula and Aglipay Streets)” amounted to ₱14.989 million was already recorded to “Road Networks” in the General Fund books of accounts with the absence of Deed of Donation (DOD) contrary to the Memoranda of Agreement (MOA) between LGU-Kibawe and the source agency, thus, tainted the propriety, validity and legality of the donation and the transfer of ownership of the asset.

The LGU made full payment to its supplier for procured diesel and gasoline amounting to ₱4.503 million, net of taxes, prior to the complete delivery and actual issuance thereof, contrary to Section 88 of Presidential Decree No. 1445, thereby exposing the LGU to the risk of incomplete delivery and potential loss of public funds. In addition, the supporting documents for the payment and eventual consumption of the procured fuel were noted irregularities showing weakness in the LGUs internal controls in violation of Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445 and Section 3.12 of the National Guidelines on Internal Control Systems, thereby undermining the reliability of financial records, impairing transparency and accountability, and diminished the LGU’s ability to safeguard public resources against misuse, loss, or irregularities.

Various travelling expenses of the Municipal Agriculture’s Office amounted to ₱0.207 million were charged against the funds transferred from Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) for the Learning Site for Agriculture (LSA) Scholarship Program in the Trust Fund in contravention to Ordinance No. 7 Series of 2022, thus, affected the propriety, validity and legality of the said disbursements.

Various discrepancies were noted relative to the collection and utilization of the 15 percent share of the Office of Building Official (OBO) in CY 2025 contrary to DPWH-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 001, thus, the monies were highly exposed to possible cash misappropriation and affected the propriety, validity and legality of the pertinent disbursements.

The balance of the Construction-in-Progress account as of December 31, 2025 is deemed unreliable due to (a) completed projects amounting to P159 million that remained in the said account as of year-end; and (b) erroneous/inconsistent information presented in the CIP Schedule as of December 31, 2025, all inconsistent with the provisions of PD No. 1445, and the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual and its corresponding Revised Chart of Accounts, thus casting doubt on the accuracy, reliability and fair presentation of the amounts reflected in the financial statements.

The Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) balances of the agency could not be relied upon in view of the following deficiencies: (a) variances in the cost of PPE reflected in the Financial Statements vis-à-vis the corresponding amounts in the supporting schedules; (b) incorrect residual value rate used in computing depreciation; and (c) delayed recognition of depreciation for PPE items, all contrary to the provisions of PD No. 1445, the NGAS Manual for LGUs, COA Circular No. 2003-007, and COA Circular No. 2015-008, thereby casting doubt on the accuracy, reliability, and faithful representation of the PPE balances presented in the Municipality’s Financial Statements as of December 31, 2025.

Disbursements amounting to ₱7.6 million were recorded in the books of accounts in December 2025 through the preparation of Journal Entry Vouchers (JEVs) in the Check Disbursements Journal (CkDJ), notwithstanding that the corresponding checks remained unclaimed by the payees and the Disbursement Vouchers (DVs) related to these checks were not yet submitted by the Municipal Treasurer’s Office (MTO) to the Municipal Accounting Office (MAccO) as of December 31, 2025, inconsistent with Section 111 of Presidential Decree (P.D.) No. 1445 and the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs) which resulted in the understatement of cash in bank and the corresponding liability accounts in the books as of December 31, 2025, thereby affecting the reliability and accuracy of the financial statements.

The balance of the Land account amounting to P191 million as of December 31, 2025 is deemed unreliable due to (a) inclusion of land deemed to be under the Ancestral Domain amounting to P1.8 million (b) non-inclusion in the subject account of parcels of land which are in the name of the Municipality of Kitaotao; and (c) land areas amounting to P105 million which are not yet titled under the name of the Municipality of Kitaotao, all inconsistent with the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 1445, the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual and its corresponding Chart of Accounts, COA Circular No. 92-386 and the relevant Land Registration Laws thus, overstating the Land account and further, the absolute ownership of the subject lands cannot be fully ascertained, all leading to doubts on the fair presentation of the amount presented in the financial statements.

Disbursement amounting to P0.732 million representing Electricity Expense for the period December 2024 was not accrued in the same year it was incurred but was recognized as expense in CY 2025 and paid under the CY 2025 appropriations, inconsistent with Presidential Decree No. 1445, Republic Act No. 7160, and the New Government Accounting System Manual (NGAS Manual), thus rendering the subject account doubtful and unreliable as it contradicts the mandated Accrual Method of Accounting.

The procedures implemented by the Municipality concerning its insurable properties were found to be non-compliant on account of the following: (a) Motor Vehicle Insurance premiums paid to Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) totaling ₱0.492 million were expensed outright and recorded under “Taxes, Duties & Licenses”; and (b) Various Municipal Buildings were not covered with property insurance from the General Insurance Fund (GIF) of the GSIS for the period July - December 2025, all contrary to the Manual on New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs), COA Circular No. 2015-009, and COA Circular No. 2018-002, thus resulting in the understatement of the “Prepaid Insurance” and “Insurance Expense” accounts and the overstatement of the “Taxes, Duties & Licenses” account thereby affecting the fair presentation of the Municipality’s Financial Statements as of year-end and further, deprives the Municipality of adequate and reliable protection against potential financial loss in the event of property damage.

Liquidation for the release of Health Emergency Allowance totaling P9.4 million contained deficiencies in the attached supporting documents and contained overpayments amounting to P0.123 million, contrary to Presidential Decree No. 1445 - ‘The Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’, COA Circular No. 2012-001, and COA Circular No. 2012-003, thus casting doubt on the legality, propriety, and regularity of the related transactions.

The Performance Bond for various contracts with an aggregate value of P57 million did not cover the period until the last date of the Defects Liability Period, inconsistent with the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA No. 9184, otherwise known as “Government Procurement Reform Act”, thus, may expose the government to unrecoverable losses and additional costs in the event there are discovered damages to the infrastructure on account of the use of materials of inferior quality and there is no guarantee posted for the contractor to undertake the repairs thereof or for the agency to forfeit in case the contractor fails to comply with its obligations.

The procedures employed by the agency in the grant of Monetization of Earned Leave Credits and Terminal Leave Benefits are deemed non- compliant with relevant rules and regulations in view of the following: (a) Payment of Monetization of Earned Leave Credits to officials and employees without observing the required limitations on Vacation Leave (VL) credits; and (b) Payment of Terminal Leave Benefits with incomplete supporting documents, all inconsistent with PD No. 1445 - ‘Government Auditing Code of the Philippines’, Section 22 of CSC Omnibus Rules on Leave, Item 5.13 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, GSIS Memorandum Circular No. 005, s. 2018 and Section 7 of CSC Omnibus Rules on the Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), thus casting doubt as to the validity and propriety of the said disbursements and further, may render the same irregular and be subjected to audit suspension or disallowance, if warranted.

The Municipality paid full monthly RATA to Sangguniang Bayan (SB) officials notwithstanding the non-rendering of the required full service or actual work performance, resulting to a total overpayment of ₱0.344 million, contrary to the provisions embodied in PD No. 1445, DBM Local Budget Circular No. 157 and COA Circular No. 2012-003, thus casting doubt as to the validity and propriety of the said disbursements and further, may render the same irregular and be subjected to audit suspension or disallowance, if warranted.

The procedures employed by the Municipality in the establishment and utilization of its Petty Cash Fund (PCF) are deemed non-compliant with the relevant rules and regulations in view of the following: a) establishment of the PCF under the custody of a non-permanently appointed official b) erroneous procedures in the handling of the PCF and c) procurement of fuel thru reimbursements from the PCF, all inconsistent with the provisions of COA Circular No. 97-002, NGAS Manual for LGUS, COA Circular No. 2012-003, and the Revised IRR of RA No. 9184, thus, contradicts the standard internal control mechanisms and casts doubt on the regularity and propriety of the subject transactions and exposes same to audit Suspension or Disallowance, if warranted.

The procedures employed by the Municipality in relation to its LDRRMF are deemed non-compliant with relevant rules and regulations in view of the following: (a) the Unexpended Balance of the prior year’s LDRRMF totaling ₱11 million covering CY 2021-2024 was not incorporated in the CY 2025 Annual Investment Program as additional fund sources wherein P7.3 million covering CY 2021-2023 was not supported with a LDRRMF Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP); and (b) the amount transferred from the General Fund to the 5% LDRRMF bank account was insufficient in relation to the amount appropriated in the CY 2025 Annual Budget for the said fund, all inconsistent with COA Circular No. 2012-002 and NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC No. 2013-1, thus resulted in the limited fund source to support LDRRM programs/projects/activities, exposes the disbursements sourced from the unexpended balances of the LDRRM Fund which are not supported with an approved LDRRMFIP and approved AIP to consequences in view of its non-adherence to the mandated procedures in the utilization of the Unexpended Balance of the LDRRMF, exposes the 5% LDRRMF bank account to overdrafts in case disbursements exceed the available cash in bank and lastly, exposes the untransferred LDRRMF funds in the General Fund bank account to GF related disbursements.

Disbursements amounting to ₱0.827 million charged against the 5% Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) for CY 2025 disclosed documentary deficiencies inconsistent with Presidential Decree No. 1445, R.A. No. 9184 and COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby casting doubt on the reliability, validity, and legality of the transactions and the regularity of the aforesaid disbursements.

Infrastructure projects charged to the 20% Local Development Fund, with a total appropriation of P19 million, were implemented belatedly compared to the targeted months of implementation per APP and were not procurement and implementation-ready, contrary to DBM-DOF-DILG JMC No. 1. Consequently, the constituents of the municipality were deprived of the desirable socio-economic benefits that could have been realized had the projects been completed earlier.

A total of 26 motor vehicles either did not bare government plates, were not marked with “For Official Use Only” and/or were not marked with the name of Office/Agency using the same, all inconsistent with the provisions of COA Circular No. 75-6 and 75-6A, COA Circular No. 77-61, PD No. 1445 and DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2010-101, thus exposing the aforementioned vehicles to misuse and further, exposing the concerned users of motor vehicles to possible consequences in view of the non-compliance with the related guidelines.

Ineffective collection efforts, non-recording of unpaid amortizations and erroneous recording of amortization payments were observed in the implementation of the Paglaum Village Project, contrary to the perfected Conditional Contracts to Sell, applicable provisions of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) and Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs), thereby casting doubt on the propriety and effectiveness of the collection efforts of the LGU and resulted to the misstatement of the Receivables and Payables account by ₱1.963 million and ₱0.929 million, respectively, adversely affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Various expenses incurred in CY 2024 totaling ₱0.362 million were erroneously recognized as expenses in CY 2025, which is inconsistent with paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, Section 4(a), Chapter 2 of the MNGAS for LGUs- Volume I, and item 5.1.3 and 5.3 of COA Circular No. 97-002. Consequently, the affected Maintenance and Other Operating Expense (MOOE) accounts were overstated by ₱0.362 million in CY 2025, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the financial reports.

Delayed submission and recording of DVs from CY 2016 to 2022 totaling ₱0.492 and DVs totaling ₱85,554.64 remained unsubmitted and unrecorded as of December 31, 2025, contrary to Article 218, Chapter 4, Title II of the Revised Penal Code (RPC), and Section No. 7.2.1 (a) of COA Circular No. 2009-006, and IPSAS 1, thereby casting doubt on the validity, propriety and legality of the transactions related to the missing and unrecorded DVs, creating delays and bottlenecks in audit, and misstated the Government Equity by ₱85,554.64.

The Reconciliation between the actual amounts reported in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) and the Statement of Financial Performance (SPER) for the year ended December 31, 2025 showed: (a) that the MOOE actual amount reported in the SCBAA does not coincide with the actual amount in the SCBAA reconciliation report, with a variance of ₱9.918 million, and (b) the existence of entity differences totaling ₱3.741 million (absolute value) without adequate breakdown and disclosure in the Notes to Financial Statements (NTFS). These conditions are not compliant with Section 111 (1) of PD 1445 and the disclosure and reconciliation requirements under IPSAS 1 and IPSAS 24, thereby adversely affecting the fair presentation of the Financial Statements as of December 31, 2025.

The Subsidiary Ledgers of the Cash in Local Treasury account were not properly accomplished and maintained due to unrecorded and delayed recording of entries/transactions with the corresponding unrecorded/erroneous amount of ₱53.089 million in the General Fund (GF), ₱10.2 million in the Special Education Fund (SEF), and ₱3.379 million Trust Fund (TF), which is contrary to Section nos. 111 and 114 (2) of PD No. 1445 and Section 10, Chapter 1 of the MNGAS for LGUs, Volume II, thereby affecting the reliability of these accounts and reports.

Various deficiencies were noted in relation to the management of cash advances which were granted for the period of December 04, 2024 to December 31, 2025, inconsistent with Section 63(f) of the BLGF-DOF Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM), Section Nos. 4.1.2 and 5.8 of COA Circular No. 97-002, thereby casting doubt on the regularity and propriety in the handling of cash advances and the reliability on the correctness of the records maintained by the accountable officers and the subsidiary ledgers with a variance totaling ₱0.300 million.

Cash Advances for various purposes totaling ₱0.761 million remain unliquidated as of December 31, 2025, and the presence of an abnormal/negative balance of ₱78,618.67 was not adjusted, contrary to Section 89 of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 97-002. As a result, it exposed the funds to the risk of misuse/loss and the negative balances affect the fair presentation of balances in the financial statements.

Various LGU receivable accounts cannot be verified due to (a) unsubstantiated or unreconciled receivables totaling ₱24.400 million and (b) abnormal or negative receivable balances of ₱0.792 million. These issues violate Sections 111 and 112 of PD No. 1445 and Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, raising doubts about the accuracy and reliability of receivable balances in the CY 2025 financial statements.

Various deficiencies were found in the LGU’s inventories and procured goods totaling ₱10.265 million in CY 2025, contrary to Section 2 and 4 (6) of PD No. 1445, Section 358 & 359 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991, Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, Section 124 and Annex 33 of the MNGAS Volume I and II for LGUs, and COA Circular No. 2009-006. Hence, the accuracy of the recorded consumption of procured goods and the existence of the inventory balances as of December 31, 2025 could not be verified and established.
