Significant discrepancies amounting to ₱558.344 million were noted in the Construction in Progress (CIP) balances between the accounting records and engineering reports as of December 31, 2025, attributable to the non- reclassification of completed projects and non-reconciliation of the CIP balances. This is contrary to the provisions of Section 58 of PD No. 1445 and Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-009. Consequently, the CIP account is overstated while the appropriate Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts are understated, including the corresponding depreciation expenses and accumulated depreciation accounts.

The liabilities accounts of the LGU as of December 31, 2025 is unreliable, due to unsubstantiated balances aggregating ₱57.978 million, and negative/abnormal balances totaling ₱40.961 million, contrary to the provisions of Section 111 of PD No. 1445, Section 10 of the MNGAS Volume II for LGUs, and IPSAS 1. As a result, the accuracy and reliability of the liabilities account balances as of December 31, 2025 cannot be ascertained, and the abnormal/negative balances may indicate possible overpayments which may be subjected to adverse audit action.

The non-submission of sufficient documentations in support of the recorded Accounts Payable (AP) in CY 2025 totaling ₱12.610 million, which affects several financial accounts, is contrary to the provisions of COA Circular No. 2012-001, Sections 4 (6), 58, 59, and 61 of PD No. 1445. Consequently, the verification of the correctness of the recorded transactions cannot be made due to the absence of the supporting documents, thus resulting in a scope limitation in audit and casting doubt on the reliability of the financial account balances as of December 31, 2025.

A motor vehicle with Plate Number SK-9284 was found missing and without a corresponding Property Acknowledgment Receipt (PAR) and various deficiencies were observed in the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) accounts, contrary to Sections 02, 105, and 111 of PD No. 1445, Paragraphs 14 and 82 of IPSAS 17, and Section 5.1 of COA Circular No. 2020-006, thereby casting doubt on the accuracy of the PPE balances and reliability of control in safeguarding the government assets.

The transfer of water system assets by LGU Lantapan to Lantapan Water District (LWD) amounting to ₱42.832 million was undertaken with significant deficiencies and non-compliance with Section 380 of RA No. 7160, PD No. 1445, and COA Circular No. 2019-003, thereby rendering the legality, validity, ownership, valuation, and financial soundness of the transaction doubtful and potentially prejudicial to the interest of the government.

Various deficiencies were found in the review of the contract and other relevant documents for the project entitled, “Construction of Lantapan Public Market Annex,” with contract price of ₱58.461 million contrary to Sections 7.1, 12, 17.2, and 34.3 of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (RIRR), of RA 9184, and COA Circular No. 2009-001, thereby casting doubt on the validity of the procurement activity conducted and creating a bottleneck in the conduct of auditorial review.

Various deficiencies were noted for the project, Construction of Lantapan Farmers Market at Kibangay, with contract price of ₱26.740 million contrary to Paragraph 4 of the Omnibus Sworn Statement, Sections 12 and 14.1 of the RIRR of RA No. 9184, and COA Circular No. 2009-001, thereby casting doubt on the procurement activity conducted and creating a bottleneck in the conduct of auditorial review.

The progress billing payments and the Statement of Work Accomplishment (SWA) for the project, Construction of Lantapan Farmers Market at Kibangay, with a contract price of ₱26.740 million, did not reconcile, contrary to Section Nos. 5.1 and 5.3 of Annex “E” of RIRR of RA No. 9184 and Section No. 2 of PD No. 1445, resulting to an increased risk of pecuniary loss or over/underpayment of progress billings and diminish reliability of the project progress reports and records, thereby, affecting management’s ability to accurately monitor project status and fund utilization.

The procurement of drugs and medicines in CY 2025 totaling ₱1.655 million, was not supported with complete documentary requirements as prescribed by Section No. 9.1.3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, and contrary to Section 16 of RA No. 7160 and Section 4 (6) of PD No. 1445. Thus, the propriety of the procured drugs and medicines cannot be ascertained and the eligibility of the winning bidder/supplier is doubtful.

Various purchases in CY 2025 under negotiated procurement- small value procurement aggregating to ₱4.254 million has lacking documentary requirements supporting the submitted disbursement vouchers, thus constituting non-compliance with Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445 and Section No. 25.3 Annex H, Appendix A of the 2016 RIRR of RA No. 9184, thereby, casting doubts on the propriety of the disbursements and the eligibility of the winning supplier/bidder.

Various deficiencies were noted on collections totaling ₱14.283 million by accountable officers, inconsistent with Section Nos. 60 (a), 62 (c), and 90 (b) of the LTOM, thus the risk of pecuniary loss may arise from a large amount of cash being retained on hand, which may be prone to theft or misuse.

The Municipal Treasurer’s Office’s (MTO) procedures for managing and monitoring stale checks issued by LGU Lantapan did not follow requisite notification to the payee one month prior to the dates of maturity of the checks in contravention to Section 59, Chapter 3, Volume 1 of the MNGAS for LGUs, thereby casting doubt on the regularity, adequacy and propriety of the internal control measures in place.

The disbursement vouchers, along with the relevant documents, related to the cash advance grants for confidential expenses for CY 2025 totaling ₱1.600 million, were not submitted within the prescribed period, contrary to Section No. 6.1.8.4 of COA-DBM-DILG-GCG-DND Joint Circular No. 2015-1 dated January 8, 2015, thereby resulting to non-compliance with established procedures and guidelines and delay in the audit and verification of the granted cash advances.

The liquidation of cash advances for various travelling expenses in CY 2025 totaling ₱0.736 million were inadequately supported and the submitted liquidation payrolls for travel aggregating ₱43,500.00 lacked proof of payment, in violation of Sections 4(6) of PD No. 1445, COA Circular No. 2012-001, Section 47 of the MNGAS for LGUs, Volume I, and COA Circular No. 2021-001, thereby raising concerns about the propriety and validity of the paid travelling expenses and propriety of the liquidated cash advances.

Inadequacies and inefficiencies were noted in the collection and billing procedures of water supply managed and operated by the LGU, contrary to Section No. 02 of PD No. 1445, hindering proper verification of the accuracy of the amounts paid and reconciliation of official receipts and billing statements.

Various deficiencies were noted during the reconciliation of the CY 2025 Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP), the CY 2023-2025 Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Plan (LDRRMP) and the CY 2025 LDRRMF Monitoring and Evaluation Report, contrary to Section 21 of RA No. 10121, which resulted to a total of ₱1.090 million non-aligned PPAs.

Disbursements for the DAR-funded Farm-to-Market Road (FMR) project were prematurely charged against the “Due to Other NGAs” account, contrary to the conditions set forth in the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and Paragraph 46 of the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 23, resulting in the non-recognition of Construction in Progress – Infrastructure and understatement of the Due to Other NGAs account by ₱8.243 million.

The Animal/Zoological Supplies Inventory account is overstated by ₱0.768 million, while the Animal/Zoological Supplies Expense account is understated by the same amount due to the non-submission of Consumption/Distribution Lists and the delayed submission of the Report on the Physical Count of Inventories (RPCI) by the Municipal Agriculture Office, in violation of Sections 111 and 123 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 and Paragraph 44 of IPSAS No. 12.

Deficiencies were noted in the implementation and accounting of Sigmatan Water System Project, as procurement and project activities were undertaken prior to the issuance of the Notice to Implement (NTI) and erroneous accounting treatment was applied in the reversal of the Due to Other NGAs account amounting ₱0.559 million, which are not in compliance with DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2025-014 and applicable government accounting standards, thereby affecting the validity and regularity of the related transactions and understatement of the assets and liabilities accounts by ₱0.559 million, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements as of December 31, 2025.

The unreconciled variance of ₱33.414 million between the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE) and the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) balances recorded by the Municipal Accounting Office, including misclassifications and other discrepancies noted in the property records, was not in accordance with the requirements of IPSAS 1 and COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020, thereby affecting the completeness, existence, accuracy, valuation, and reliability of the PPE balances reported in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025.

Completed projects totaling ₱14.122 million were not reclassified from CIP to their appropriate Asset accounts and were not depreciated, contrary to Section 50 of Volume I of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs. This was due to the non-submission of Certificates of Completion and other supporting documents, thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the year-end Financial Statements.

The Drugs and Medicine Inventory account with a recorded balance of ₱8.317 million, includes a total amount of ₱0.779 million of Medical, Dental and Laboratory Supplies, while the remaining balance in the total amount of ₱7.538 million could not be ascertained due to insufficient and unreliable inventory and utilization reports submitted by the Municipal Health Office (MHO), contrary to Section 111 of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015.

Disbursements on Municipal College Educational Assistance Program (MCEAP) in total amount of ₱1.932 million were recorded on Donation Expense account, which should be the Scholarship Grants/Expense account, in accordance to Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-009, resulting to misclassification of account, affecting the fair presentation of proper expenses in the financial statements.

Inaccurate recording of the transfer and closing entries caused the Trust Fund to report a surplus totaling ₱72.501 million for the period ending December 31, 2025, contrary to Paragraphs 44, 45, and 46 and Basis for Conclusion (BC) No. 11 of IPSAS 23, thus overstating the revenue accounts of the LGU.

The reconciliation between the Actual Amounts in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) and the Statement of Financial Performance for the year ended December 31, 2025, showed material items without proper disclosures regarding the breakdown and information of the aforementioned items, contrary to Section 111 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, Paragraphs 7 and 46 of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1, and Paragraphs 14, 39, and 47 of IPSAS 24, thereby adversely affecting the fair presentation of the Notes to Financial Statements (NTFS) and the SCBAA.

The accuracy and reliability of the reported Inventory accounts’ balance as of December 31, 2025 totaling ₱62.150 million could not be ascertained due to the doubtful existence of items with an aggregate amount of ₱30.173 million and the unquantified amount of inventory items found during the count but were not recorded in the books, thereby affecting the fairness of the balance presented in the Statement of Financial Position at the end of CY 2025 and inconsistent with IPSAS No. 27.

The accuracy and existence of the reported Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) account, with a total net book value of ₱3.286 billion as of December 31, 2025, could not be ascertained due to (a) doubtful existence of PPE items with an aggregate net book value of ₱273.091 million; (b) failure to complete the one-time cleansing of PPE accounts; (c) non-reclassification of PPE items with individual costs below ₱50,000.00 aggregating ₱32.070 million; and (d) non-reclassification of completed infrastructure projects amounting to ₱2.289 million to the appropriate PPE accounts, thereby materially affecting the fair presentation of PPE and related accounts in the CY 2025 Financial Statement.

The Accounting Office recorded a journal entry to set up the Output Value Added Tax (VAT) for income derived from market stall rentals and waterworks system fees for CY 2025 in the amounts of ₱1.842 and ₱1.779 million, respectively, without the requisite appropriation authority from the Sanggunian, contrary to Section 305(a) of RA No. 7160, casting doubt to the validity and propriety of the recognized obligation.

The contribution of ₱5 million by the City Government of Malaybalay to the Malaybalay City Credit Surety Fund (MCCSF), pursuant to the Deed of Trust executed with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP), Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP), Industrial Guarantee Loan Fund (IGLF), Cooperative Development Authority (CDA) and participating primary member cooperatives, may have been erroneously classified as “Other Investments”, contrary to Section 112 of PD No. 1445 and the provisions under COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby resulting in the misclassification of assets and affecting the faithful presentation of the City’s financial position.

The delay in the submission of DVs and the accompanying supporting documents decreased by 56 percent, or 107 days, between CYs 2024 and 2025; however, DVs and the supporting documents were still submitted late ranging from 7 to 84 days after the reglementary period and DVs/JEVs representing cash and non-cash transactions aggregating ₱2.602 billion remained unsubmitted due to the processing time and the volume of documents, contrary to Section 347 of RA No. 7160, Section 122 of PD No. 1445, COA Circular No. 2009-006, COA Circular No. 95-006, and Section 44 of the Manual on New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs), thus the validity and regularity of the ₱1.602 billion transactions could not be determined.

The accounting office erroneously recorded the foreign travel of the City Government of Malaybalay officials to Jinju City, South Korea in the total amount of ₱0.676 million under the Traveling Expenses – Local, resulting in overstatement of the account and understatement of the Travelling Expenses-Foreign account. In addition, the Daily Subsistence Allowance claimed by the delegates exceeded by ₱80,093.64, these are inconsistent to Sections 111 and 112 of the PD No. 1445, the provision of Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, and Section 14 (C) of Executive Order No. 77, respectively.

Cash advances amounting to ₱0.423 million remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2025 and additional cash advances were granted despite the non-liquidation of the previous advances, contrary to COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997. Moreover, some cash advances were granted beyond the authorized maximum cash accountability prescribed by Treasury Circular No. 1-2022 dated May 30 2022, while the recording of certain cash advance transactions was inconsistent with Sections 111 and 112 of the PD No. 1445, the provision of Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thereby exposing government funds to increased risk of misuse or misappropriation and resulting in the misstatement of the affected accounts in the financial statements.

Payments made by the City Government of Malaybalay to the regular and casual employees for the CY 2025 Cultural and Athletics activities in the total amount of ₱1.375 million did not comply with the budgetary and documentary requirements, thus affecting the validity and propriety of the transactions.

The City Government of Malaybalay (CGM) was not able to return the undisbursed Department of Health (DOH) funds for the Health Emergency Allowance (HEA) in CY 2025 amounting to ₱0.970 million, contrary to the executed Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between the CGM and DOH, thereby exposing the City Government of Malaybalay (CGM) to possible sanctions or refund demands from the DOH.

The accuracy and correctness of the City’s Report on Sources and Utilization of the DRRMF and the Accounting and Budget records and related disclosures in the NTFS for CY 2025 could not be ascertained due to the noted variance aggregating ₱38.835 million between the utilization report and the related records and disclosures, contrary to the pertinent provisions of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2012-002.

The inclusion of programs, projects, activities (PPAs) that are not implementation ready in the 20% Local Development Fund (LDF), General Fund -Proper, Economic Enterprise and Special Education Fund’s PPAs for CY 2025 and prior years resulted in a low implementation and utilization rate of the Current Year and Continuing Appropriations, thus, impeding the optimum utilization of the funds which consequently deprived the public of the benefits that could have been derived from its immediate implementation and maximum utilization.

Deficiencies in the submission and reporting of the Gender and Development (GAD) Plan and Budget (GPB) and Accomplishment Report (AR), including delayed submission, non-compliance with prescribed budgeting and reporting guidelines, and absence of supporting documents, contrary to the relevant provisions in PCW-DILG-DBM-NEDA Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2013-01 and Item V of COA Circular No. 2014001, impair the timely determination of the judicious use of the funds and the efficiency and effectiveness of interventions in addressing existing gender issues.

Inter-agency payables representing withheld premium contributions and loan amortizations for the GSIS, Pag-IBIG and Philhealth aggregating ₱8.449 million as of December 31, 2025 were not remitted in full within the prescribed period, contrary to Sections 14.1 to 14.3 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA No. 8291, Section E.4 of HDMF Circular No. 275 dated January 22, 2010 and Section 18 of the IRR of the National Health Insurance Act of 2013, thereby exposing the City Government and the employees to the possible imposition of penalty and surcharges for the late remittance thereof.

Seventeen (17) reconciling items (comprising of book error, stale checks and returned check deposit) remained unrecorded/unadjusted in the books of accounts, amounting to ₱1.759 million, contrary to Section Sections 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the balances of Cash in Bank and the corresponding accounts reflected in the financial statements for calendar year 2025.

Inaccurate and unreliable balances of the Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivable accounts were presented in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025 due to the non-reconciliation of the accounting, treasury, and assessor's records, inconsistent with the provisions of PD No. 1445 and NGAS Manual for LGU, thereby overstated the said accounts by ₱4.148 million and ₱4.814 million, respectively, while the Deferred RPT and Deferred SET payable accounts were overstated by ₱4.090 million and ₱4.746 million, respectively.

The costs of the completed Rural Health Unit (RHU) donated by Department of Health (DOH) Region X thru its Health Facilities Enhancement Program (HFEP) were not recorded in the books of accounts, while visible cracks were noted in the facility, inconsistent with the pertinent provisions of PD 1445, COA Circulars, and the Revised IRR of RA 9184, resulting in misstatement of the municipality’s financial position, non-establishment of accountability over government assets, and potentially compromising safety and convenience for health personnel and the public.

Several General Ledger (GL) account balances did not reconcile with their corresponding Subsidiary Ledgers (SLs) by ₱216.053 million, exacerbated by the presence of temporary, unidentifiable/generic, negative, unnamed, or redundant SLs, inconsistent with the provisions of PD 1445 and the NGAS Manual for LGUs, thereby undermining the reliability and accuracy of the CY 2025 Statement of Financial Position's account balances, warranting the issuance of a modified audit opinion, and depriving users of financial statements of accurate, reliable, and decision‑useful information.

The Municipality did not prepare and submit the required year-end financial statements for its 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) account, contrary to RA No. 7160 and NGAS Manual for LGUs, thereby, the transparency and accountability in the receipt and usage of the 20% LDF could not be established depriving the intended users of relevant financial information that are vital in the making of well-informed and sound decision.

The Municipal Accounting Office prematurely recorded fourteen (14) unsubmitted disbursement vouchers aggregating ₱0.574 million in the Check Disbursement Journal prior to their submission by the Municipal Treasurer’s Office, a clear deviation from Sections 43 and 44, Chapter 3, Volume I of the NGAS Manual for LGUs, resulted in unreliable accounting records, hampering audit verification of check disbursement transactions, indicating weak internal control over check disbursements, and posing accountability/legal risks to the Municipal Accountant for conclusively recording transactions in the books of accounts without any supporting document as basis.

The timely and proper remittance and deposit of collections, as well as the timely submission of monthly collection reports, were not strictly observed incurring delays of up to 322, 35, and 40 calendar days, respectively, contrary to the provisions under PD No. 1445, Local Treasury Operations Manual, and NGAS Manual for LGUs, thus resulted in weak internal control system over cash management, exposing government funds to risks of loss, misuse, or misappropriation due to undeposited cash balances, and adversely affecting the timeliness of audit procedures and the prompt verification of reported collections.

The maintenance of the unnecessary and remotely located five (5) bank accounts is contrary to the One Fund Concept of accounting and the provisions of DOF-DBM-COA Permanent Committee Joint Circular No. 4-2012 dated September 11, 2012, thereby, the monitoring, reconciliation, and timely access of these bank accounts provides undue burden to the management.

As of cash examination dated December 3, 2025, at least 202 transactions aggregating ₱80.969 million were unrecorded/unadjusted in the cashbooks of Cash in Bank accounts maintained by the Municipal Treasurer, a blatant disregard to the provisions of PD 1445, NGAS Manual for LGUs, and Local Treasury Operations Manual, thereby rendering the cashbooks' balances as of date of cash examination unreliable, indicating a weak internal control on cash management, and undermining the municipality's full adherence to established financial management and accountability standards.

The remittance of shares from the collected Real Property Taxes (RPT) and Community Tax Certificates (CTC) accruing to the component barangays and the Provincial Government of Bukidnon (PGB) were either delayed/unprocessed or doubly made by LGU Malitbog, a non-compliance to the provisions under PD 1445, RA 7160, and Local Treasury Operations Manual, thereby depriving the respective government agencies of the timely access to funds needed to implement their programs and projects.

A total of 5,034 obsolete checks were not requested for destruction by the MTO to the audit team, inconsistent with Section 86 (H) of the Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM), 2nd Edition, resulting in inefficient use of storage space and unnecessary accountability of the Municipal Treasurer.

Payments for the monthly subscription of the accounting and budget management systems developed by ECPAC Systems Corporation totaling ₱0.240 million were made without proper procurement procedures and complete supporting documents, contravening procurement laws and regulations and COA Circular 2012-001, thereby undermining transparency, competitiveness, and accountability envisioned by the procurement law, as well as casting doubt on the regularity and validity of the incurred disbursements.

Salaries and wages paid to all regular and casual employees of LGU Malitbog in CY 2025 have various noted deficiencies, contrary to the provisions of PD 1445, COA Circular 2012-001, and Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, thus, weakened internal controls over employee attendance and payroll processing, diminished accountability of employees and supervisors, created unnecessary workloads and documentation, and cast doubt on the validity and propriety of the consummated disbursements aggregating ₱64.243 million.

Various office supplies and other supplies procured by LGU-Malitbog were improperly consolidated in the APP by presenting these items by department rather than as a single procuring entity, with differing unit prices, and with other noted observations, contrary to applicable provisions of RA 9184 and RA 12009, thereby preventing management from fully adhering to the principles of efficiency and economy, as evidenced by the presence of multiple prices for identical items across POs, Bid Forms/RFQs, PRs, APP and PPMPs, exposing government funds to wastage, and casting doubt on the appropriateness and validity of the disbursed transactions.

Lands under the Paglaum Housing Project with market value totaling ₱94.764 million are not recorded in the LGU’s books of accounts, contrary to Paragraphs 14 and 27 of the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 17- PPE, resulting in the understatement of assets by the same amount and affecting the fair presentation of the Financial Statements as of December 31, 2025.

Completed projects totaling ₱31.605 million were not reclassified to the appropriate asset accounts and were not provided with the corresponding depreciation, contrary to Section 50 of Volume I of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS), the LGU Chart of Accounts and applicable standards under IPSAS 17, thereby understating the Accumulated Depreciation by at least ₱9.123 million and overstating the Government Equity account by the same amount, affecting the reliability of the year-end Financial Statements.

The continued recognition by the Municipality of the completed Multi-Purpose Drying Pavement (MPDP) with Storage Shed projects located in Barangays Mampayag and Kalugmanan under the PPE – Buildings and Other Structures account, despite the apparent transfer of beneficial ownership and control to the concerned Barangays, is not in consonance with the Sections 111 and 112 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 and International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1 and 17, thereby overstated the PPE accounts by ₱3.990 million and affected the fair presentation of the Financial Statements.

The deficiencies in property recording and reconciliation procedures resulted in the non-recognition of land assets with a market value totaling at least ₱1.816 million and the risk of understatement of land properties by up to ₱553.754 million, contrary to Paragraph 14 of IPSAS 17- PPE, understating the PPE-Land account by at least ₱1.816 million and incomplete reporting of assets in the financial statements.

The statutory shares of the barangays and province arising from advance collections of Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) in CY 2025 were not timely recognized under the Due to LGUs account, contrary to IPSAS 1- Presentation of Financial Statements and the Local Government Chart of Accounts. thereby resulting in the misclassification of liabilities accounts by overstating the Other Deferred Credits and understating the Due to LGUs account by ₱72.136 million as of December 31, 2025.

Other Receivables account totaling ₱4.575 million remained unsettled and/or unliquidated for more than 10 years, thereby raising uncertainty as to whether the funds were utilized for their intended purposes and in accordance with the terms and conditions stipulated in the agreements, contrary to Section 2 of Presidential Decree No. 1445; and COA Circular No. 2007-001 dated October 25, 2007, which may result to loss or wastage.

The Due to National Government Agencies (NGAs) account includes dormant and long-outstanding balances in the total amount of ₱22.174 million, pertaining to completed and fully liquidated projects, but lacks the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and other completion documents to establish the nature of obligations and for closing of the account, which is contrary to COA Circular No. 2023-008 dated August 17, 2023, IPSAS 1- Presentation of Financial Statements and the Local Government Chart of Accounts, affecting the reliability, accuracy and fair presentation of the affected accounts in the Financial Statements.

Disbursements for Banog-Banog Trail Run 2025 utilizing the Financial Assistance from the Department of Tourism- Office of the Secretary (DOT-SEC) on sponsorship for the Banog-Banog Festival 2023 in the total amount of ₱0.250 million is not in accordance with the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA), that the Financial Assistance should be used exclusively to defray expenses for Banog-Banog 2023, resulting in unauthorized disbursements.

Land acquisition amounting to ₱ 3.7 million was paid in full by the LGU despite the lack of sufficient documentary requirements to establish transfer of ownership contrary to Section 4 of PD 1445, Section 13.1 COA Circular 2012-001, and Section 13 of EO 1035, thereby tainting the regularity and propriety of the said payment.

Land with an area of 39,600 square meters under Tax Declaration No. 22-016-0002-01759 named after the Municipal Government of Maramag, Bukidnon Maramag was not recorded in the General Fund books of accounts which was inconsistent to COA Circular No. 2015-009 and section 3.1 of COA Circular No. 2024-006, thereby, it understated the total assets and total government equity by its market value amounted to ₱ 71.28 million.

The unspent CY 2020 LDRRMF amounting to ₱ 2.28 million was not reverted to the General Fund as of December 31, 2025 despite the lapse of the five-year utilization period contrary to Section 5.1.13 of COA Circular No. 2012-002, thereby overstating the Trust Liabilities – DRRMF account and correspondingly understating Government Equity, which affected the accuracy and reliability of the financial statements.

Disbursements related to welfare goods totalling ₱ 0.98 million were noted with various deficiencies & irregularities which were contrary to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, hence, regularity, validity and transparency of the procurement and distribution of welfare goods were not assured and could not be properly evaluated.

Monetization of leave credits and maternity leave benefits totalling to ₱ 5.19 million and ₱ 0.09 million, respectively, were booked as “Terminal Leave Benefits Expense” and disbursements thereof without corresponding appropriation, which was inconsistent to International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1 and violation of Section 305 (a) of Republic Act (RA 7160, thereby, tainting the accuracy, reliability, and fair presentation of the affected accounts in the LGU’s financial statements and undermining the legality of the transactions.

Various deficiencies were noted in the grant and payment of Hazard Pay and Subsistence Allowance to its Public Health Workers, Social Workers and Meat Inspector of the LGU’s slaughterhouse with an initial computation of overpayment of P603,647.10, contrary to COA Circular No. 2012-001, DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1 s. of 2018, DBM-DOH JC No. 1 s. of 2012 and DBM-DOH JC No. 1 s. of 2016, thereby affecting the reliability, validity and accuracy of the disbursed funds, depleted the funds for its purpose and loss on the part of the government.

The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) of LGU-Maramag already issued a Notice of Award (NOA) and Notice to Proceed (NTP) to the winning bidder of the trust fund project entitled “Supply, Delivery, and Installation of Rooftop Solar Power System for Eight (8) Municipal Buildings” amounted to ₱ 39.99 million even without the availability of funds amounted to ₱ 33.995 million and prior approval from the People’s Survival Fund Board (PSFB) which was inconsistent to Section 5.7 of Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Circular 2010-9 and Article 3.4 of the Financing Agreement between LGU-Maramag and PSFB respectively, thus, it tainted the propriety, validity and legality of the said procurement.

Various procurements of mixed sand and gravel, and limestone aggregating to ₱ 1.36 million were not subjected to competitive bidding due to the splitting of contracts contrary to Section 26 of COA Circular 92-386 dated October 20, 1992 and Section 39 of the RA No. 12009, thus, affected the validity, propriety and legality of the procurements and the municipality missed to avail volume/wholesale discounts or lower prices associated with bulk purchases through competitive bidding.

LGU Maramag granted an additional 90-day time extension to the supplier for the delivery of goods which was beyond the maximum allowable period and the latter’s request letter was dated and received by the Municipal Mayor after the lapse of the original delivery date provided in the original contracts/purchase orders of the two sub-projects which aggregated to ₱ 10.765 million funded by the People’s Survival Fund (PSF) in contravention to Generic Procurement Manual, Volume 2 - Manual of Procedures for the Procurement of Goods, thus, tainted the propriety, validity and legality of the procurement process.

The Local Government Unit (LGU) of Maramag issued checks for fund transfers with the total amount of ₱ 5.1 million in CY 2025 to Barangay LGUs (BLGUs) with incomplete supporting documents and unliquidated previous years’ fund transfers contrary to Memorandums of Agreement (MOA) between the Municipality and the Barangays, and pertinent COA Circulars, tainting the regularity and propriety of the said fund transfers.

The newly completed Super Health Center amounted to ₱ 8.428 million was turned-over to LGU-Maramag by Department of Health-Center for Health Development Northern Mindanao (DOH-CHDNM) and was immediately recorded in the General Fund book of accounts with only Certificate of Project Acceptance and without Deed of Donation contrary to Section C of the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between the abovementioned parties, thereby, tainting the propriety, validity and legality of the donation and the transfer of ownership of the asset.

Buildings and Motor Vehicles with an aggregate cost of ₱ 284.24 million were not covered with property insurance from the General Insurance Fund (GIF) of the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) which is not in accordance with RA No. 656. In addition, the pertinent Property Inventory Form (PIF) was not prepared nor submitted within the prescribed deadline contravening COA Circular No. 2018-002, thereby exposing the LGU to the risk of not being indemnified or compensated for any damage to, or loss of its property in case of destruction thereof through fire, flood or other force majeure for government properties not covered by insurance.

Various discrepancies and errors were noted relative to the collections and utilization of the 15 percent share of the Office of Building Official (OBO) contrary to DPWH-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 001, thus, the monies were highly exposed to possible cash misappropriation and affected the propriety, validity and legality of the pertinent disbursements.

Several offices of LGU Maramag conducted activities outside the jurisdiction of the municipality, incurring expenses amounting to ₱ 4.48 million which contravened the provisions of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2011‑59 dated April 25, 2011, and resulted in costs that could have been avoided had the activities been conducted within the locality. Moreover, the related disbursement vouchers and supporting documents were found to have deficiencies inconsistent with the requirements of Republic Act (RA) 9184, as amended by RA 12009 thereby impairing the reliability, accountability, and transparency in the utilization of public funds.

The “Construction in Progress” accounts as of December 31, 2025, totaling P151 million, include completed projects that have not been transferred to the appropriate Property, Plant and Equipments (PPE) accounts, unidentified balances, and inactive projects that were no longer under construction or development as at year-end; owing to the non-reconciliation of engineering and accounting reports, contrary to Paragraphs 14 and 71 of the IPSAS 17, COA Circular No. 2015-009, Sections 111 and 112 of P.D. No. 1445, and Section 10 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units Volume I. Consequently, affecting the fair presentation and cast doubt on the accuracy and reliability of the PPE accounts in the CY 2025 consolidated financial statements.

The Municipality paid full monthly Representation and Transportation Allowance (RATA) to Sanggunian Bayan (SB) officials notwithstanding the non-rendering of the required full service or actual work performance, resulting to a total overpayment of P0.508 million, contrary to the provisions embodied in P.D. No. 1445, Section 52(a) of R.A. 7160, DBM Local Budget Circular (LBC) No. 157 and COA Circular No. 2012-003; thereby, validity and propriety of the disbursements could not be established, which may warrant the issuance of a Notice of Suspension or Disallowance, as the case may be.

The Municipality paid Hazard Pay and Subsistence Allowance to its Public Health and Public Social Workers and Meat Inspector was based on improper computations, with incomplete supporting documents, and were paid in advance, resulting in overpayments and underpayments of P0.650 million and 44,214.65, respectively. These disbursements were non-compliant with relevant rules and regulations and are inconsistent with DBM-DOH Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2012, as amended; DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2018; COA Circular No. 2012-001; and Presidential Decree No. 1445, thus casting doubt on the validity and propriety of the disbursements.

Disbursement of financial assistance to the 19 barangays of LGU Pangantucan totaling ₱0.510 million for the conduct of various barangay activities funded out of the General Fund were not supported with complete documentation and were erroneously recorded as an outright expense instead as “Due from Local Government Units (Due from LGUs)”, a non-compliance to Section 4 (8) of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circulars No. 2012-001 and No. 94-013, thereby affecting the propriety and transparency of the disbursed transaction, as well as overstating the operating expenses and understating the government equity by ₱510,000.00 in the CY 2025 Financial Statements.

The non-compliance to the accrual basis of accounting and proper recording for payments of insurance and fidelity bond premiums resulted in the overstatement of the ‘Insurance Expense’ and ‘Fidelity Bond Premium’ accounts by P77,156.56 and P40,748.68, respectively, and the understatement of the ‘Prepaid Insurance’ and ‘Other Prepayments’ accounts. Moreover, erroneous recording of payments of motor vehicle registration/renewal resulted in overstatement of ‘Insurance expense’ amounting to P196,818.10 and understatement of ‘Taxes, Duties and Licenses’ of the same amount contrary to IPSAS No. 1, Section 4.a of Volume 1 of the Manual on NGAS for LGUs and the Revised Chart of Accounts for LGUs, thereby, casting doubt on the accuracy and reliability of related account balances presented in the financial statements.

The current year appropriation for the seventy percent (70%) Disaster Prevention and Mitigation, Preparedness, Response, Rehabilitation, and Recovery portion of the CY 2025 five percent (5%) Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) was not optimally utilized in implementing disaster-related programs, projects, and activities incorporated in the LDRRMF Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP), a non-conformance to NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC No. 2023-1, resulting in non-implementation/partial implementation of some PPAs, thereby affecting the Municipality’s goal of building a resilient community, depriving the public of the essential benefits that could be derived therefrom, and potentially leading to heightened community risks exposure and limited responses during calamities.

The agency’s various disbursements charged to the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF), totaling P1.30 million, were not directly linked to the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) activities and program, contrary to NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC-2013-1 dated March 25, 2013, NDRRMC-DILG-DBM JMC-2014-1 dated April 4, 2014, and Section 3 of COA Circular No. 2012-002; thus, the fund was not fully utilized for its intended purpose of supporting programs, projects, and activities related to disaster prevention and mitigation, disaster preparedness, disaster response, disaster rehabilitation, and recovery.

P75.60 million or 52.09 percent of the total appropriation of P145.13 million for the 20% Local Development Fund was not utilized as at December 31, 2025, due to non-implementation and/or delayed implementation of planned development projects and the inclusion of non-“procurement-and-implementation-ready” projects; thus, optimum utilization of funds was not achieved and unable to provide the constituents the purpose intended at the time expected.

The municipality failed to maintain a separate trust fund for the fifteen percent (15%) Office of the Building Official (OBO) share and the five percent (5%) Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) share of the collected building permit fees and other charges due to the improper recognition of the shares as income of the LGU, contrary to Section 208 of P.D. No. 1096, DPWH-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 001 series of 2013 and DILG MC No. 2014-153, thereby defeating the purpose of the mandatory allocation of the 15% OBO and 5% DPWH share and resulting in non-remittance to the DPWH and improper disposition of funds.

Releases of shares to each component barangay in the collection of the Real Property Tax (RPT) for the period December 2024 to October 2025, totaling P2.16 million, were delayed contrary to RA No. 7160, thereby depriving the barangays of the immediate use of the funds for the implementation of programs, projects, and activities beneficial to the constituents.

The latest Municipal Tax Code and its tax rates were not updated and adjusted from calendar year 2019 to 2025 or for the last seven (7) years, a non-adherence to Section 129 of RA No. 7160, thereby depriving the Municipality and its constituents of additional revenue sources to fund its projects.

Inclusion of the cost of the IP Housing Project at Paitan, Quezon in the total amount of ₱8.948 million as part of the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) account of the Municipality is not in accordance with Section 50 Chapter 3Volume I of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System and the COA Circular 2015-009, thereby misstating the financial statements of the Municipality as of December 31, 2025.

The ‘Land’ account with a total balance of ₱131.547 million presented under Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position of the Municipality as of December 31, 2025 was found to have deficiencies, a non-compliance with Section 111 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and Section 148 of COA Circular No. 92-386, thus, the accuracy, completeness, and reliability of the ‘Land” account cannot be reasonably assured.

Various financial transactions were erroneously recorded under the “Other Payables” account contrary to Section 3 Chapter 1 Volume 3 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System, resulting in an overstatement of the “Other Payables” account by ₱7.092 million and “Salaries and Wages” account by ₱0.101 million while understating the Municipality’s income accounts by ₱0.904 million, “Deferred Credits/Unearned Income” by ₱3.832 million and Government Equity by ₱2.255 million for the calendar year ended December 31, 2025.

LGU counterpart for the construction of school buildings was recorded as Property, Plant, and Equipment of the Municipality, which is not in compliance with Section 50 Chapter III Volume I of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS Manual) and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thus, overstating the Property, Plant, and Equipment of the Municipality in the total amount of ₱8.249 million.

The Municipality transferred PhilHealth reimbursements for “Health Care Institution (HCI) Facility Fee” from the General Fund HCI Charges bank account to the General Fund proper bank account resulting in the commingling of earmarked funds, a non-compliance to Section 45 of the Revised IRR of National Health Insurance Act of 2013, thereby rendering the utilization untraceable to their legally intended purpose.

PhilHealth reimbursements for “Health Care Institution (HCI) Facility Fee” may have been used for unintended purposes due to absence of Special Purpose Appropriation directly linking this fund, a non-compliance to Section 45 of the Revised IRR of National Health Insurance Act of 2013, which limits the transparency and accountability over the use of the fund and increases the risk that PhilHealth reimbursements were not fully utilized as intended.

Some liquidation reports of cash advances granted to Special Disbursing Officers were found to be non-compliant to COA Circular No. 97-002, which weakened the accountability over the use of public funds and impaired the reliability of liquidation reports and supporting documents, thereby increasing the risk of error and misapplication of fund.

Actual work accomplished in the concreting of Farm to Market Road at Barangay Minongan Phase I and II were not in accordance with the contract and variations thereof were not supported with variation orders, a non-compliance to the IRR of RA 9184 and RA12009, thus, cast doubt on the propriety, validity and legality of the project modifications.

Deficiencies were noted in the payments of progress billings totaling to ₱40.754 million which is not in accordance with Section 4 (6) and 4 (7) of P.D. No. 1445, otherwise known as the “Government Auditing Code of the Philippines,” and COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thus, cast doubt on the validity and propriety of the claims.

Payrolls of Casual Employees in CY 2025 were incomplete, were not supported with complete application for leave of absences, certificate of appearances, travel order, accomplishment report, the necessary certification for first salary claim, contrary to Section 4(6) of P.D. No. 1445, Section 4.1.3 COA Circular No 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, Section 21, 51 and 53 of CSC MC No. 41, s. 1998, thus, the validity, propriety and legality of the disbursements for salaries and wages-casual/contractual could not be established.

Deficiencies in the documentation of Repairs and Maintenance - Machinery and Equipment in the total amount of ₱1.825 million, contrary to Section 4(6) of P.D. No. 1445, Section 9.1.3.4 of COA Circular 2012-001 and operating procedures provided under Chapter IV of the Training Handbook on Property & Supply Management System, thus, cast doubt as to the validity and propriety of the disbursements and adequacy of the internal control for the same.

The Municipal Accountant recorded insurance premium payments totaling ₱1.575 million as outright expense, contrary to the accrual basis of accounting under International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1 and the provisions of COA Circular No. 2015-009, resulting in the overstatement of expenses and understatement of assets by ₱1.005 million, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Improper recognition of ‘Accounts Payable’ and ‘Inventories’ for undelivered goods, contrary to IPSAS No. 1 and Sections 4(s) and 126, Volume I of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs, resulted in the overstatement of both accounts by ₱1.969 million as of December 31, 2025, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Various accounting errors were noted in relation to the project, “Construction of Multi-Purpose Building at Barangay Bulalang, Dao, San Jose, and Sto. Domingo Phases 2 to 3”, with a total asset book value of ₱10.994 million, contrary to IPSAS 1 and 19 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, casting doubt on the reliability of the balances of the affected accounts, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements as of December 31, 2025.

LGU San Fernando did not comply with the requirement to submit periodic inspection and monitoring reports to DOH-CHDNM and likewise did not record in its books the Department of Health (DOH) turned over project, Construction of New San Fernando Super Health Center, including the donated parcel of land for said project with an aggregate estimated value of ₱8.520 million contrary to the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and IPSAS 17; thereby casting doubt on the diligence of the LGU in fulfilling its responsibilities under the MOA and resulting in the understatement of the Property, Plant, and Equipment (PPE) and income by the same amount.

Construction in Progress (CIP) totaling ₱367.153 million were found to have various deficiencies in relation to the accuracy and correctness of accounting records and the inconsistency of status of different projects as recorded in the CIP account when compared against the reports of the MEO, contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009, IPSAS Nos. 1 and 17, Section No. 58 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445; hence, the reliability and fair presentation of the PPE and related accounts in the financial statements as of December 31, 2025, are materially affected.

Cash Advances totaling ₱4.530 million granted for various purposes remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2025, contrary to Section 89 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 and pertinent provisions of COA Circular No. 97-002. Moreover, the presence of abnormal/negative balances amounting to P25,743.41 coupled with the delayed recording of liquidation transactions affected the fair presentation of balances in the financial statements, overstated the Advances to Special Disbursing Officer account and understated the corresponding expenses by P0.390 million, inconsistent with Sections 111 and 112 of the PD No. 1445.

Various deficiencies were noted in the review and reconciliation of PPE accounts with the Report on Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE) and subsidiary records, contrary to Sections 58 and 111 (1) and (2) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445, thereby casting doubt on the existence, completeness and valuation of PPE as well as the fair presentation of the PPE accounts in the Financial Statements as of December 31, 2025.

Various deficiencies were noted in the audit of the CY 2024 Seal of Good Local Governance Incentive Fund (SGLGIF) amounting to ₱1.153 million, contrary to DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2025-014 dated February 27, 2025, and Section 50, Chapter 3 of Volume 1 of the MNGAS for LGUs, thereby casted doubt on the compliance of the Municipality of San Fernando with prescribed guidelines, created bottlenecks in the monitoring of the project, and adversely affected the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Significant non-compliance was observed in the implementation, monitoring, reporting and accounting of the CY 2023 SGLGIF project, “Construction of Solar Street Lights Barangay Little Baguio & Mabuhay,” amounting to ₱1.800 million, which was not in accordance with DILG MC No. 2024-006 and the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA No. 9184, thereby raising doubt on the regularity, adequacy and propriety of the overall implementation, monitoring and financial reporting, and potentially adversely affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Consumed food and welfare goods totaling ₱3.894 million, intended for LGU initiatives, remained recorded under Inventories as of December 31, 2025 due to the non-submission of documents evidencing consumption, contrary to IPSAS 12, Sections No. 121 and 122 of MNGAS for LGUs, and Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445; thereby resulted in the overstatement of the Inventory account and the understatement of the corresponding expense accounts by the same amount.

Significant deficiencies were observed in the implementation of and compliance with the requirements of the NCDC project- Construction of National Child Development Center, amounting to ₱3.067 million, contrary to the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) signed by the Early Childhood Care and Development (ECCD) Council and the Municipality of San Fernando, Section 4.6 of COA Circular 94-013, and Section 12 of RA No. 12199, thereby casting doubt on the compliance of the LGU to the terms and conditions of the MOA and RA No. 12199, the propriety of the project’s implementation, and adversely affect the fair presentation in the financial statements.

Inconsistencies were noted in the recording of identical transactions amounting to ₱29.215 million in the Subsidiary Ledger (SL) of the General Fund – Cash in Local Treasury, contrary to Section 111 of PD No. 1445 and Paragraph 38 of IPSAS 1- Presentation of Financial Statements, thereby casting doubt on the regularity, reliability and accuracy of the accounting records.

Various deficiencies were found in the review of the contract and other relevant documents for the project entitled, “Construction of Solar Street Lights, Little Baguio, San Fernando, Bukidnon,” with contract price of ₱1.148 million contrary to Sections 12 and 34.3 of the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (R-IRR) of RA 9184, and COA Circular No. 2009-001, thereby casting doubt on the validity of the procurement activity conducted and creating a bottleneck in the conduct of auditorial review.

The Municipal Treasurer’s Office’s (MTO) procedures for managing and monitoring stale/lost checks issued by LGU San Fernando showed various deficiencies in contravention to Section Nos. 58 and 59, Chapter 3, Volume No. 1 of the NGAS for LGUs, thereby casting doubt on the regularity, adequacy and propriety of the internal control measures in place.

The Local Economic Enterprises (LEEs) of LGU San Fernando did not have a separate Annual Operating Budget and was wholly appropriated in the General Fund Annual Budget, contrary to the Manual on the Setting Up and Operation of LEEs of 2016, and Section 325 of the Local Government Code, thereby casting doubt on the propriety of appropriations totaling ₱10.318 million and obligations.

The procurement of drugs and medicines totaling ₱1.934 million in CY 2025, was not supported with complete documentary requirements as prescribed under Section No. 9.1.3.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, contrary to Section 16 of RA No. 7160 and Section 4 (6) of PD No. 1445. Thus, the propriety of the transactions cannot be ascertained, and the eligibility of the winning bidder/supplier is rendered doubtful.

The Municipality incurred deficiencies in their application for Kadiwa Financial Grant Assistance program amounting to ₱5 million contrary to Section 2 of PD No. 1445, Department of Agriculture (DA) MC No. 22, Series of 2023, signed MOA and COA Circular No. 2015 -009; thereby risking possible loss of grant eligibility, delaying the benefits of timely project implementation to stakeholders, and casting doubt on the correctness of the accounting entry for the transfer of LGU Equity.

The Municipality granted Medical Allowances totaling ₱1.295 million to various officers and employees for CY 2025, however, documentary deficiencies and non-compliance were noted, contrary to Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Budget Circular (BC) No. 2024-6 dated December 12, 2024, thereby casting doubt on the eligibility of the recipients and validity of the grant of allowances, while also creating a risk of double payment in CY 2026 totaling ₱0.182 million, if grants in the succeeding year are not properly monitored.

Advance payments to the contractors of various infrastructure projects implemented by the LGU totaling ₱2.521 million were made without the required irrevocable standby letters of credit/security bonds/bank guarantees, contrary to Section 4.2 of Annex “E” of the 2016 R- IRR of RA No. 9184 and Section 9.1.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, thereby exposing the advance payment to an additional layer of risk that could have been mitigated through the prescribed safeguards.

The grant of cash advance for confidential expenses in CY 2025 along with the relevant documents, amounting to ₱2.5 million, incurred deficiencies contrary to Section Nos. 4.2 and 6.1.8.4 of COA-DBM-DILG-GCG-DND Joint Circular No. 2015-1 dated January 8, 2015, thereby causing delay in the implementation of programmed peace and order activities of the LGU and non-compliance with established procedures and guidelines.

Various deficiencies were noted in the four approved request for work time extensions at 51.34 percent physical work accomplishment, corresponding to progress billings totaling ₱123.764 million, contrary to Parts 49.3 and 81.5 of the Philippine Rural Development Project (PRDP) Scale-Up Module 1 Guidelines for the Procurement of Infrastructure Subprojects, thereby casting doubt on the propriety, regularity, and validity of the time extension granted.

Various deficiencies were found in the review of the contract and other relevant documents for the project, “Construction of Multi-Purpose Hall Bonacao, Phase 1,” with contract price of ₱3.499 million, contrary to Sections 12 and 34.3 of the R-IRR, of RA 9184, and COA Circular No. 2009-001, thereby casting doubt on the validity of the procurement activity conducted and creating a bottleneck in the conduct of auditorial review.

Significant deficiencies were observed during the review of documents and ocular inspection of projects, “Construction of Multi-Purpose Hall at Brgys. Bulalang, Dao, San Jose, and Sto. Domingo (Phase 2 – Doors & Windows Installation ),” and “Construction of Multi-Purpose Building at Brgy. Bulalang, Sto. Domingo, and San Jose (Phase 3 – Ceiling, Electrical, Plumbing, Septic,etc.),” with a total contract price of ₱3.698 million, contrary to Section Nos. 2.1 to 2.2 of COA Circular No. 2013-004, Article 171 of Section 4 of the Revised Penal Code, Section 3(e) of RA 3019, and Section 2 of PD No. 1445, thereby casting doubt on the legality, veracity, and propriety of the procedures, reports, and actions of the personnel involved. The assets are also put at risk due to lack of security in the project sites exposing government properties to damage and loss.

Journal entries related to the transfers of the 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) shares from the National Tax Allotment (NTA) totaling ₱87.646 million for CY 2025 were incorrectly recorded, contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby resulting in the misclassification and misstatement of affected accounts as of December 31, 2025.

Various deficiencies were noted during the reconciliation of the CY 2025 Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP), the CY 2023-2025 Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Plan (LDRRMP) and the CY 2025 LDRRMF Monitoring and Evaluation Report (MER) and during the review of the Statement of Comparison of Budgeted and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) for CY 2025, Annual and Supplemental Budgets, and the Statement of Appropriations, Allotments, Obligations, and Balances (SAAOB) as of December 31, 2025, contrary to Section 21 of RA No. 10121 and Paragraph 14 of IPSAS 24, which resulted to a total of ₱1.450 million non-aligned PPAs, appropriations variance and unreported obligation of ₱1.050 million and ₱0.84 million, respectively.

The accuracy and reliability of the year-end balances of the Cash Local Treasury and Cash in Bank- Local Currency, Current Accounts in the amount of ₱40,118.97 and ₱113.797 million, respectively are doubtful due to: (a) inclusion of closed bank accounts totaling ₱1.333 million; (b) recording of deposits made in the ensuing year amounting ₱5.881 million and treating them as deposit in transit in the bank reconciliation statement as of December 31, 2025; (c) non-recording of collections amounting ₱0.128 million; (d) unadjusted reconciling items totaling (net) ₱9.831 million; and (e) other deficiencies noted contrary to Paragraph 27 of the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1, COA Circular No. 96-011, and Section 74 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445.

The accuracy, existence, completeness and valuation of the reported Inventory account balance in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position (CSFP) as of December 31, 2025 totaling ₱1.298 million could not be ascertained due to i) the variance between the balances reported in the Report of Physical Count of Inventories (RPCI) and those reflected in the CSFP, including the absence of RPCI for other Inventory accounts, resulting in a net overstatement of at least ₱0.323 million; (ii) inconsistent and incorrect preparation of the RPCI; iii) non- compliance with the Perpetual Inventory Method prescribed under the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs; and iv) other deficiencies noted in inventory recording, monitoring, and reporting, thereby casting doubt on the reliability and fairness of the inventory account balance presented in the CY 2025 Financial Statements, contrary to pertinent accounting rules and regulations.

The existence, completeness, and valuation of the Property and Equipment (PPE) account balance of ₱381.410 million as of December 31, 2025 could not be ascertained due to the: a) presence of unspecified/unidentified PPE items aggregating ₱66.559 million b) discrepancy of ₱44.319 million between the balances per books of accounts and the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE) c) other inconsistencies found which are not in consonance with the provisions of Sections 63, 111(1), and 114 (2) of PD No. 1445, IPSAS 1, pertinent provision of MNGAS for LGUs, COA Circular No. 2022-004 and COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020.

The collectability, existence and correctness of valuation of the “Due from LGUs” account is doubtful due to the inclusion of (a) dormant receivables totaling ₱1.803 million and (b) long outstanding fund transfers to barangays aging nine years totaling ₱0.600 million, contrary to IPSAS 1 and COA Circular Nos. 94-013, 2016-005, and 2025-005, resulting to unreliable account balance and delayed recognition of the appropriate Asset and/or Expense account for the utilization of funds transferred.

The validity and legality of reported Accounts Payable (AP) balance in the aggregate amount of ₱21.374 million could not be established due to the (a) presence of dormant accounts aggregating ₱0.272 million, (b) recording of liabilities in the absence of proof to warrant obligations totaling ₱8.518 million, and (c) various noted deficiencies, which is not in consonance with the IPSAS No. 1 and Section 4(s), Volume I of the MNGAS, thus, affecting the true financial position of the municipality at the end of CY 2025.

The PPE account was misstated due to (a) deficiencies and lack of essential information in the depreciation schedule, (b) nonrecognition of depreciation expense and absence of depreciation schedule for certain depreciable PPE Accounts, which overstated the Assets and Government Equity accounts by at least ₱0.993 million as a result of understated provision of depreciation by the same amount; (c) non-provision of depreciation to PPE accounts with aggregate acquisition cost of ₱30 million; and (d) other deficiencies in the computation and recognition of depreciation, thereby casting doubts on the accuracy reliability and fair presentation of the reported carrying amount of PPE and Government Equity accounts in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025.

The reconciliation between the ‘Actual Amounts’ in the Statement of Comparison of Budget and Actual Amounts (SCBAA) and the Statement of Financial Performance for the year ended December 31, 2025, showed material items without proper disclosures regarding the breakdown and information of the aforementioned items, contrary to Section 111 of PD No. 1445, Paragraphs 7 and 46 of IPSAS 1, and Paragraphs 14, 39, and 47 of IPSAS 24, thereby adversely affecting fair presentation of the Notes to Financial Statements (NTFS) and the SCBAA.

The amount of variance between the balances of Intra-agency accounts decreased by 83.42 percent, or ₱1.445 million, for CYs 2024 and 2025; however, a total variance of ₱0.287 million remained unreconciled at year-end, a non-compliance to paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, thereby casting doubt on the correctness and reliability of the balances in the financial statements.

Inter-agency payables representing withheld premium contributions and loan amortizations for the accounts Due to BIR and Due to PhilHealth in the amount of ₱1.427 million and ₱0.174 million respectively were not remitted in full within the prescribed period contrary to pertinent Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Revenue Regulations and Section 18 of the IRR of the National Health Insurance Act of 2013, thereby exposing the Municipality and the employees to the possible imposition of penalty and surcharges for the late remittance thereof. While the Due to GSIS and Due to PAG-IBIG accounts reported a negative ending balances in the amount of ₱0.527 million and ₱47,527.30 respectively as of December 31, 2025, thus casting doubt on the reliability of the affected balances as reflected in the Financial Statement contrary to IPSAS 1, and its compliance to the Republic Act (RA) No. 8291, Section E.4 of HDMF Circular No. 275 dated January 22, 2010.

The payment of salaries to casual and regular employees of the LGU totaling ₱31.563 million was not supported with complete and appropriate documentary requirements, contrary to Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445 and Item 1.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 dated June 14, 2012, thereby affecting the validity, accuracy, and propriety of the disbursements.

Cash advances amounting to ₱0.555 million remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2025 and additional cash advances were granted despite the non- liquidation of previous cash advances, contrary to COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997. Moreover, some cash advances were granted beyond the authorized maximum cash accountability prescribed by Treasury Circular No. 1-2022 dated May 30 2022, while the recording of certain cash advance transactions was inconsistent with Sections 111 and 112 of the PD No. 1445, the provision of Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, thereby exposing government funds to increased risk of misuse or misappropriation and resulting in the misstatement of the affected accounts in the financial statements.

Deficiencies in the submission and reporting of the Gender and Development (GAD) Plan and Budget (GPB) and Accomplishment Report (AR), including delayed submission to the audit team, non-compliance with prescribed budgeting and reporting guidelines, and absence of supporting documents, contrary to the relevant provisions in PCW-DILG-DBM-NEDA Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2013-01 and Item V of COA Circular No. 2014-001, thereby impairing the timely determination of the judicious use of the funds and the efficiency and effectiveness of interventions in addressing existing gender issues.

Sixteen (16) reconciling items (comprising of unbooked check disbursements, credit memo, and interest income) remained unrecorded/unadjusted in the books of accounts, aggregating a net understatement of ₱0.259 million, contrary to Section 112 of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, thereby affecting the accuracy and reliability of the Cash in Bank and the corresponding accounts reflected in the financial statements for CY 2025, while the non-submission to the audit team of the eight (8) unrecorded check disbursements already encashed per bank statements totaling ₱1.283 million may warrant the issuance of audit suspension or disallowance, as the case may be.

Inaccurate and unreliable balances of the Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivable accounts were presented in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025 owing to the non-reconciliation of the accounting, treasury, and assessor's records, inconsistent with the provisions of PD No. 1445 and NGAS Manual for LGU, thereby understated the said accounts by ₱16.822 million and ₱17.001 million, respectively, while the Deferred RPT and Deferred SET payable accounts were understated by ₱16.787 million, and ₱17.018 million, respectively.

Construction costs amounting ₱83.047 million incurred for the construction of the Talakag Government Center was not recorded by MAccO in the Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2025 due to MEO’s non-preparation of progress reports, inconsistent with Section 4, Volume I of the Manual on NGAS for LGUs, Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated 1 December 2015, and Section IV item 41 of the General Conditions of Contract, resulting in the understatement of both the Construction in Progress and Accounts Payable accounts by ₱83.047 million, casting doubt on the accuracy, and reliability of the said account balances presented in the financial statements.

Thirty-one (31) completed projects recorded under Building and Other Structures accounts totaling ₱38.414 million as of December 31, 2025 were not depreciated due to untimely reconciliation of engineering and accounting reports, contrary to IPSAS No. 45 replacing IPSAS No. 17, and Section 4.o of the Manual on NGAS for LGUs, Volume No. 1, thereby, overstated the Property, Plant and Equipment and Government Equity accounts both by ₱0.967 million, while understated the Depreciation Expense and overstated the Surplus/(Deficit) accounts both by ₱0.792 million in the consolidated financial statements.

Absence of verifiable documents to establish the transactions in the amount of ₱16.957 million recorded in Accounts Payable is not in accordance to Section 4 (6) of Presidential Decree No. 1445, Section 157 Volume 1 of Government Accounting and Auditing Manual, and COA Circular No. 2015-009, thereby, precluding the auditor to validate the existence and validity of transactions affecting the accuracy and reliability of the financial statements as of December 31, 2025.

The Municipality did not prepare and submit the required year-end financial statements for its 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) account, contrary to RA No. 7160 and NGAS Manual for LGUs, thereby, the transparency and accountability in the receipt and usage of the 20% LDF could not be established depriving the intended users of relevant financial information that are vital in the making of well-informed and sound decision.

The timely and proper remittance and deposit of collections, as well as the timely submission of monthly collection reports, were not strictly observed incurring delays of up to 77, 214, and 63 calendar days, respectively, contrary to the provisions under PD No. 1445, Local Treasury Operations Manual, and NGAS Manual for LGUs, thus resulted in weak internal control system over cash management, exposing government funds to risks of loss, misuse, or misappropriation due to undeposited cash balances, and adversely affecting the timeliness of audit procedures and the prompt verification of reported collections.

The maintenance of five (5) unnecessary and eleven (11) remotely located bank accounts is contrary to the One Fund Concept of accounting and the provisions of DOF-DBM-COA Permanent Committee Joint Circular No. 4-2012 dated September 11, 2012, thereby, the monitoring, reconciliation, and timely access of these bank accounts provides undue burden to the management.

A total of 406 obsolete checks were not requested for destruction by the MTO to the audit team, inconsistent with Section 86 (H) of the Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM), 2nd Edition, resulting in inefficient use of storage space and unnecessary accountability of the Municipal Treasurer.

The LGU’s procurement and distribution of premium rice totaling ₱1.369 million in CY 2025 have various noted deficiencies, contrary to provisions of the IRR of RA No. 12009, and Section 447 of the RA No. 7160, thereby compromising the propriety of the procurement process and undermining the fairness and transparency of rice distribution during barangay visitation of the Sangguniang Bayan.

Monetized leave credits at most ₱2.076 million were improperly paid to officials and employees of LGU Talakag despite: (1) insufficient vacation leave balances, (2) being charged to sick leave credits, and (3) leaving employees with less than the required five days of retained leave after monetization, inconsistent to Sections 22 and 23 of the Amended Omnibus Rules on Leave Implementing Book V of Administrative Code of 1987, thus, the legality and validity of these disbursed transactions could not be ascertained.

The LGU failed to comply with certain provisions of the procedural guidelines on the disposition and use of the 20% share from building permit fees and other charges, contrary to PD No. 1445 and DPWH-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 001 dated 4 July 2013, resulting in the non-utilization of the 15% OBO share and non-remittance of the 5% DPWH share, leaving public funds idle in the trust fund.

The Local School Board (LSB) of LGU Talakag failed to submit the required SEF Utilization Reports, as prepared by the Local Accountant, to the DepEd, DBM, and Sangguniang Bayan, contrary to Item 6.1 of the DepEd-DBM-DILG Joint Circular no. 1 s. 2017, thus, the intention of such guidelines to promote and enhance transparency and accountability over the utilization of SEF was not properly achieved for failure to provide relevant information to the intended users of said reports.

The existence and accuracy of the Cash-in-Bank account amounting to ₱704.629 million as of December 31, 2025 could not be established due to: a) five hundred twenty-two (522) book reconciling items totaling to ₱94.284 million (additions) and ₱67.721 million (deductions) remained unadjusted at year-end; b) two hundred forty-eight (248) items were presented as “Deposits in Transit” in the bank reconciliation statements totaling ₱19.714 million aging 3 years to over 20 years; and c) non-adjustment of fifty (50) stale checks aging from 7 months to over 10 years totaling to ₱0.575 million at year-end, which is inconsistent with Section 74 and 112 of Presidential Decree (PD) 1445, Sec. 3.3 COA Circular No. 96-011, and Sections 32 and 59 of Manual on the New Government accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs).

The Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivables with balances of (₱1.716) million and ₱3.402 million, respectively, as of December 31, 2025, cannot be relied upon due to the following: a) the RPT and SET Receivables per books do not tally with the List of Delinquent Real Property Taxpayers with a discrepancy of ₱160.324 million; and b) presence of balances that have remained outstanding for more than 10 years totaling ₱113.462 million, thus were not in accordance with Paragraph 27 of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1, Paragraph 37 of IPSAS 3 and MNGAS for LGUs, and affecting the fairness of presentation of the accounts in the financial statements.

The existence and accuracy of the reported inventory balances totaling ₱202.660 million could not be fully ascertained due to: a) the non-submission of the Report on the Physical Count of Inventories (RPCI) to COA Auditor within the prescribed period; b) the non-preparation and non-maintenance Supplies Ledger Cards (SLCs) and Stock Cards (SCs); and c) the variance totaling ₱181.349 million between the records maintained by the CAO and the submitted RPCI prepared by the CGSO, contrary to Section 111(2) of PD No. 1445, Section 114 and 124 of the MNGAS for LGUs, Volume I, Item V (1) of COA Circular No. 80-124 and Item 5.8 of COA Circular No. 2020-006, affecting the fair presentation of the inventory account balances in the CY 2025 Consolidated Statement of Financial Position.

The accuracy, completeness and existence of the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts totaling ₱5.136 billion as at December 31, 2025, excluding Construction in Progress (CIP) accounts, could not be ascertained due to the unreconciled variance amounting to ₱492.204 million between the accounting records and the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant, and Equipment (RPCPPE), contrary to Paragraph 27 of IPSAS 1, Volume I; COA Circular No. 2020-006 dated January 31, 2020; Paragraph 4, Section 114 of the MNGAS for LGUs, Volume I; and Section 491(b) of the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual (GAAM), Volume I, thus, affecting the fair presentation of the PPE balances in the financial statements.

The reliability of the CIP account, with a reported balance of ₱254.687 million as of December 31, 2025, could not be relied upon due to: (a) erroneous entries/recordings in the books resulting in negative balances totaling ₱71.997 million; (b) failure to reclassify completed projects totaling ₱77.853 million to the appropriate PPE accounts; and (c) presence of unidentified balances amounting to ₱2.624 million, which are not in strict adherence to Sections 111 and 112 of PD No. 1445, MNGAS for LGUs and IPSAS 1.

The Accounts Payable with reported year-end balance of ₱249.89 million is unreliable because of the inclusion of goods procured: a) but were delivered and received only after December 31, 2025, amounting to ₱3.155 million and b) which neither the delivery date of the supplier nor the acceptance date by the LGU are indicated in the supporting documents, amounting to ₱2.480 million, which were not in accordance with Section 4.6 of PD No. 1445, COA Circular No. 2015-009, Section 118 of the MNGAS for LGUs, Volume I, and IPSAS 1, affecting the fair presentation of the account in the financial statements.

Expenses related to the Support to Peace and Order Programs of the City amounting to ₱29.996 million were erroneously recorded as Intelligence Expense which is not in accordance to IPSAS 1, COA Circular No. 2015-009 and COA-DBM-DILG-GCG-DND JMC No. 2015-01 thereby affecting the accuracy of the said accounts as reported in the Statement of Financial Performance.
