The accuracy and reliability of the Advances to Special Disbursing Officers (SDOs) and Advances to Officers and Employees (O&E) accounts in the CY 2025 Consolidated Financial Statements, totaling ₱30.813 million and ₱12.118 million, respectively, could not be ascertained due to an unreconciled balance of ₱10.674 million between the financial statements and the supporting schedules for the General Fund, contrary to the IPSAS No. 1, Section 111 of PD No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2015-009, affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

Various deficiencies were noted in the payment of FY 2023 Performance Based Bonus (PBB) to LGU officials and employees amounting to ₱17.325 million, to wit: a) the payment was made prior to the issuance of the Notice of Eligibility by DILG; b) potentially ineligible officials and employees were granted PBB totaling ₱0.817 million; c) the total FY 2023 PBB exceeded the recognized Accounts Payable for the said benefits by ₱1.525 million, and (d) actual payment exceeded the appropriation for the purpose, contravening items 5.8 and 6.8 (d) of DILG-DBM Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2025-001 dated April 30, 2025, COA Circular No. 2015-009 and Section 4(1) of PD No. 1445, thereby affecting the accuracy of financial records and the regularity of the transactions.

Personnel Motivation Incentives (PMIs) totaling to ₱31.230 million were granted to its appointive and elective officials and employees without adhering to the policies and other requirements of Section 33 of PD No. 807, s. 1975, Civil Service Commission (CSC) Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 01, s. 2001, the CSC-approved Program on Awards and Incentives for Service Excellence (PRAISE) of the City Government of Valencia, and such other pertinent laws, rules and regulations on Employee Suggestions and Incentive Awards System, thus, the validity, propriety, and legality of the disbursements could not be ascertained.

Communication Allowances were granted to officials and employees at rates ranging from one hundred fifty percent (150%) up to five hundred (500%) of the maximum amounts prescribed under DBM Budget Circular No. 2024-2, resulting in excessive expenditures totaling ₱368,726.59.

The procurement process observed by the City of Valencia is attended by various deficiencies/irregularities, as manifested by: (a) non-preparation and submission of Procurement Monitoring Report (PMR); (b) 11 transactions totaling ₱3.683 million were implemented or goods were delivered prior to the dates indicated in the Notice of Award (NOA), Purchase Order (PO), and Notice to Proceed (NTP); and 24 contracts totaling ₱58.777 million were not executed within ten calendar days from receipt of NOA, contrary to pertinent provision of RA No. 9184 and its Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) and other relevant regulations, indicating weakness in controls and impairing the principles of transparency and competitiveness.

The City of Valencia incurred excessive Government Share contributions to Pag-IBIG Fund for its officials and employees aggregating ₱4.485 million, contrary to RA No. 9679 and HDMF Circular No. 460, resulting in the incurrence of unnecessary favor at the expense of the City’s coffer.

Payments for monetization amounting to ₱14.364 million were found to have the following deficiencies, to wit: a) 416 personnel were allowed to monetize more than ten (10 days) totaling ₱11.189 million which were not supported with “Request for monetization of leave covering more than 10 days duly approved by the Head of the Agency”; b) Monetization of 482 personnel amounting to ₱13.630 million were deducted from their sick leave credits without exhausting first the remaining vacation leave credits balance; and c) 13 personnel were left with less than five (5) vacation leave credits after monetization amounting to ₱0.482 million, contrary to Section 5.14 of COA Circular No. 2012-001, CSC Resolution No. 000034, and section 23 of Omnibus Rule on Leave, thereby casting doubt on the propriety and validity of the transactions.

The implementation and monitoring of the City’s priority development projects funded under the 20% Local Development Fund (LDF) for CY 2025 revealed the following deficiencies: a) only 12 out of 27 development projects or 44 percent, amounting to ₱61.500 million (excluding projects financed through loans), were fully implemented; and b) the required quarterly reports on the utilization of the 20% LDF were not prepared, contrary to Items 3.2.3, 4.0, and 6.0 of DBM-DOF-DILG JMC No. 1 dated November 4, 2020, thus, the desired socio-economic development and potential benefits from the unimplemented PPAs were not timely achieved and the evaluation of LDF utilization could not be properly undertaken.

Deficiencies were noted in planning and implementation GAD PPAs, to wit: (a) the GAD Database was not properly established and maintained; (b) a gender-responsive Monitoring and Evaluation System has yet to be established and operationalized; (c) the DILG-endorsed GAD Plan and Budget and GAD Accomplishment Report (AR) for CY 2025 were not submitted to the COA Audit Team within the prescribed period; and (d) the GAD budget was not fully utilized, resulting in a material unexpended balance of ₱36.674 million, hence the direction in setting and monitoring the GAD initiatives towards the achievement of its gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE) goals were affected contrary to the provisions in Item B and Items 3.4 and 5.0 of PCW-DILG-DBM-NEDA JMC No. 2013-01, Section 9, Chapter VI, Section 36 (a) & (c) of the Magna Carta for Women, and Item V of COA Circular No. 2014-001 dated March 18, 2014.

A comparison between the CY 2025 Financial Statements and the Statement of Sources and Application of Funds (SSAF) as of December 31, 2025 for the PRDP still disclosed a variance of ₱197,148.57. This discrepancy contravenes Section 111(1) of PD 1445 and Item 6.4.1(a)1 of the PRDP Financial Management Operations Guidelines, thereby casting doubt on fair presentation of the financial reports.

Various furniture, fixtures, equipment and other property, plant and equipment (PPE) amounting to ₱220,000.00, turned-over by contractors to the LGU upon completion of PRDP Concreting of Jct. Mabuhay to Barangay Banlag Proper to Sitio Pantaron Farm to Market Road, were not appropriately recognized in the books which is not in accordance to IPSAS and COA Circular No. 2024-006, thereby affecting the fair presentation of the financial statements.

The required monthly and quarterly financial reports and statements for CY 2025 were submitted beyond the prescribed deadline, contrary to Chapters 3.4.1, 3.4.2, 3.4.3, and 6.7.1 of the Philippine Rural Development Project (PRDP) Financial Management Operations Guidelines, and Part 2.13.3 of PRDP Intensified Building-Up of Infrastructure and Logistics for Development I-Build, thereby casting doubt on the propriety and regularity of financial reporting.
